knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stage and Newton-Step Bounds for the Multistage Process
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds the number of stages and cumulative Newton steps under the theorem's stated stage-length and exact stage-update conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that \(f\) is twice strongly convex with parameter \(\sigma_2(f)>0\), has Lipschitz-continuous third derivative with constant \(L_3(f)>0\), and has unique minimizer \(x^*\). Fix \(R>0\), let \(\|y_0-x^*\|\le R\), and define \(R_k=R2^{-k}\). Suppose the multistage process produces \(y_k\) and \(m_k\in\mathbb N\) such that, for every \(k\ge0\), \[m_k\ge4\left(\frac{L_3(f)R}{\sigma_2(f)}\right)^{1/3},\qquad f(y_{k+1})-f(x^*)=\frac{8L_3(f)\|y_k-x^*\|^3}{m_k(m_k+1)(m_k+2)}.\] Then it terminates after at most \[\frac1{\ln4}\ln\left(\frac83\left(\frac{L_3(f)R}{\sigma_2(f)}\right)^3\right)\] stages, and, if \(m_0\) is the number of Newton steps in the first stage, the total number of Newton steps is at most \(4m_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated strong-convexity, third-derivative regularity, initialization, stage-length, and exact stage-update assumptions, the multistage process has the displayed logarithmic stage bound and uses at most four times the first-stage number of Newton steps in total.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is twice strongly convex with parameter }\sigma_2(f)>0
f\text{ has Lipschitz-continuous third derivative with constant }L_3(f)>0
x^*\text{ is the unique minimizer of }f
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{stages}}\le\frac1{\ln4}\ln\left(\frac83\left(\frac{L_3(f)R}{\sigma_2(f)}\right)^3\right),\qquad N_{\mathrm{Newton}}\le4m_0.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Newton for Nonlinear Equations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact Newton repeatedly solves the Jacobian linearization and takes the full correction; near a regular root, the iterates converge quadratically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) and an initial point \(x_0\), at iteration \(k\) solve the exact linearized equation \[F'(x_k)p_k=-F(x_k).\] If the solve succeeds, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\). Stop and output \(x_k\) when \(F(x_k)=0\), or in numerical use when a prescribed residual or step tolerance is met. If \(F'(x_k)\) is nonsingular, the direction is uniquely \(p_k=-F'(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k)\). Near a regular root \(x_*\), Lipschitz continuity of \(F'\) yields local quadratic convergence for sufficiently close \(x_0\).
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable near the iterates.
\(F'(x_k)\) is nonsingular whenever a step is computed.
For quadratic convergence, \(F'\) is locally Lipschitz and \(F'(x_*)\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-F'(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k)\), with local quadratic convergence near \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Undamped Newton iteration for a square regular nonlinear system.

equivalent_formulations_latex: The correction \(s_k\) is the unique vector satisfying the first-order model equation \(F(x_k)+J(x_k)s_k=0\).
Componentwise, \(F_i(x_k)+\nabla F_i(x_k)^Ts_k=0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
special_cases_latex: For a scalar equation \(F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\), the update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k-F(x_k)/F'(x_k)\).
If \(F\) is affine with nonsingular Jacobian, one iteration reaches its root.
immediate_consequences_latex: The method is invariant under multiplication of the equations by a fixed nonsingular matrix.
Each step exactly annihilates the current affine model, not necessarily the nonlinear residual itself.
boundary_notes: No global convergence or feasibility safeguard is part of the definition.
Rectangular systems, singular Jacobians, finite-difference Jacobians, and inexact linear solves require nearby variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Newton for Unconstrained Minimization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unconstrained exact Newton solves the Hessian equation and takes the full step; local quadratic convergence holds near a nondegenerate minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimizing a twice differentiable function \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\), choose \(x_0\). At iteration \(k\), solve \[
abla^2f(x_k)p_k=-
abla f(x_k)\] exactly and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\). Stop and output \(x_k\) when \(
abla f(x_k)=0\), or numerically when a prescribed stationarity or step tolerance holds. If \(x_*\) is a stationary point, \(
abla^2f(x_*)\) is positive definite, and the Hessian is locally Lipschitz, then all sufficiently close initial points generate well-defined full Newton steps converging quadratically to \(x_*\). Away from this neighborhood, the direction need not be descending.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable near the iterates.
The Hessian is nonsingular whenever a step is computed.
For local convergence, \(\nabla^2f(x_*)\succ0\) and \(\nabla^2f\) is locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-[\nabla^2f(x_k)]^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\), locally with quadratic convergence to \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-step Newton iteration applied to unconstrained first-order stationarity.

notation.meaning: objective Hessian at the current iterate

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[H_ks_k^N=-g_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k^N.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact Newton for unconstrained minimization computes the stationary point of the current quadratic Taylor model by solving \(\nabla^2f(x_k)s_k^N=-\nabla f(x_k)\), then accepts the full step.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on an open set containing the iterates.
\(H_k\) is nonsingular whenever a Newton correction is computed.
The gradient, Hessian, and linear-system solution are exact in the defining model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_{k+1}=x_k-\nabla^2f(x_k)^{-1}\nabla f(x_k).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(s_k^N\) is the unique stationary point of \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\).
The method is exact Newton applied to the nonlinear stationarity equation \(\nabla f(x)=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx+b^Tx+c\) with nonsingular \(Q\), one iteration reaches the unique stationary point.
When \(H_k\succ0\), \(s_k^N\) is the unique minimizer of the quadratic model and is a descent direction whenever \(g_k\ne0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(H_k\) is indefinite, the defining step may be directed toward a saddle point or maximizer of the model.
The update contains neither damping nor Hessian modification.
boundary_notes: The word minimization identifies the target problem but does not make an indefinite Newton model convex.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient-Equation Form of Unconstrained Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses smooth convex minimization as a nonlinear stationarity equation and identifies its Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a differentiable convex function \(\varphi:\mathbb E_1\to\mathbb R\), define \(F(x):=\nabla\varphi(x)\). Then \(x\) minimizes \(\varphi\) if and only if \(F(x)=0\). If \(\varphi\) is twice differentiable, then \(F'(x)=\nabla^2\varphi(x)\). Under strong convexity, this solution is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth convex unconstrained minimization is equivalent to solving the gradient equation F(x) = 0. When the objective is twice differentiable, the Jacobian of F is its Hessian; strong convexity makes the solution unique.
assumptions_latex: \varphi:\mathbb E_1\to\mathbb R\text{ is differentiable and convex}
\varphi\in C^2(\mathbb E_1)\text{ for the Jacobian identity}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb E_1}\varphi(y)\iff F(x)=0,\qquad F'(x)=\nabla^2\varphi(x).

assumptions_latex: The Lagrangian Hessian is nonsingular on \(\ker J_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed saddle-point solve is the exact Newton correction for \(R(x,\lambda)=0\).

knowledge_statements.source_title: Newton Step for Equality KKT Systems
knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coupled Newton step for equality-constrained KKT equations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\). Define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\lambda^Tc(x)\), \(A(x)=Dc(x)\), and \(W(x,\lambda)=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Twice-smooth finite-dimensional equality-constrained optimization, using the exact Newton linearization of primal-dual stationarity and feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\begin{bmatrix}W_k&-A_k^T\\-A_k&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p_k\\d_k\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_k)\\-c(x_k)\end{bmatrix},\qquad (x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})=(x_k+p_k,\lambda_k+d_k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality-KKT Newton step is the coupled primal-dual correction obtained by linearizing both \(\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)=0\) and \(c(x)=0\) and solving the resulting saddle-point system.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every component of \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable.
The displayed KKT matrix is nonsingular at the current primal-dual iterate.
The coupled linear system is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[D\!\begin{bmatrix}\nabla_xL\\c\end{bmatrix}_{(x_k,\lambda_k)}\begin{bmatrix}p_k\\d_k\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_k)\\c(x_k)\end{bmatrix}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With the alternative convention \(L=f+\lambda^Tc\), the off-diagonal signs change while the Newton correction represents the same KKT linearization.
The primal step and updated multiplier can equivalently be obtained from the equality-constrained quadratic model with linearized constraint \(A_kp+c(x_k)=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m=0\), the system reduces to the unconstrained Hessian Newton equation.
For a quadratic objective and affine equality constraints, the KKT residual is affine and one nonsingular full step solves it.
immediate_consequences_latex: The primal correction satisfies the linearized feasibility equation \(A_kp_k=-c(x_k)\).
The KKT matrix is symmetric but generally indefinite.
boundary_notes: Inequality constraints require active-set or primal-dual complementarity blocks.
Nonsingularity typically depends on constraint rank and reduced-Hessian conditions, but those are not part of this step definition.

notation.meaning: Exact Hessian of the Lagrangian with respect to \(x\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Damped Newton iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(R:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable, let \(J_k=DR(x_k)\) be nonsingular, and let \(\Phi\) be a scalar objective or merit function used to assess trial points.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic Newton globalization by line search along the exact Newton direction; the damping affects step length, not the Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[J_kp_k^N=-R(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k^N,\qquad 0<\alpha_k\le1,\] where \(\alpha_k\) is selected by a stated acceptance rule for \(\Phi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A damped Newton method first computes the exact Newton direction and then multiplies it by an accepted step length \(\alpha_k\) between zero and one. The full step is tried first in the standard backtracking realization.
assumptions_latex: The Newton linear system is solved exactly.
The direction \(p_k^N\) is acceptable as a descent direction for the chosen differentiable merit function whenever a descent-based rule is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kJ_k^{-1}R(x_k),\qquad \alpha_k\in(0,1].\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The accepted point lies on the segment \(\{x_k+\alpha p_k^N:0<\alpha\le1\}\).
Backtracking initializes \(\alpha=1\) and repeatedly replaces it by a smaller positive value until the acceptance inequality holds.
special_cases_latex: \(\alpha_k=1\) gives the exact full-step Newton update.
For unconstrained minimization, \(R=\nabla f\) and \(\Phi=f\).
For nonlinear equations, a standard choice is \(\Phi(x)=\tfrac12\|R(x)\|_2^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Damping preserves the Newton direction but may shorten its norm.
Any accepted \(\alpha_k<1\) distinguishes the iteration from the exact full-step method.
boundary_notes: Trust-region steps not collinear with \(p_k^N\) are not damped Newton steps in this sense.
The definition does not prescribe one unique acceptance condition.

notation.meaning: Scalar objective or merit function used for acceptance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Armijo objective-merit damping policy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, let \(x_k\) be current, and let \(p_k\) be a Newton or modified-Newton direction satisfying \(\nabla\Phi(x_k)^Tp_k<0\). Fix \(c_1\in(0,1)\) and a contraction interval \(0<\ell\le u<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone differentiable objective or merit-function backtracking along a supplied descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\alpha_k\in(0,1]\text{ is accepted when }\Phi(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le\Phi(x_k)+c_1\alpha_k\nabla\Phi(x_k)^Tp_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The policy tries the full step and accepts a trial length when the objective or merit function achieves Armijo sufficient decrease. If the test fails, the step length is contracted and retested.
assumptions_latex: \(0<c_1<1\), and each rejected trial \(\alpha\) is replaced by \(\rho\alpha\) for some \(\rho\in[\ell,u]\subset(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\alpha_k=\max_{\text{tested }\alpha}\{\alpha:\Phi(x_k+\alpha p_k)\le\Phi(x_k)+c_1\alpha\nabla\Phi(x_k)^Tp_k\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The accepted average decrease satisfies \(\bigl(\Phi(x_k)-\Phi(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\bigr)/\alpha_k\ge-c_1\nabla\Phi(x_k)^Tp_k\).
special_cases_latex: For unconstrained minimization, take \(\Phi=f\).
For constrained methods, \(\Phi\) may be a differentiable penalty or augmented merit function, provided the chosen direction is a descent direction.
immediate_consequences_latex: Because \(\nabla\Phi(x_k)^Tp_k<0\), every accepted nonzero step strictly decreases \(\Phi\).
The full Newton step is accepted whenever it satisfies the same inequality with \(\alpha_k=1\).
boundary_notes: Merely requiring \(\Phi(x_{k+1})<\Phi(x_k)\) is weaker than this sufficient-decrease policy.
Nonsmooth merit functions require directional derivatives or a different acceptance formulation.

notation.meaning: Permitted interval of backtracking contraction factors.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Function Damping
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack a descent Newton direction until the objective achieves Armijo sufficient decrease. With an Armijo parameter below one half, full exact-Newton steps are eventually accepted near a nondegenerate minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an iterate \(x_k\), a direction \(p_k\) satisfying \(
abla f(x_k)^	op p_k<0\), parameters \( eta\in(0,1)\) and \(\sigma\in(0,	frac12)\), initialize \(\alpha=1\). While \[f(x_k+\alpha p_k)>f(x_k)+\sigma\alpha
abla f(x_k)^	op p_k,\] replace \(\alpha\) by \( eta\alpha\). Set \(\alpha_k=\alpha\) and output \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). If \(p_k\) is the exact Newton direction, \(x_k\) converges to a stationary point \(x_*\), \(
abla^2 f(x_*)\) is positive definite, and \(
abla^2 f\) is locally Lipschitz, then the test accepts \(\alpha_k=1\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable on the trial segment.
For eventual unit-step acceptance, \(p_k\) is the exact Newton direction, \(x_k\to x_*\), \(\nabla^2f(x_*)\succ0\), and \(\nabla^2f\) is locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns an Armijo-acceptable step \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\); under the stated local Newton assumptions, \(\alpha_k=1\) eventually.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo damping of a descent Newton direction using the objective alone.

knowledge_statements.title: Merit-Function Damping
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack until a scalar merit function measuring objective and constraint violation achieves sufficient directional decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Psi_\rho:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be a merit function with penalty parameter \(\rho>0\), and let \(p_k\) satisfy a negative one-sided directional derivative \(D\Psi_\rho(x_k;p_k)<0\). Choose \(\beta,\sigma\in(0,1)\), initialize \(\alpha=1\), and repeatedly set \(\alpha\leftarrow\beta\alpha\) until \[\Psi_\rho(x_k+\alpha p_k)\le\Psi_\rho(x_k)+\sigma\alpha D\Psi_\rho(x_k;p_k).\] Output \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha p_k\). For example, an equality-constrained exact-penalty merit is \(\Psi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\lVert c(x)\rVert_1\); its directional derivative, rather than an ordinary gradient, governs acceptance at nonsmooth points.
assumptions_latex: \(\Psi_\rho\) is directionally differentiable along the trial steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted \(\alpha\) satisfies the stated merit-function sufficient-decrease condition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo damping based on a scalar constrained-optimization merit function.

notation.meaning: scalar merit function with penalty parameter rho
one-sided directional derivative in direction p

knowledge_statements.title: Acceptance-Measure Selection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a scalar acceptance measure whose relevant local minimizers match the intended target and for which the computed direction gives verifiable sufficient decrease. Residual measures may identify the target through their zeros, whereas an objective need not be nonnegative or vanish at a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_k\) be a Newton or Newton-like direction for a target set \(\mathcal S\), and let \(M:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be the scalar measure used by a line search. In a neighborhood \(U\) relevant to the local method, a compatible measure should have its local minimizers in \(U\) coincide with \(\mathcal S\cap U\), admit a computable one-sided directional derivative \(DM(x_k;p_k)\), and make the proposed direction descending whenever \(x_k\notin\mathcal S\): \(DM(x_k;p_k)<0\). The step may then be accepted by \[M(x_k+\alpha p_k)\le M(x_k)+\sigma\alpha DM(x_k;p_k),\qquad \sigma\in(0,1).\] For unconstrained minimization one may use \(M=f\). For equations one may use \(M(x)=\tfrac12\lVert R(x)\rVert_2^2\), whose zero set agrees with \(R(x)=0\). For constrained problems, the chosen merit function must balance objective progress and infeasibility so that its relevant local minimizers correspond to the intended constrained solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(M:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is continuous and one-sided directionally differentiable along the trial steps.
In a relevant neighborhood \(U\), the local minimizers of \(M\) coincide with the intended target set \(\mathcal S\cap U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An Armijo test based on \(M\) supplies a locally target-compatible step-acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility criterion for choosing a damping acceptance measure.

notation.meaning: intended local target or solution set
nonlinear or optimality residual used in a residual-style measure
one-sided directional derivative of the acceptance measure

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Based Damping
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use squared residual norm as the merit function and backtrack the Newton correction until it gives sufficient residual decrease.

For solving \(F(x)=0\), define \(\psi(x)=	frac12\lVert F(x)Vert_2^2\). Given a Newton direction \(p_k\) satisfying \(F'(x_k)p_k=-F(x_k)\), choose \( eta,\sigma\in(0,1)\), initialize \(\alpha=1\), and backtrack via \(\alpha\leftarrow eta\alpha\) until \[\psi(x_k+\alpha p_k)\le\psi(x_k)+\sigma\alpha
abla\psi(x_k)^	op p_k.\] Since \(
abla\psi(x_k)^	op p_k=F(x_k)^	op F'(x_k)p_k=-\lVert F(x_k)Vert_2^2<0\) when \(F(x_k)
e0\), the exact Newton direction is descending for \(\psi\). Output \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha p_k\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted step satisfies Armijo decrease for \(\tfrac12\lVert F\rVert_2^2\).

\(c_1\in(0,1)\), with the usual Armijo choice commonly restricted to \(c_1<\tfrac12\).

children.title: Full Newton-Step Recovery
children.top_down_role: The local transition from safeguarded steps to undamped Newton steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Newton-Step Recovery
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular root, an Armijo residual line search eventually accepts every full Newton step, restoring quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_*\) be a regular solution of \(F(x)=0\), let \(F'\) be locally Lipschitz, and let \(p_k\) solve \(F'(x_k)p_k=-F(x_k)\). Suppose a backtracking line search uses \(\psi(x)=\tfrac12\lVert F(x)\rVert_2^2\) and the Armijo test with \(0<\sigma<\tfrac12\). If \(x_k\to x_*\), then there exists \(K\) such that for every \(k\ge K\), the trial \(\alpha=1\) satisfies \[\psi(x_k+p_k)\le\psi(x_k)+\sigma\nabla\psi(x_k)^\top p_k.\] Hence backtracking eventually returns \(\alpha_k=1\), after which the damped method coincides locally with exact Newton and inherits its quadratic convergence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block symmetric-indefinite factorization as a Hessian-modification basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The universally existing pivoted block factorization of a real symmetric matrix and the failure boundary of insisting on diagonal pivots, stated in its indefinite-Hessian-modification context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n} with A=A^T, there exist a permutation matrix P, a unit lower-triangular matrix L, and a block-diagonal matrix B whose diagonal blocks have order 1 or 2 such that PAP^T=LBL^T. Allowing 2\times2 blocks guarantees existence and permits a numerically stable factorization process, providing a basis for an indefinite-Hessian modification strategy. In contrast, an LDL^T factorization constrained to diagonal D may fail to exist for an indefinite A or may contain entries much larger than those of A, thereby amplifying rounding errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every real symmetric matrix has a symmetrically pivoted block LDL-transpose factorization with one-by-one or two-by-two diagonal blocks. The two-by-two blocks ensure that such a factorization exists and can be computed stably, making it a basis for modifying an indefinite Hessian. Requiring a diagonal D instead can fail or produce very large factors that amplify rounding errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists P,L,B:\quad PAP^T=LBL^T,\quad \operatorname{diag}(L)=\mathbf1,\quad B=\operatorname{blkdiag}(B_1,\ldots,B_r),\quad \dim(B_q)\in\{1,2\};\quad \text{the block form always exists and admits stable computation.}

abla f(x_k)<0$.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Hessian Modification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip every Hessian eigenvalue below a positive floor, solve the resulting positive-definite Newton system, and globalize the resulting descent direction if necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric Hessian approximation \(H=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)Q^{\mathsf T}\), a gradient \(g\), and a curvature floor \(\delta>0\), define \(\widehat\lambda_i=\max\{\lambda_i,\delta\}\) and \(B=Q\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\lambda_1,\ldots,\widehat\lambda_n)Q^{\mathsf T}\). Compute the modified Newton direction \(p=-B^{-1}g\). Then \(B\succeq\delta I\); hence \(p\) is uniquely defined, and \(g^{\mathsf T}p=-g^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}g<0\) whenever \(g\ne0\). Stop when the chosen first-order test is satisfied; otherwise globalize \(p\) by a line search or trust region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\succeq\delta I\) and \(g^{\mathsf T}p<0\) for \(g\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvalue clipping for an unconstrained modified-Newton step.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Eigenvalue-clipping Hessian modification
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H=H^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) have spectral decomposition \(H=Q\Lambda Q^T\), with orthogonal \(Q=[q_1,\ldots,q_n]\) and \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)\). Fix \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense finite-dimensional symmetric Hessian modification defined through an exact spectral decomposition and a positive eigenvalue floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\widehat\lambda_i=\max\{\lambda_i,\delta\},\qquad B=Q\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\lambda_i)Q^T=H+Q\operatorname{diag}\bigl((\delta-\lambda_i)_+\bigr)Q^T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral Hessian modification leaves every eigenvalue already at least \(\delta\) unchanged and raises each smaller eigenvalue to \(\delta\), preserving the Hessian eigenvectors.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is orthogonal and \(\lambda_i\) are the eigenvalues of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[B\succeq\delta I,\qquad Bp=-g,\qquad p=-\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{q_i^Tg}{\max\{\lambda_i,\delta\}}q_i.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The correction is \(E=B-H=Q\operatorname{diag}((\delta-\lambda_i)_+)Q^T\).
Among symmetric corrections producing \(\lambda_{\min}(H+E)\ge\delta\), this eigenvalue clipping is the standard minimum-Frobenius-norm correction stated by the source.
special_cases_latex: If \(H\succeq\delta I\), then \(B=H\) and \(E=0\).
For \(\delta\) small, negative and near-zero eigenvalues are replaced by the same positive floor.
immediate_consequences_latex: The modified matrix and original Hessian have the same eigenvectors.
The Newton-like direction is unique and is a descent direction for every nonzero gradient.
boundary_notes: A very small \(\delta\) can produce an excessively long component along a clipped eigendirection.
Computing a complete eigendecomposition may be too expensive for large-scale problems.
Replacing negative eigenvalues by their absolute values is a different spectral policy.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual pure-Newton behavior and the loss of that guarantee near singular limiting Hessians.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x_k\to x^*\) in Algorithm 3.2 and the Hessian modification strategy returns \(E_k=0\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), as occurs under the stated sufficiently positive-definite limiting-Hessian regime. Then \(\alpha_k=1\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), the iteration eventually coincides with pure Newton iteration, and \(x_k\) converges quadratically to \(x^*\). If \(\nabla^2 f(x^*)\) is close to singular, \(E_k\) need not eventually vanish, so quadratic convergence is not guaranteed and the rate may be only linear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the iterates converge to a point whose Hessian is positive definite enough that Hessian modifications eventually vanish, full Newton steps are eventually accepted and convergence is quadratic. knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal-Shift Regularization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a scalar multiple of the identity large enough to make the Newton matrix positive definite; increasing the shift can also improve spectral conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric matrix \(H\), gradient \(g\), and floor \(\delta>0\), set \(\tau=\max\{0,\delta-\lambda_{\min}(H)\}\), define \(B=H+\tau I\), and solve \(Bp=-g\). Then \(\lambda_{\min}(B)\ge\delta\), so the system is positive definite. More generally, any \(\tau>-\lambda_{\min}(H)\) yields \(B\succ0\); if \(H+\tau I\succ0\), its spectral condition number is \(\kappa_2(B)=(\lambda_{\max}(H)+\tau)/(\lambda_{\min}(H)+\tau)\). Stop by the prescribed first-order test, otherwise globalize \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H+\tau I\succeq\delta I\), so \(p=-(H+\tau I)^{-1}g\) is well defined.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar identity shifts enforcing positive curvature and improving conditioning.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scalar diagonal-shift regularization of a Newton matrix
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H=H^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be a Hessian or symmetric Newton matrix, let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and fix a desired eigenvalue floor \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform scalar shifting of a finite-dimensional symmetric Newton matrix; every eigenvalue is translated by the same amount.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\tau=\max\{0,\delta-\lambda_{\min}(H)\},\qquad B=H+\tau I,qquad Bp=-g.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal-shift regularization adds a nonnegative scalar multiple of the identity to the Newton matrix. The minimal spectral shift for floor \(\delta\) is \(\tau=\max\{0,\delta-lambda_{min}(H)\}\).
assumptions_latex: If \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\) is not explicitly available, an implementation chooses or increases \(\tau\) until a positive-definite factorization succeeds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\lambda_i(B)=\lambda_i(H)+\tau\ge\delta\quad(i=1,\ldots,n),\qquad p=-(H+	au I)^{-1}g.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The regularization matrix is the diagonal correction \(E=	au I\).
The step uniquely minimizes \(g^Tp+tfrac12p^T(H+	au I)p\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge\delta\), then \(\tau=0\) and the original Newton matrix is retained.
A Cholesky trial scheme can start from \(\tau=0\) when the diagonal is positive and enlarge \(\tau\) after a failed factorization.
immediate_consequences_latex: The shift preserves all eigenvectors of \(H\) and all pairwise eigenvalue gaps.
The resulting direction is a strict descent direction whenever \(g\ne0\).
boundary_notes: A scalar shift may alter already satisfactory large eigenvalues unnecessarily.
A shift chosen only to ensure nonsingularity need not ensure positive curvature.
Repeated trial shifts can require multiple factorizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Modified Cholesky Regularization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Modify unsafe pivots during a symmetric factorization, thereby constructing a nearby positive-definite Newton matrix and a descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given symmetric \(H\), gradient \(g\), and safeguards \(0<\delta\le\Delta\), perform a pivoted symmetric factorization while modifying unacceptable pivots to construct \(B=P L D L^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}=H+E\), where \(P\) is a permutation, \(L\) is unit lower triangular, and \(D\) is positive diagonal with \(\delta\le D_{ii}\le\Delta\). Solve successively with \(P\), \(L\), \(D\), and \(L^{\mathsf T}\) to obtain \(Bp=-g\). The modification rules should keep \(E\) small subject to the pivot safeguards. The resulting matrix satisfies \(B\succ0\), so \(p\) is a descent direction when \(g\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=H+E\succ0\) and \(g^{\mathsf T}p<0\) whenever \(g\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite Newton models produced during symmetric factorization.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The positive-definite factorization would imply the stated descent property, but the precise diagonal-pivot safeguards, upper bound on D, and small-correction objective describe a variant-specific modified Cholesky procedure. The cited chapter-opening locator does not establish that this exact variant or its safeguards are supported.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modified-Cholesky regularization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H=H^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be a Hessian or symmetric Newton matrix and let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\). A modified Cholesky procedure produces a permutation \(P\), a unit lower-triangular matrix \(L\), and a positive diagonal matrix \(D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric direct-factorization regularization that alters pivots during factorization to construct a positive-definite model matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[P^T(H+E)P=LDL^T,\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n),\quad d_i>0,\qquad (H+E)p=-g.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Modified Cholesky regularization changes selected diagonal pivots, and if necessary associated entries, while factorizing a symmetric matrix so that the factors represent a positive-definite matrix \(H+E\). The Newton-like step is computed with this regularized matrix.
assumptions_latex: The factorization procedure enforces strictly positive, sufficiently bounded pivots \(d_i\).
The constructed correction \(E=E^T\) vanishes when \(H\) is already sufficiently positive definite under the procedure's threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[B:=H+E=P^{-T}LDL^TP^{-1}\succ0,qquad p=-B^{-1}g.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With a permutation matrix, \(P^{-1}=P^T\), so the factorization may be written \(B=P LDL^TP^T\).
The correction may be defined implicitly by the computed factors: \(E=P LDL^TP^T-H\).
special_cases_latex: If \(H\) is sufficiently positive definite, ordinary Cholesky succeeds and the modification can be \(E=0\).
Unpivoted \(LDL^T\) modification is a special realization when the prescribed stability tests do not require permutations.
immediate_consequences_latex: The regularized quadratic model \(g^Tp+tfrac12p^TBp\) has a unique minimizer.
For \(g\ne0\), the computed direction satisfies \(g^Tp<0\).
The factors can be used directly to solve for \(p\) without explicitly forming \(B^{-1}\).
boundary_notes: Modified Cholesky is a family of factorization strategies, so pivot thresholds and bounds must be specified by an implementation.
Positive definiteness alone does not guarantee that the correction is small or that the condition number is satisfactory.
This definition concerns model construction, not a convergence guarantee.

notation.meaning: Symmetric correction implicitly or explicitly generated by modified factorization.
Permutation, unit lower-triangular factor, and positive diagonal factor.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modified Cholesky design criteria and the positive-definite LDL factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The positive-definite LDL-transpose representation underlying modified Cholesky, together with the stated design requirements for Hessian modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every real symmetric positive-definite matrix A has a factorization A=LDL^T, where L is unit lower triangular and D is diagonal with positive diagonal entries. For a symmetric Hessian H_k=\nabla^2 f(x_k) that is not sufficiently positive definite, modified Cholesky increases diagonal quantities during factorization as needed so that the modified factors exist and are bounded relative to \|H_k\|; when H_k is sufficiently positive definite, the procedure leaves it unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every real symmetric positive-definite matrix has an LDL-transpose factorization with unit lower-triangular L and a positive diagonal D. Modified Cholesky adjusts diagonal quantities while factoring an insufficiently positive Hessian to obtain controlled factors, while making no adjustment when the Hessian is already sufficiently positive definite.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n},\quad A=A^T\succ0\quad\text{for the unmodified factorization}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A=LDL^T,\quad \operatorname{diag}(L)=\mathbf 1,\quad d_j>0;\qquad H_k\mapsto B_k\text{ with controlled modified factors, and }B_k=H_k\text{ when }H_k\text{ is sufficiently positive definite.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact Modified-Cholesky Shift Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled incomplete-Cholesky construction with an adaptively increased diagonal shift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), form \[T=\operatorname{diag}(\|Be_1\|,\ldots,\|Be_n\|),\qquad \bar B=T^{-1/2}BT^{-1/2},\qquad \beta=\|\bar B\|.\] Set \(\alpha_0=0\) if \(\min_i b_{ii}>0\), and otherwise set \(\alpha_0=\beta/2\). For \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\), attempt incomplete Cholesky factorization in the form \[LL^T=\bar B+\alpha_kI.\] Return \(L\) if the factorization succeeds; otherwise set \[\alpha_{k+1}=\max\{2\alpha_k,\beta/2\}\] and retry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale the matrix using the norms of its columns, initialize a diagonal shift from the diagonal-sign test, and attempt incomplete Cholesky. Whenever factorization fails, increase the shift to at least twice its current value and at least half the norm of the scaled matrix. Return the first successful lower-triangular factor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{If an attempt succeeds at index }k,\text{ the algorithm returns }L\text{ satisfying }LL^T=\bar B+\alpha_kI.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cholesky Factorization with an Adaptive Identity Shift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A modified-Cholesky procedure that increases a scalar identity shift after each unsuccessful factorization attempt.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A=(a_{ij})\) and \(\beta>0\), set \(\tau_0=0\) if \(\min_i a_{ii}>0\), and otherwise set \(\tau_0=-\min_i a_{ii}+\beta\). For \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\), attempt to compute \(L\) such that \(LL^T=A+\tau_k I\). If the Cholesky factorization succeeds, stop and return \(L\); otherwise set \(\tau_{k+1}=\max\{2\tau_k,\beta\}\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize an identity shift from the smallest diagonal entry. Attempt Cholesky factorization of the shifted matrix; after each failure, replace the shift by the larger of twice its current value and a positive safeguard, and return the factor at the first successful attempt.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{At the first successful trial, return }L\text{ satisfying }LL^T=A+\tau_k I

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bound-controlled modified Cholesky factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal modification during LDL-transpose factorization, its local pivot and scaled-entry bounds, the resulting diagonally modified positive-definite factorization, and the failure boundary of correcting a diagonal LDL factorization only after factoring an indefinite matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A=A^T and let \delta,\beta>0. In the columnwise LDL^T recurrence, define \theta_j=\max_{j<i\le n}|c_{ij}| for j<n and \theta_n=0, and replace the provisional diagonal pivot by d_j=\max\{|c_{jj}|,(\theta_j/\beta)^2,\delta\}. Then d_j\ge\delta and |l_{ij}\sqrt{d_j}|\le\beta for every i>j. The detailed modified Cholesky procedure, with symmetric interchanges represented by P, produces PAP^T+E=LDL^T=MM^T, where E is diagonal and entrywise nonnegative and is zero when A is sufficiently positive definite. When that procedure is applied to exact Hessians to form B_k, the stated conditioning guarantee is \kappa(B_k)\le C for some k-independent C. For indefinite A, attempting an unmodified factorization with diagonal D may fail to exist or may produce arbitrarily large factors; modifying D only afterward may therefore fail or yield a matrix drastically different from A.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each column, replace the provisional pivot by the maximum of its absolute value, a term that controls the scaled subdiagonal entries, and a positive floor. This ensures pivots of at least delta and scaled entries of at most beta. With symmetric interchanges, the detailed method factors a nonnegatively diagonally modified matrix, makes no modification for a sufficiently positive-definite input, and yields the stated uniform conditioning bound for modified exact Hessians. Factoring an indefinite matrix with diagonal pivots first and correcting the diagonal afterward is unsafe because the factorization may fail or contain arbitrarily large factors.
assumptions_latex: B_k\text{ is produced by the detailed modified Cholesky procedure applied to }\nabla^2 f(x_k)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_j\ge\delta,\quad |l_{ij}\sqrt{d_j}|\le\beta\ (i>j),\quad PAP^T+E=LDL^T=MM^T,\quad E\ge0\text{ diagonal},\quad E=0\text{ for sufficiently positive-definite }A,\quad \exists C>0\ \forall k:\ \kappa(B_k)\le C.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative-Curvature Newton Modification
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R,\qquad g_k=\nabla f(x_k),\qquad H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)=H_k^T.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, twice continuously differentiable, generally nonconvex unconstrained optimization; the definition concerns step construction and does not itself impose a globalization rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathcal M_{\rm nc}(g_k,H_k)=\left\{p_k:\ \begin{array}{l}\text{either }p_k=-B_k^{-1}g_k\text{ for a symmetric }B_k\succ0\text{ obtained by modifying }H_k,\\[2pt]\text{or }p_k\text{ is constructed using }d_k\ne0\text{ with }d_k^TH_kd_k<0\end{array}\right\}.\] A negative-curvature Newton modification is any Newton-type step rule selecting \(p_k\in\mathcal M_{\rm nc}(g_k,H_k)\), with the sign of an explicit curvature direction chosen so that \(g_k^Td_k\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-curvature Newton modification is a Newton-type rule for a smooth nonconvex objective that responds to an indefinite Hessian in one of two ways: it replaces the Hessian by a symmetric positive-definite modification and solves the resulting Newton system, or it explicitly uses a nonzero direction \(d_k\) satisfying \(d_k^T H_k d_k<0\). When the direction is used explicitly, its sign is selected so that \(g_k^T d_k\le 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p_k=-B_k^{-1}g_k\text{ with }B_k\succ0,\quad\text{or}\quad p_k=\Phi_k(g_k,H_k,d_k)\text{ with }d_k^TH_kd_k<0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[H_k\text{ has negative curvature}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\lambda_{\min}(H_k)<0.\]
special_cases_latex: \[B_k=H_k+E_k\succ0\] is a curvature-modified Newton step.
\[p_k=-g_k+\tau_k d_k,\qquad \tau_k\ge0,\quad d_k^TH_kd_k<0\] is an explicit negative-curvature augmentation.
immediate_consequences_latex: \[g_k^T(-B_k^{-1}g_k)<0\qquad(g_k\ne0,\ B_k\succ0).\]
\[m_k(td_k)=f(x_k)+t g_k^Td_k+\tfrac12t^2d_k^TH_kd_k\to-\infty\quad(t\to\infty)\] for the local quadratic model whenever \(d_k^TH_kd_k<0\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert that an unbounded negative-curvature ray is an acceptable full step; line-search or trust-region safeguards remain separate.
At a positive-semidefinite Hessian no strict negative-curvature direction exists, although singular or nearly singular curvature may require other modifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Based Negative Curvature
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative pivot or indefinite pivot block in a symmetric factorization yields, through a triangular solve, a verifiable negative-curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a symmetric matrix have the pivoted factorization \(P^{\mathsf T}HP=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), with nonsingular \(L\) and symmetric block-diagonal \(D\). If a vector \(y\ne0\), supported on one diagonal block of \(D\), satisfies \(y^{\mathsf T}Dy<0\), define \(d=PL^{-\mathsf T}y\). Direct triangular solves make \(d\) computable, and \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd=y^{\mathsf T}Dy<0\). Thus \(d\) is a verifiable direction of negative curvature. A negative scalar pivot supplies \(y\) immediately; for a \(2\)-by-\(2\) pivot block, an eigenvector associated with its negative eigenvalue supplies \(y\).
assumptions_latex: \(P^{\mathsf T}HP=LDL^{\mathsf T}\) is available with nonsingular \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d=PL^{-\mathsf T}y\) satisfies \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd<0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative-curvature certificates extracted from an indefinite symmetric factorization.

notation.meaning: negative-curvature vector for a pivot block
negative-curvature direction in the original coordinates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative Curvature Exposed by an Indefinite Factorization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n},\qquad PHP^T=LBL^T,\] where \(P\) is a permutation, \(L\) is nonsingular unit lower triangular, and \(B\) is block diagonal with \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) symmetric blocks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic definition for real symmetric matrices; stable pivoted symmetric-indefinite factorizations are the intended numerical realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\text{If }z\ne0\text{ is supported in a diagonal block of }B\text{ and }z^TBz<0,\quad d=P^TL^{-T}z,\] then \[d^THd=z^TBz<0.\] Factorization-based negative curvature is the certificate-direction pair \((z,d)\) obtained in this way from a negative \(1\times1\) pivot or a negative eigenvector of a \(2\times2\) pivot block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factorization-based negative curvature is obtained from a pivoted symmetric-indefinite factorization \(P H P^T=L B L^T\). A negative scalar pivot, or a negative eigenvector of a two-by-two pivot block, supplies a vector \(z\) with \(z^T Bz<0\). Transforming it by \(d=P^T L^{-T}z\) yields a direction satisfying \(d^T H d<0\). Thus the factors both detect indefiniteness through inertia and construct an explicit curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d=P^TL^{-T}z\ne0,\qquad d^THd=z^TBz<0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\operatorname{inertia}(H)=\operatorname{inertia}(B),\] so \(H\) has a negative eigenvalue exactly when \(B\) has a negative eigenvalue.
special_cases_latex: For a negative scalar pivot \(b_{ii}<0\), take \(z=e_i\).
For an indefinite \(2\times2\) block \(B_I\), take \(z_I\) to be an eigenvector associated with \(\lambda_{\min}(B_I)<0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: \[\lambda_{\min}(H)<0\] is certified without forming a full eigendecomposition of \(H\).
Replacing the negative eigenvalues of the small blocks of \(B\) by values at least \(\delta>0\) defines a modified positive-curvature factorization.
boundary_notes: A negative pivot in an unstable unpivoted factorization is not, by itself, a reliable finite-precision certificate; stable symmetric pivoting is assumed.
The transformed vector need not approximate an eigenvector of \(H\); only its negative Rayleigh quotient is required.

notation.meaning: Permutation matrix used by symmetric pivoting.
Recovered negative-curvature direction for the original matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Krylov Negative Curvature
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative Ritz value from Lanczos, or a strictly negative curvature test in conjugate gradients, exposes a negative-curvature direction using Hessian-vector products; a zero-curvature test establishes only nonpositive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric \(H\), let \(Q_j\) have orthonormal columns spanning a Lanczos Krylov subspace and let \(T_j=Q_j^{\mathsf T}HQ_j\). If \(T_jz=\theta z\), \(\lVert z\rVert_2=1\), and \(\theta<0\), then \(d=Q_jz\) satisfies \(\lVert d\rVert_2=1\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd=z^{\mathsf T}T_jz=\theta<0\). Hence a negative Ritz value and its Ritz vector form a computable negative-curvature certificate using only matrix-vector products with \(H\). In a truncated conjugate-gradient implementation, a search vector \(v\ne0\) with \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv<0\) likewise provides a strict negative-curvature certificate; the equality case \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv=0\) certifies only nonpositive curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_jz=\theta z\) with \(\theta<0\) implies \((Q_jz)^{\mathsf T}H(Q_jz)=\theta<0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ritz certificates of negative curvature obtained from Lanczos subspaces.

notation.meaning: conjugate-gradient search vector tested for curvature

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Krylov-Subspace Negative-Curvature Certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n},\quad r\ne0,\quad \mathcal K_j(H,r)=\operatorname{span}\{r,Hr,\ldots,H^{j-1}r\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric Newton systems treated by conjugate-gradient or Lanczos-type iterations using matrix-vector products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\text{A Krylov negative-curvature certificate at iteration }j\text{ is }d_j\in\mathcal K_j(H,r)\setminus\{0\}\text{ such that }d_j^THd_j\le0.\] Strict negative curvature is certified when the inequality is strict. In Lanczos form, if \(V_j\) spans \(\mathcal K_j(H,r)\), a Ritz vector \(u\ne0\) with \(u^T(V_j^THV_j)u<0\) gives \(d_j=V_ju\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Krylov negative curvature is a nonzero vector generated inside a Krylov subspace whose quadratic curvature is nonpositive. In truncated conjugate gradients it is detected by the test \(d_j^T H d_j\le0\) on a search direction. In Lanczos form it can be obtained from a negative Ritz value of the projected matrix \(V_j^T H V_j\), with the corresponding full-space vector \(V_j u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_j^THd_j\le0,\quad\text{and strict negative curvature when }d_j^THd_j<0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\lambda_{\min}(V_j^THV_j)<0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists d\in\mathcal K_j(H,r)\setminus\{0\}:d^THd<0.\]
special_cases_latex: In truncated CG, the first search direction satisfying \(d_j^THd_j\le0\) terminates the inner solve.
In Lanczos, a Ritz pair \((\theta,u)\) with \(\theta<0\) yields \(d=V_ju\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The certificate requires only products \(Hv\), not an assembled factorization of \(H\).
For a trust-region model, a detected negative-curvature ray is truncated at the trust-region boundary.
boundary_notes: Failure to detect negative curvature in a small Krylov subspace does not prove that \(H\succeq0\) on the whole space.
The nonpositive test includes zero curvature; strict saddle-escaping curvature requires \(d_j^THd_j<0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Curvature Step Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the quadratic model over a bounded subspace containing a negative-curvature direction, optionally together with a Newton-like direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an iterate with gradient \(g\), symmetric model matrix \(H\), radius \(\Delta>0\), and direction \(d\) satisfying \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd<0\), orient \(d\) so that \(g^{\mathsf T}d\le0\). Let \(p_N\) denote an available Newton-like direction and choose either \(S=\operatorname{span}\{d\}\) for a replacement step or \(S=\operatorname{span}\{p_N,d\}\) for an augmented step. Compute a global minimizer of \(q(p)=g^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Hp\) over \(p\in S\) with \(\lVert p\rVert_2\le\Delta\). Accept or further globalize this step, and stop under the prescribed first- or second-order test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in\arg\min\{q(s):s\in S,\ \lVert s\rVert_2\le\Delta\}\) incorporates detected negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subspace construction unifying pure, augmented, and replacement negative-curvature steps.

\[g=

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonconvex minimization; admissibility of a step length is delegated to a line search or trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathcal P_{\rm nc}(g,H,d)=\{\alpha p_N+\tau d:\alpha,\tau\ge0,\ (\alpha,\tau)\ne(0,0)\},\] where \(p_N\) is a Newton or modified-Newton component. The associated step family consists of replacement steps \(p=\tau d\), augmented steps \(p=\alpha p_N+\tau d\), and curvilinear paths \(p(t)=a(t)p_N+b(t)d\), provided the selected point is a descent or model-decrease step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-curvature step family is a parameterized collection of trial steps formed from a Newton-like component and a signed negative-curvature direction. The curvature direction may replace the Newton step, augment it linearly, or define a curvilinear path with it. The direction satisfies \(d^T H d<0\) and is signed so that \(g^T d\le0\); a separate globalization mechanism chooses a finite member of the family.
assumptions_latex: \[p_N\text{ is a Newton or modified-Newton component whenever it is included}.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p\in\{\tau d,\ \alpha p_N+\tau d,\ p(t)=a(t)p_N+b(t)d\}.\]
special_cases_latex: Pure curvature replacement: \(p=\tau d\).
Linear augmentation: \(p=p_N+\tau d\).
Steepest-descent augmentation: \(p=-g+\tau d\).
immediate_consequences_latex: \[\frac{d^2}{dt^2}m(td)=d^THd<0\] for the local quadratic model along the curvature direction.
Changing \(d\) to \(-d\) leaves \(d^THd\) unchanged and permits the convention \(g^Td\le0\).
boundary_notes: The family definition does not select \(\alpha\), \(\tau\), or \(t\), and therefore does not by itself guarantee convergence.
An unrestricted quadratic model is unbounded below along \(d\); a finite step must be selected.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton Iteration with a Reused Derivative Matrix
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n,\quad A_k=DG(x_{\rho(k)}),\quad 0\le\rho(k)\le k.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth square nonlinear systems, including stationarity systems \(G=\nabla f\); exact linear solves are used in the defining form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[A_k s_k=-G(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k,\qquad A_k=DG(x_{\rho(k)}),\] where the refresh map \(\rho:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\) is nondecreasing, satisfies \(\rho(k)\le k\), and may remain constant over several iterations. A reused-Jacobian Newton family is the collection of these iterations over admissible refresh maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reused-Jacobian Newton method solves the Newton correction equation using a derivative matrix evaluated at an earlier refresh iterate. A nondecreasing refresh map \(\rho(k)\le k\) determines the stored matrix \(A_k=DG(x_{\rho(k)})\), which may be used for several successive residual evaluations and corrections before it is recomputed.
assumptions_latex: \[DG(x_{\rho(k)})\text{ is nonsingular whenever a correction is computed}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The same factorization of \(DG(x_{\rho(k)})\) may be reused for every \(k\) in a refresh block.
special_cases_latex: \[\rho(k)=k\] gives ordinary Newton iteration.
\[\rho(k)=0\] gives a fixed-Jacobian chord iteration.
A blockwise constant \(\rho\) gives periodic or Shamanskii-type refreshes.
immediate_consequences_latex: Derivative evaluation and factorization occur only at indices satisfying \(\rho(k)=k\).
Residuals \(G(x_k)\) continue to be evaluated at every correction, even while the derivative matrix is reused.
boundary_notes: Reusing a matrix is distinct from a quasi-Newton update: between refreshes the matrix is unchanged rather than modified by a secant equation.
The definition alone gives no local rate; the rate depends on refresh frequency and regularity.

notation.meaning: Most recent derivative-refresh index used at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Linearization Newton Iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n,\quad \bar x\in\mathbb R^n,\quad B=DG(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth square nonlinear systems; for minimization take \(G=\nabla f\) and \(B=\nabla^2f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[B s_k=-G(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k,\qquad B=DG(\bar x)\text{ for every }k.\] A fixed-linearization Newton method is this stationary iteration with one derivative matrix, and normally one factorization, retained throughout the correction sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-linearization Newton method chooses an anchor \(\bar x\), forms the derivative matrix \(B=DG(\bar x)\) once, and computes every later correction from \(B s_k=-G(x_k)\). Only the nonlinear residual changes with the iterate. When \(\bar x=x_0\), this is the classical chord method; for optimization the fixed matrix is the Hessian at the anchor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_{k+1}=x_k-B^{-1}G(x_k),\qquad B\text{ independent of }k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[x_{k+1}=T_B(x_k),\qquad T_B(x)=x-B^{-1}G(x),\] so the method is a fixed-point iteration with a stationary linear preconditioner.
special_cases_latex: \[\bar x=x_0\] is the chord method.

For \(G=
abla f\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k-
abla^2f( ar x)^{-1}
abla f(x_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Only triangular solves are needed after a factorization of \(B\), until the process is restarted.
For affine \(G(x)=Bx-c\), one correction reaches the root.
boundary_notes: A lagged derivative that is later refreshed belongs to the broader reused-Jacobian family, not to a single fixed-linearization run.
Nonsingularity of \(B\) does not ensure global convergence.

notation.meaning: Derivative matrix retained throughout the run.

knowledge_statements.title: Chord Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the initial Jacobian once, then repeatedly solve against current residuals with that unchanged matrix until the stopping test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), choose an initial point \(x_0\), form \(A=F'(x_0)\), and factorize nonsingular \(A\) once. For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), solve \(As_k=-F(x_k)\) using the stored factorization and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\). Terminate when a prescribed residual or step test, such as \(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\le\varepsilon\), holds. The defining chord restriction is that \(A\) is never refreshed; consequently each iteration reuses the same linear operator even though the residual is evaluated at the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root-finding iteration using the Jacobian at the initial point throughout.

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 3 Newton-like Methods p. 44

knowledge_statements.title: Simplified Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse one nonsingular approximate Jacobian for all corrections; the matrix may be a simplified approximation rather than the initial exact Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), select an initial point \(x_0\) and a nonsingular fixed linearization \(A\) approximating \(F'(x)\) in the region of interest. Factorize \(A\) once. At iteration \(k\), solve \(As_k=-F(x_k)\), optionally apply a globalization parameter \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_ks_k\). Stop when the prescribed residual or step test holds. Unlike the chord specialization, the fixed matrix need not equal \(F'(x_0)\); it may be an analytically simplified, preconditioned, or otherwise inexpensive approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is defined on the generated iterates.
\(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is fixed and nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed approximate-Jacobian iteration, including but not limited to the chord choice.

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 3 Newton-like Methods p. 44

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Linearization Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently accurate fixed Jacobian gives local linear convergence; fixing the exact solution Jacobian yields quadratic convergence when the derivative is Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x_*)=0\), let \(A\) be nonsingular, and consider \(x_{k+1}=x_k-A^{-1}F(x_k)\). If \(F'\) is continuous near \(x_*\) and an induced norm satisfies \(\lVert I-A^{-1}F'(x_*)\rVert=\rho<1\), then all sufficiently close initial points generate iterates converging locally at least linearly, with asymptotic contraction bounded by any number greater than \(\rho\). If additionally \(A=F'(x_*)\) and \(F'\) is locally Lipschitz, then \(\lVert x_{k+1}-x_*\rVert=O(\lVert x_k-x_*\rVert^2)\). Thus a generic fixed approximation gives linear convergence, while the exact solution Jacobian permits quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to x_*\) locally linearly; if \(A=F'(x_*)\) and \(F'\) is Lipschitz, the convergence is quadratic.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence regimes determined by fixed-linearization accuracy.

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 3 Newton-like Methods p. 44

knowledge_statements.title: Lagged-Linearization Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refresh the Jacobian only at selected iterations and reuse its factorization between refreshes; fixed and ordinary Newton are limiting schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For differentiable \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), choose refresh indices \(0=r_0<r_1<\cdots\). At each refresh \(r_j\), form and factorize \(A_j=F'(x_{r_j})\). For \(r_j\le k<r_{j+1}\), solve \(A_js_k=-F(x_k)\) and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\); terminate under the prescribed residual or step test. Equivalently, \(x_{k+1}=x_k-F'(x_{\ell(k)})^{-1}F(x_k)\), where \(\ell(k)\le k\) is the most recent refresh. The regime is fixed-linearization when \(\ell(k)=0\), ordinary Newton when \(\ell(k)=k\), and lagged Newton otherwise.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is differentiable at every refresh iterate.
\(F'(x_{r_j})\) is nonsingular for every refresh index.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton iteration with Jacobians refreshed intermittently at earlier iterates.

notation.meaning: most recent refresh index at iteration k
Jacobian reused during refresh cycle j

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiple Newton Corrections per Derivative Refresh
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n,\quad m\in\mathbb N,\ m\ge1.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth square nonlinear systems with exact corrections; the fixed number \(m\) counts corrections performed with one freshly formed derivative matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[y_\ell^{(0)}=y_\ell,\quad B_\ell=DG(y_\ell),\quad y_\ell^{(j+1)}=y_\ell^{(j)}-B_\ell^{-1}G(y_\ell^{(j)}),\ j=0,\ldots,m-1,\] \[y_{\ell+1}=y_\ell^{(m)}.\] A multi-correction Newton method refreshes \(B_\ell\) once per outer cycle and applies \(m\) residual corrections with that same matrix or factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multi-correction Newton method begins each outer cycle at \(y_\ell\), evaluates and factors \(DG(y_\ell)\), and then performs \(m\) successive corrections using that unchanged matrix while reevaluating the nonlinear residual at each inner point. The final inner point becomes the next refresh point. This is the fixed-block Shamanskii construction.
assumptions_latex: \[DG(y_\ell)\text{ is nonsingular for every outer cycle}.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[y_{\ell+1}=\underbrace{T_{B_\ell}\circ\cdots\circ T_{B_\ell}}_{m\text{ corrections}}(y_\ell),\qquad T_B(x)=x-B^{-1}G(x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The refresh map is blockwise constant on each group of \(m\) correction indices.
special_cases_latex: \[m=1\] gives ordinary Newton iteration.
Allowing an unbounded number of corrections without refresh approaches a chord iteration within the cycle.
immediate_consequences_latex: Each outer cycle uses one derivative evaluation and factorization but \(m\) residual evaluations and linear solves.
All inner corrections share the same coefficient matrix.
boundary_notes: The correction count convention varies in the literature; here \(m\) is explicitly the number of solves after one refresh.
Adaptive refresh rules are outside this fixed-\(m\) definition.

notation.meaning: Derivative matrix shared by one correction block.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterated Newton Corrections
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Freeze and factor one linearization at each outer iterate, then apply several residual corrections before choosing the next outer iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an outer iterate \(x_k\), choose a nonsingular matrix \(A_k\), factorize it once, and set \(y_{k,0}=x_k\). For \(j=0,\ldots,m_k-1\), solve \(A_ks_{k,j}=-F(y_{k,j})\) and update \(y_{k,j+1}=y_{k,j}+s_{k,j}\). Set \(x_{k+1}=y_{k,m_k}\). The inner cycle may terminate early when its residual, correction, or forcing test is met; the outer process terminates under the prescribed nonlinear-system test. Choosing \(m_k=1\) gives one Newton-like correction, whereas \(m_k>1\) amortizes the factorization across several updated residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is defined at every inner iterate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple residual corrections performed with one frozen linearization.

notation.meaning: linearization frozen during outer cycle k
number of corrections in outer cycle k

knowledge_statements.title: Shamanskii-Type Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With one Jacobian frozen for m corrections, the Shamanskii cycle converges locally with order at least m+1 under standard smoothness and nonsingularity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) have a root \(x_*\), with \(F'(x_*)\) nonsingular, and suppose \(F'\) is locally Lipschitz. Fix an integer \(m\ge1\). From \(x_k\), set \(y_0=x_k\), factorize \(F'(x_k)\), and define \(y_{j+1}=y_j-F'(x_k)^{-1}F(y_j)\) for \(j=0,\ldots,m-1\); then set \(x_{k+1}=y_m\). For every sufficiently close \(x_0\), the iteration is well defined and converges to \(x_*\), with \(\lVert x_{k+1}-x_*\rVert=O(\lVert x_k-x_*\rVert^{m+1})\). Thus one derivative evaluation and factorization per cycle yields local order at least \(m+1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x_{k+1}-x_*\rVert=O(\lVert x_k-x_*\rVert^{m+1})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local order of a fixed-length Shamanskii derivative-refresh cycle.

notation.meaning: number of corrections per derivative refresh

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The stated order m+1 is plausible for the specified Shamanskii cycle under the given local Lipschitz and nonsingularity assumptions, but it is a nontrivial exact convergence theorem. The generic chapter-opening citation does not specifically locate or establish this theorem, and the record itself flags the exact theorem locator as pending.

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 3 Newton-like Methods p. 44

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Refresh Cycles
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each outer cycle assembles and factors one Jacobian, applies up to m Newton-like corrections with that matrix frozen, and then refreshes it unless the residual tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a differentiable mapping \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), an initial point \(x_0\), an inner-cycle length \(m\ge 1\), and a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), set \(k=0\). At cycle \(k\), form and factor \(J_k=F'(x_k)\), set \(y_0=x_k\), and compute
\[J_k s_j=-F(y_j),\qquad y_{j+1}=y_j+s_j,\qquad j=0,\ldots,m-1.\]
Stop and return \(y_{j+1}\) whenever \(\lVert F(y_{j+1})\rVert\le\varepsilon\); otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=y_m\), increment \(k\), and refresh the derivative. Thus one derivative assembly and factorization supports at most \(m\) corrections.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is differentiable wherever a derivative is assembled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=y_m\) after at most \(m\) solves using the single refreshed matrix \(J_k=F'(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic Jacobian refresh with multiple frozen-Jacobian corrections per outer cycle.

notation.meaning: Jacobian assembled at the start of cycle k
j-th inner correction point in the current cycle

review_flags: A precise source for the periodic-refresh algorithm and its conventions is required.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Derivative-Refresh Cycles leaf and is internally coherent, but no inspectable source supports the precise refresh convention, inner-cycle indexing, or claim that one factorization supports up to m corrections.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Correction Limits
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Frozen-Jacobian corrections stop at a correction cap, residual tolerance, or step tolerance; unlimited corrections are justified only when the frozen iteration is contractive on an invariant set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an outer point \(x_k\), let \(J_k=F'(x_k)\) be nonsingular, and define \(T_k(y)=y-J_k^{-1}F(y)\). Inner corrections are \(y_{j+1}=T_k(y_j)\), starting from \(y_0=x_k\), and are limited by
\[j<m_{\max},\qquad \lVert F(y_j)\rVert>\varepsilon_F,\qquad \lVert y_j-y_{j-1}\rVert>\varepsilon_x.\]
If \(T_k\) maps a closed set \(D_k\) into itself and is a contraction there with factor \(q_k<1\), unlimited corrections converge to the unique fixed point in \(D_k\), which is a zero of \(F\). Without this contraction condition, increasing \(m_{\max}\) need not improve the outer iterate.
assumptions_latex: For the convergence conclusion, \(T_k(D_k)\subseteq D_k\) and \(\lVert T_k(u)-T_k(v)\rVert\le q_k\lVert u-v\rVert\) with \(q_k<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the contraction conditions hold, then \(y_j\to y_*\in D_k\) and \(F(y_*)=0\); otherwise no convergence guarantee follows merely from allowing more corrections.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible termination and convergence limits for corrections using one frozen Jacobian.

notation.meaning: iteration map induced by the frozen Jacobian

review_flags: The contraction formulation is standard, but a source specific to frozen-Jacobian inner limits is missing.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the frozen-Jacobian contraction formulation. The record also mixes stopping conditions, a contraction theorem, and a failure boundary under content_kind condition; moreover, the step test involving y_j-y_{j-1} is undefined at j=0 unless its starting index is specified.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Derivative-Realization Classification of Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n,\quad A_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n,\quad A_ks_k=-G(x_k).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth Newton systems; a realization may provide an assembled matrix or only the action of the derivative on vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathfrak R_k\in\{\text{assembled analytic},\text{finite difference},\text{automatic differentiation},\text{operator action}\}\] is a derivative realization if it supplies either \(A_k\approx DG(x_k)\) or a map \(v\mapsto A_kv\) used to compute \(s_k\) from \(A_ks_k=-G(x_k)\). Two Newton variants differ by derivative realization when their nonlinear model is the same but the construction or application of \(A_k\) differs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative realization variant of Newton's method is specified by how the derivative in the Newton system is obtained and represented. The realization may assemble analytic entries, approximate entries or actions by finite differences, propagate derivatives through a computational graph by automatic differentiation, or expose only matrix-vector products to an iterative solver. The defining Newton equation remains \(A_k s_k=-G(x_k)\).
assumptions_latex: \[A_k\text{ is available either as a matrix or as a linear operator action}.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A_ks_k=-G(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k,\qquad A_k\approx DG(x_k).\]
special_cases_latex: Analytic assembly sets \((A_k)_{ij}=\partial G_i(x_k)/\partial x_j\).
Finite differences approximate columns or products from perturbed residual evaluations.
Automatic differentiation computes derivative entries or actions by chain-rule propagation.
immediate_consequences_latex: The same formal Newton system may have different storage, accuracy, and evaluation costs under different realizations.
Matrix-free realizations can be paired with Krylov linear solvers.
boundary_notes: Quasi-Newton secant updates approximate derivatives from iteration history and are not included merely as a derivative-evaluation realization.
The classification does not assert that all realizations produce identical floating-point steps.

notation.meaning: Derivative realization used at iteration k.
Realized derivative matrix or linear operator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Third derivative as the directional derivative of the Hessian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A smooth multivariate-calculus definition, independent of any particular Newton implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f\in C^3(\mathbb{R}^n)\) and \(x,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the third-derivative operator applied to \(u\) is the matrix \[f'''(x)[u]:=\lim_{\alpha\to0}\frac{\nabla^2f(x+\alpha u)-\nabla^2f(x)}{\alpha},\] where the limit is taken in matrix norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The third derivative applied in a direction u is the matrix-valued directional derivative of the Hessian in that direction.
assumptions_latex: \text{the limit is taken in matrix norm}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f'''(x)[u]=\lim_{\alpha\to0}\frac{\nabla^2f(x+\alpha u)-\nabla^2f(x)}{\alpha}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}.

knowledge_statements.title: Assembled Analytic-Derivative Newton
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit analytic formulas assemble the complete Jacobian at every iteration; the resulting matrix system supplies the full Newton correction until the residual tolerance or a solve failure occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) with analytically available partial derivatives, choose \(x_0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\). At iteration \(k\), explicitly assemble
\[J_k=F'(x_k)=\left[\frac{\partial F_i}{\partial x_j}(x_k)\right]_{i,j=1}^n,\]
solve \(J_kp_k=-F(x_k)\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\). Stop and return \(x_k\) when \(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\le\varepsilon\), or report linear-solve failure when \(J_k\) is singular or the prescribed solve cannot be completed. The defining realization is explicit storage of the analytic derivative matrix before solving the Newton system.
assumptions_latex: Every component \(F_i\) is differentiable at the iterates.
The analytic partial derivatives used in the assembly equal those of the modeled mapping.
The Newton system is solvable at every accepted iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-F'(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k)\) whenever the assembled Jacobian is nonsingular.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton Iteration with a Finite-Difference Jacobian
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n,\quad e_j\text{ is the }j\text{th coordinate vector},\quad h_{k,j}\ne0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth square nonlinear systems with forward coordinate differences; central differences and matrix-free directional differences are nearby variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[(A_k)_{:j}=\frac{G(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-G(x_k)}{h_{k,j}},\quad j=1,\ldots,n,\] \[A_ks_k=-G(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k.\] A finite-difference Newton method is Newton's iteration with the exact Jacobian replaced by this numerically sampled derivative matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-difference Newton replaces the exact Jacobian by columns obtained from residual differences. At iteration \(k\), column \(j\) is \([G(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-G(x_k)]/h_{k,j}\). The resulting matrix is used in the Newton correction equation, after which the iterate is updated by the computed correction.
assumptions_latex: \[A_k\text{ is nonsingular whenever the correction is computed}.\]
special_cases_latex: A common scaled choice is \(h_{k,j}=\sqrt{\eta}\max\{|(x_k)_j|,\operatorname{typ}x_j\}\operatorname{sign}((x_k)_j)\).
For \(G=\nabla f\), differencing the gradient gives a finite-difference Hessian.
immediate_consequences_latex: A dense forward-difference Jacobian requires the base residual and up to \(n\) additional residual evaluations.
In exact arithmetic, the column error is first order in \(|h_{k,j}|\) under a Lipschitz derivative.
boundary_notes: Very small intervals amplify cancellation and evaluation noise; interval selection is part of the numerical realization.
A fixed nonvanishing differencing interval generally limits attainable local accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Finite-Difference Newton
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dense method approximates each Jacobian column with its own coordinate perturbation, solves the approximate Newton system, and uses n+1 residual evaluations per forward-difference assembly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), choose \(x_0\), nonzero increments \(h_{k,j}\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). At iteration \(k\), evaluate \(F(x_k)\) and assemble every column independently by
\[B_ke_j=\frac{F(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-F(x_k)}{h_{k,j}},\qquad j=1,\ldots,n.\]
Solve \(B_kp_k=-F(x_k)\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\), and stop when \(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\le\varepsilon\). Without sparsity grouping, one forward-difference Jacobian requires \(n+1\) residual evaluations when the base value is shared; central differences analogously require \(2n\) perturbed evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is defined at every base and perturbed point.
Each approximate Newton system used for an update is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k-B_k^{-1}F(x_k)\), with \(B_k\) assembled from ungrouped coordinate differences.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-difference Jacobian construction using one separate residual evaluation per coordinate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ungrouped Dense Finite-Difference Newton
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n,\quad h_j\ne0,\quad A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-difference construction without a prescribed sparsity pattern or simultaneous column perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[A_{:j}=\frac{G(x+h_je_j)-G(x)}{h_j},\quad j=1,\ldots,n,\] with one distinct perturbed residual evaluation for every coordinate column. Dense finite-difference Newton computes \(As=-G(x)\) using this fully materialized matrix and updates \(x_+=x+s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense finite-difference Newton constructs every Jacobian column separately. Starting from one base residual \(G(x)\), it evaluates \(G(x+h_j e_j)\) for each of the \(n\) coordinates, forms a full \(n\)-by-\(n\) matrix, and solves the resulting approximate Newton system. No structural zeros or column groups are assumed during derivative construction.
assumptions_latex: \[A\text{ is nonsingular for the stated step}.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_+=x-A^{-1}G(x),\qquad A=\left[\frac{G(x+h_1e_1)-G(x)}{h_1}\ \cdots\ \frac{G(x+h_ne_n)-G(x)}{h_n}\right].\]
special_cases_latex: A common interval rule assigns a separate scale-sensitive \(h_j\) to each coordinate.
Central differences replace each forward column by \([G(x+h_je_j)-G(x-h_je_j)]/(2h_j)\) at twice the perturbed-evaluation cost.
immediate_consequences_latex: Forward construction uses \(n+1\) residual values when the base value is counted.
Storage is that of a general dense \(n\times n\) matrix unless later compression is applied.
boundary_notes: The adjective dense refers to ungrouped full construction, even if some computed entries happen to be zero.
Sparse coloring or grouped perturbations belong to sparse finite-difference Newton.
