children.title: Sparse Finite-Difference Newton
children.top_down_role: Finite-difference derivative construction exploiting sparsity and grouped evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Finite-Difference Newton
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Columns with disjoint row supports share one perturbation. Their entries are decoded from a grouped residual difference, reducing forward-difference assembly from n+1 to q+1 evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the known structural supports of the Jacobian columns be \(S_j=\{i:\partial F_i/\partial x_j\text{ may be nonzero}\}\). Partition the columns into groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_q\) satisfying \(S_j\cap S_\ell=\varnothing\) whenever distinct \(j,\ell\in G_r\). For each group, evaluate
\[d_r=F\!\left(x_k+\sum_{j\in G_r}h_{k,j}e_j\right)-F(x_k).\]
Recover \((B_k)_{ij}=(d_r)_i/h_{k,j}\) for \(j\in G_r\) and \(i\in S_j\), set structurally zero entries to zero, solve \(B_kp_k=-F(x_k)\), and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\). Forward grouping uses \(q+1\) residual evaluations per assembly.
assumptions_latex: The structural supports \(S_j\) contain every potentially nonzero Jacobian entry.
Columns in each group have pairwise disjoint supports.
All increments \(h_{k,j}\) are nonzero and the recovered system is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A sparse approximation \(B_k\) is recoverable from \(q\) grouped perturbations, and \(x_{k+1}=x_k-B_k^{-1}F(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structurally orthogonal column grouping for sparse finite-difference Jacobian recovery.

notation.meaning: structural row support of Jacobian column j

review_flags: The supplied finite-difference locators do not explicitly identify sparse column grouping or structural orthogonality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparse Finite-Difference Newton with Grouped Perturbations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n,\quad \mathcal S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}^2\text{ is the structural support of }DG.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Square nonlinear systems with a known, iterate-independent Jacobian sparsity pattern and forward grouped differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{\Gamma_1,\ldots,\Gamma_q\}\) partition the columns so that, for every group \(\Gamma_c\) and row \(i\), at most one \(j\in\Gamma_c\) satisfies \((i,j)\in\mathcal S\). Define \[w_c=G\!\left(x+\sum_{j\in\Gamma_c}h_je_j\right).\] For \((i,j)\in\mathcal S\) with \(j\in\Gamma_c\), set \[A_{ij}=\frac{(w_c)_i-G_i(x)}{h_j},\qquad A_{ij}=0\text{ for }(i,j)\notin\mathcal S.\] Sparse finite-difference Newton solves \(As=-G(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse finite-difference Newton uses a known structural Jacobian pattern to perturb several compatible variables in one residual evaluation. Columns are grouped so that no two columns in a group have structural nonzeros in the same row. One simultaneous perturbation per group then determines all supported entries in those columns, after which the sparse approximate Newton system is solved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[As=-G(x),\qquad x_+=x+s,\qquad A\text{ reconstructed from }q\text{ grouped evaluations}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Compatible column grouping is a coloring of the column-intersection graph of the structural Jacobian.
special_cases_latex: For a tridiagonal Jacobian, three residue classes of column indices form valid groups.
Singleton groups \(\Gamma_j=\{j\}\) recover the ungrouped dense construction.
immediate_consequences_latex: The number of additional residual evaluations equals the number \(q\) of groups rather than \(n\).
Structural zeros need neither evaluation nor storage.
boundary_notes: An incorrect sparsity pattern can alias contributions from simultaneously perturbed columns.
Finding a minimum grouping for a general sparse pattern is a combinatorial problem; any valid grouping defines the method.

notation.meaning: Known structural support of the Jacobian.
Residual evaluated at the simultaneous perturbation for group c.

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic-Differentiation Newton
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Automatic differentiation supplies either the full Jacobian or Jacobian-vector products for the Newton solve, after which the iterate receives the computed correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a differentiable program evaluate \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\). Starting from \(x_0\), at iteration \(k\) use automatic differentiation either to assemble \(J_k=F'(x_k)\) or to provide exact-arithmetic products \(v\mapsto J_kv\) to a linear solver. Compute \(p_k\) from
\[J_kp_k=-F(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k.\]
Stop when \(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\le\varepsilon\), or when the linear solve meets its prescribed residual criterion in a matrix-free realization. The differentiated program must follow the same active computational branch as the residual evaluation at \(x_k\).
assumptions_latex: The executed residual program is differentiable along its active trace at each iterate.
Automatic differentiation covers every operation contributing to \(F\).
The assembled or matrix-free Newton system is solved to the required accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: In exact arithmetic, the derivative information used by the solve equals \(F'(x_k)\) for the executed differentiable program trace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton iteration whose derivative matrix or matrix-vector products are generated by automatic differentiation.

notation.meaning: Jacobian produced or applied by automatic differentiation
Newton correction obtained from the assembled or matrix-free solve

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton Method with Automatically Differentiated Operators
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\] is evaluated by a finite computational graph of differentiable elementary operations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth program-defined residuals; derivatives are exact in real arithmetic for the executed computational graph, subject to floating-point effects in implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An automatic-differentiation realization supplies \[J_k=DG(x_k),\qquad v\mapsto J_kv,\text{ or }w\mapsto J_k^Tw\] by repeated application of the chain rule to the executed elementary operations. Automatic-differentiation Newton computes \[J_ks_k=-G(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k,\] using an assembled \(J_k\) or an operator-only AD action.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Automatic-differentiation Newton obtains the Jacobian, a Jacobian-vector product, or a transposed-Jacobian product by propagating derivatives through the computational graph used to evaluate the residual. It then solves the usual Newton system. Unlike finite differences, the derivative realization has no differencing interval and differentiates the executed program by the chain rule.
assumptions_latex: Every executed elementary operation on the active path is differentiable at the current values.
The AD-generated derivative operator is sufficient for the selected linear solver.
The resulting Newton system is solvable for the stated correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_{k+1}=x_k-DG(x_k)^{-1}G(x_k),\] where \(DG(x_k)\) or its required actions are produced by automatic differentiation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Forward mode propagates \(J_kv\); reverse mode propagates \(J_k^Tw\).
Applying forward mode to coordinate seeds assembles the Jacobian columns.
special_cases_latex: For scalar \(f\), reverse mode supplies \(\nabla f\).
Nested or higher-order AD may supply Hessian-vector products for Newton-CG.
immediate_consequences_latex: No truncation error from a finite-difference quotient is introduced in exact arithmetic.
Operator actions permit matrix-free Newton-Krylov implementations.
boundary_notes: AD differentiates the implemented computation, which may differ from an ideal mathematical model because of branches, iterative tolerances, or discretization error.
Nondifferentiable executed operations fall outside this smooth definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Classification of Newton Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[G:X\supset D\to X,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k-DG(x_k)^{-1}G(x_k),\] where \(X\) is a normed space and the inverse is required wherever the iteration is defined.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A classificatory definition spanning local regular-root, semilocal, globalized, and singular-root analyses; individual convergence theorems require regime-specific hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Newton convergence regime is a tuple \[\mathcal R=(D,\mathcal I,\mathcal H,\mathcal G,\mathcal Q)\] specifying an admissible initial set \(\mathcal I\subseteq D\), analytic hypotheses \(\mathcal H\) on \(G\) and \(DG\), an optional globalization mechanism \(\mathcal G\), and a convergence conclusion \(\mathcal Q\). It is local if \(\mathcal I\) is a neighborhood of a known regular root, semilocal if hypotheses at \(x_0\) imply existence of a root in a certified region, globalized if \(\mathcal G\) controls acceptance from a broader initial set, and singular if \(DG(x_*)\) is noninvertible and the regular-root rate statement is replaced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Newton convergence regime theory classifies results by the information assumed and the conclusion obtained. A local regime starts near a known nonsingular root; a semilocal regime uses data at the starting point to certify a nearby root and convergence; a globalized regime adds step acceptance or restriction to obtain convergence from a broader set; and a singular regime treats roots where the derivative is noninvertible and classical quadratic conclusions need not hold.
assumptions_latex: \[G\text{ and the iteration domain }D\text{ are specified}.\]
Each regime explicitly states its initial-set, regularity, invertibility, and globalization hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal R\in\{\mathcal R_{\rm local},\mathcal R_{\rm semilocal},\mathcal R_{\rm globalized},\mathcal R_{\rm singular}\}.\]
special_cases_latex: Regular-root local theory takes \(DG(x_*)^{-1}\) bounded and \(DG\) locally Lipschitz.
Newton–Kantorovich theory is semilocal.
Line-search and trust-region Newton methods instantiate globalized regimes.
immediate_consequences_latex: A convergence rate is meaningful only together with its regime's initial-set and regularity hypotheses.
Singular-root behavior cannot be inferred from the regular-root quadratic theorem.
boundary_notes: This definition organizes theorem families; it is not itself a convergence theorem.
A single source locator supporting all four categories was not established from the supplied source hints.
review_flags: Needs a single inspectable source or coordinated source set explicitly supporting the four-way local, semilocal, globalized, and singular classification.

knowledge_statements.source_title: Local Quadratic Convergence of Newton's Method
knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Q-Quadratic Convergence of Newton Iterates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n,\quad F(x_*)=0,\quad x_{k+1}=x_k-J(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k),\quad J=DF.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Newton iteration near a regular root of a continuously differentiable finite-dimensional system with locally Lipschitz Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Newton's method is locally Q-quadratically convergent to \(x_*\) if there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(C>0\) such that every \(x_0\) with \(\|x_0-x_*\|<\varepsilon\) generates a well-defined sequence converging to \(x_*\) and satisfying \[\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\le C\|x_k-x_*\|^2\qquad(k\ge0).\] Under \(\|J(x_*)^{-1}\|\le\beta\) and a Jacobian Lipschitz constant \(\gamma\), one may take \(C=\beta\gamma\) on a sufficiently small neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain:
Local Q-quadratic convergence of Newton's method means that all sufficiently close starting points generate well-defined Newton iterates converging to the root, and the next error is bounded by a constant times the square of the current error. For a regular root with a locally Lipschitz Jacobian, the classical estimate uses the constant \(C=\beta
gamma\), where \(\beta\) bounds the inverse root Jacobian and \(\gamma\) is a local Lipschitz constant.
assumptions_latex: \[F\in C^1(D,\mathbb R^n),\qquad D\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ open and convex}.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists\varepsilon>0\ \forall x_0:\|x_0-x_*\|<\varepsilon\Longrightarrow \|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\le\beta\gamma\|x_k-x_*\|^2.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If no iterate equals \(x_*\) finitely, Q-quadratic convergence implies \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|}{\|x_k-x_*\|^2}<\infty.\]
special_cases_latex: For affine \(F\) with nonsingular Jacobian, Newton reaches the root in one iteration.
For unconstrained minimization, apply the statement to \(F=\nabla f\) at a nondegenerate stationary point.
immediate_consequences_latex: Once \(C\|x_k-x_*\|<1\), the error contracts at least linearly and subsequently obeys the quadratic bound.
The result is local and does not imply convergence from an arbitrary starting point.
boundary_notes: A multiple or singular root is excluded by invertibility of \(J(x_*)\).
Inexact solves, damping, and finite-difference derivatives require additional error conditions to retain this rate.

notation.meaning: Bound on the inverse Jacobian at the root.

abla^2f(x^*)\succ0\), continuity of the Hessian makes \(
abla^2f(x)\succ0\) in a neighborhood of \(x^*\), so the Newton step is well defined there; when the step lengths are eventually \(\alpha_k=1\), the local Newton iteration has quadratic convergence. Away from this neighborhood, globalization may modify the Hessian to obtain line-search descent or minimize the Hessian-based quadratic model inside a trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton direction need not be a descent direction when the Hessian is indefinite. Near a solution with positive-definite Hessian, the step is well defined and eventual full steps give the stated quadratic local regime; globally, curvature modification or a trust region can be used.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quantitative local quadratic convergence of Newton's method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded local convergence theorem with an explicit invariant radius and error estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}$ be twice continuously differentiable, let $
abla f(x^*)=0$, assume $
abla^2f(x^*)\succeq\mu I_n$ for some $\mu>0$, and suppose $\|
abla^2f(x)-
abla^2f(y)\|\le M\|x-y\|$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n$, where $M>0$ and the Euclidean norm and induced operator norm are used. Set $ ar r=2\mu/(3M)$. If $\|x_0-x^*\|< ar r$, then every exact Newton iterate is well defined, remains in this ball, and satisfies $\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\le  rac{M\|x_k-x^*\|^2}{2(\mu-M\|x_k-x^*\|)}$ for every $k\ge0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a stationary point has a uniformly positive-definite Hessian there and the Hessian is globally Lipschitz, then every Newton step starting within the stated strict radius exists, stays within that radius, and obeys an explicit quadratic error bound.
assumptions_latex: The vector norm is Euclidean and the matrix norm is its induced operator norm
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k\ge0:\quad \nabla^2f(x_k)\text{ is invertible},\quad \|x_k-x^*\|<\bar r,\quad \|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\le\frac{M\|x_k-x^*\|^2}{2(\mu-M\|x_k-x^*\|)}.

children.title: Regular-Root Local Rate
children.top_down_role: The local rate regime for isolated nonsingular equation roots.

knowledge_statements.title: Regular-Root Local Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a root with nonsingular Jacobian and locally Lipschitz derivative, full Newton steps are well-defined and the next error is bounded by a constant times the squared current error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(x_*\), satisfy \(F(x_*)=0\), and have nonsingular \(F'(x_*)\). If \(F'\) is Lipschitz continuous near \(x_*\), then there exist a neighborhood \(V\) of \(x_*\) and a constant \(C>0\) such that, for every \(x_0\in V\), the full Newton iterates
\[x_{k+1}=x_k-F'(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k)\]
are well-defined, remain in \(V\), and satisfy \(\lVert x_{k+1}-x_*\rVert\le C\lVert x_k-x_*\rVert^2\). Consequently, the iterates converge quadratically to the locally isolated root \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all sufficiently close \(x_0\), \(x_k\to x_*\) and \(\lVert x_{k+1}-x_*\rVert\le C\lVert x_k-x_*\rVert^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic convergence of full Newton iteration near a nonsingular isolated root.

notation.meaning: regular root of the nonlinear system

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular Root and Its Newton Local-Rate Regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n,\qquad F(x_*)=0,\qquad J_*=DF(x_*).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Isolated nonsingular roots of smooth square systems in finite dimensions; the rate statement uses an exact full Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A root \(x_*\) is regular when \[F(x_*)=0,\qquad \det J_*\ne0.\] Its classical Newton local-rate regime consists of a neighborhood \(N(x_*,\varepsilon)\) on which Newton iterates are well defined and satisfy \[\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\le C\|x_k-x_*\|^2.\] If \(J\) is Lipschitz with constant \(\gamma\) and \(\|J_*^{-1}\|\le\beta\), a valid classical bound is \(C=eta\gamma\) after reducing \(\varepsilon\) if necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain:
A regular root is a zero \(x_*\) whose Jacobian is nonsingular. The regular-root local rate of exact Newton iteration is Q-quadratic when the Jacobian is locally Lipschitz: sufficiently close starting points remain in the regular neighborhood, converge to the root, and satisfy an error estimate of the form \(\|e_{k+1}\|\le C\|e_k\|^2\). The classical constant can be taken as \(C=\beta
gamma\) under the stated local bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists\varepsilon>0\ \forall x_0\in N(x_*,\varepsilon):\ x_k\to x_*,\quad \|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\le\beta\gamma\|x_k-x_*\|^2.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: In finite dimensions, regularity is equivalent to \(J_*\) being bijective or to \(\sigma_{\min}(J_*)>0\).
By the inverse function theorem, a regular root is locally isolated.
special_cases_latex: For \(n=1\), regularity is \(F'(x_*)\ne0\).
For \(F=\nabla f\), regularity is nonsingularity of \(\nabla^2f(x_*)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The inverse Jacobian remains bounded on a sufficiently small neighborhood of a regular root.
The number of correct digits typically grows rapidly once the iterates enter the quadratic neighborhood.
boundary_notes: If \(J_*\) is singular, the root is outside this regime and Newton may converge only linearly or fail.
Regularity alone does not give a global basin of attraction; local Lipschitz control and a sufficiently close initial point are essential to the stated rate.

knowledge_statements.title: Nondegenerate-Minimizer Local Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a stationary point with positive-definite Hessian and locally Lipschitz curvature, sufficiently close full Newton iterates converge quadratically to the strict local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(x_*\), with \(
abla f(x_*)=0\) and \(
abla^2f(x_*)\) positive definite. If \(
abla^2f\) is Lipschitz continuous near \(x_*\), then \(x_*\) is a strict local minimizer and there exist a neighborhood \(V\) and \(C>0\) such that every full-step Newton sequence
\[x_{k+1}=x_k-
abla^2f(x_k)^{-1}
abla f(x_k),\qquad x_0\in V,\]
is well-defined and obeys \(\lVert x_{k+1}-x_*Vert\le C\lVert x_k-x_*Vert^2\). Hence the convergence to \(x_*\) is quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For sufficiently close \(x_0\), \(x_k\to x_*\) quadratically and \(x_*\) is a strict local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic convergence of full Newton minimization near a positive-definite stationary point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nondegenerate-minimizer quadratic Newton regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable near \(x^*\), let \(
abla f(x^*)=0\), and define the full Newton step by \(
abla^2 f(x_k)p_k=-
abla f(x_k)\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, unconstrained optimization with exact Hessians and full Newton steps near a strict nondegenerate local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence is in the nondegenerate-minimizer local quadratic regime at \(x^*\) when \(\nabla^2 f(x^*)\succ0\), the Hessian is Lipschitz continuous on some neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\), every sufficiently late iterate belongs to \(U\), and there are \(C>0\) and \(K\) such that \[\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\le C\|x_k-x^*\|^2\qquad(k\ge K).\] The regime includes local well-definedness: \(\nabla^2 f(x)\) is nonsingular throughout a possibly smaller neighborhood of \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-step Newton sequence has the nondegenerate-minimizer local rate when it approaches a stationary point \(x^*\) with positive-definite Hessian, the Hessian is locally Lipschitz, and its errors satisfy \(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\le C\|x_k-x^*\|^2\) eventually. Positive definiteness also makes the nearby Newton systems nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2 f(x^*)\succ0\) and local Hessian Lipschitz continuity define the regime in which the full-step error is eventually bounded by \(C\|x_k-x^*\|^2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The rate condition is Q-quadratic convergence: \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|/\|x_k-x^*\|^2<\infty\).
special_cases_latex: For a strictly convex quadratic with constant positive-definite Hessian, Newton's method reaches \(x^*\) in one step.
immediate_consequences_latex: The gradient norms also converge Q-quadratically under the same local hypotheses.
boundary_notes: Positive semidefiniteness alone is insufficient: a singular Hessian lies outside this nondegenerate regime.
Damped iterations are included only after their step lengths become exactly one.

children.title: Regular Equality-KKT Local Rate
children.top_down_role: The local rate regime for regular equality-constrained primal-dual systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Regular Equality-KKT Local Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice-smooth equality-constrained problem, full row rank of the constraint Jacobian and nonsingularity of the reduced Lagrangian Hessian make the KKT Jacobian nonsingular. If the KKT derivative is locally Lipschitz, sufficiently close full primal-dual Newton iterates converge quadratically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:U\to\mathbb{R}^m\), with \(m\le n\), be twice continuously differentiable, and define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\) for \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and
\[G(x,\lambda)=\begin{bmatrix}\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\\c(x)\end{bmatrix}.\]
Let \(z_*=(x_*,\lambda_*)\in U\times\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfy \(G(z_*)=0\). Suppose \(c'(x_*)\) has full row rank, and let \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) have columns forming a basis of \(\ker c'(x_*)\). If the reduced Hessian \(Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_*,\lambda_*)Z\) is nonsingular and \(G'\) is Lipschitz continuous near \(z_*\), then \(G'(z_*)\) is nonsingular. Consequently, there exist a neighborhood \(V\) of \(z_*\) and a constant \(C>0\) such that, for every \(z_0\in V\), the full Newton iterates
\[z_{k+1}=z_k-G'(z_k)^{-1}G(z_k)\]
are well-defined and satisfy \(\lVert z_{k+1}-z_*\rVert\le C\lVert z_k-z_*\rVert^2\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:U\to\mathbb{R}^m\) are twice continuously differentiable on an open set \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
For a basis matrix \(Z\) of \(\ker c'(x_*)\), the matrix \(Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_*,\lambda_*)Z\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every sufficiently close \(z_0\), the full primal-dual Newton iterates converge to \(z_*\) and satisfy \(\lVert z_{k+1}-z_*\rVert\le C\lVert z_k-z_*\rVert^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic convergence of Newton iteration for a regular equality-constrained KKT system.

notation.meaning: combined primal-dual variable in the product space
matrix whose columns form a basis of the null space of the constraint Jacobian at the solution

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular equality-KKT quadratic regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(A(x)=c'(x)\), and \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\lambda^Tc(x)\). Define \(F(x,\lambda)=(\nabla_x\mathcal L(x,\lambda),c(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality-constrained optimization, exact primal-dual Newton steps, LICQ, and second-order sufficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A KKT pair \(z^*=(x^*,\lambda^*)\) is regular when \(F(z^*)=0\), \(A(x^*)\) has full row rank, and \(d^T\nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)d>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\ker A(x^*)\). Equivalently, the KKT Jacobian \[F'(z^*)=\begin{bmatrix}\nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)&-A(x^*)^T\\A(x^*)&0\end{bmatrix}\] is nonsingular. The regular equality-KKT local quadratic regime consists of full Newton iterates \(z_{k+1}=z_k-F'(z_k)^{-1}F(z_k)\) for which \(\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|\le C\|z_k-z^*\|^2\) eventually.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular equality-KKT point satisfies feasibility and stationarity, has a full-row-rank constraint Jacobian, and has a Lagrangian Hessian positive definite on the constraint tangent space. These conditions make the primal-dual KKT Jacobian nonsingular. The associated exact Newton iteration has the local quadratic regime when its primal-dual error is eventually bounded by \(C\|z_k-z^*\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Regularity is characterized by nonsingularity of the displayed KKT Jacobian, and the local rate regime is Q-quadratic convergence of the exact primal-dual Newton iteration.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(Z\) spanning \(\ker A(x^*)\), tangent-space positivity is \(Z^T\nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)Z\succ0\).
special_cases_latex: When \(m=0\), the definition reduces to the nondegenerate unconstrained minimizer regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: The primal and multiplier components converge quadratically together in any norm on \(\mathbb R^{n+m}\).
boundary_notes: Rank-deficient equality constraints are excluded.
Inequality constraints require an identified active set and additional complementarity regularity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton-Kantorovich semilocal certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable on the open ball \(N(x_0,r)\), write \(J=F'\), and use a vector norm and its induced operator norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite-dimensional semilocal Newton theory based entirely on data at an initial point and a Lipschitz bound over a surrounding ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Newton-Kantorovich certificate at \(x_0\) is a tuple \((\beta,\gamma,\eta,r)\) satisfying \[\|J(x_0)^{-1}\|\le\beta,\qquad \|J(x_0)^{-1}F(x_0)\|\le\eta,\qquad \|J(x)-J(y)\|\le\gamma\|x-y\|\] for all \(x,y\in N(x_0,r)\). With \(\alpha=\beta\gamma\eta\), it is admissible when \(\alpha\le\tfrac12\) and \[r\ge r_0:=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-2\alpha}}{\beta\gamma}.\] The certified Newton sequence is \(x_{k+1}=x_k-J(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k)\), and the certificate asserts its well-definedness, convergence, and existence and local uniqueness of a zero in the certified ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Newton-Kantorovich theory uses an invertibility bound at \(x_0\), a Lipschitz constant for the Jacobian, and the size of the first Newton correction. Their dimensionless product \(\alpha=\beta\gamma\eta\) must not exceed one half, and the domain must contain the explicitly computed radius \(r_0\). This certificate supplies both a root-existence region and a convergence guarantee without assuming a root in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An admissible certificate has \(\alpha\le1/2\) and domain radius at least \(r_0\), thereby defining a semilocal existence, uniqueness, and Newton-convergence guarantee.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The quantity \(\beta\gamma\) is a bound on relative Jacobian nonlinearity, while \(\eta\) bounds the first Newton displacement.
special_cases_latex: If \(\gamma=0\), then \(F\) is affine on the ball and one Newton step solves the system whenever \(J(x_0)\) is nonsingular.
immediate_consequences_latex: The certified root lies in \(\overline{N(x_0,r_0)}\).
boundary_notes: The certificate is sufficient, not necessary, and its norm-based bounds may be conservative.
The stated form is finite-dimensional; Banach-space variants require corresponding Fréchet-derivative hypotheses.

children.title: Semilocal Newton Convergence
children.top_down_role: Newton convergence inferred from neighborhood information at the initial point.

knowledge_statements.title: Semilocal Newton Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible initial Jacobian, a scaled Lipschitz derivative bound, and Kantorovich parameter at most one-half guarantee that Newton iterates remain in a computable ball and converge to a locally unique zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and convex, let \(F:D\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable, and suppose \(F'(x_0)\) is nonsingular. Set \(\eta=\lVert F'(x_0)^{-1}F(x_0)\rVert\), and assume
\[\lVert F'(x_0)^{-1}(F'(x)-F'(y))\rVert\le L\lVert x-y\rVert\]
throughout \(D\), with \(h=L\eta\le\tfrac12\). Define \(r_-=(1-\sqrt{1-2h})/L\) and suppose the closed ball \(\overline B(x_0,r_-)\subset D\). Then Newton iterates are well-defined, remain in this ball, and converge to a zero \(x_*\) of \(F\). The zero is unique in \(B(x_0,r_+)\cap D\), where \(r_+=(1+\sqrt{1-2h})/L\).
assumptions_latex: The scaled derivative satisfies the stated Lipschitz bound with \(L>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Newton iteration converges to \(x_*\in\overline B(x_0,r_-)\), and this zero is unique in \(B(x_0,r_+)\cap D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical Newton–Kantorovich theorem using initial residual, inverse derivative, and a neighborhood Lipschitz bound.

notation.meaning: norm of the initial Newton correction

review_flags: The exact Newton–Kantorovich normalization and uniqueness radius require an authoritative theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semilocal Newton convergence from initial-point data
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable on a neighborhood \(D\) of \(x_0\), and define \(x_{k+1}=x_k-F'(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k)\) whenever the inverse exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional root finding; semilocal means that existence of the limiting root is concluded from initial-point and neighborhood data rather than assumed beforehand.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Newton's method is semilocally convergent from \(x_0\) with certified region \(D_0\subseteq D\) when quantities computable or bounded on \(D_0\)—including nonsingularity of \(F'(x_0)\), a bound on \(\|F'(x_0)^{-1}\|\), a bound on the first correction \(\|F'(x_0)^{-1}F(x_0)\|\), and a Lipschitz bound for \(F'\)—imply all of the following: every \(x_k\) is defined and belongs to \(D_0\); \(x_k\to x^*\); \(F(x^*)=0\); and \(x^*\) is the unique zero in a stated neighborhood. No root or inverse-Jacobian bound at an unknown root is assumed in the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semilocal convergence is a certified Newton regime whose hypotheses concern the initial point and a surrounding region. Those data guarantee that all iterates remain in the region, converge to an existing root, and identify a neighborhood in which the root is unique. It differs from local convergence theory because the root need not be known or assumed to exist before the certificate is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Initial-point inverse, residual, and neighborhood-Lipschitz bounds certify an invariant Newton sequence, existence of its limiting zero, and stated local uniqueness.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A Newton-Kantorovich certificate with \(\beta\gamma\eta\le1/2\) is a canonical sufficient realization of semilocal convergence.
special_cases_latex: For affine \(F\) with nonsingular derivative, the semilocal region may be the whole domain and convergence occurs in one step.
immediate_consequences_latex: The certificate supplies an a priori initialization test without requiring the unknown distance \(\|x_0-x^*\|\).
boundary_notes: A merely local theorem that assumes a regular root and requires \(x_0\) to be sufficiently close is not semilocal in this sense.
Failure of a sufficient certificate does not imply divergence.

notation.meaning: Certified invariant neighborhood containing the Newton sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton Convergence Radii
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two roots of the Kantorovich majorant give a smaller guaranteed convergence ball and a larger uniqueness ball around the initial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the Newton–Kantorovich hypotheses with \(L>0\), \(\eta=\lVert F'(x_0)^{-1}F(x_0)\rVert\), and \(h=L\eta\le\tfrac12\), the roots of the scalar majorant
\[m(t)=\frac{L}{2}t^2-t+\eta\]
are
\[r_- =\frac{1-\sqrt{1-2h}}{L},\qquad r_+=\frac{1+\sqrt{1-2h}}{L}.\]
If \(\overline B(x_0,r_-)\) lies in the derivative-control domain, then \(r_-\) is a guaranteed containment radius for the Newton sequence and its limiting zero. The larger radius \(r_+\) bounds a neighborhood in which that zero is unique, subject to intersection with the domain where the Lipschitz estimate holds.

\(\overline B(x_0,r_-)\) is contained in the problem domain.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kantorovich convergence and uniqueness radii
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Assume a Newton-Kantorovich certificate \((\beta,\gamma,\eta,r)\) at \(x_0\), with \(\alpha=\beta\gamma\eta\le1/2\), for \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit sufficient radii for the classical finite-dimensional Kantorovich theorem; these are certified lower bounds on safe neighborhoods, not exact basin boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inner Newton convergence radius is \[r_-:=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-2\alpha}}{\beta\gamma}.\] When \(\alpha<1/2\), the associated uniqueness radius is \[r_+:=\min\!\left\{r,\frac{1+\sqrt{1-2\alpha}}{\beta\gamma}\right\}.\] Provided \(r\ge r_-\), the Newton iterates beginning at \(x_0\) are defined, remain in the certified region, and converge to a zero \(x^*\in\overline{N(x_0,r_-)}\); that zero is unique in \(N(x_0,r_+)\). Thus \(r_-\) controls initialization and root enclosure, whereas \(r_+\) controls the larger uniqueness neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Kantorovich smallness parameter determines two radii. The smaller radius \(r_-\) encloses the Newton trajectory and its limiting root, provided the available domain is at least that large. Under the strict smallness condition, the larger radius \(r_+\) is a uniqueness radius. These values certify safe neighborhoods but need not equal the true attraction or uniqueness radii of the nonlinear system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_-\) is the certified convergence/root-enclosure radius and \(r_+\) is the certified uniqueness radius under \(\alpha<1/2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The two untruncated scalar roots of the Kantorovich majorant equation are \((1\mp\sqrt{1-2\alpha})/(\beta\gamma)\).
special_cases_latex: At \(\alpha=1/2\), the two scalar radii coincide at \(1/(\beta\gamma)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Increasing either the Jacobian Lipschitz bound \(\gamma\) or inverse bound \(\beta\) generally decreases the certified neighborhood.
boundary_notes: The formulas require separate interpretation when \(\beta\gamma=0\); the affine nonsingular case terminates in one Newton step.
The actual basin of attraction can be much larger than the certified ball.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Globalized Newton convergence framework
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, with Newton model \(m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\), where \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(B_k\) is the Hessian or a safeguarded approximation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth unconstrained deterministic optimization using line-search, modified-Hessian, or trust-region safeguards.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A Newton-type iteration is globalized when it computes a model-based direction or step \(p_k\), applies an acceptance safeguard that may shorten, reject, restrict, or regularize that step, and sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) only after an explicit sufficient-decrease or model-agreement test. It has globalized convergence on an initial level set \(\mathcal L_0=\{x:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}\) when, for every permitted \(x_0\), either it terminates at \(
abla f(x_k)=0\), or its infinite sequence satisfies \(\liminf_{k	o\infty}\|
abla f(x_k)\|=0\); under stronger standard hypotheses the defining conclusion may be strengthened to \(\|
abla f(x_k)\|	o0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globalization augments a Newton model with an acceptance mechanism that controls steps away from a solution. A line search controls step length, while a trust region controls the domain over which the model is trusted. Globalized convergence means that the resulting sequence cannot remain uniformly separated from first-order stationarity, with full gradient convergence available under stronger assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining global guarantee is termination at a stationary point or \(\liminf_k\|\nabla f(x_k)\|=0\), produced by an explicit step-acceptance safeguard.
special_cases_latex: Line-search Newton uses \(s_k=\alpha_kp_k\) with a sufficient-decrease test.
Trust-region Newton restricts \(p_k\) by \(\|p_k\|\le\Delta_k\) and uses actual-to-predicted reduction.
immediate_consequences_latex: Globalization separates far-from-solution reliability from eventual local Newton acceleration.
boundary_notes: Unmodified full-step Newton is not globalized merely because it converges on a particular problem.
Global convergence here means convergence toward stationarity, not guaranteed convergence to a global minimizer.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition on modified Newton matrices used to invoke line-search global-convergence results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence $\{B_k\}$ has the bounded modified factorization property when boundedness of the Hessian sequence implies uniform boundedness of the condition numbers of the modified matrices: $\sup_{k\ge0}\|\nabla^2 f(x_k)\|<\infty\Rightarrow\sup_{k\ge0}\kappa(B_k)<\infty$. Together with the other assumptions of the applicable line-search theory, it is the stated condition used to obtain global convergence.

children.title: Line-Search Newton Globalization

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Newton Globalization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtracking shortens each Newton correction until the squared residual satisfies Armijo decrease; compactness, Lipschitz derivatives, and uniform Jacobian invertibility then force residual convergence to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\lVert F(x)\rVert^2\), and choose \(c\in(0,\tfrac12)\), \(\rho\in(0,1)\), and \(x_0\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(F'(x_k)p_k=-F(x_k)\). Choose the first \(\alpha_k\in\{1,\rho,\rho^2,\ldots\}\) satisfying
\[\phi(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le\phi(x_k)+c\alpha_k\nabla\phi(x_k)^{\mathsf T}p_k,\]
and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). Stop when \(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\le\varepsilon\). If the initial level set is compact, \(F'\) is Lipschitz there, and \(F'(x)^{-1}\) is uniformly bounded there, then backtracking terminates and \(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\to0\).
assumptions_latex: \(F'\) is Lipschitz continuous on a neighborhood of that level set.
\(F'(x)\) is nonsingular there with uniformly bounded inverse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted step decreases \(\phi\), the line search terminates finitely, and \(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo backtracking applied to Newton directions for the squared-residual merit function.
review_flags: The locator must be checked for direct coverage of residual-merit Newton globalization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Line-search globalization of a Newton direction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable. At \(x_k\), let a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(B_k\) define \(B_kp_k=-g_k\), where \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth unconstrained minimization with a descent-producing exact or modified Newton matrix and Armijo-Wolfe step-length control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A line-search Newton globalization chooses \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), where \(g_k^Tp_k<0\) and \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfies an acceptance condition. In the Armijo-Wolfe form, constants \(0<c_1<c_2<1\) are fixed and \[f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_kg_k^Tp_k,\qquad \nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)^Tp_k\ge c_2g_k^Tp_k.\] A backtracking Armijo variant retains the first inequality and selects \(\alpha_k\) from a decreasing trial sequence. The Newton character lies in \(B_k\), while globalization lies in the accepted step length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method first forms a descent direction from an exact or positive-definite modified Newton system, then chooses a step length satisfying sufficient decrease, optionally together with the Wolfe curvature condition. The iteration therefore preserves Newton curvature information while preventing an unacceptable full extrapolation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) with a descent direction and an Armijo or Armijo-Wolfe acceptable step length.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because \(B_k\succ0\), \(g_k^Tp_k=-p_k^TB_kp_k<0\) whenever \(g_k\ne0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\succ0\), then \(p_k\) is the classical Newton direction.
When \(\alpha_k=1\), the accepted update is an unmodified Newton-type step.
immediate_consequences_latex: Trying \(\alpha=1\) first permits eventual recovery of the local fast Newton rate.
boundary_notes: If the unmodified Hessian is indefinite, its Newton direction need not be a descent direction and must be modified or replaced.
Armijo decrease alone does not define how the direction is safeguarded.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Newton Globalization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimize the Newton model inside a radius, accept steps only when actual and predicted reductions agree, and update the radius according to that agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\Delta_0>0\), and \(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\), form \(m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\), where \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\). Compute an approximate minimizer \(p_k\) of \(m_k\) subject to \(\|p\|\leq\Delta_k\), and define \[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+p_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)}.\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\) when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\), and otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Decrease \(\Delta_k\) after poor agreement, retain it after moderate agreement, and permit an increase when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\) and \(\|p_k\|\) is near \(\Delta_k\). Stop when a prescribed stationarity tolerance is met.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable and bounded below on the relevant level set.
Each subproblem step supplies a positive, sufficiently large fraction of the available model decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x_k\}\) is generated by globally safeguarded Newton-model steps whose acceptance and scale are controlled by \(\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained smooth minimization with ratio-based acceptance and trust-radius control.

knowledge_statements.title: Eventual Unmodified Newton Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a nonsingular strict minimizer, standard globalization eventually accepts full Newton steps, after which the classical quadratic local rate is recovered.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable near a limit point \(x_*\), with \(
abla f(x_*)=0\) and \(
abla^2f(x_*)\) positive definite. Suppose \(
abla^2f\) is Lipschitz near \(x_*\), \(x_k	o x_*\), and a line-search or trust-region Newton method tests the exact Newton step \(p_k=-
abla^2f(x_k)^{-1}
abla f(x_k)\). If the globalization acceptance test accepts steps whose model error is asymptotically negligible relative to their predicted decrease, then there exists \(K\) such that every \(k\geq K\) accepts \(p_k\) without damping or truncation. Consequently, the iterates satisfy \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|=O(\|x_k-x_*\|^2)\).
assumptions_latex: The acceptance rule recognizes asymptotically accurate Newton models.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\geq K\), the unmodified Newton step is accepted and \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|=O(\|x_k-x_*\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local recovery of full Newton steps after a successful globalization phase.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Eventual acceptance of full Newton steps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a globalized method generate \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) for a twice differentiable objective, and let \(p_k^N=-\nabla^2f(x_k)^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\) whenever the Hessian is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local phase of a line-search, modified-Hessian, or trust-region Newton method near a nondegenerate minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A globalized Newton sequence enters the eventual unmodified Newton regime when there exists \(K\) such that \[s_k=p_k^N\qquad\text{for every }k\ge K.\] For a line-search method this means simultaneously that the Hessian modification vanishes and \(\alpha_k=1\). For a trust-region method it means that the radius constraint is inactive and the chosen subproblem solution equals \(p_k^N\). Once this identity holds, the tail of the globalized sequence is exactly the classical full-step Newton iteration rather than merely asymptotically similar to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The eventual unmodified regime begins when every sufficiently late accepted step is exactly the ordinary full Newton step. In a line search, the method accepts unit length and applies no Hessian modification. In a trust-region scheme, the Newton step lies inside the region and is selected as the subproblem solution. The global safeguard then remains present algorithmically but no longer changes the iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is \(K\) such that \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\nabla^2f(x_k)^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\) for all \(k\ge K\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For line search, eventual unmodified behavior is \(E_k=0\) and \(\alpha_k=1\) eventually.
For trust regions, it is \(\|p_k^N\|<\Delta_k\) together with selection of the unconstrained model minimizer eventually.
immediate_consequences_latex: Under a locally Lipschitz Hessian and a positive-definite limiting Hessian, the tail inherits Q-quadratic Newton convergence.
boundary_notes: Asymptotic similarity \(\|s_k-p_k^N\|=o(\|p_k^N\|)\) gives superlinear behavior but is weaker than this exact regime.
Repeatedly damped steps with \(\alpha_k\to1\) but \(\alpha_k\ne1\) do not satisfy the definition.

children.title: Newton Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Classical boundaries at which unmodified Newton systems or steps become unreliable.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Classical failure boundary of an unmodified Newton step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For smooth unconstrained minimization, let \(g(x)=\nabla f(x)\), \(H(x)=\nabla^2f(x)\), and define \(p^N(x)=-H(x)^{-1}g(x)\) whenever \(H(x)\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic classification for exact, unmodified, full Newton steps; it identifies loss of classical safeguards rather than asserting divergence in every instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The classical Newton failure boundary is the union of points or steps satisfying at least one of \[\det H(x)=0,\qquad g(x)^Tp^N(x)\ge0,\qquad f(x+p^N(x))\ge f(x),\] together with points where the quadratic model has materially poor agreement with the objective, as measured for positive predicted reduction by \[\rho(x,p^N)=\frac{f(x)-f(x+p^N)}{m_x(0)-m_x(p^N)}\le\eta\] for a prescribed acceptance threshold \(\eta\ge0\). These conditions respectively mark an undefined or ill-conditioned solve, loss of descent, failure of full-step decrease, and extrapolation beyond a reliable model region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unmodified Newton step reaches a classical failure boundary when the Hessian is singular, the computed direction is not descending, the full step fails to decrease the objective, or actual reduction is unacceptable relative to model prediction. The boundary is diagnostic: crossing it removes a standard reason for trusting the full Newton step and motivates damping, Hessian modification, or a trust-region restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The failure set is the stated union of singular-system, non-descent, non-decrease, and poor-model-agreement conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(H(x)\) is nonsingular, \(g(x)^Tp^N(x)=-p^N(x)^TH(x)p^N(x)\); positive definiteness therefore excludes the non-descent boundary.
special_cases_latex: At a stationary point \(g(x)=0\), the zero step is a termination condition rather than a failure.
immediate_consequences_latex: A globalization mechanism can respond by modifying curvature, reducing step length, or restricting step norm.
boundary_notes: The definition does not claim that every point in the set causes divergence.
Ill-conditioning is quantitative and requires a chosen numerical threshold if it is added to the exact singularity condition.

notation.meaning: Quadratic Newton model based at x.

children.title: Singular Newton Local Behavior
children.top_down_role: Rate degradation and instability near singular solution systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Newton Local Behavior
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiple scalar root has singular derivative; ordinary Newton iteration then converges only linearly and becomes increasingly sensitive to perturbations near the root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(m\geq2\), consider \(F(x)=x^m\) with solution \(x_*=0\). For every \(x_k\neq0\), the ordinary Newton update is \[x_{k+1}=x_k-\frac{F(x_k)}{F'(x_k)}=\left(1-\frac1m\right)x_k.\] Hence \(F'(x_*)=0\), the usual nonsingular-Jacobian hypothesis fails, and convergence is only linear with exact factor \((m-1)/m\), rather than quadratic. Moreover, the formal Newton system is singular at \(x_*\), so perturbations or finite-precision errors near the solution can be amplified by division through the small derivative \(F'(x_k)=m x_k^{m-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k=((m-1)/m)^k x_0\), so the convergence order is one and the nonsingular local Newton theory does not apply.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicity-induced loss of quadratic convergence for a singular scalar root.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Newton behavior at a singular solution
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable near a zero \(x^*\), and consider Newton iterates \(x_{k+1}=x_k-F'(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k)\) whenever the inverse exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional root finding near a solution whose limiting Jacobian is singular; the definition classifies observed behavior without assigning a universal rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convergent Newton sequence has singular local behavior at \(x^*\) when \[F(x^*)=0,\qquad \det F'(x^*)=0,\qquad x_k\to x^*,\] while \(F'(x_k)\) remains invertible for the computed iterates. Its local Q-rate is classified by the error ratios: it is Q-linear if \(0<\limsup_k\|e_{k+1}\|/\|e_k\|<1\), Q-superlinear if that ratio tends to zero, and Q-quadratic only if \(\limsup_k\|e_{k+1}\|/\|e_k\|^2<\infty\), where \(e_k=x_k-x^*\). Singular behavior also includes breakdown when some \(F'(x_k)\) is noninvertible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singular Newton behavior occurs when the iteration approaches a root with singular limiting Jacobian. Nearby systems may still be invertible, allowing a convergent sequence whose rate is measured directly from successive errors, or an iterate may encounter an actually singular system and break down. Singularity removes the regular-root hypothesis, so quadratic convergence is not part of the definition and must be established separately for a particular structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining feature is \(F'(x^*)\) singular, with either rate-classified convergence through invertible nearby systems or finite breakdown at a singular Newton system.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For minimization with \(F=\nabla f\), the singularity condition is \(\det\nabla^2f(x^*)=0\).

immediate_consequences_latex: The standard regular-root quadratic-convergence theorem cannot be invoked.
boundary_notes: Singularity alone does not determine a unique convergence rate.

children.title: Non-Descent Newton Directions
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by indefinite or misleading model curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Non-Descent Newton Directions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-definite curvature makes a Newton direction descending; indefinite curvature can instead produce an ascent direction that a descent line search must reject.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable at \(x\), let \(g=
abla f(x)
eq0\), and suppose the nonsingular Hessian \(H=
abla^2f(x)\) defines the Newton direction \(p_N=-H^{-1}g\). Its directional derivative is \[g^Tp_N=-g^TH^{-1}g.\] Thus \(p_N\) is guaranteed to be a strict descent direction when \(H\succ0\), but not when \(H\) is indefinite. For example, with \(H=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1)\) and \(g=(1,0)^T\), one obtains \(p_N=(1,0)^T\) and \(g^Tp_N=1>0\), so every sufficiently small positive step along \(p_N\) increases \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Indefiniteness of \(H\) removes the implication \(g^Tp_N<0\); the Newton direction may be an ascent direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent fails when the Hessian does not give positive curvature along the Newton direction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Non-descent exact Newton direction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable at \(x\), set \(g=\nabla f(x)\) and \(H=\nabla^2f(x)\), and assume \(H\) is nonsingular so that \(p^N=-H^{-1}g\) exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Newton directions in smooth unconstrained minimization; the definition concerns first-order descent of the objective, not solvability alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Newton direction \(p^N\) is a non-descent direction at a nonstationary point \(x\) when \[g\ne0\qquad\text{and}\qquad g^Tp^N\ge0.\] Since \(Hp^N=-g\), this is equivalently \[(p^N)^THp^N\le0.\] Strict inequality \(g^Tp^N>0\) defines an ascent Newton direction, while equality defines a first-order neutral direction. If \(H\succ0\), then \(g^Tp^N=-(p^N)^THp^N<0\), so non-descent can arise only after positive definiteness is lost, although an indefinite Hessian can still produce descent for particular gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton direction is non-descending when its directional derivative is nonnegative. The Newton equation makes this equivalent to nonpositive quadratic curvature along the step. A positive-definite Hessian rules this out, but nonsingularity alone does not: an indefinite Hessian can yield either descent or non-descent depending on the gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(g\ne0\), non-descent is exactly \(g^Tp^N\ge0\), equivalently \((p^N)^THp^N\le0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The strict descent condition is \(g^Tp^N<0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(H\prec0\), every nonzero Newton direction is an ascent direction because \(g^Tp^N>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A standard descent line search cannot use a non-descent Newton direction without modifying or replacing it.
boundary_notes: If \(H\) is singular, the classical Newton direction may be undefined rather than merely non-descending.
At \(g=0\), the zero direction represents stationarity and is excluded from the failure definition.

children.title: Poor-Model Extrapolation
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by taking Newton steps outside the reliable local-model region.

knowledge_statements.title: Poor-Model Extrapolation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even for a smooth strictly convex objective, full Newton steps can diverge when the iterate is outside the neighborhood where the quadratic model is reliable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the strictly convex function \(f(x)=\sqrt{1+x^2}\) on \(\mathbb R\). Since \(f'(x)=x/\sqrt{1+x^2}\) and \(f''(x)=(1+x^2)^{-3/2}>0\), its unique minimizer is \(x_*=0\). Nevertheless, the unglobalized Newton update is \[x_{k+1}=x_k-\frac{f'(x_k)}{f''(x_k)}=-x_k^3.\] If \(|x_0|>1\), then \(|x_{k+1}|=|x_k|^3>|x_k|\), so the iterates alternate signs and diverge in magnitude. The failure occurs despite strict convexity because the full quadratic-model minimizer lies outside the region where the local model predicts the objective reliably.
assumptions_latex: The undamped Newton update is used from \(|x_0|>1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|x_k|=|x_0|^{3^k}\to\infty\), although \(f\) has the unique minimizer \(x_*=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A full Newton step can diverge when used beyond the reliable quadratic-model neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Poor extrapolation of a local Newton model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x\), define \(m_x(p)=f(x)+\nabla f(x)^Tp+\tfrac12p^T Bp\), the predicted reduction \(P(p)=m_x(0)-m_x(p)\), and actual reduction \(A(p)=f(x)-f(x+p)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth unconstrained optimization using a quadratic Newton or quasi-Newton model and a trial step with positive predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed agreement tolerance \(\eta\in[0,1)\), a trial step \(p\) is a poor-model extrapolation when \[P(p)>0\qquad\text{and}\qquad \rho(p):=\frac{A(p)}{P(p)}\le\eta.\] The case \(\rho(p)<0\) is severe poor extrapolation because the objective increases although the model predicts decrease. A scale-free model-error form is \[\frac{|A(p)-P(p)|}{P(p)}=|\rho(p)-1|,\] so a step also has poor agreement when this relative discrepancy exceeds a prescribed tolerance. The term “extrapolation” records that the step has left the region where the local quadratic model is acceptably predictive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A step is poor-model extrapolation when its quadratic model predicts positive reduction but the actual reduction is too small relative to that prediction. The actual-to-predicted ratio provides the formal test. A negative ratio is especially poor because the objective rises. The definition depends on an explicit agreement threshold and does not identify poor agreement merely from a large step norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Poor-model extrapolation is characterized by positive predicted reduction and \(\rho(p)\le\eta\), or equivalently excessive relative disagreement \(|\rho(p)-1|\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(A(p)-P(p)\) is the signed model-reduction error, and \(|A(p)-P(p)|/P(p)=|\rho(p)-1|\).
special_cases_latex: With the exact Hessian and locally Lipschitz Hessian, sufficiently small steps have model error of order \(\|p\|^3\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A trust-region method rejects or restricts such steps and reduces its radius when agreement is sufficiently poor.
boundary_notes: The definition requires \(P(p)>0\); zero predicted reduction needs a separate termination or degeneracy rule.
A low ratio diagnoses model reliability for the particular step, not global inaccuracy of the model.

children.title: Over-Regularized Newton Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Loss of second-order progress when safeguards dominate the Newton model.

knowledge_statements.title: Over-Regularized Newton Stagnation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If regularization grows so quickly that effective step fractions are summable, even a quadratic objective can stagnate at a nonstationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), consider the regularized Newton equation \((1+\lambda_k)p_k=-x_k\) with \(\lambda_k\geq0\), followed by \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\). Then \[x_{k+1}=\frac{\lambda_k}{1+\lambda_k}x_k.\] If \(x_0\neq0\), \(\lambda_k>0\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(1+\lambda_k)^{-1}<\infty\), the infinite product \(\prod_{k=0}^{\infty}\lambda_k/(1+\lambda_k)\) has a positive limit. Consequently, \(x_k\) converges to a nonzero point and \(|f'(x_k)|=|x_k|\not\to0\). Thus safeguards that grow too aggressively can dominate the Newton curvature and cause nonstationary stagnation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotic stagnation caused by dominant Newton regularization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable and let regularized steps satisfy \((H_k+R_k)p_k=-g_k\), where \(H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(R_k\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth unconstrained optimization near a point where the unregularized Hessian is nonsingular; this definition isolates stagnation attributable to a safeguard that does not become asymptotically negligible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An infinite regularized Newton sequence exhibits over-regularized stagnation relative to the full Newton step \(p_k^N=-H_k^{-1}g_k\) when \(g_k\ne0\) eventually and either \[\frac{\|p_k\|}{\|p_k^N\|}\longrightarrow0\] or, for accepted steps \(s_k=\alpha_kp_k\), \[\frac{\|s_k\|}{\|p_k^N\|}\longrightarrow0.\] A sufficient diagnostic of persistent safeguard dominance is that \(\|R_kH_k^{-1}\|\not\to0\); scalar regularization \(R_k=\lambda_kI\) is asymptotically noninterfering only when its effect vanishes relative to the local Hessian. The definition concerns loss of Newton-scale progress, not ordinary convergence caused by \(g_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over-regularized stagnation means that the computed or accepted step becomes negligible compared with the unmodified Newton step even though the gradient has not vanished. The regularization continues to dominate the local Hessian instead of disappearing as the iteration enters a well-conditioned Newton neighborhood. This suppresses the second-order scale of progress and prevents entry into the eventual unmodified Newton regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining stagnation ratio is \(\|s_k\|/\|p_k^N\|\to0\) while \(g_k\ne0\) eventually, with persistent non-negligible \(R_k\) as the associated mechanism.
special_cases_latex: For \((H_k+\lambda_kI)p_k=-g_k\), very large \(\lambda_k\) gives \(p_k\approx-g_k/\lambda_k\), which can be negligible relative to \(p_k^N\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The sequence cannot satisfy \(p_k=p_k^N\) eventually.
Classical local quadratic convergence cannot be inferred while the step ratio tends to zero.
boundary_notes: Small steps caused solely by \(g_k\to0\) are not stagnation under this relative definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximate-solve Newton family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be differentiable, or let \(F=\nabla f\) for smooth minimization. At \(x_k\), denote the linearization by \(J_k=F'(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear equations and optimization; linearized systems may be solved iteratively, truncated, preconditioned, or through matrix-vector products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The approximate-solve Newton family consists of iterations \[x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k,\qquad J_kp_k=-F(x_k)+r_k,\] in which the linear residual \(r_k\) is permitted to be nonzero but is controlled by a prescribed rule, commonly \[\|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|,\qquad 0\le\eta_k<1.\] Membership depends on controlled approximation of the Newton system, not on explicitly forming \(J_k\). Thus iterative truncation, Krylov subspace solves, preconditioning, and matrix-free products \(J_kv\) are allowed when they produce a step satisfying the selected residual, model-reduction, or trust-region accuracy condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate-solve Newton method updates with a step that solves the current linearized Newton equation only to controlled accuracy. The residual may be bounded relative to the nonlinear residual. The definition includes truncated iterative solves, Krylov and preconditioned variants, and matrix-free implementations because none requires an explicit factorization or stored Jacobian, provided the resulting step meets the stated accuracy rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is defined by \(J_kp_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\) with explicitly controlled nonzero residual \(r_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex:
For minimization, \(J_k=
abla^2f(x_k)\), \(F(x_k)=
abla f(x_k)\), and \(r_k=
abla^2f(x_k)p_k+
abla f(x_k)\).
special_cases_latex: Exact Newton is recovered when \(r_k=0\).
Newton-CG and Newton-Krylov methods are members when their truncated steps satisfy the chosen accuracy condition.
immediate_consequences_latex: The forcing sequence can balance linear-solve work against nonlinear convergence speed.
Only derivative actions are required in a matrix-free implementation.
boundary_notes: An arbitrary approximate direction without a stated accuracy or model-reduction condition is not included.
Globalization is a separate property; an approximate solve alone does not guarantee convergence from remote starting points.

notation.meaning: Residual of the approximate linearized solve.
Relative linear-solve tolerance or forcing term.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-controlled inexact Newton iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable and set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth unconstrained minimization with a controlled approximate solution of each Hessian system; globalization and negative-curvature handling are not built into the core definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a forcing sequence \(\{\eta_k\}\subset[0,1)\), an inexact Newton step is any \(p_k\) whose linear residual \[r_k:=H_kp_k+g_k\] satisfies \[\|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|g_k\|.\] The inexact Newton iteration is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\), or \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) when a separate globalization is applied. The forcing term measures required relative accuracy of the inner linear solve: \(\eta_k=0\) gives the exact Newton equation, while larger values allow earlier termination of an iterative solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inexact Newton method computes a step whose Hessian-system residual is at most a chosen fraction of the gradient norm. The fractions \(\eta_k\) form the forcing sequence and control how accurately each inner linear system is solved. Exact Newton is the zero-residual case. A line search or trust region may subsequently globalize the step but is not part of the residual definition itself.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An inexact Newton step is exactly a vector satisfying \(\|H_kp_k+g_k\|\le\eta_k\|g_k\|\) for some \(0\le\eta_k<1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The approximate system can be written \(H_kp_k=-g_k+r_k\) with \(\|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|g_k\|\).
special_cases_latex: \(\eta_k=0\) recovers the exact Newton step when \(H_k\) is nonsingular.
A fixed bound \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1\) is the standard local linear-convergence accuracy regime.
The choice \(\eta_k\to0\) is associated with local superlinear convergence under regularity assumptions.
immediate_consequences_latex: The inner solver can stop as soon as the residual test is met.
The definition applies independently of whether the approximate solve uses CG, another Krylov method, or a direct incomplete solve.
boundary_notes: The residual condition alone does not ensure that \(p_k\) is a descent direction when \(H_k\) is indefinite.
Quadratic convergence requires additional smoothness and a sufficiently fast-decaying forcing sequence.

notation.meaning: Residual in the Newton linear system.
Forcing term controlling relative solve accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Controlled Inexact Newton
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The approximate Newton step must reduce the norm of the linearized equation residual to at most a prescribed fraction of the current nonlinear residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable, and write \(J_k=F'(x_k)\). A step \(s_k\) is a residual-controlled inexact Newton step with forcing term \(\eta_k\in[0,1)\) when there exists a linear-solve residual \(r_k\) satisfying \[J_ks_k=-F(x_k)+r_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|.\] Equivalently, \(\|F(x_k)+J_ks_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\). The next trial iterate is \(x_k+s_k\); the condition controls only the linearized-system residual and does not by itself guarantee acceptance or global convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k\) satisfies \(\|F(x_k)+J_ks_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative residual condition for an approximate solution of the Newton linearization.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the nonlinear residual at the current iterate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-controlled inexact Newton iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable, let \(J(x)=F'(x)\), and let \(x_k\in\mathcal D\). Norms are fixed vector norms and their induced matrix norms.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, deterministic inexact Newton for a smooth square nonlinear system; the definition controls the defect of the linearized Newton equation rather than the error relative to its exact solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \((x_k)\) is generated by a residual-controlled inexact Newton method with forcing sequence \((\eta_k)\) if, for every nonterminal iteration \(k\), a step \(p_k\in\mathbb R^n\) is chosen so that \[r_k^{\mathrm{lin}}:=F(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k,\qquad \|r_k^{\mathrm{lin}}\|\leq \eta_k\|F(x_k)\|,\qquad 0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1,\] and the full local update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\). The scalar \(\eta_k\) is the forcing term and \(r_k^{\mathrm{lin}}\) is the linearized-system residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each nonterminal iterate, the method computes an approximate Newton step whose residual in the linearized equation is no larger than a prescribed fraction of the current nonlinear residual, and then takes the full step. The fractions form the forcing sequence and are uniformly below one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall k:\quad x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k,\qquad \|F(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|,\qquad 0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Introducing \(q_k:=F(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k\), the computed step solves the perturbed Newton equation \[J(x_k)p_k=-F(x_k)+q_k,\qquad \|q_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|.\]
special_cases_latex: When \(\eta_k=0\) and \(J(x_k)\) is nonsingular, \(p_k=-J(x_k)^{-1}F(x_k)\), so the iteration is exact Newton.

For unconstrained minimization, take \(F=
abla f\) and \(J=
abla^2 f\); then the condition is \(\|
abla^2 f(x_k)p_k+
abla f(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Controlled Inexact Newton
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The computed correction must lie within a prescribed relative distance of the exact Newton correction, possibly certified by an a posteriori error estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J_k=F'(x_k)\) be nonsingular and let \(s_k^N=-J_k^{-1}F(x_k)\) denote the exact Newton step. An approximate step \(s_k\) is error-controlled with tolerance \(\theta_k\in[0,1)\) when \[\|s_k-s_k^N\|\leq\theta_k\|s_k^N\|.\] More generally, a computable bound \(E_k\) is a valid error-control certificate when \(\|s_k-s_k^N\|\leq E_k\leq\theta_k\|s_k^N\|\). If the linear-solve residual is \(r_k=F(x_k)+J_ks_k\), then \(s_k-s_k^N=J_k^{-1}r_k\), linking residual control to step-error control through the conditioning of \(J_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|s_k-s_k^N\|\leq\theta_k\|s_k^N\|\), with \(s_k-s_k^N=J_k^{-1}r_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate Newton accuracy expressed as error relative to the exact Newton correction.

notation.meaning: a posteriori upper bound on step error

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Solve-error-controlled inexact Newton iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable. At iteration \(k\), assume \(J_k:=F'(x_k)\) is nonsingular and define the exact Newton step \(p_k^{N}:=-J_k^{-1}F(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear equations with nonsingular linearizations; inexactness is measured directly as step error, not as a linearized residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An error-controlled inexact Newton method chooses, at every nonterminal iteration \(k\), a computed step \(p_k\) satisfying \[e_k:=p_k-p_k^N,\qquad \|e_k\|\leq\xi_k\|p_k^N\|,\qquad 0\leq\xi_k\leq\bar\xi<1,\] and sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\). More generally, an absolute-relative error budget may be used: \[\|p_k-p_k^N\|\leq a_k+\xi_k\|p_k^N\|,\qquad a_k\geq0.\] The canonical relative form is obtained when \(a_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method compares the computed step with the exact solution of the current Newton linear system. Its relative step error must not exceed a prescribed fraction of the exact Newton-step norm; an optional absolute allowance can be added. This is distinct from terminating solely on the linear-system residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall k:\quad x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k,\qquad \|p_k+J_k^{-1}F(x_k)\|\leq\xi_k\|J_k^{-1}F(x_k)\|.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(r_k^{\mathrm{lin}}:=F(x_k)+J_kp_k\), one has the exact identity \[r_k^{\mathrm{lin}}=J_ke_k.\] Hence error control is equivalently \(\|J_k^{-1}r_k^{\mathrm{lin}}\|\leq\xi_k\|p_k^N\|\).
If \(J_k\) is symmetric positive definite, then \[\|e_k\|_{J_k}=\|r_k^{\mathrm{lin}}\|_{J_k^{-1}},\] so energy-norm step-error control equals dual-energy residual control.
special_cases_latex: The choice \(\xi_k=0\) gives the exact Newton step.
A uniform \(\xi_k=\xi<1\) defines fixed relative solve-error accuracy; \(\xi_k\to0\) defines progressively exact step computation.
immediate_consequences_latex: The criterion is sensitive to the norm used for the step space.
Unlike an unpreconditioned residual test, it directly measures the quantity by which the computed update differs from the exact Newton update.
boundary_notes: The definition requires the exact Newton step to exist, although an implementation may estimate its error without explicitly computing that step.
Residual and error tolerances are not uniformly interchangeable when the linearizations become ill-conditioned.
No inspected source precisely presented this named variant with the stated relative step-error criterion.

knowledge_statements.title: Globally Convergent Inexact Newton
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute an inexact Newton direction, then backtrack on the squared-residual merit function; inaccurate non-descent directions are recomputed or regularized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\), choose \(0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\) and compute \(s_k\) satisfying \(\|F(x_k)+J_ks_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\). With merit function \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|^2\), select \(\alpha_k\in\{1,\beta,\beta^2,\ldots\}\), where \(0<\beta<1\), as the first value satisfying \[\phi(x_k+\alpha_ks_k)\leq\phi(x_k)+c\alpha_k\nabla\phi(x_k)^Ts_k,\qquad 0<c<1.\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_ks_k\), and stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|\) meets the prescribed tolerance. If necessary, reject a non-descent \(s_k\) and recompute it with stronger inner accuracy or regularization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update produces monotone merit decrease unless the stopping test holds, providing a globalization mechanism for inexact Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-merit line search applied to residual-controlled inexact Newton directions.

notation.meaning: uniform upper bound on forcing terms
