knowledge_statements.statement_title: Line-search-globalized inexact Newton method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable and twice differentiable wherever a Newton model is formed. Write \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(B_k=\nabla^2 f(x_k)\). Fix \(c_1\in(0,1)\) and a forcing bound \(\bar\eta<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic unconstrained smooth optimization; globalization is expressed by an Armijo-type line search applied to a safeguarded inexact Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A line-search-globalized inexact Newton method computes \(p_k\) with \[\|B_kp_k+g_k\|\leq\eta_k\|g_k\|,\qquad 0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1,\] replaces it by a prescribed descent safeguard when \(g_k^Tp_k\geq0\), and chooses \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) satisfying \[f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\leq f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_kg_k^Tp_k.\] It then sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). A method belongs to this globalized class only when its step-generation and acceptance rules are defined away from a local solution neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method computes an approximate Newton direction, safeguards it if it is not a descent direction, and accepts a possibly shortened step only when a sufficient-decrease condition holds. Thus approximate linear solves are combined with an explicit mechanism intended to obtain progress from nonlocal starting points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k,\quad g_k^Tp_k<0,\quad f(x_{k+1})\leq f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_kg_k^Tp_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A trust-region-globalized member replaces the line search by the model \(m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\), the constraint \(\|p\|\leq\Delta_k\), and acceptance based on the ratio of actual to predicted reduction.
special_cases_latex: If \(\alpha_k=1\) is accepted eventually and no safeguard is invoked, the method locally reduces to a full-step residual-controlled inexact Newton iteration.
When the inner solver is conjugate gradients with negative-curvature truncation, the line-search form becomes line-search Newton-CG.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every accepted nonzero line-search step satisfies strict objective decrease because \(g_k^Tp_k<0\).
The globalization rule is logically separate from the forcing sequence: the former controls outer acceptance, while the latter controls inner linear-system accuracy.
boundary_notes: The definition does not itself assert convergence without standard bounded-level-set, smoothness, and angle or model-decrease hypotheses.
For nonlinear equations, a residual merit function such as \(\tfrac12\|F(x)\|^2\) requires corresponding descent safeguards and is not automatically covered by the optimization Hessian model.
Global convergence means convergence from a prescribed nonlocal domain under additional assumptions, not convergence from every point in \(\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Newton model matrix, here the Hessian at \(x_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditioning-dependent angle and stationarity guarantees for Newton directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded globalization bounds for exact and residual-controlled inexact Newton directions applied to a residual merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\nabla f_k=J_k^T r_k\), with nonsingular \(J_k\). For the exact Newton direction \(p_k=-J_k^{-1}r_k\), \(\cos\theta_k\ge 1/\kappa(J_k)\). For an inexact Newton direction satisfying \(\|r_k+J_kp_k\|\le\eta_k\|r_k\|\), where \(0\le\eta_k\le\eta<1\), one has \(p_k^T\nabla f_k\le-(1-\eta_k^2)\|r_k\|^2/2\) and \(\cos\theta_k\ge(1-\eta)/(2\kappa(J_k))\). Thus, if \(\kappa(J_k)\) is uniformly bounded, both direction families satisfy a uniform positive-angle condition. Together with Zoutendijk summability, this gives \(J_k^T r_k\to0\); if additionally \(\|J_k^{-1}\|\) is uniformly bounded, then \(r_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact and residual-controlled inexact Newton directions are uniformly gradient-related when the Jacobians remain uniformly well conditioned. With Zoutendijk summability this yields stationarity of the residual merit function, and uniformly bounded inverse Jacobians further yield residual convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla f_k=J_k^T r_k\) and every \(J_k\) is nonsingular
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\cos\theta_k\ge\kappa(J_k)^{-1}\) in the exact case and \(\cos\theta_k\ge(1-\eta)/(2\kappa(J_k))\) in the inexact case; hence, under the stated additional assumptions, \(J_k^Tr_k\to0\) and then \(r_k\to0\).\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Forcing-term strategy for inexact Newton solves
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For residual-controlled inexact Newton, let \(R_k(p)=F(x_k)+J(x_k)p\). Let \(\mathcal H_k\) denote the information available before the inner solve at iteration \(k\), including current and previous nonlinear residuals, steps, and model data.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional inexact Newton; the strategy specifies requested relative inner accuracy and is independent of the particular linear solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A forcing-term strategy is a sequence of admissible decision rules \(\Psi_k\) producing \[\eta_k=\Psi_k(\mathcal H_k)\in[0,\bar\eta],\qquad \bar\eta<1,\] together with the inner stopping requirement \[\|R_k(p_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|.\] The rule is fixed if \(\Psi_k\) is a constant, vanishing if its generated sequence satisfies \(\eta_k\to0\), and adaptive if \(\Psi_k\) depends nontrivially on observed outer-iteration data. The strategy concerns the requested tolerance; the attained residual may be smaller.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forcing-term strategy maps information available at each outer iteration to a relative tolerance for the approximate Newton solve. The inner iteration stops only after the linearized residual is at most that tolerance times the current nonlinear residual. Fixed, vanishing, and adaptive schedules are distinguished by how this tolerance is selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\eta_k=\Psi_k(\mathcal H_k)\in[0,\bar\eta],\qquad \|F(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using an absolute inner tolerance \(\epsilon_k:=\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\), the stopping test is \(\|R_k(p_k)\|\leq\epsilon_k\).
special_cases_latex: For optimization, one may use \(\eta_k=\min\{0.5,\sqrt{\|\nabla f(x_k)\|}\}\), giving \(\epsilon_k=\eta_k\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\).
The rule \(\eta_k\equiv\eta\in[0,1)\) requests uniform relative accuracy.
immediate_consequences_latex: The forcing term separates outer convergence requirements from inner-solver implementation.
As \(\eta_k\) decreases, the allowable linearized residual decreases relative to the current nonlinear residual.
boundary_notes: A forcing rule does not specify which Krylov or direct method computes the step.
An attained residual below the requested threshold does not change the forcing term that was requested.
The uniform restriction below one is part of the canonical local convergence regime; schedules reaching or exceeding one require separate analysis.

notation.meaning: Decision rule selecting the forcing term.
Information available when the iteration-\(k\) tolerance is chosen.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Forcing Terms
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently small fixed inner residual tolerance gives local linear convergence, but persistent relative solve error generally prevents superlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable near a root \(x_*\), suppose \(J_*=F'(x_*)\) is nonsingular, and assume \(F'\) is Lipschitz near \(x_*\). Consider inexact Newton steps satisfying \(\|F(x_k)+J_ks_k\|\leq\bar\eta\|F(x_k)\|\) for one fixed \(\bar\eta\in[0,1)\). For \(x_0\) sufficiently close to \(x_*\), and for \(\bar\eta\) sufficiently below one, the iterates \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) converge locally at least linearly. A fixed positive forcing term generally leaves a first-order error contribution and therefore does not, by itself, imply superlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For nearby \(x_0\), \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\leq q\|x_k-x_*\|\) eventually for some \(q\in(0,1)\); superlinear convergence is not guaranteed when \(\bar\eta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local rate under a uniform, nonvanishing relative residual tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-forcing inexact Newton regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable, and let \(p_k\) be an approximate solution of \(J(x_k)p=-F(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform relative-residual accuracy for deterministic smooth inexact Newton iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fixed-forcing inexact Newton regime is specified by one constant \(\eta\in[0,1)\) such that every computed step satisfies \[\|F(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k\|\leq\eta\|F(x_k)\|\qquad\text{for every nonterminal }k.\] Equivalently, the forcing sequence is constant: \(\eta_k\equiv\eta\). The update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\), unless a separately specified globalization mechanism scales or rejects the step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same relative residual tolerance is imposed on every approximate Newton solve. Thus the allowed residual of the linearized system is always a fixed fraction, strictly smaller than one, of the current nonlinear residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists\eta\in[0,1)\ \forall k:\quad \eta_k=\eta,\qquad \|F(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k\|\leq\eta\|F(x_k)\|.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The induced absolute tolerance is iteration dependent even though the forcing term is fixed: \[\epsilon_k=\eta\|F(x_k)\|.\]

For unconstrained minimization, the criterion becomes \[\|
abla^2f(x_k)p_k+
abla f(x_k)\|\leq\eta\|
abla f(x_k)\|.\]
special_cases_latex: The choice \(\eta=0\) requires exact Newton solves.
Any \(0<\eta<1\) permits persistent relative inexactness even as the outer residual tends to zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: The absolute inner tolerance tightens automatically when \(\|F(x_k)\|\) decreases.
The definition supplies a uniform upper bound away from the failure threshold \(\eta=1\).
boundary_notes: Fixed forcing generally characterizes a linear local-rate regime; it does not by itself require the progressively increasing relative accuracy associated with superlinear convergence.
A fixed absolute tolerance \(\epsilon_k\equiv\epsilon\) is not a fixed forcing term because its relative value is \(\epsilon/\|F(x_k)\|\).
Globalized or damped updates require additional acceptance rules.

notation.meaning: Constant relative residual tolerance used at all iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Forcing Terms
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounding the forcing terms below one gives the local convergence regime; driving them to zero yields superlinear convergence, and making them proportional to the nonlinear residual yields quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable near \(x_*\), with \(F(x_*)=0\) and nonsingular \(J_*=F'(x_*)\). Suppose \(F'\) is Lipschitz continuous near \(x_*\). Let \(0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\), and let the inexact Newton iterates satisfy \(J_ks_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\), \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\). For \(x_0\) sufficiently close to \(x_*\), the iterates converge to \(x_*\). If \(\eta_k\to0\), the convergence is superlinear. If, additionally, \(\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|)\), then \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|=O(\|x_k-x_*\|^2)\), so the quadratic Newton rate is retained.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x_*)=0\), \(F'(x_*)\) is nonsingular, and \(F'\) is Lipschitz continuous near \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterates converge locally; \(\eta_k\to0\) implies superlinear convergence, while \(\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|)\) implies quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Superlinear and quadratic local regimes obtained by tightening uniformly bounded inner residual accuracy.

notation.meaning: uniform upper bound on the forcing terms

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing-forcing inexact Newton regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable, and suppose approximate Newton steps satisfy a relative linearized-residual test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progressively tightened relative inner solves for local deterministic inexact Newton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A forcing sequence \((\eta_k)\) is vanishing if \[0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\quad\text{for all }k,\qquad \lim_{k\to\infty}\eta_k=0.\] A vanishing-forcing inexact Newton iteration chooses \(p_k\) satisfying \[\|F(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\] and updates \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\). Vanishing refers to relative linearized-residual tolerance, not necessarily to the absolute number of inner iterations or to monotonicity of \((\eta_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relative tolerance for the Newton linear solve tends to zero while remaining uniformly below one. Consequently, the computed Newton equations become progressively more accurate relative to the current nonlinear residual. The forcing terms need not decrease monotonically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\eta_k\to0,\qquad \|F(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists \(K\) such that \(k\geq K\) implies \[\|F(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k\|\leq\varepsilon\|F(x_k)\|.\]
special_cases_latex: For optimization, \(\eta_k=\min\{0.5,\sqrt{\|\nabla f(x_k)\|}\}\) is vanishing whenever \(\nabla f(x_k)\to0\).
A schedule \(\eta_k=1/(k+2)\) is vanishing independently of observed residuals.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(F(x_k)\to0\), then the allowable absolute linearized residual \(\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\) tends to zero.
Vanishing forcing excludes any positive asymptotic lower bound on the requested relative solve accuracy.
boundary_notes: Vanishing forcing alone does not assert convergence of the outer iterates; local regularity and a suitable starting point or globalization are still required.
The definition does not require \(\eta_{k+1}\leq\eta_k\).
A vanishing absolute tolerance does not imply a vanishing forcing term unless it vanishes faster than \(\|F(x_k)\|\).

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Forcing Terms
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate the preceding linearization error and use it to tighten or relax the next linear solve while enforcing fixed safety bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose constants \(0\leq\eta_{\min}<\eta_{\max}<1\), \(\gamma>0\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1]\). After accepting \(s_{k-1}=x_k-x_{k-1}\), compute the normalized model defect \[d_k=\frac{\|F(x_k)-F(x_{k-1})-J_{k-1}s_{k-1}\|}{\max\{\|F(x_{k-1})\|,\varepsilon\}},\qquad \varepsilon>0.\] Set \(\eta_k=\min\{\eta_{\max},\max\{\eta_{\min},\gamma d_k^{\alpha}\}\}\), then compute \(s_k\) satisfying \(\|F(x_k)+J_ks_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\). Stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|\) meets tolerance. Small observed model defect tightens the inner solve; large defect avoids oversolving an unreliable linearization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next forcing term is selected from observed model disagreement and remains in \([\eta_{\min},\eta_{\max}]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forcing accuracy selected from the preceding nonlinear-model defect.

notation.meaning: normalized defect of the preceding linear model

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adaptive forcing-term rule
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For an inexact Newton iteration, let \(\mathcal H_k\) contain quantities observed before the iteration-\(k\) inner solve, such as \(\|F(x_k)\|\), previous residuals, accepted steps, and discrepancies between nonlinear changes and linear predictions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feedback selection of deterministic relative residual tolerances; no particular inner linear solver is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An adaptive forcing-term rule is a nonconstant feedback map \[\eta_k=\Psi_k(\mathcal H_k),\qquad 0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1,\] followed by the stopping condition \[\|F(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|.\] The dependence on \(\mathcal H_k\) must be causal: \(\eta_k\) may use data available before or during the current inner solve but not future outer iterates. A residual-magnitude rule has the form \(\eta_k=\min\{\eta_{
max},\phi(\|F(x_k)\|)\}\), where \(\phi(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive rule chooses each forcing term from observed nonlinear or model behavior instead of using a predetermined constant sequence. The selected value is uniformly below one and becomes the relative stopping tolerance for the current approximate Newton solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\eta_k=\Psi_k(\mathcal H_k)\in[0,\bar\eta],\qquad \|F(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: In optimization, a standard residual-magnitude instance is \[\eta_k=\min\{0.5,\sqrt{\|\nabla f(x_k)\|}\},\qquad \epsilon_k=\eta_k\|\nabla f(x_k)\|.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(\Psi_k\equiv\eta\), the rule degenerates to fixed forcing and is not nontrivially adaptive.
If the adaptive output satisfies \(\eta_k\to0\), it is simultaneously an adaptive and vanishing forcing strategy.
immediate_consequences_latex: The requested inner accuracy can loosen when the current Newton model is uninformative and tighten as the outer residual approaches zero.
Capping by \(\bar\eta<1\) preserves the uniform relative-residual restriction even when the uncapped feedback value is large.
boundary_notes: The inspected source explicitly supports residual-magnitude-dependent choices but not every possible model-discrepancy feedback formula.
Adaptivity does not by itself guarantee that the generated forcing terms vanish.
A rule depending on unavailable future quantities is not an admissible adaptive strategy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure and oversolving boundaries for inner accuracy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\rho_k:=\|F(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k\|/\|F(x_k)\|\) whenever \(F(x_k)\neq0\). Let \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\) denote the requested forcing term and \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{rate}}\) an accuracy scale required by a specified target local rate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic definition for residual-controlled inexact Newton; it separates loss of the basic relative-residual contraction certificate from unnecessary inner accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The residual-control failure boundary is \(\rho_k=1\). An iteration is under-solved relative to the canonical inexact-Newton condition when \(\rho_k\geq1\), because its linearized residual is not strictly smaller than the unsolved residual \(\|F(x_k)\|\). Relative to a declared target-rate budget \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{rate}}>0\), it is over-solved when \[\rho_k=o(\eta_k^{\mathrm{rate}})\] while the additional inner accuracy is not required by the outer-rate specification. The admissible balanced region is \[0\leq\rho_k\leq\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\leq\bar\eta<1\] with \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{req}}\) chosen at the scale required by the target outer regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The principal failure boundary occurs when the computed linearized residual is as large as the original right-hand side: relative residual one. Values at or above this boundary lose the standard strict relative reduction. At the opposite extreme, solving much more accurately than the tolerance needed for the requested outer rate is classified as oversolving.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\rho_k:=\frac{\|F(x_k)+J(x_k)p_k\|}{\|F(x_k)\|};\quad \rho_k\geq1\ \text{is the under-solving boundary, while }\rho_k=o(\eta_k^{\mathrm{rate}})\ \text{is the target-relative oversolving region}.\]
special_cases_latex: For a fixed-forcing target \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{rate}}\equiv\eta\), persistent \(\rho_k\ll\eta\) represents accuracy beyond the specified uniform regime.
For quadratic-rate recovery, the relevant comparison scale is commonly \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{rate}}=O(\|F(x_k)\|)\), not a fixed constant.
immediate_consequences_latex: The boundary depends on relative, not absolute, residual size.
A step can satisfy the requested inner tolerance and still be computationally over-solved if its attained residual is far smaller than necessary.
boundary_notes: This is a diagnostic classification, not a convergence theorem or a machine-independent work-complexity criterion.
Actual work imbalance depends on the inner solver, conditioning, preconditioning, and stopping-test cost.
No inspected source gave this exact named two-sided failure-boundary definition.

notation.meaning: Accuracy scale sufficient for a declared target outer rate.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure and oversolving boundaries for inner accuracy
Oversolving Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forcing the linear residual below the nonlinear Taylor error still yields only quadratic local convergence, so the extra inner accuracy is asymptotically unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) have a root \(x_*\), with Lipschitz-continuous Jacobian \(J\) near \(x_*\) and nonsingular \(J(x_*)\). Suppose \(J(x_k)s_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), and \(\|r_k\|\leq \eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\). If \(\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|^q)\) for some \(q>1\), then locally
\[
\|F(x_{k+1})\|=O(\|F(x_k)\|^2)+O(\|F(x_k)\|^{q+1})=O(\|F(x_k)\|^2).
\]
Thus reducing the linear residual below order \(\|F(x_k)\|^2\) does not improve the generic quadratic convergence order under merely Lipschitz Jacobian regularity.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable near \(x_*\), and \(J\) is locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|^q),\ q>1\Longrightarrow \|F(x_{k+1})\|=O(\|F(x_k)\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy beyond the nonlinear-model error cannot improve the generic local quadratic order.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the nonlinear residual map F at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Undersolving Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If admissible relative solve errors do not vanish, even a linear residual equation can produce only linear outer convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy the usual local Newton regularity conditions, and let \(J(x_k)s_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\) with \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\). If \(\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\), local convergence is guaranteed but need not be superlinear. Sharpness already occurs for \(F(x)=x\): choosing \(r_k=\bar\eta x_k\) gives \(s_k=-(1-\bar\eta)x_k\) and hence \(x_{k+1}=\bar\eta x_k\). Therefore any regime allowing \(\limsup_k\eta_k>0\) admits problems and admissible inner solves whose asymptotic rate is only linear.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable with locally Lipschitz Jacobian near a regular root.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup_k\eta_k>0\) does not guarantee superlinear convergence; \(F(x)=x\) realizes a linear rate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A forcing term bounded away from zero permits only linear convergence in general.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Accuracy Balance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the relative forcing term proportional to the current nonlinear residual so linear-solve error and Taylor error are both second order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an inexact Newton step \(J(x_k)s_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\), Taylor expansion under a locally Lipschitz Jacobian gives
\[
\|F(x_{k+1})\|\leq C_1\|F(x_k)\|^2+C_2\|r_k\|
\]
for all sufficiently large \(k\). Imposing \(\|r_k\|=O(\|F(x_k)\|^2)\), equivalently \(\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|)\) under \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\), makes the inner-solve contribution and nonlinear Taylor remainder have the same asymptotic order. This is the least stringent standard forcing scale that preserves the generic quadratic local rate.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) has a regular root and a locally Lipschitz Jacobian.
The iterates and inexact steps remain in a sufficiently small neighborhood of the root.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|)\Longrightarrow \|F(x_{k+1})\|=O(\|F(x_k)\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The balanced forcing scale matches linear-solve error to Newton’s nonlinear truncation error.

notation.meaning: Positive local constants independent of k.

knowledge_statements.title: Rate-Loss Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forcing term of residual-power alpha gives guaranteed order min(2,1+alpha), with boundaries at alpha zero and one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume the local inexact-Newton residual estimate
\[
\|F(x_{k+1})\|\leq C_1\|F(x_k)\|^2+C_2\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|
\]
and let \(\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|^\alpha)\) for \(\alpha\geq0\). Then
\[
\|F(x_{k+1})\|=O\!\left(\|F(x_k)\|^{\min\{2,1+\alpha\}}\right).
\]
Consequently \(\alpha=0\) permits only linear convergence, \(0<\alpha<1\) yields order at least \(1+\alpha\), and \(\alpha\geq1\) recovers quadratic order. These boundaries are generic guarantees; special problem structure may produce faster behavior.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) has a regular root and locally Lipschitz Jacobian.
The stated local residual recurrence holds for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|^\alpha)\Longrightarrow q\geq\min\{2,1+\alpha\}\) for the guaranteed residual convergence order \(q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-law forcing terms determine the transition from linear through superlinear to quadratic convergence.

notation.meaning: Relative residual tolerance for the Newton system.
Power governing decay of the forcing term.
Guaranteed local order measured in nonlinear residual norm.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Forcing-term convergence classification
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable near a strict local minimizer \(x^*\), with \(
abla^2f(x^*)\) positive definite. Let full inexact Newton steps satisfy \(\|
abla^2f(x_k)p_k+
abla f(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|
abla f(x_k)\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local full-step deterministic inexact Newton for smooth unconstrained minimization; this record defines the rate-classification family rather than asserting a new theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inexact-Newton forcing-term convergence family is the classification of admissible forcing sequences by the asymptotic relation between \(\eta_k\) and the current first-order residual: \[(i)\ \sup_k\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1;\qquad (ii)\ \eta_k\to0;\qquad (iii)\ \eta_k=O(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|).\] Under the corresponding local regularity hypotheses, these classes are associated respectively with local linear convergence, superlinear convergence, and recovery of quadratic convergence. The third class is a quantified subclass of the second whenever \(\nabla f(x_k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This convergence family organizes forcing sequences into three nested accuracy regimes. A uniform bound below one corresponds to the local linear regime; forcing terms tending to zero correspond to the superlinear regime; and forcing terms no larger than a constant multiple of the gradient norm correspond, with a Lipschitz Hessian, to quadratic-rate recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\Rightarrow\text{linear regime},\qquad \eta_k\to0\Rightarrow\text{superlinear regime},\qquad \eta_k=O(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|)\Rightarrow\text{quadratic regime under Lipschitz Hessian regularity}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For nonlinear equations, replace \(\nabla f(x_k)\) by \(F(x_k)\) and \(\nabla^2f(x_k)\) by \(J(x_k)\); the three forcing classes are unchanged in form.
special_cases_latex: The schedule \(\eta_k=\min\{0.5,\sqrt{\|\nabla f(x_k)\|}\}\) lies in the superlinear class near stationarity.
The schedule \(\eta_k=\min\{0.5,\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\}\) lies in the quadratic-recovery class.
immediate_consequences_latex: The rate classification is determined by asymptotic forcing behavior, not by the identity of the inner linear solver.
The quadratic forcing class implies vanishing forcing along any convergent sequence with \(\nabla f(x_k)\to0\).
boundary_notes: The classification assumes eventual full steps; globalization may alter the pre-asymptotic behavior.
Positive definiteness or nonsingularity of the limiting derivative and an appropriate local starting point remain essential.
The Lipschitz-Hessian requirement belongs specifically to the quadratic-rate association.

notation.meaning: Forcing terms bounded by a constant multiple of the gradient norm eventually.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Inexact-Newton Rate Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform relative residual tolerance strictly below one gives local q-linear convergence of the nonlinear residual and R-linear convergence of the iterates from a sufficiently close initial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable near \(x_*\), where \(F(x_*)=0\), and suppose \(J(x_*)\) is nonsingular and \(J\) is locally Lipschitz. For \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), require
\[
J(x_k)s_k=-F(x_k)+r_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|,
\]
where \(0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\). If \(x_0\) is sufficiently close to \(x_*\), then the iterates are well defined and converge to \(x_*\). Moreover, for every \(q\in(\bar\eta,1)\), there is \(k_0\) such that
\[
\|F(x_{k+1})\|\leq q\|F(x_k)\|\qquad(k\geq k_0).
\]
Consequently, \(F(x_k)\) converges q-linearly to zero and \(x_k\) converges R-linearly to \(x_*\).
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable and its Jacobian is locally Lipschitz near \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(q\in(\bar\eta,1)\), eventually \(\|F(x_{k+1})\|\leq q\|F(x_k)\|\); hence \(F(x_k)\to0\) q-linearly and \(x_k\to x_*\) R-linearly.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local q-linear residual convergence and R-linear iterate convergence under uniformly bounded relative Newton-system residuals.

notation.meaning: An eventual residual contraction factor strictly between the forcing bound and one.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear local rate regime for inexact Newton
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable near a minimizer \(x^*\), with \(H_*:=\nabla^2f(x^*)\) positive definite. Let \(p_k\) satisfy the inexact Newton residual condition and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local full-step smooth unconstrained optimization with uniformly controlled relative linear-solve residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linear inexact-Newton rate regime consists of forcing sequences satisfying \[0\leq\eta_k\leq\eta<1\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }k,\] together with the local error contraction \[\|H_*(x_{k+1}-x^*)\|\leq\widehat\eta\,\|H_*(x_k-x^*)\|,\qquad \eta<\widehat\eta<1.\] Thus the defining rate is Q-linear in the equivalent \(H_*\)-scaled norm, while the inner solves are required only to maintain a uniform relative residual bound below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This regime uses forcing terms uniformly bounded away from one. Near a regular minimizer and with full steps, the errors contract by a fixed factor smaller than one in the Hessian-scaled norm, which is the local Q-linear convergence regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sup_{k\geq K}\eta_k\leq\eta<1,\qquad \|H_*(x_{k+1}-x^*)\|\leq\widehat\eta\|H_*(x_k-x^*)\|\quad(\eta<\widehat\eta<1).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because \(H_*\) is nonsingular, \(\|H_*(x-x^*)\|\) is locally equivalent to \(\|x-x^*\|\); hence the displayed contraction represents Q-linear convergence in an equivalent norm.
special_cases_latex: A fixed forcing term \(\eta_k\equiv\eta<1\) belongs to this regime.
Exact Newton, \(\eta_k=0\), satisfies the uniform bound but normally lies in a stronger rate regime under stronger smoothness.
immediate_consequences_latex: Persistent nonvanishing forcing is permitted.
The definition supplies a uniform asymptotic contraction factor but does not specify the number of inner iterations.
boundary_notes: The condition \(\eta_k<1\) pointwise without a uniform margin below one is weaker than this regime.
The result is local and assumes the starting point is sufficiently near \(x^*\).
Damped steps may require a separate argument until unit steps are accepted.

knowledge_statements.title: Superlinear Inexact-Newton Rate Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the relative linear-solve residual tends to zero, the locally convergent inexact Newton iteration becomes q-superlinear.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable near a regular root \(x_*\), and assume that \(J\) is locally Lipschitz. Let
\[
J(x_k)s_k=-F(x_k)+r_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k,
\]
with \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\), \(0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\), and \(\eta_k\to0\). For every sufficiently close \(x_0\), the iterates converge to \(x_*\), and
\[
\frac{\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|}{\|x_k-x_*\|}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus progressively more accurate relative solves recover q-superlinear convergence, without requiring the stronger quadratic forcing scale.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable with locally Lipschitz Jacobian near \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|}{\|x_k-x_*\|}=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing relative Newton-system residuals yield local q-superlinear convergence.

Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable near a minimizer \(x^*\), with \(

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The superlinear inexact-Newton rate regime is defined by a convergent iterate sequence \(x_k\to x^*\) and a vanishing forcing sequence \[\eta_k\to0.\] Its rate property is \[\frac{\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|}{\|x_k-x^*\|}\to0,\] equivalently in any fixed norm on \(\mathbb R^n\). In residual form, the associated asymptotic relation is \[\frac{\|\nabla f(x_{k+1})\|}{\|\nabla f(x_k)\|}\to0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regime requires forcing terms to tend to zero, so approximate Newton solves become relatively more accurate. For a convergent full-step sequence near a regular minimizer, successive errors have a ratio tending to zero, which is Q-superlinear convergence.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under local nonsingularity of the Hessian, Q-superlinear convergence of \((x_k)\) is equivalent to Q-superlinear decay of \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\).
special_cases_latex: The schedule \(\eta_k=\min\{0.5,\sqrt{\|\nabla f(x_k)\|}\}\) enters this regime when \(\nabla f(x_k)\to0\).
Quadratic convergence is a stronger special case of superlinear convergence.

The asymptotic contraction becomes arbitrarily stronger than any prescribed fixed linear factor.

The definition excludes merely R-superlinear descriptions unless they also yield the displayed Q-superlinear ratio.
Globalization must eventually permit the local full-step behavior for this formulation to apply.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Inexact-Newton Rate Recovery
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic convergence is recovered when the relative forcing term is at most proportional to the current nonlinear residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) have a regular root \(x_*\), and suppose its Jacobian is Lipschitz continuous near \(x_*\). Consider
\[
J(x_k)s_k=-F(x_k)+r_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k,
\]
where \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\). If \(x_0\) is sufficiently close to \(x_*\) and \(\eta_k\leq C\|F(x_k)\|\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), then there is a constant \(M>0\) such that
\[
\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\leq M\|x_k-x_*\|^2
\]
for all sufficiently large \(k\). Hence the inexact iteration converges q-quadratically.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable with Lipschitz Jacobian near \(x_*\).
\(\eta_k\leq C\|F(x_k)\|\) eventually, and \(x_0\) is sufficiently close.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\leq M\|x_k-x_*\|^2\) eventually.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-proportional forcing preserves the classical local quadratic Newton rate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic-rate recovery by matched forcing accuracy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) have a Lipschitz-continuous Hessian near a minimizer \(x^*\), with \(\nabla^2f(x^*)\) positive definite. Let \(x_k\to x^*\) by full inexact Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local deterministic smooth optimization; inner residual accuracy is matched to the current first-order residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The quadratic inexact-Newton rate-recovery regime consists of forcing sequences satisfying \[\eta_k=O(\|
abla f(x_k)\|),\] meaning that there exist \(C>0\) and \(K\) such that \(\eta_k\leq C\|
abla f(x_k)\|\) for all \(k\geq K\). With the residual test \[\|
abla^2f(x_k)p_k+
abla f(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|
abla f(x_k)\|,\] the defining recovered rate is \[\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\leq C_q\|x_k-x^*\|^2\] for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To preserve the classical quadratic Newton rate, the relative linear-solve tolerance must be no larger than a constant multiple of the current gradient norm. With a Lipschitz Hessian and a regular minimizer, the resulting full-step errors are bounded by a constant times the square of the preceding errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\eta_k\leq C\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \|x_{k+1}-x^*\|\leq C_q\|x_k-x^*\|^2\quad\text{eventually}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For nonlinear equations, the matched condition is \(\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|)\), with a Lipschitz Jacobian near a nonsingular root.

The residual allowance is then second order: \[\|
abla^2f(x_k)p_k+
abla f(x_k)\|=O(\|
abla f(x_k)\|^2).\]
special_cases_latex: The choice \(\eta_k=\min\{0.5,\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\}\) satisfies the matched forcing condition near stationarity.
Exact Newton, \(\eta_k=0\), is contained in this regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: The matched forcing condition implies \(\eta_k\to0\) along a sequence with \(\nabla f(x_k)\to0\).
Quadratic-rate recovery requires greater relative inner accuracy than generic vanishing forcing.
boundary_notes: A merely vanishing forcing sequence can yield superlinear convergence without satisfying the quadratic matching condition.
Lipschitz continuity of the Hessian is part of the stated regime.
The conclusion is local and assumes eventual full steps.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coupled function, derivative, and solve-error budget
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) have Jacobian \(J_k=F'(x_k)\). Suppose an implementation uses approximate data \(\widetilde F_k\), an approximate Jacobian \(B_k\), and a step \(p_k\) whose computed linear residual is \(s_k:=\widetilde F_k+B_kp_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear equations with simultaneous deterministic errors in function data, derivative data, and the inner linear solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coupled inexactness budget consists of nonnegative allocations \(\eta_k^F,\eta_k^J,\eta_k^S\) satisfying \[\eta_k^F+\eta_k^J+\eta_k^S\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1,\] and the component bounds \[\|F(x_k)-\widetilde F_k\|\leq\eta_k^F\|F(x_k)\|,\] \[\|(J_k-B_k)p_k\|\leq\eta_k^J\|F(x_k)\|,\qquad \|\widetilde F_k+B_kp_k\|\leq\eta_k^S\|F(x_k)\|.\] The update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\). The allocations are coupled because their sum controls the defect in the exact Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The total admissible inexactness is divided among inaccurate function values, inaccurate derivatives acting on the computed step, and incomplete solution of the approximate linear system. Each contribution is normalized by the exact nonlinear residual, and their allocated fractions must fit within one overall forcing budget below one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|F(x_k)+J_kp_k\|\leq(\eta_k^F+\eta_k^J+\eta_k^S)\|F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The exact Newton defect decomposes algebraically as \[F(x_k)+J_kp_k=(F(x_k)-\widetilde F_k)+(J_k-B_k)p_k+s_k.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(\eta_k^F=\eta_k^J=0\), the definition reduces to ordinary residual-controlled inexact Newton.
If \(\eta_k^S=0\), the approximate linear system is solved exactly but data and derivative errors may remain.
immediate_consequences_latex: Tightening one component cannot compensate for another component whose allocation already exceeds the total budget.
Rate-oriented schedules can require the total budget \(\eta_k\) to vanish or to be proportional to \(\|F(x_k)\|\).
boundary_notes: The derivative error is controlled only in the computed-step direction, not necessarily in the full operator norm.
Stochastic high-probability or expectation budgets require a separate probabilistic formulation.
No inspected source supplied this exact three-way coupled budget and its local convergence scope.

notation.meaning: Approximate Jacobian used in the computed linear system.
Function, derivative, and linear-solve budget allocations.

review_flags: The decomposition is mathematically explicit, but an authoritative source matching the exact combined budget and convergence scope was not located.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled function, derivative, and solve-error budget
Function-Data Inexactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive function error enters the exact Newton residual without attenuation and must be bounded relative to the true nonlinear residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the available function data be \(\widetilde F_k=F(x_k)+\delta f_k\), and suppose a step is computed from \(B_ks_k=-\widetilde F_k+\rho_k\). Relative to the exact Jacobian \(J_k=J(x_k)\), the exact Newton-equation residual is
\[
d_k:=J_ks_k+F(x_k)=\rho_k-\delta f_k-(B_k-J_k)s_k.
\]
The function-data component is therefore acceptable at forcing level \(\eta_k^{f}\) when
\[
\|\delta f_k\|\leq\eta_k^{f}\|F(x_k)\|.
\]
If this is the only inexactness, the step satisfies the standard inexact-Newton condition with forcing term \(\eta_k=\eta_k^{f}\).
assumptions_latex: \(F(x_k)\), \(J(x_k)\), and the computed step are defined in a common finite-dimensional normed space.
Function data have the additive-error form \(\widetilde F_k=F(x_k)+\delta f_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k=J_k\) and \(\rho_k=0\Longrightarrow \|J_ks_k+F(x_k)\|=\|\delta f_k\|\leq\eta_k^{f}\|F(x_k)\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive function-evaluation error contributes directly to the effective Newton residual.

notation.meaning: Jacobian approximation used in the computed system.
Residual of the computed linear system.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic decomposition and isolated function-error condition are internally correct and fit the condition leaf, but no source is supplied for the coupled perturbation model or its interpretation as an inexact-Newton budget. An authoritative source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Data Inexactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative error affects inexact Newton convergence through the product of the Jacobian error and the computed step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_k=J(x_k)+E_k\), and suppose \(B_ks_k=-F(x_k)+\rho_k\). Then the residual measured in the exact Newton equation is
\[
d_k:=J(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)=\rho_k-E_ks_k.
\]
Accordingly, derivative-data inexactness is acceptable at relative level \(\eta_k^{J}\) when
\[
\|E_ks_k\|\leq\eta_k^{J}\|F(x_k)\|.
\]
The stronger operator-norm condition \(\|E_k\|\,\|s_k\|\leq\eta_k^{J}\|F(x_k)\|\) is sufficient. If \(\rho_k=0\), either condition makes the approximate-Jacobian step an inexact Newton step with forcing term at most \(\eta_k^{J}\).
assumptions_latex: \(B_k=J(x_k)+E_k\), and the displayed approximate system is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k=0\) and \(\|E_ks_k\|\leq\eta_k^{J}\|F(x_k)\|\Longrightarrow \|J(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k^{J}\|F(x_k)\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jacobian approximation error matters through its action on the computed step.

notation.meaning: Derivative-data error B_k minus the exact Jacobian.
Residual in the exact Newton equation.
Relative budget assigned to derivative error.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The exact-equation residual identity and derivative-action bound are mathematically consistent and the condition kind fits the leaf. However, the record has no citation supporting this perturbation model or its forcing-term interpretation. A specifically located authoritative source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Solve Inexactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear-solve inexactness is measured by the residual of the computed Newton system, scaled against the true nonlinear residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given function data \(\widetilde F_k\) and a system matrix \(B_k\), define the computed linear residual by
\[
\rho_k:=B_ks_k+\widetilde F_k.
\]
A relative linear-solve budget \(\eta_k^{L}\) requires
\[
\|\rho_k\|\leq\eta_k^{L}\|F(x_k)\|.
\]
When \(\widetilde F_k=F(x_k)\) and \(B_k=J(x_k)\), this is exactly the standard inexact-Newton forcing condition. With additional data errors, \(\rho_k\) remains one additive component of the exact-equation residual \(J(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)\), so its budget must be combined with the function- and derivative-data budgets.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k\), \(s_k\), and \(\widetilde F_k\) are represented in compatible normed spaces.
The true residual norm \(\|F(x_k)\|\) is available for defining the relative budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k=J(x_k)\) and \(\widetilde F_k=F(x_k)\Longrightarrow \|J(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\eta_k^{L}\|F(x_k)\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The computed linear-system residual is the direct inner-solve contribution to inexactness.

notation.meaning: Residual of the computed linear system.
Matrix used for the Newton-system solve.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The cited inexact-Newton section can provisionally support the standard exact-data residual condition, but the statement also asserts how the computed residual participates in a broader function/derivative/solve perturbation model. That extension is not supported by the supplied locator, so a specifically located source for the coupled model is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Error Budgets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The effective forcing term is bounded by the sum of function, derivative-action, and linear-solve error budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(\widetilde F_k=F(x_k)+\delta f_k\), \(B_k=J(x_k)+E_k\), and \(B_ks_k=-\widetilde F_k+\rho_k\). Then
\[
J(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)=\rho_k-\delta f_k-E_ks_k.
\]
Let nonnegative component budgets satisfy
\[
\|\delta f_k\|\leq\eta_k^{f}\|F(x_k)\|,\quad
\|E_ks_k\|\leq\eta_k^{J}\|F(x_k)\|,\quad
\|\rho_k\|\leq\eta_k^{L}\|F(x_k)\|.
\]
By the triangle inequality, the computed step satisfies the standard forcing condition with \(\eta_k=\eta_k^{f}+\eta_k^{J}+\eta_k^{L}\). Thus convergence requirements apply to the sum of the component budgets, not to any component alone.
assumptions_latex: All perturbations are measured in a common compatible norm.
The approximate data and system obey the displayed additive perturbation model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function, derivative, and solve errors share one effective inexact-Newton forcing budget.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The displayed identity and triangle-inequality aggregation are internally correct and the condition kind matches the leaf. Nevertheless, no source supports the adopted additive perturbation model or its use as a convergence budget. A specifically located authoritative reference is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Rate-Recovery Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear, superlinear, and quadratic recovery require the total error budget respectively to stay below one, vanish, or scale with the nonlinear residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the additive perturbation model, define
\[
\widehat\eta_k:=\eta_k^{f}+\eta_k^{J}+\eta_k^{L},
\]
so that \(\|J(x_k)s_k+F(x_k)\|\leq\widehat\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\). Near a regular root with locally Lipschitz Jacobian, a uniform bound \(\widehat\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\) gives the linear regime, \(\widehat\eta_k\to0\) gives the superlinear regime, and \(\widehat\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|)\) gives the quadratic regime. Failure of the corresponding aggregate condition prevents that rate from being guaranteed, even when two of the three component errors are asymptotically negligible.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) has a regular root and locally Lipschitz Jacobian.
The component errors satisfy the coupled residual bound with nonnegative budgets.
The initial iterate is sufficiently close to the root.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\), \(\widehat\eta_k\to0\), and \(\widehat\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|)\) are respectively the standard linear, superlinear, and quadratic rate thresholds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The aggregate effective residual, rather than individual error components, determines the recovered local rate.

notation.meaning: Fixed upper bound strictly below one.
Regular root of the nonlinear system.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The thresholds are consistent with standard inexact-Newton theory once the aggregate residual bound is established, and failure_boundary is the appropriate content kind. No source, however, supports the coupled aggregate model or the asserted rate-recovery and non-guarantee boundaries. A specifically located authoritative source is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Truncated Newton method for unconstrained optimization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable, with \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\). The Newton system is \(B_kp=-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-scale deterministic smooth unconstrained optimization; the Newton system is solved only approximately by an iterative linear method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A truncated Newton method computes \(p_k\) by starting an iterative solver for \[B_kp=-g_k\] and terminating it before exact solution when a prescribed event occurs, such as \[\|B_kp_k+g_k\|\leq\eta_k\|g_k\|,\qquad d_j^TB_kd_j\leq0,\] or, in a trust-region variant, \(\|p\|=\Delta_k\). The returned \(p_k\) is then globalized by a line search or trust-region acceptance rule, producing \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) or an accepted trust-region update. When conjugate gradients supplies the inner iterates, the method is Newton-CG.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated Newton method does not factor and solve the Newton system exactly. It runs an iterative linear solver and stops when sufficient residual accuracy, nonpositive curvature, or a trust-region boundary is encountered. The approximate step is then handled by an outer globalization mechanism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p_k\in\{\text{inner iterative approximations to }B_kp=-g_k\},\quad \text{terminated by residual, curvature, or trust-region criteria}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For positive-definite \(B_k\), truncated CG approximately minimizes \[q_k(p)=g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\] over the current Krylov subspace.
The line-search Newton-CG method is also called a truncated Newton method.
special_cases_latex: Residual-only truncation near a positive-definite solution yields the standard inexact Newton condition.
Negative-curvature truncation returns an iterate before CG attempts to solve an indefinite Newton system as though it were positive definite.
immediate_consequences_latex: The method can be implemented using Hessian-vector products without forming \(B_k\) explicitly.
The amount of inner work is controlled by the truncation rule rather than by an exact factorization requirement.
boundary_notes: Truncation is not synonymous with a fixed number of inner iterations.
Without a descent or trust-region safeguard, an indefinite Hessian may produce an unsuitable outer step.
The definition concerns smooth unconstrained optimization; constrained truncated-Newton methods require additional subproblem structure.

notation.meaning: Trust-region radius when a trust-region truncation is used.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-specific failure boundary motivating trust-region control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When $B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)$ is nearly singular, the line-search Newton--CG direction can be excessively long and of poor quality, requiring many function evaluations in the line search while yielding only a small reduction in $f$. Step normalization or a positive threshold in place of the test $d_j^TB_kd_j\leq0$ may alleviate the problem, but suitable rules are difficult to choose and may undermine rapid Newton convergence when the pure Newton step is well scaled. Trust-region Newton--CG handles this regime more effectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nearly singular Hessian can produce an excessively long, poor Newton–CG direction, leading to an expensive line search and little objective decrease. Normalization and thresholded-curvature remedies are difficult to tune and may damage fast Newton behavior in well-scaled cases; the source therefore prefers trust-region Newton–CG for this regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Line-search Newton--CG may be inefficient in this regime, and trust-region control is the preferred remedy stated by the source.}

abla f_k$, and $d_0=-r_0$. For $j=0,1,\ldots$, if $d_j^TB_kd_j\leq0$, return $p_k=-
abla f_k$ when $j=0$ and $p_k=z_j$ otherwise. If the curvature is positive, set $a_j=(r_j^Tr_j)/(d_j^TB_kd_j)$, $z_{j+1}=z_j+a_jd_j$, and $r_{j+1}=r_j+a_jB_kd_j$. For a nonstationary iterate, the adaptation returns a descent direction. The stated forcing sequence targets superlinear convergence, while admissible unit steps preserve the fast local Newton behavior under the surrounding local theory.

\alpha_k=1\text{ is used whenever it satisfies the acceptance criteria}

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Newton-CG
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately solve the Newton equation by truncated CG, safeguard descent, and backtrack until the Armijo decrease condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and apply CG to \(H_kp=-g_k\), using only products \(H_kv\). Stop when \(\|H_kp+g_k\|\leq\eta_k\|g_k\|\), a prescribed iteration limit is reached, or nonpositive curvature \(d^\top H_kd\leq0\) is detected. Let \(p_k\) be the accepted CG iterate or a safeguarded direction satisfying \(g_k^\top p_k<0\); if necessary, take \(p_k=-g_k\). Starting with \(\alpha=1\), reduce \(\alpha\leftarrow\beta\alpha\) until \(f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\leq f(x_k)+c_1\alpha g_k^\top p_k\), then set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha p_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is twice continuously differentiable near the iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), where \(p_k\) is an inexact safeguarded Newton direction and \(\alpha_k\) satisfies Armijo decrease.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained truncated Newton-CG with Armijo backtracking and a descent safeguard.

notation.meaning: Hessian or symmetric Newton-model operator at the current iterate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Line-search Newton-CG method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable. At outer iteration \(k\), set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\), and choose \(\epsilon_k>0\). Inner CG starts from \(z_0=0\), \(r_0=g_k\), and \(d_0=-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic smooth unconstrained optimization with an Armijo, Wolfe, or Goldstein line search and CG truncation for inexact Newton directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Line-search Newton-CG applies CG to \(B_kp=-g_k\). At inner iteration \(j\), it returns \(p_k=z_j\) when \(d_j^TB_kd_j\leq0\), except that at \(j=0\) it returns \(p_k=-g_k\); otherwise it performs the CG update and returns \(p_k=z_{j+1}\) when \(\|r_{j+1}\|<\epsilon_k\). The outer method chooses \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) satisfying an accepted line-search condition and sets \[x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k,\] using \(\alpha_k=1\) whenever it satisfies the acceptance criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method uses conjugate gradients to approximate the Newton direction. CG stops when the linear residual is sufficiently small or when nonpositive curvature appears. The returned direction is passed to a line search, which preferably accepts the full step but shortens it when needed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p_k=\begin{cases}-g_k,&j=0\text{ and }d_0^TB_kd_0\leq0,\\z_j,&j>0\text{ and }d_j^TB_kd_j\leq0,\\z_{j+1},&\|r_{j+1}\|<\epsilon_k,\end{cases}\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(\epsilon_k=\eta_k\|g_k\|\), residual termination is the inexact Newton condition \(\|B_kp_k+g_k\|<\eta_k\|g_k\|\).
special_cases_latex: A source-supported superlinear tolerance is \[\epsilon_k=\min\{0.5,\sqrt{\|g_k\|}\}\|g_k\|.\]
When \(B_k\) remains positive definite and the residual test triggers, no negative-curvature safeguard is used.
immediate_consequences_latex: The first-iteration curvature fallback \(-g_k\) is a descent direction whenever \(g_k\neq0\).
Only products \(B_kd_j\) are required, so an explicitly stored Hessian is unnecessary.
boundary_notes: Nearly singular Hessians can produce long, poor-quality line-search directions.
The method is distinct from trust-region Newton-CG because it does not truncate at a radius boundary.
Finite-difference Hessian-vector products introduce additional approximation error not represented in the exact algorithmic definition.

notation.meaning: Inner CG iterate approximating the Newton step.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Newton-CG
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run CG on the quadratic Newton model, truncating at nonpositive curvature, the Euclidean trust-region boundary, or a residual tolerance, and then use the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio for acceptance and radius updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and define \(m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top H_kp\). For radius \(\Delta_k>0\), initialize \(p_0=0\), \(r_0=g_k\), and \(d_0=-r_0\). At iteration \(j\), if \(d_j^\top H_kd_j\leq0\), return \(p_j+\tau d_j\), where \(\tau\geq0\) is the boundary point satisfying \(\|p_j+\tau d_j\|_2=\Delta_k\) that minimizes the model on the feasible ray. Otherwise take the ordinary CG step. If that step crosses the boundary, return its first boundary intersection; if the new residual meets the prescribed tolerance, return the new iterate. For the returned step \(p_k\), form \(\rho_k=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+p_k)]/[m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)]\) when the denominator is positive, and use a prescribed trust-region policy based on \(\rho_k\) to accept or reject the trial point and update \(\Delta_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable near the trial points, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(H_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric.
Products \(H_kv\) are available, \(\Delta_k>0\), and the returned step used in the ratio satisfies \(m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned step \(p_k\) satisfies \(\|p_k\|_2\leq\Delta_k\) and is a truncated Krylov approximation for the trust-region model; trial-point acceptance and radius adjustment are governed by \(\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Steihaug-type truncated CG for a Euclidean trust-region subproblem.

notation.meaning: quadratic Newton model at the current iterate
ratio of actual reduction to predicted model reduction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-region Newton-CG by CG-Steihaug truncation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable. At iteration \(k\), define \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and model \(m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic smooth unconstrained trust-region optimization using the Steihaug conjugate-gradient inner method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Trust-region Newton-CG applies CG from \(z_0=0\), \(r_0=g_k\), and \(d_0=-g_k\) to the trust-region model. It terminates and returns \(p_k=z_j+\tau d_j\) on \(\|p_k\|=\Delta_k\) if \(d_j^TB_kd_j\leq0\), choosing the boundary intersection that minimizes \(m_k\) along that line. It also returns the first boundary intersection if the next CG iterate would satisfy \(\|z_{j+1}\|\geq\Delta_k\), or returns \(p_k=z_{j+1}\) when \(\|r_{j+1}\|<\epsilon_k\). The outer trust-region method accepts or rejects \(p_k\) using actual versus predicted reduction and updates \(\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method approximately minimizes the quadratic Newton model inside a trust region by conjugate gradients. CG stops at the trust-region boundary when it encounters nonpositive curvature or would leave the region, and otherwise stops when its residual is small. An outer trust-region ratio controls step acceptance and radius changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p_k\in\{z_{j+1}:\|r_{j+1}\|<\epsilon_k\}\cup\{z_j+\tau d_j:\|z_j+\tau d_j\|=\Delta_k\},\] where boundary termination occurs for nonpositive curvature or impending radius violation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inner problem is \[\min_{\|p\|\leq\Delta_k}m_k(p).\]
When the trust-region bound is inactive near a regular solution, residual termination reduces the method to a full-step inexact Newton iteration.
special_cases_latex: If \(d_0^TB_kd_0\leq0\), the returned boundary step is the Cauchy step \(-\Delta_kg_k/\|g_k\|\).
If \(B_k\) is positive definite and the unconstrained truncated-CG iterate reaches the residual tolerance before the boundary, an interior step is returned.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every returned step satisfies \(\|p_k\|\leq\Delta_k\).
Negative curvature is handled by moving to the trust-region boundary rather than by attempting to solve an indefinite system to high residual accuracy.
The method requires Hessian-vector products but need not form or factor the Hessian.
boundary_notes: The CG-Steihaug step need not be the exact global minimizer of an indefinite trust-region subproblem.
The initial residual test may return \(p_k=0\) when \(\|g_k\|<\epsilon_k\).
Preconditioned trust-region Newton-CG requires a modified metric and separate preconditioner specification.

notation.meaning: Scalar locating an intersection of a CG line with the trust-region boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Newton-Lanczos
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the quadratic Newton model onto a growing Lanczos Krylov space, solve the reduced Euclidean trust-region problem, lift its minimizer to the full space, and globalize it using the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\neq0\), and define \(m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top H_kp\). Starting with \(q_1=g_k/\|g_k\|_2\), Lanczos iteration builds an orthonormal basis \(Q_j=[q_1,\ldots,q_j]\) of \(\mathcal K_j(H_k,g_k)\) and the projected matrix \(T_j=Q_j^\top H_kQ_j\). With \(e_1\in\mathbb{R}^j\) denoting the first coordinate vector, solve \(y_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|y\|_2\leq\Delta_k}\{\|g_k\|_2e_1^\top y+\tfrac12y^\top T_jy\}\) and set \(p_j=Q_jy_j\). Expand the basis until a prescribed reduced-problem stopping criterion is met and return \(p_k=p_j\). Form \(\rho_k=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+p_k)]/[m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)]\) when the denominator is positive, and apply a prescribed trust-region policy based on \(\rho_k\) to accept or reject the trial point and update \(\Delta_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable near the trial points, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\neq0\), and \(H_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric.
Products \(H_kv\) are available, \(\Delta_k>0\), and the returned step used in the ratio satisfies \(m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned step \(p_k\) lies in \(\mathcal K_j(H_k,g_k)\), satisfies \(\|p_k\|_2\leq\Delta_k\), and minimizes the quadratic model over the selected Krylov subspace and radius.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lanczos reduction of a symmetric large-scale trust-region Newton model.

notation.meaning: Krylov space generated by the Hessian model and gradient
first coordinate vector in the reduced space
ratio of actual reduction to predicted model reduction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-Region Newton-Lanczos Step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice differentiable at \(x_k\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), let \(B_k=\nabla^2 f(x_k)\) or a symmetric Hessian model, and let \(\Delta_k>0\). Define \(\mathcal K_j(B_k,g_k)=\operatorname{span}\{g_k,B_kg_k,\ldots,B_k^{j-1}g_k\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, large-scale unconstrained optimization with a Euclidean trust region and a symmetric, possibly indefinite Newton model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A trust-region Newton-Lanczos step of dimension \(j\) is a vector \(p_{k,j}=Q_jw_j\), where \(Q_j\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times j}\) has orthonormal columns spanning \(\mathcal K_j(B_k,g_k)\), \(T_j=Q_j^TB_kQ_j\) is symmetric tridiagonal, and
\[
w_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|w\|_2\leq\Delta_k}\left\{(Q_j^Tg_k)^Tw+\tfrac12w^TT_jw\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(p_{k,j}\) minimizes the quadratic Newton model over the Lanczos subspace intersected with the trust region:
\[
p_{k,j}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in\mathcal K_j(B_k,g_k),\ \|p\|_2\leq\Delta_k}\left\{g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method constructs an orthonormal Lanczos basis \(Q_j\) for the Krylov space generated by the symmetric Newton matrix \(B_k\) and gradient \(g_k\). It projects \(B_k\) to the tridiagonal matrix \(T_j=Q_j^TB_kQ_j\), solves the trust-region quadratic problem in the reduced coordinates \(w\), and returns \(p_{k,j}=Q_jw_j\). Thus the returned step is precisely a minimizer of the Newton model over the current Lanczos subspace subject to \(\|p\|_2\leq\Delta_k\). Indefiniteness is retained in \(T_j\), so negative-curvature information exposed by Lanczos remains available to the reduced trust-region solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p_{k,j}=Q_jw_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in\mathcal K_j(B_k,g_k),\ \|p\|_2\leq\Delta_k}\bigl(g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\bigr).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[w_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|w\|_2\leq\Delta_k}\bigl((Q_j^Tg_k)^Tw+\tfrac12w^TT_jw\bigr),\qquad T_j=Q_j^TB_kQ_j.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(j=n\) and \(Q_n\) is square orthogonal, the reduced problem is orthogonally equivalent to the full trust-region subproblem.
If the reduced minimizer is interior and \(T_j\) is nonsingular, it satisfies \(T_jw_j=-Q_j^Tg_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The construction needs products \(B_kv\) and does not require explicit factorization of \(B_k\).
Because \(T_j\) is tridiagonal, the reduced trust-region problem can be treated using shifted systems \(T_j+\lambda I\).
boundary_notes: This definition does not prescribe a Lanczos stopping tolerance, reorthogonalization policy, preconditioner, or trust-region acceptance update.
It differs from immediate CG truncation at the first negative-curvature direction: the Lanczos subspace may continue to collect curvature information.

notation.meaning: The order-\(j\) Krylov subspace generated by \(B_k\) and \(g_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Curvature Truncation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop the Krylov recurrence when a direction has nonpositive model curvature, then move to the trust-region boundary or return a safeguarded descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: While approximately minimizing \(m(p)=g^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Hp\), test every nonzero Krylov search direction \(d_j\). If \(d_j^\top Hd_j\leq0\), terminate the positive-curvature recurrence. In a trust region, choose an endpoint \(p_j+\tau d_j\) with \(\|p_j+\tau d_j\|=\Delta\) that gives the smaller model value among the feasible ray-boundary intersections. In a line-search method, return a safeguarded direction formed from \(p_j\) or \(d_j\) that satisfies \(g^\top p<0\); otherwise use \(-g\). If no such curvature event occurs, continue until the ordinary residual or boundary stopping test holds.
assumptions_latex: The globalization mechanism is either a Euclidean trust region or a line search requiring descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Detection of \(d_j^\top Hd_j\leq0\) prevents an invalid positive-definite CG step and exposes a direction along which the quadratic model is nonconvex or flat.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature-triggered truncation for symmetric Newton-model Krylov iterations.

notation.meaning: Krylov search direction at the curvature event
trust-region radius when that globalization is used

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative-Curvature Truncation of an Inner Newton Solve
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(p)=g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp\), where \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric, and suppose an inner CG-type iteration has current iterate \(z_j\) and nonzero search direction \(d_j\). For a trust-region variant, let \(\Delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric Newton systems. The definition covers the standard line-search truncation and the trust-region boundary truncation, which return different objects after detecting nonpositive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Negative-curvature truncation is the stopping rule triggered at the first index \(j\) for which
\[
d_j^TBd_j\leq0.
\]
In the line-search Newton-CG form initialized by \(z_0=0\) and \(d_0=-g\), the truncated direction is
\[
p=\begin{cases}-g,&j=0,\\z_j,&j>0.\end{cases}
\]
In the trust-region Newton-CG form, the truncated step is
\[
p=z_j+\tau d_j,
\]
where \(\tau\geq0\) is chosen so that \(\|p\|_2=\Delta\) and, among the feasible boundary intersections on the current ray, \(q(p)\) is minimized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner symmetric Krylov solve is truncated as soon as its current search direction \(d_j\) has nonpositive model curvature, meaning \(d_j^TBd_j\leq0\). In a line-search Newton-CG method, the returned direction is the negative gradient if curvature fails at the first inner iteration and otherwise the current CG iterate \(z_j\). In a trust-region Newton-CG method, the algorithm follows the detected direction from \(z_j\) until it meets the trust-region boundary, choosing the boundary intersection that gives the smaller quadratic-model value. The defining event is curvature failure, not merely a residual tolerance or iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_j^TBd_j\leq0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{terminate the inner solve and return the prescribed truncated line-search or trust-region step}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For nonzero \(d_j\), the strict condition \(d_j^TBd_j<0\) says that \(d_j\) is a negative-curvature direction of \(q\); equality is the zero-curvature boundary case included by the standard truncation test.
special_cases_latex: At \(j=0\), \(d_0=-g\); line-search truncation therefore returns \(-g\).
In a trust-region method, if \(z_j=0\), the returned step is a signed multiple of \(d_j\) with norm \(\Delta\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The inner CG recurrence is not continued through a denominator \(d_j^TBd_j\) that is nonpositive.
Trust-region truncation produces a boundary step, whereas line-search truncation need not do so.
boundary_notes: Some implementations use a positive threshold \(d_j^TBd_j\leq\epsilon\|d_j\|^2\); that safeguarded variant is not part of this canonical definition.
Lanczos methods that continue after detecting indefiniteness are outside this truncation rule.

notation.meaning: The local quadratic Newton model without its constant term.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matrix-Free Realization of Newton Linear Algebra
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be differentiable with Jacobian \(J(x)\), or let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice differentiable with Hessian \(H(x)=\nabla^2f(x)\). Let \(A_k\) denote the Newton operator used by an iterative inner solver.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear equations, optimization, or KKT linearizations solved iteratively without explicit assembly of the full Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A Newton computation is matrix-free with respect to \(A_k\) if the inner linear or Krylov solver accesses \(A_k\) only through an operator oracle
\[
\mathcal A_k:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m,\qquad \mathcal A_k(v)=A_kv,
\]
and, when required by the solver, an adjoint oracle \(\mathcal A_k^*(w)=A_k^Tw\), while no entrywise matrix representation of \(A_k\) is formed or stored. The Newton step is then characterized by a residual condition such as
\[
\|A_ks_k+b_k\|\leq\eta_k\|b_k\|,
\]
with all Krylov products evaluated by the oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix-free Newton operations replace an assembled Jacobian, Hessian, or KKT matrix by routines that return its action on arbitrary vectors. An iterative solver constructs its residuals and Krylov spaces using calls \(v\mapsto A_kv\), and possibly \(w\mapsto A_k^Tw\), while the full coefficient matrix is neither formed entry by entry nor stored. A computed Newton step is still defined by the original linearized equation or by an explicit residual tolerance; “matrix-free” describes how the operator is accessed, not a different Newton equation. The operator action may be exact, automatically differentiated, or approximated by directional finite differences, provided that its chosen status is stated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{matrix-free access to }A_k\iff\text{the inner solver uses operator actions }A_kv\text{ (and, if needed, }A_k^Tw\text{) without assembling }A_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For Hessian-free Newton-CG, \(\mathcal A_k(v)=\nabla^2f(x_k)v\).
For Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov, \(\mathcal A_k(v)=J(x_k)v\).
special_cases_latex: A preconditioner may be represented by a separate solve oracle \(r\mapsto M_k^{-1}r\) without changing the matrix-free status of \(A_k\).
If \(A_k\) is symmetric, only the forward action is needed by CG, MINRES, or Lanczos-type methods.
immediate_consequences_latex: Krylov bases can be generated with storage proportional to a collection of vectors rather than the number of entries of \(A_k\).
The mathematical residual is evaluated using the same operator action used by the inner iteration.
boundary_notes: Storing a preconditioner does not imply that the Newton operator itself has been assembled.
Finite-difference actions are inexact operator products and must not be identified with exact products in finite precision.

notation.meaning: The Newton, Jacobian, Hessian, or KKT linearization operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Jacobian-Vector Products
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Jacobian-vector product is the directional derivative of the residual mapping and can be supplied without explicitly forming the Jacobian matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be Fréchet differentiable at \(x\in U\). For any \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the Jacobian-vector product is the directional derivative \[J_F(x)v=DF(x)[v]=\left.\frac{d}{dt}F(x+tv)\right|_{t=0}=\lim_{t\to0}\frac{F(x+tv)-F(x)}{t}.\] Thus a Newton-Krylov method may expose the linear operator \(v\mapsto J_F(x)v\) without assembling \(J_F(x)\). For a KKT residual mapping \(R(z)\), the same identity with \(F=R\) defines the required KKT Jacobian action.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is open and \(F\) is Fréchet differentiable at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_F(x)v=DF(x)[v]\) for every \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact directional-derivative representation of a matrix-free Jacobian action.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the residual mapping at x
Fréchet derivative applied to direction v
