knowledge_statements.statement_title: Jacobian-Vector Product as a Directional Derivative
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(F:U\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be Fréchet differentiable at \(x\in U\), and let \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Write \(J_F(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) for the Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth mappings, including nonlinear residual maps and primal-dual KKT residual maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Jacobian-vector product of \(F\) at \(x\) in direction \(v\) is
\[
\operatorname{JVP}(F,x;v):=J_F(x)v=DF(x)[v]=\lim_{t\to0}\frac{F(x+tv)-F(x)}{t}.
\]
The limit is taken over nonzero \(t\) for which \(x+tv\in U\). It defines a linear map of the direction: for all \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(u,v\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
\operatorname{JVP}(F,x;au+bv)=a\operatorname{JVP}(F,x;u)+b\operatorname{JVP}(F,x;v).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Jacobian-vector product is the derivative of a vector-valued mapping in one specified input direction. For a differentiable residual map \(F\), it is the vector \(J_F(x)v\), equivalently the Fréchet derivative \(DF(x)\) applied to \(v\), or the limit of the directional difference quotient. Its output lies in \(\mathbb{R}^m\), and its dependence on \(v\) is linear. In a nonlinear-equation or KKT Newton solve, this product supplies the action required to build a Krylov subspace without requiring every entry of \(J_F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{JVP}(F,x;v)=J_F(x)v=DF(x)[v]=\lim_{t\to0}\frac{F(x+tv)-F(x)}{t}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_m)^T\), \(\operatorname{JVP}(F,x;v)=(\nabla F_1(x)^Tv,\ldots,\nabla F_m(x)^Tv)^T\).
special_cases_latex: For \(v=e_i\), the product is the \(i\)-th column of \(J_F(x)\).
For scalar-valued \(F\), the product reduces to the directional derivative \(\nabla F(x)^Tv\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A sequence of JVPs generates \(\mathcal K_j(J_F(x),r)\) for a Jacobian-based Krylov method.
The zero direction satisfies \(\operatorname{JVP}(F,x;0)=0\).
boundary_notes: The definition is the exact derivative action; a finite-difference quotient with fixed nonzero step is only an approximation.
For nonsmooth \(F\), generalized directional derivatives are distinct objects and are not covered here.

notation.meaning: The Fréchet derivative applied to direction \(v\).

source_refs.locator: §8.1, “Approximating a Sparse Jacobian,” equations (8.9)–(8.11), especially the definition of J(x) and the directional product J(x)p

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hessian-Vector Product as a Gradient Directional Derivative
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice Fréchet differentiable at \(x\in U\), and let \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth scalar optimization models with an exact Hessian action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Hessian-vector product of \(f\) at \(x\) in direction \(v\) is
\[
\operatorname{HVP}(f,x;v):=\nabla^2f(x)v=D(\nabla f)(x)[v]=\lim_{t\to0}\frac{\nabla f(x+tv)-\nabla f(x)}{t}.
\]
It is linear in \(v\). When \(f\) has continuous second derivatives near \(x\), the Hessian is symmetric, so for all \(u,v\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
u^T\operatorname{HVP}(f,x;v)=v^T\operatorname{HVP}(f,x;u).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hessian-vector product is the action of the Hessian on one direction. It equals \(\nabla^2f(x)v\) and also the directional derivative of the gradient map at \(x\). Thus it can be supplied to Newton-CG or Lanczos methods without materializing the entire Hessian. The product is an \(n\)-vector, depends linearly on \(v\), and, under the usual continuous-second-derivative condition, represents a symmetric linear operator. The quadratic curvature along \(v\) is obtained from the scalar \(v^T\operatorname{HVP}(f,x;v)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{HVP}(f,x;v)=\nabla^2f(x)v=D(\nabla f)(x)[v].\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(u^T\operatorname{HVP}(f,x;v)=D^2f(x)[u,v]\).
special_cases_latex: For \(v=e_i\), the HVP is the \(i\)-th Hessian column.
The directional curvature is \(v^T\operatorname{HVP}(f,x;v)=D^2f(x)[v,v]\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A symmetric Krylov method can use repeated HVP calls as its only access to the Newton matrix.
Negative curvature along \(v\) is detected by \(v^T\operatorname{HVP}(f,x;v)<0\).
boundary_notes: This definition concerns the exact Hessian action, not a finite-difference or quasi-Newton approximation.
For nonsmooth objectives, generalized Hessians require a separate definition.

notation.meaning: The directional derivative of the gradient in direction \(v\).

source_refs.locator: §8.1, “Approximating the Hessian,” equations (8.19)–(8.20); §7.1, Hessian-free Newton discussion following Algorithm 7.1

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Difference Operator Products
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward function differences approximate Jacobian actions and forward gradient differences approximate Hessian actions with first-order truncation error. Centered differences give second-order truncation error under one additional derivative, with separate smoothness requirements for the residual and gradient mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, \(x\in U\), \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(F:U	o\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(f:U	o\mathbb{R}\). For \(h>0\) such that the sampled points lie in \(U\), the forward formulas are \[J_F(x)v\approx rac{F(x+hv)-F(x)}{h},\qquad 
abla^2f(x)v\approx rac{
abla f(x+hv)-
abla f(x)}{h}.\] If \(F\) has two continuous derivatives with locally bounded second derivative along the sampled segment, the first error is \(O(h\|v\|_2^2)\). If \(f\) has three continuous derivatives with locally bounded third derivative there, the second error is \(O(h\|v\|_2^2)\). The centered formulas \([F(x+hv)-F(x-hv)]/(2h)\) and \([
abla f(x+hv)-
abla f(x-hv)]/(2h)\) have errors \(O(h^2\|v\|_2^3)\) when \(F\) has three continuous derivatives and \(f\) has four continuous derivatives, respectively, with the relevant derivatives locally bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open, \(x\in U\), \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and every sampled point belongs to \(U\).

For the stated forward orders, \(F\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(f\) is three times continuously differentiable along the sampled segment, with the relevant derivatives locally bounded.

For the stated centered orders, \(F\) is three times continuously differentiable and \(f\) is four times continuously differentiable along the sampled segment, with the relevant derivatives locally bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulas provide matrix-free approximations to \(J_F(x)v\) and \(\nabla^2f(x)v\) with the stated forward and centered truncation orders.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward and centered finite-difference approximations of Jacobian and Hessian actions.
review_flags: Verify that the locator covers both residual and gradient differences and the stated forward and centered error orders.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional Finite-Difference Approximation of Derivative Operators
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be differentiable near \(x\), let \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and choose \(h\neq0\) with \(x+hv\in U\). For Hessian products, let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) have a differentiable gradient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth mappings. These are approximate matrix-free actions based on function or gradient evaluations, not exact derivative products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The forward finite-difference operator product is
\[
\widehat{J_hv}:=\frac{F(x+hv)-F(x)}{h}.
\]
When approximating a Hessian action through gradients, it is
\[
\widehat{H_hv}:=\frac{\nabla f(x+hv)-\nabla f(x)}{h}.
\]
If \(J_F\) is Lipschitz near the segment from \(x\) to \(x+hv\), then \(\widehat{J_hv}=J_F(x)v+O(|h|\|v\|^2)\). If \(\nabla^2f\) is Lipschitz there, then \(\widehat{H_hv}=\nabla^2f(x)v+O(|h|\|v\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-difference operator product approximates a Jacobian action by differencing two values of the residual map along a selected direction. The same construction applied to the gradient approximates a Hessian-vector product. For a fixed direction and the stated Lipschitz regularity, the forward formulas have first-order truncation error in the differencing step \(h\). They supply approximate products to a matrix-free Krylov solver without constructing the derivative matrix, at the cost of one additional function or gradient evaluation when the base value has already been computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[J_F(x)v\approx rac{F(x+hv)-F(x)}{h},\qquad 
abla^2f(x)v\approx rac{
abla f(x+hv)-
abla f(x)}{h}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The centered Jacobian product \(\bigl(F(x+hv)-F(x-hv)\bigr)/(2h)\) is a two-sided variant when both points lie in the domain.
special_cases_latex: With \(v=e_i\), the forward formula approximates one column of the derivative matrix.
For linear \(F(x)=Ax+b\), the forward quotient equals \(Av\) for every nonzero admissible \(h\) in exact arithmetic.
immediate_consequences_latex: A Jacobian-free or Hessian-free Krylov iteration can replace each formal matrix-vector product by the corresponding difference quotient.
The differencing step controls a tradeoff between truncation error and finite-precision cancellation.
boundary_notes: The formulas do not define an assembled finite-difference Jacobian or Hessian.
The asymptotic error statements omit evaluation noise and roundoff amplification, which can dominate for very small \(|h|\).

source_refs.locator: §8.1, equations (8.10)–(8.11) for Jacobian-vector products and equations (8.19)–(8.20) for Hessian-vector products

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic-Derivative Operator Products
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Automatic differentiation propagates directional derivatives through a program to compute Jacobian and Hessian actions without finite-difference truncation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a differentiable program evaluating \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), forward-mode automatic differentiation propagates the tangent pair \((x,v)\) and returns \((F(x),J_F(x)v)\). For a twice differentiable scalar program \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), applying a Jacobian-vector product to the reverse-mode gradient program returns \((\nabla f(x),\nabla^2f(x)v)\). These identities are exact in exact arithmetic for the differentiable operations represented by the program; floating-point results remain subject to rounding and nondifferentiable program branches require an explicit derivative convention.
assumptions_latex: The executed computational graph consists of operations equipped with valid derivative rules at the evaluation point.
For the Hessian action, the scalar program is twice differentiable along the executed branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Forward tangent propagation yields \(J_F(x)v\), and differentiation of the gradient action yields \(\nabla^2f(x)v\), without assembling either matrix.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic Jacobian and Hessian actions computed by automatic differentiation.
review_flags: No supplied locator covers automatic-differentiation operator products or branch conventions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Automatic-Differentiation Realization of Operator Products
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a differentiable program evaluate \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) through a finite composition of differentiable elementary operations. Let \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(w\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact chain-rule differentiation of a differentiable computational graph, up to floating-point effects; no finite-difference perturbation is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An automatic-derivative operator product is obtained by propagating derivative data through the computational graph according to the chain rule. A forward-mode sweep seeded by \(v\) returns
\[
\operatorname{AD}_{\mathrm{fwd}}(F,x;v)=J_F(x)v.
\]
A reverse-mode sweep seeded at the outputs by \(w\) returns
\[
\operatorname{AD}_{\mathrm{rev}}(F,x;w)=J_F(x)^Tw.
\]
For scalar \(f\), a forward-over-reverse or reverse-over-forward construction applied to \(\nabla f(x)^Tv\) returns \(\nabla^2f(x)v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Automatic differentiation supplies derivative-operator actions by applying the chain rule to the elementary operations used to evaluate a function. Forward mode attaches tangents to the graph, initializes the input tangent with \(v\), and returns the Jacobian-vector product \(J_F(x)v\). Reverse mode attaches adjoints, initializes the output adjoint with \(w\), and returns \(J_F(x)^Tw\). For a scalar objective, combining modes gives a Hessian-vector product. These are derivative actions of the represented program, rather than difference quotients based on perturbed inputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{AD}_{\mathrm{fwd}}(F,x;v)=J_F(x)v,\qquad \operatorname{AD}_{\mathrm{rev}}(F,x;w)=J_F(x)^Tw.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_m)^T\), forward mode returns all directional derivatives \(D_vF_i(x)\) in one seeded sweep.
Reverse mode differentiates the scalar map \(x\mapsto w^TF(x)\), whose gradient is \(J_F(x)^Tw\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m=1\) and the reverse seed is \(1\), reverse mode returns \(\nabla f(x)\).
For a succession of Krylov directions \(v_j\), one forward sweep per seed supplies \(J_F(x)v_j\).
immediate_consequences_latex: AD-based Newton-Krylov products avoid explicit derivative-matrix assembly.
Unlike finite differencing, the mathematical construction has no differencing-step parameter.
boundary_notes: Branching, nondifferentiable primitives, iterative subprograms, and floating-point behavior require implementation-specific semantics beyond this definition.
The definition does not claim that an AD product is free of roundoff error.

notation.meaning: Input-tangent and output-adjoint seed vectors, respectively.

source_refs.locator: §8.2, “Automatic Differentiation,” especially forward-mode directional products, vector-function products J(x)p and J(x)^Tq, and the Hessian-vector construction on pp. 201–216

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton-Krylov Inner Solver Family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At nonlinear iteration \(k\), let \(A_ks=-b_k\) be a Newton or KKT linearization, with \(A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). In the square case let \(s_0\) be an initial inner iterate and \(r_0=A_ks_0+b_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional inexact Newton methods whose linearized systems are solved in Krylov spaces; solver selection depends on the algebraic class of the Newton operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A Newton-Krylov method computes an inexact Newton correction \(s_j\) in an affine Krylov space and terminates according to a residual condition. For a square operator,
\[
s_j\in s_0+\mathcal K_j(A_k,r_0),\qquad \mathcal K_j(A_k,r_0)=\operatorname{span}\{r_0,A_kr_0,\ldots,A_k^{j-1}r_0\},
\]
with
\[
\|A_ks_j+b_k\|\leq\eta_k\|b_k\|.
\]
The canonical family chooses CG for symmetric positive-definite operators, MINRES-type methods for symmetric indefinite operators, GMRES-type methods for general nonsymmetric operators, and projected or reduced-space Krylov methods when corrections must remain in a constraint-compatible subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton-Krylov method solves each Newton linearization only approximately, searching in a Krylov space generated by the current operator and residual. The inner solve ends when its residual meets a prescribed forcing tolerance or another explicitly stated truncation rule. The family name covers several solvers distinguished by operator structure: conjugate gradients for symmetric positive-definite systems, minimum-residual symmetric methods for symmetric indefinite systems, GMRES for nonsymmetric systems, and projected or reduced-space iterations for constrained corrections. Matrix-vector products may be supplied without assembling the operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_j\in s_0+\mathcal K_j(A_k,r_0),\qquad \|A_ks_j+b_k\|\leq\eta_k\|b_k\|,\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(s_0=0\), the search space is \(\mathcal K_j(A_k,b_k)\) up to the sign of its generator.
Under left preconditioning, the corresponding Krylov space is generated by \(M_k^{-1}A_k\) and \(M_k^{-1}r_0\).
special_cases_latex: For unconstrained minimization, \(A_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\) and \(b_k=\nabla f(x_k)\).
For nonlinear equations, \(A_k=J_F(x_k)\) and \(b_k=F(x_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The Newton matrix can be accessed through products \(A_kv\).
The inner accuracy is separated from the outer nonlinear iteration through \(\eta_k\).
boundary_notes: The family definition does not assert that every listed Krylov solver is suitable for every operator.
Least-squares Krylov methods for rectangular systems require a separately stated residual or normal-equation formulation.

notation.meaning: The initial residual of the inner Newton solve.
The forcing tolerance for the inexact Newton equation.

children.title: Conjugate-Gradient Newton Systems
children.top_down_role: Krylov solves for symmetric positive-curvature Newton models.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate-Gradient Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CG approximately solves a positive-definite Newton system using only Hessian-vector products and terminates in at most the dimension in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To solve \(Hp=-g\) with symmetric positive-definite \(H\), initialize \(p_0\), \(r_0=-g-Hp_0\), and \(d_0=r_0\). For \(j=0,1,\ldots\), set \(\alpha_j=(r_j^\top r_j)/(d_j^\top Hd_j)\), \(p_{j+1}=p_j+\alpha_jd_j\), and \(r_{j+1}=r_j-\alpha_jHd_j\). Stop when \(\|r_{j+1}\|\leq\eta\|g\|\); otherwise set \(\beta_{j+1}=(r_{j+1}^\top r_{j+1})/(r_j^\top r_j)\) and \(d_{j+1}=r_{j+1}+\beta_{j+1}d_j\). In exact arithmetic, the method terminates in at most \(n\) iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(0\leq\eta<1\), and arithmetic is exact for the finite-termination claim.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(p\) satisfies \(\|-g-Hp\|\leq\eta\|g\|\), unless exact termination at \(Hp=-g\) occurs earlier.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CG solution of a symmetric positive-definite Newton equation using operator products.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate-Gradient Solve of a Positive-Definite Newton System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite and let the Newton system be \(Bp=-g\). Define \(q(p)=g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp\), choose \(p_0\), and let \(r_0=Bp_0+g\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric positive-definite Newton models. Indefinite truncations belong to Newton-CG variants but fall outside the classical CG system definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A conjugate-gradient Newton iterate of order \(j\) is the unique vector
\[
p_j\in p_0+\mathcal K_j(B,r_0)
\]
that minimizes the Newton quadratic over this affine Krylov space:
\[
p_j=\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in p_0+\mathcal K_j(B,r_0)}q(p).
\]
Equivalently, its residual \(r_j=Bp_j+g\) satisfies the Galerkin condition
\[
r_j\perp\mathcal K_j(B,r_0),
\]
and the generated nonzero search directions are mutually \(B\)-conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a symmetric positive-definite Newton matrix \(B\), conjugate gradients computes successive approximations to the solution of \(Bp=-g\). At order \(j\), the iterate is the minimizer of the Newton quadratic over the affine Krylov space generated from the initial residual. Equivalently, its residual is orthogonal to that Krylov space. Positive definiteness makes the quadratic strictly convex and the minimizer unique. The method requires products \(Bv\) but no matrix factorization, making it suitable for large positive-curvature Newton models.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p_j=\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in p_0+\mathcal K_j(B,r_0)}\left(g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp\right),\qquad Bp_j+g\perp\mathcal K_j(B,r_0).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The error \(p_j-p_*\), where \(Bp_*=-g\), has minimum \(B\)-norm over \(p_0+\mathcal K_j(B,r_0)\).
special_cases_latex: With \(p_0=0\), \(r_0=g\) and \(p_j\in\mathcal K_j(B,g)\).
In exact arithmetic, CG reaches the exact solution in at most \(n\) iterations.
immediate_consequences_latex: Each denominator \(d_j^TBd_j\) is positive for a nonzero CG search direction.
Only Hessian-vector products are needed when \(B=\nabla^2f(x_k)\).
boundary_notes: Classical CG is not defined by this minimization property when \(B\) is indefinite.
Trust-region boundary termination and negative-curvature truncation are additional rules, not part of the SPD CG definition.

notation.meaning: The Krylov space generated by \(B\) and \(r_0\).

children.title: MINRES Newton Systems
children.top_down_role: Symmetry-preserving solves for indefinite Newton and KKT systems.

knowledge_statements.title: MINRES Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MINRES uses a Lanczos basis to minimize the residual norm for a symmetric Newton or KKT system, including indefinite systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Az=b\) with symmetric \(A\), an initial vector \(z_0\), and residual \(r_0=b-Az_0\), Lanczos iteration constructs an orthonormal basis \(V_j\) of \(\mathcal K_j(A,r_0)\) and a tridiagonal relation \(AV_j=V_{j+1}\underline T_j\). At iteration \(j\), choose \(y_j\) solving \(\min_y\|\|r_0\|e_1-\underline T_jy\|_2\) and set \(z_j=z_0+V_jy_j\). Stop when \(\|b-Az_j\|_2\leq\eta\|b\|_2\), or report the prescribed breakdown or iteration-limit status. Unlike CG, the construction does not require positive definiteness.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and products \(Av\) are available.
The system is consistent for an exact-solution interpretation; otherwise the returned iterate is residual minimizing in its Krylov affine space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_j\in z_0+\mathcal K_j(A,r_0)\) minimizes \(\|b-Az\|_2\) over that affine Krylov space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-minimizing Krylov iteration for symmetric, possibly indefinite Newton or KKT systems.

notation.meaning: j-dimensional Krylov space generated by A and the initial residual

review_flags: No supplied locator directly covers MINRES for symmetric indefinite Newton or KKT systems.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-Residual Krylov Solve of a Symmetric Newton System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, possibly indefinite, and consider \(As=b\). Choose \(s_0\), define \(r_0=b-As_0\), and assume only products \(Av\) are required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real symmetric Newton or KKT systems. The defining residual minimization permits indefiniteness but does not by itself cover singular inconsistent systems or preconditioner restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The order-\(j\) MINRES Newton iterate is any vector
\[
s_j\in s_0+\mathcal K_j(A,r_0)
\]
satisfying
\[
\|b-As_j\|_2=\min_{s\in s_0+\mathcal K_j(A,r_0)}\|b-As\|_2.
\]
The Krylov basis is generated by the symmetric Lanczos recurrence, so the projected coefficient matrix is tridiagonal. When the minimizer is unique, this condition defines \(s_j\) uniquely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MINRES applied to a Newton system with a real symmetric coefficient operator selects, at each Krylov dimension, the affine Krylov iterate having the smallest Euclidean residual norm. Symmetry permits a Lanczos three-term recurrence even when the operator is indefinite, so the method does not require the positive-definiteness assumed by conjugate gradients. This makes the formulation appropriate for symmetric indefinite Newton and saddle-point systems, subject to the usual consistency, breakdown, and preconditioning qualifications.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in s_0+\mathcal K_j(A,r_0)}\|b-As\|_2.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With an orthonormal Lanczos basis \(V_j\), write \(s=s_0+V_jy\); the reduced problem minimizes the norm of the Lanczos residual representation over \(y\in\mathbb{R}^j\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A\) is symmetric positive definite, MINRES remains defined, although CG exploits the stronger energy-minimization structure.
For a symmetric KKT matrix, primal and multiplier corrections are treated as one block vector.
immediate_consequences_latex: The residual norm is nonincreasing as the nested Krylov spaces expand.
No explicit factorization of \(A\) is required.
boundary_notes: A symmetric preconditioner must preserve the self-adjoint structure in the relevant inner product.

notation.meaning: The Krylov space generated by the symmetric operator and initial residual.

children.title: GMRES Newton Systems
children.top_down_role: Residual-minimizing solves for general or nonsymmetric Newton operators.

knowledge_statements.title: GMRES Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: GMRES builds an Arnoldi basis and minimizes the linear residual over a Krylov affine space for general, possibly nonsymmetric Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Az=b\), initialize \(z_0\) and \(r_0=b-Az_0\). Arnoldi iteration constructs an orthonormal basis \(V_j\) of \(\mathcal K_j(A,r_0)\) and \(AV_j=V_{j+1}\bar H_j\), where \(\bar H_j\) is upper Hessenberg. Compute \(y_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\|\|r_0\|e_1-\bar H_jy\|_2\) and set \(z_j=z_0+V_jy_j\). Stop when \(\|b-Az_j\|_2\leq\eta\|b\|_2\), or at the prescribed restart length or iteration limit. Restarted GMRES uses the current residual as the next cycle's starting vector.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is a general linear operator with available products \(Av\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_j\in z_0+\mathcal K_j(A,r_0)\) and \(\|b-Az_j\|_2=\min_{z\in z_0+\mathcal K_j(A,r_0)}\|b-Az\|_2\) before restarting.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arnoldi residual minimization for general matrix-free Newton operators.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly covers GMRES residual minimization or restarting.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: GMRES Solve of a General Newton System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be a general square Newton or Jacobian operator, consider \(As=b\), choose \(s_0\), and define \(r_0=b-As_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional general or nonsymmetric Newton systems, using unrestarted GMRES for the canonical mathematical definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The order-\(j\) GMRES Newton iterate is
\[
s_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in s_0+\mathcal K_j(A,r_0)}\|b-As\|_2,
\qquad
\mathcal K_j(A,r_0)=\operatorname{span}\{r_0,Ar_0,\ldots,A^{j-1}r_0\}.
\]
With an Arnoldi basis \(V_j\) and relation \(AV_j=V_{j+1}\bar H_j\), it has the form \(s_j=s_0+V_jy_j\), where
\[
y_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^j}\|\beta e_1-\bar H_jy\|_2,
\qquad \beta=\|r_0\|_2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: GMRES applied to a Newton or Jacobian system searches the affine Krylov space generated by the initial residual and chooses the vector with minimum Euclidean residual norm. Arnoldi orthogonalization converts this problem into a small least-squares problem involving an upper-Hessenberg matrix. Unlike CG and symmetric Lanczos methods, the definition does not require symmetry or positive definiteness. It is therefore a standard Newton-Krylov choice for general nonsymmetric Jacobians. The unrestarted method enlarges its space at every step; restarted GMRES periodically discards that accumulated basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in s_0+\mathcal K_j(A,r_0)}\|b-As\|_2.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[s_j=s_0+V_jy_j,\qquad y_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y}\|\|r_0\|_2e_1-\bar H_jy\|_2.\]
special_cases_latex: For a nonlinear equation \(F(x)=0\), take \(A=J_F(x_k)\) and \(b=-F(x_k)\).
Restarted GMRES\((m)\) repeats the definition over spaces of dimension at most \(m\) using the latest residual.
immediate_consequences_latex: For unrestarted GMRES, residual norms are nonincreasing with \(j\).
The method requires products \(Av\) and storage of Arnoldi basis vectors.
boundary_notes: Restarting can destroy the monotonic comparison with the unrestarted spaces across cycles.
Right- and left-preconditioned GMRES minimize different explicitly transformed residuals.

children.title: Projected Krylov Newton Systems

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Krylov Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the Newton equation into the constraint null space and apply a suitable symmetric Krylov method there, preserving linearized feasibility while reducing the projected residual; projected CG requires positive definiteness on the null space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank and define the orthogonal null-space projector \(P=I-A^\top(AA^\top)^{-1}A\). For a linearized-feasible step satisfying \(Ap=0\), solve \(PHPp=-Pg\) over \(\operatorname{range}(P)=\ker(A)\). Initialize \(p_0\in\ker(A)\) and apply a symmetry-compatible Krylov method using projected products \(v\mapsto PHPv\), reprojecting computed vectors when necessary. For a prescribed tolerance \(0\leq\eta<1\), stop when \(\|P(g+Hp_j)\|_2\leq\eta\|Pg\|_2\), and return \(p_j\). If \(PHP\) is positive definite on \(\ker(A)\), projected CG is applicable; if it is symmetric but indefinite, use a symmetry-compatible indefinite Krylov solver instead.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric, and \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
Products with \(H\) and \(P\), including the solve involving \(AA^\top\), are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the residual stopping test is reached, the returned step satisfies \(Ap_j=0\) and \(\|P(g+Hp_j)\|_2\leq\eta\|Pg\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space-compatible Krylov solution of an equality-constrained Newton equation.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the null space of the constraint Jacobian

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected Krylov Solve in a Constraint Null Space
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, and let \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) have columns spanning \(\ker A\). Assume \(Z^TGZ\) is positive definite. Let \(x_p\) satisfy \(Ax_p=b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained quadratic or Newton systems whose tangential correction is solved by CG in the constraint null space, explicitly or through a projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A projected Krylov Newton iteration computes feasible iterates
\[
x_j=x_p+Zz_j,
\]
where \(z_j\) is a Krylov iterate for the reduced system
\[
Z^TGZz=-Z^T(Gx_p+c).
\]
Equivalently, using a symmetric matrix \(H\) with \(Z^THZ\succ0\), define
\[
P=Z(Z^THZ)^{-1}Z^T.
\]
The full-space projected CG recurrence uses preconditioned residuals \(g_j=Pr_j\) and search directions \(d_j\in\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\), so that every update \(x_{j+1}=x_j+\alpha_jd_j\) remains feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected Krylov Newton system restricts iterative corrections to directions compatible with the linear constraints. With a null-space basis \(Z\), this means solving the reduced positive-definite Newton system involving \(Z^TGZ\). The equivalent full-space formulation applies the scaled projector \(P=Z(Z^THZ)^{-1}Z^T\) to residuals, generating directions in \(\ker A\). Starting from a feasible point, every iterate remains feasible because each displacement is annihilated by \(A\). The projection can be implemented through an augmented system without explicitly forming \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Ax_0=b,\ d_j\in\ker A\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Ax_j=b\text{ for every projected Krylov iterate}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The reduced-space method applies CG to \((Z^TGZ)z=-Z^T(Gx_p+c)\).
The full-space method uses \(P=Z(Z^THZ)^{-1}Z^T\) and never needs an explicit reduced Hessian.
special_cases_latex: If \(Z\) is orthonormal and \(H=I\), then \(P=ZZ^T\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Constraint feasibility is invariant in exact arithmetic.
Only products with \(G\), projections, and reduced preconditioner actions are required.
boundary_notes: Finite-precision projection errors may require refinement or explicit feasibility correction.
Positive definiteness is required on \(\ker A\), not necessarily on all of \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: A basis matrix for the null space of \(A\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioned Newton-Krylov Inner Iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_ks=-b_k\) be a Newton linearization and let \(M_k\) be a nonsingular operator for which systems \(M_kz=r\) can be solved comparatively cheaply. Let \(s_0\) be an initial inner iterate and \(r_0=A_ks_0+b_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Newton-Krylov methods with left, right, or symmetric preconditioning. The exact Krylov optimality property depends on the selected solver and transformed inner product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A left-preconditioned Newton-Krylov method applies a Krylov solver to
\[
M_k^{-1}A_ks=-M_k^{-1}b_k,
\]
thereby generating a space based on \(M_k^{-1}A_k\) and \(M_k^{-1}r_0\). A right-preconditioned method writes \(s=M_k^{-1}y\) and solves
\[
A_kM_k^{-1}y=-b_k.
\]
For a symmetric positive-definite Newton matrix and factorization \(M_k=C_k^TC_k\), symmetric preconditioning uses
\[
C_k^{-T}A_kC_k^{-1}\widehat s=-C_k^{-T}b_k,
\qquad s=C_k^{-1}\widehat s.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preconditioned Newton-Krylov method replaces the inner Newton system by an equivalent transformed system whose operator is intended to have a more favorable spectrum or conditioning. Left preconditioning transforms the residual equation, right preconditioning transforms the correction variables, and symmetric preconditioning preserves symmetry for suitable positive-definite problems. The preconditioner must be inexpensive to apply relative to the original Newton solve. It may approximate the Hessian, Jacobian, a block factorization, or a constraint-aware operator, but it need not equal the Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A_ks=-b_k\quad\text{is solved through an equivalent Krylov system involving }M_k^{-1}A_k,\ A_kM_k^{-1},\text{ or }C_k^{-T}A_kC_k^{-1}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Right-preconditioned residuals remain the original residuals \(b_k+A_ks\), whereas left-preconditioned methods naturally measure \(M_k^{-1}(b_k+A_ks)\).
special_cases_latex: For SPD \(A_k\) and SPD \(M_k\), preconditioned CG is defined in the \(M_k\)-induced geometry.
Incomplete Cholesky supplies a factor-based preconditioner for positive-curvature Newton-CG models.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(M_k=A_k\), the ideal transformed operator is the identity, assuming exact applications.
Matrix-free access to \(A_k\) is compatible with a separately assembled or matrix-free preconditioner.
boundary_notes: A nonsymmetric preconditioner can destroy symmetry required by CG or MINRES.
Changing \(M_k\) within one inner solve requires a flexible Krylov formulation unless additional invariance conditions hold.

notation.meaning: The correction in symmetrically transformed coordinates.

children.title: Primal-Block Preconditioning
children.top_down_role: Preconditioning centered on the primal Jacobian or Hessian block.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Block Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-block preconditioner separately approximates the primal Newton block and scales the constraints, while Krylov iteration retains the original primal-dual coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the saddle-point Newton matrix \(K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\), choose nonsingular \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) approximating the primal Hessian or Jacobian block \(H\), and nonsingular constraint scaling \(D\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\). A primal-block preconditioner is \[P_{\mathrm p}=\begin{pmatrix}B&0\\0&D\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_{\mathrm p}^{-1}K=\begin{pmatrix}B^{-1}H&B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\\D^{-1}A&0\end{pmatrix}.\] Its application requires solves with \(B\) and \(D\), without forming an inverse explicitly. When \(B\) is spectrally equivalent to \(H\) on the relevant primal subspace and \(D\) scales the constraint equations, the preconditioned operator retains the KKT coupling while normalizing the primal action.
assumptions_latex: \(H,B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(D\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\).
\(B\) and \(D\) are nonsingular and their linear systems can be solved approximately or exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\mathrm p}^{-1}K\) has the displayed block form and can be applied using separate solves with \(B\) and \(D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-diagonal preconditioning of an equality-constrained Newton system using an approximation of the primal block.

notation.meaning: approximation to the primal Hessian or Jacobian block

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the primal-block preconditioning container, and the displayed block multiplication is consistent. However, the cited Newton-method section is not a direct locator for this preconditioner or its spectral-equivalence claim. The final sentence also requires symmetry/positive-definiteness assumptions and a precise definition of the relevant primal subspace before spectral equivalence is meaningful.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-Block Preconditioner for a Saddle-Point Newton System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Consider the saddle-point Newton system \(Kz=r\) with
\[
K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&-C\end{bmatrix},
\]
where \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is the primal Hessian or Jacobian block, \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional block Newton or KKT systems. This candidate uses “primal-block” for a block preconditioner whose principal approximation is an efficiently invertible surrogate of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A primal-block preconditioner is a nonsingular block operator
\[
P_{\mathrm{PB}}=\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde H&0\\0&\widetilde D\end{bmatrix}
\quad\text{or}\quad
P_{\mathrm{PB}}=\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde H&A^T\\0&\widetilde D\end{bmatrix},
\]
where \(\widetilde H\) is an efficiently invertible approximation to the primal block \(H\) and \(\widetilde D\) is a nonsingular multiplier-space scaling. Its action is defined by solving \(P_{\mathrm{PB}}y=r\), with the principal computational operation being a solve with \(\widetilde H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-block preconditioner for a KKT or saddle-point Newton system is organized around an approximate solve with the primal Hessian or Jacobian block. In block-diagonal form it combines an invertible approximation \(\widetilde H\) with a multiplier-space scaling \(\widetilde D\); in block-triangular form it may retain the coupling block \(A^T\). Applying the preconditioner means solving the displayed block system, not multiplying by the block matrix itself. The definition specifies a structural family and does not assert spectral equivalence for arbitrary choices of its two approximate blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_{\mathrm{PB}}^{-1}r\text{ is computed using a principal solve with }\widetilde H\approx H\text{ and a multiplier-space solve with }\widetilde D.\]
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(\widetilde D=I\) yields a primal-block/Jacobi scaling.
If \(A=0\), the primal component reduces to ordinary preconditioning of \(H\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The primal and multiplier block dimensions remain explicit in the transformed Krylov system.
The quality and cost of the method depend primarily on applications of \(\widetilde H^{-1}\) and \(\widetilde D^{-1}\).
boundary_notes: This family is distinct from a Schur-complement preconditioner whose multiplier block explicitly approximates \(C+A\widetilde H^{-1}A^T\).
The supplied local sources did not expose a precise, named primal-block preconditioning definition matching this exact scope.

notation.meaning: The primal Newton or Hessian block.

children.title: Schur-Complement Preconditioning
children.top_down_role: Block preconditioning organized around constraint-space reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schur-complement preconditioning reduces primal-dual coupling to solves with an approximate primal block and an induced constraint-space operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular and define the constraint-space Schur complement \(S_B=AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\). The associated saddle-point approximation admits the factorization \[\begin{pmatrix}B&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\AB^{-1}&I\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}B&0\\0&-S_B\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}I&B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\\0&I\end{pmatrix}.\] Schur-complement preconditioning replaces \(B\) and \(S_B\) by computationally accessible approximations and applies the corresponding diagonal or triangular factors. If \(B\) is symmetric positive definite and \(A\) has full row rank, then \(S_B\) is symmetric positive definite, so its constraint-space solve is well defined.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
For positive definiteness of \(S_B\), \(B\) is symmetric positive definite and \(A\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed block factorization holds, and under the positivity assumptions \(S_B=AB^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-space reduction and block preconditioning for equality-constrained Newton systems.

notation.meaning: constraint-space Schur complement induced by the primal approximation

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The block factorization and positive-definiteness statement are mathematically consistent and the representation kind fits the leaf. The cited equality-constrained Newton section is nevertheless only indirect evidence and does not inspectably support the stated Schur-complement preconditioning construction or approximation policy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Schur-Complement Block Preconditioner
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let
\[
K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&-C\end{bmatrix}
\]
with nonsingular primal block \(H\). Define the positive-sign Schur operator \(S=C+AH^{-1}A^T\), so the algebraic Schur complement of \(H\) in \(K\) is \(-S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional KKT and saddle-point systems with an invertible primal block. Approximate Schur blocks are permitted, but their quality is not assumed automatically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A Schur-complement preconditioner is a block diagonal or block triangular nonsingular operator built from approximations \(\widetilde H\approx H\) and \(\widetilde S\approx C+A\widetilde H^{-1}A^T\), for example
\[
P_D=\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde H&0\\0&\widetilde S\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
P_T=\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde H&A^T\\0&-\widetilde S\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Application of \(P_D^{-1}\) uses separate approximate primal and Schur solves; application of \(P_T^{-1}\) additionally performs the block back-substitution induced by \(A^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schur-complement preconditioning organizes a saddle-point solve around an approximate elimination of the primal variables. Eliminating through \(H\) yields the multiplier-space operator \(C+AH^{-1}A^T\), up to the displayed sign convention. A practical preconditioner replaces the primal and Schur operators by efficiently invertible approximations and combines them in block-diagonal or block-triangular form. The preconditioner is applied through block solves. The definition does not require the exact Schur complement, whose formation may be as expensive as solving the original system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widetilde S\approx C+A\widetilde H^{-1}A^T\quad\text{is the defining multiplier-space block of a Schur-complement preconditioner}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exact block elimination factors \(K\) into triangular factors and a diagonal factor containing \(H\) and \(-S\); approximate block-factorization preconditioners replace these exact factors by tractable ones.
special_cases_latex: If \(\widetilde H=H\) and \(\widetilde S=S\), the triangular block factor reproduces exact block elimination under the compatible factorization convention.
immediate_consequences_latex: The multiplier-space preconditioning problem has dimension \(m\).
The action of \(\widetilde S\) may itself be implemented through primal solves rather than explicit formation.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint preconditioner replaces the primal curvature block but preserves the constraint Jacobian, yielding a nonsingular structured solve under reduced-space positivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\), a constraint preconditioner has the form \[P_{\mathrm c}=\begin{pmatrix}G&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix},\] where \(G\) is a tractable approximation to \(H\), while the constraint blocks are retained exactly. If \(A\) has full row rank and \(G\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), then \(P_{\mathrm c}\) is nonsingular. Application of \(P_{\mathrm c}^{-1}\) therefore amounts to solving an approximate equality-constrained quadratic system that preserves feasibility coupling. The preconditioner may be applied through a null-space, range-space, or block-factorization solve without explicitly forming \(P_{\mathrm c}^{-1}\).
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(G\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and positive definite on \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\mathrm c}\) is nonsingular and preserves the exact off-diagonal constraint blocks of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Saddle-point preconditioning that preserves the original constraint Jacobian blocks.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The structured matrix and reduced-space nonsingularity conditions fit constraint preconditioning, and the content kind is appropriate. The supplied locator concerns Newton-like equality-constrained methods but is not direct evidence for this named preconditioner, its null-space/range-space application alternatives, or the asserted interpretation as an approximate equality-constrained quadratic solve.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint Preconditioner for Projected Newton Iterations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be the primal Newton block, and let \(Z\) span \(\ker A\). Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and satisfy \(Z^THZ\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained quadratic or Newton systems. The preconditioner preserves the constraint Jacobian exactly while approximating the primal block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The constraint preconditioner associated with \(H\) and \(A\) is the saddle-point matrix
\[
P_C=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}.
\]
For a residual \(r\in\mathbb{R}^n\), its projected preconditioning action is the primal component \(g\) of
\[
\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}g\\v\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}r\\0\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
g=Pr,
\qquad P=Z(Z^THZ)^{-1}Z^T,
\]
so \(Ag=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint preconditioner replaces the primal Newton block by a tractable symmetric matrix \(H\) while retaining the constraint Jacobian blocks \(A\) and \(A^T\) in the augmented system. Applying it to a primal residual means solving the augmented system with zero constraint right-hand side and taking its primal component. This component equals the scaled null-space projection \(Z(Z^THZ)^{-1}Z^Tr\) and therefore lies in \(\ker A\). It can be used within projected conjugate gradients without explicitly constructing a null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_C=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad P_C\begin{bmatrix}g\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}r\\0\end{bmatrix}\Longrightarrow g=Z(Z^THZ)^{-1}Z^Tr\in\ker A.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(H=I\), the primal action is the orthogonal projector \(I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A\).
Choosing \(H=G\) gives the exact or “perfect” reduced-space preconditioner when the required solves are available.
immediate_consequences_latex: Projected residuals and search directions satisfy the homogeneous linearized constraints in exact arithmetic.
The null-space basis need not be formed if the augmented system can be solved.
boundary_notes: The requirement is positive definiteness of \(Z^THZ\), not necessarily of \(H\) on the entire primal space.
Roundoff in augmented solves can violate \(Ag=0\), so refinement may be required in implementations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioner Lifecycle Policy for a Newton-System Sequence
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K_k z_k=b_k\) be a sequence of nonsingular Newton or KKT linear systems on \(\mathbb R^{n_k}\). Let \(M_k\) be a nonsingular left preconditioner, let \(\mathcal H_k\) contain all system, iteration, and diagnostic data available after outer iteration \(k\), and let \(\mathfrak M(K_k,\mathcal H_{k-1})\) denote the admissible preconditioners for the current system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic Newton or Newton-Krylov systems. The definition specifies lifecycle control, not a particular factorization or convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A preconditioner lifecycle policy is a measurable rule \(\Pi_k:\mathcal H_{k-1}\times\{K_k\}\to\{\mathrm{reuse},\mathrm{update},\mathrm{rebuild}\}\times\mathfrak M(K_k,\mathcal H_{k-1})\). If \(\Pi_k=(a_k,M_k)\), then \(a_k=\mathrm{reuse}\) requires \(M_k=M_{k-1}\); \(a_k=\mathrm{update}\) requires \(M_k=\mathcal U_k(M_{k-1},K_{k-1},K_k,\mathcal H_{k-1})\); and \(a_k=\mathrm{rebuild}\) requires \(M_k=\mathcal B_k(K_k,\mathcal H_{k-1})\). The selected matrix is used in \(M_k^{-1}K_kz=M_k^{-1}b_k\), and the policy must define its action for every admissible history and current system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifecycle policy assigns, at every Newton system \(K_kz_k=b_k\), exactly one action—reuse, update, or rebuild—and an admissible nonsingular preconditioner \(M_k\). Reuse preserves \(M_{k-1}\); update applies a specified transformation \(\mathcal U_k\) to prior and current information; rebuild constructs \(M_k\) through \(\mathcal B_k\). The resulting preconditioned equation is \(M_k^{-1}K_kz=M_k^{-1}b_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(K_k\) and \(b_k\) are available when \(\Pi_k\) is evaluated.
Every returned \(M_k\) is nonsingular and dimensionally compatible with \(K_k\).
The diagnostics used by \(\Pi_k\) belong to the available history \(\mathcal H_{k-1}\); the policy does not use future information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Pi_k(\mathcal H_{k-1},K_k)=(a_k,M_k),\qquad a_k\in\{\mathrm{reuse},\mathrm{update},\mathrm{rebuild}\},\quad M_k\in\mathfrak M(K_k,\mathcal H_{k-1}).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The policy may equivalently be represented by disjoint decision regions \(R_k,U_k,B_k\) whose union is the admissible history-system space, together with the associated constructions of \(M_k\).
special_cases_latex: A periodic rebuild policy has \(a_k=\mathrm{rebuild}\) when \(k\equiv0\pmod q\) and \(a_k=\mathrm{reuse}\) otherwise.
A diagnostic-triggered policy rebuilds when an observed Krylov iteration count or residual-reduction factor exceeds a prescribed threshold.
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition separates the lifecycle decision from the algebraic type of \(M_k\).
A constant preconditioner is the special case \(a_k=\mathrm{reuse}\) for every \(k>0\).
boundary_notes: No spectral-equivalence, conditioning, or Krylov-complexity guarantee follows solely from this definition.
The inspected local sources discuss preconditioned Newton-CG constructions but do not provide this three-action lifecycle definition.

notation.meaning: Information history through outer iteration k.

review_flags: No inspected source states the exact reuse-update-rebuild policy as a canonical mathematical definition.
A precise authoritative locator is required before promotion.
knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Lifecycle Policy for a Newton-System Sequence
Preconditioner Reuse Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse is admissible while the preconditioned change in the Newton matrix remains uniformly below a chosen threshold; an exact reference preconditioner then remains nonsingular and close to identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J_k\) be the Newton matrix at outer iteration \(k\), and let \(P_r\) be a nonsingular preconditioner constructed at iteration \(r\). A reuse regime on indices \(k=r,\ldots,r+q\) is admissible when \[\|P_r^{-1}(J_k-J_r)\|\leq\eta<1\quad\text{for every }k=r,\ldots,r+q.\] If \(P_r=J_r\), then \(P_r^{-1}J_k=I+E_k\) with \(\|E_k\|\leq\eta\); hence every reused preconditioned matrix is nonsingular and differs from the identity by at most \(\eta\). For an approximate \(P_r\), the same policy applies after incorporating the baseline defect \(I-P_r^{-1}J_r\) into the admissibility threshold.
assumptions_latex: The norm is a consistent operator norm and \(\eta\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(P_r=J_r\), then \(P_r^{-1}J_k\) is nonsingular throughout the stated reuse regime and \(\|P_r^{-1}J_k-I\|\leq\eta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which one preconditioner may serve several neighboring Newton systems.

notation.meaning: Newton matrix at outer iteration k
preconditioner constructed at reference iteration r

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The exact-reference perturbation implication is mathematically standard, and condition is a suitable content kind for this lifecycle leaf. No source is registered for treating the displayed norm threshold as a preconditioner reuse regime or for the unspecified baseline-defect extension to approximate preconditioners.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Refresh Policies
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a new preconditioner when monitored Krylov performance exceeds a threshold or the current preconditioner reaches its maximum permitted age; otherwise reuse it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given Newton matrices \(J_k\), residuals \(b_k\), a preconditioner builder \(\mathcal B\), a refresh threshold \(\tau>0\), and a maximum reuse age \(q\), initialize \(r=0\) and \(P_r=\mathcal B(J_0)\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(J_ks_k=-b_k\) by a preconditioned Krylov method and record a performance indicator \(\rho_k\), such as the iteration count or achieved residual-contraction factor. Before iteration \(k+1\), set \[P_{k+1}=\mathcal B(J_{k+1}),\quad r=k+1\] if \(\rho_k>\tau\) or \(k+1-r\geq q\); otherwise retain \(P_{k+1}=P_r\). Stop according to the outer Newton termination test and return the final iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B(J)\) returns a nonsingular operator suitable for preconditioning \(J\).
\(\rho_k\) is computable after each inner solve, with \(\tau>0\) and integer \(q\geq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy reuses \(P_r\) for at most \(q\) consecutive outer iterations and refreshes it whenever \(\rho_k>\tau\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A monitored policy for updating a reusable preconditioner during successive Newton solves.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct role for this leaf, but the particular age/performance refresh rule has no cited source. Moreover, a single threshold comparison rho_k>tau is not uniformly meaningful when rho_k may denote either an iteration count or a residual-contraction factor; those diagnostics require separately defined scales and trigger conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Replacement Triggers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace the preconditioner when it is too old, Krylov work is excessive, residual reduction is inadequate, or the preconditioned Newton matrix has drifted too far.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_r\) be the current preconditioner, \(J_k\) the present Newton matrix, \(a_k=k-r\) its age, \(\nu_k\) the Krylov iteration count, and \(\gamma_k=\|r_{\mathrm{out}}\|/\|r_{\mathrm{in}}\|\) the achieved inner residual ratio. For prescribed limits \(q\in\mathbb N\), \(N_{\max}\in\mathbb N\), \(\bar\gamma\in(0,1)\), and \(\eta>0\), replacement is triggered when \[a_k\geq q\quad\text{or}\quad \nu_k>N_{\max}\quad\text{or}\quad \gamma_k>\bar\gamma\quad\text{or}\quad \|P_r^{-1}(J_k-J_r)\|>\eta.\] If any predicate holds, construct a new preconditioner from \(J_k\); otherwise continued reuse is permitted by this policy.
assumptions_latex: \(P_r\) is nonsingular and the displayed diagnostics are available or estimable.
All trigger thresholds are fixed before evaluating the replacement decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The replacement decision is the disjunction of the four displayed age, work, convergence, and matrix-drift predicates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observable conditions that force construction of a new preconditioning model.

notation.meaning: Krylov iterations used by the current solve

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the replacement-trigger container and the four predicates are internally understandable as a proposed policy. No evidence supports this particular disjunction, its thresholds, or the claim that continued reuse is permitted whenever all four tests are false.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Staleness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioner reuse is safely guaranteed below unit relative matrix drift. At unit drift, a rank-one change can make the new Newton matrix singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J_r\) be nonsingular and reuse the exact reference preconditioner \(P_r=J_r\) for \(J_k=J_r+\Delta_k\). If \(\|J_r^{-1}\Delta_k\|<1\), then \(J_k\) is nonsingular and \[\|J_k^{-1}\|\leq\frac{\|J_r^{-1}\|}{1-\|J_r^{-1}\Delta_k\|}.\] The strict boundary cannot be weakened to \(\leq1\): with \(J_r=I\) and \(\Delta_k=-uu^{\mathsf T}\) for any unit vector \(u\), one has \(\|J_r^{-1}\Delta_k\|=1\), while \(J_k=I-uu^{\mathsf T}\) is singular. Thus unit preconditioned drift is a sharp worst-case staleness boundary for norm-only guarantees.
assumptions_latex: The norm is a subordinate matrix norm; the sharp example uses its Euclidean specialization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condition \(\|J_r^{-1}\Delta_k\|<1\) guarantees nonsingularity, whereas equality at one permits the concrete singular example \(I-uu^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A perturbation boundary separating guaranteed safe reuse from possible singularity.

notation.meaning: change from the reference Newton matrix
unit vector defining the sharp rank-one example

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is exact, and the strict perturbation bound and Euclidean rank-one boundary example are mathematically coherent. A source with a specific theorem or section locator is required for the inverse perturbation estimate and sharp norm-only boundary claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Class of Newton Subspace Methods
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be differentiable, or let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable. At iteration \(k\), write \(J_k=F'(x_k)\), or \(H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\) and \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\). Let \(\mathcal S_k\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) have basis \(V_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_k}\) of full column rank.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equations and optimization. The class includes reduced, null-space, active-space, spectral, and Krylov realizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Newton subspace method is an iteration \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) in which \(p_k=V_ks_k\in\mathcal S_k\) and \(s_k\) is obtained from a restriction of the Newton model to \(\mathcal S_k\). For minimization, the canonical Galerkin restriction is \(V_k^TH_kV_ks_k=-V_k^Tg_k\). For nonlinear equations it is \(V_k^TJ_kV_ks_k=-V_k^TF(x_k)\) when trial and test spaces coincide. A globalization or truncation rule may select \(\alpha_k\), constrain \(s_k\), or terminate the reduced solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Newton subspace methods compute each step inside a selected space \(\mathcal S_k=\operatorname{range}(V_k)\). The reduced coordinates solve the Newton equation after its model and residual are projected onto that space. Thus the optimization form is \(V_k^TH_kV_ks_k=-V_k^Tg_k\), with full step \(p_k=V_ks_k\); an analogous projected Jacobian equation applies to nonlinear systems.
assumptions_latex: \(V_k\) has full column rank and \(1\le r_k\le n\).
The reduced equation is solvable, or a specified regularized, truncated, or least-squares reduced solution is used.
Any constraints imposed on the step are incorporated through the definition of \(\mathcal S_k\) or an explicitly constrained reduced model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p_k\in\mathcal S_k,\qquad p_k=V_ks_k,\qquad V_k^T(H_kp_k+g_k)=0\] for the unconstrained optimization form.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(V_k^TV_k=I\), the defining stationarity condition is \(P_k(H_kp_k+g_k)=0\), where \(P_k=V_kV_k^T\).
The reduced step is a stationary point of \(m_k(V_ks)=f(x_k)+g_k^TV_ks+\tfrac12s^TV_k^TH_kV_ks\).
special_cases_latex: \(V_k=I\) gives the ordinary Newton equation.
Choosing \(\mathcal S_k\) as a Krylov space gives Newton-CG or Newton-Lanczos-type steps.
Choosing \(\mathcal S_k=\ker A_k\) gives a null-space reduced Newton step.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only products of the Newton operator with columns or generated vectors in \(\mathcal S_k\) may be required.
The reduced system has dimension \(r_k\), which may be much smaller than \(n\).
boundary_notes: Petrov-Galerkin methods with distinct trial and test spaces require replacing \(V_k^T\) by a separate test basis.
Subspace membership alone does not guarantee adequate decrease, feasibility, or convergence.

notation.meaning: Basis matrix for the selected Newton trial space.
Orthogonal projector when the basis is orthonormal.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton Method Restricted to a Selected Subspace
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable. At \(x_k\), set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\), and select \(\mathcal S_k=\operatorname{range}(V_k)\) with full-column-rank \(V_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_k}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional unconstrained minimization; constrained variants arise by choosing a feasible or tangent subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Newton subspace step is any \(p_k=V_ks_k\) whose coordinates satisfy the restricted Newton stationarity equation \(V_k^T(H_kV_ks_k+g_k)=0\). If \(V_k^TH_kV_k\) is nonsingular, the step is uniquely \(p_k=-V_k(V_k^TH_kV_k)^{-1}V_k^Tg_k\). A Newton subspace method generates \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), with \(\alpha_k>0\) supplied by its local or global acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method selects a subspace \(\mathcal S_k\), restricts the quadratic Newton model to that space, solves its reduced stationarity equation, lifts the coordinate solution to \(p_k=V_ks_k\), and updates \(x_k\). When the reduced Hessian is nonsingular, the lifted step has the explicit formula \(-V_k(V_k^TH_kV_k)^{-1}V_k^Tg_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable at every iterate where the step is defined.
For the explicit inverse formula, \(V_k^TH_kV_k\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[V_k^T(H_kp_k+g_k)=0,
\qquad p_k\in\mathcal S_k,
\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(s_k\) is a stationary point of \(\phi_k(s)=g_k^TV_ks+\tfrac12s^TV_k^TH_kV_ks\).
If \(V_k^TV_k=I\), then the Newton residual is orthogonal to \(\mathcal S_k\): \(H_kp_k+g_k\perp\mathcal S_k\).
special_cases_latex: The full-space choice \(r_k=n\) and nonsingular \(V_k\) recovers the ordinary Newton step.
A Krylov basis generated from \(g_k\) and \(H_k\) produces a truncated Newton step.
A null-space basis produces a tangent or feasible reduced step.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive definiteness of \(V_k^TH_kV_k\) makes \(p_k\) the unique minimizer of the restricted quadratic model.
Changing the basis to \(V_kR\), with nonsingular \(R\), leaves the physical step invariant.
boundary_notes: An indefinite or singular reduced Hessian requires an explicitly specified truncation, regularization, or trust-region rule.
This definition does not assert that the selected subspace captures the full Newton direction.

notation.meaning: Quadratic Newton model in reduced coordinates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Subspace Newton Iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable and let a single subspace \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{range}(V)\) be prescribed before the iteration, where \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional minimization on the affine space \(x_0+\mathcal S\). The subspace is fixed, although the gradient and Hessian vary with the iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fixed-subspace Newton method is the iteration \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kVs_k\), where the same basis range \(\operatorname{range}(V)=\mathcal S\) is used for every \(k\), and \(s_k\) satisfies \(V^T\nabla^2f(x_k)V s_k=-V^T\nabla f(x_k)\). If the reduced Hessian is nonsingular, \(s_k\) is unique. Consequently every iterate satisfies \(x_k-x_0\in\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-subspace Newton applies Newton's method to the reduced objective \(\widehat f(y)=f(x_0+Vy)\). At each iteration it solves the reduced Newton equation using the same prescribed space \(\mathcal S\), lifts the result by \(V\), and therefore remains in the affine set \(x_0+\mathcal S\).
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is independent of \(k\) and has rank \(r\).
\(f\) is twice differentiable on the relevant part of \(x_0+\mathcal S\).
The reduced system is solvable; uniqueness requires \(V^T\nabla^2f(x_k)V\) to be nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[V^T\nabla^2f(x_k)V s_k=-V^T\nabla f(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kVs_k\in x_0+\mathcal S.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(x_k=x_0+Vy_k\), the coordinate update is ordinary Newton applied to \(\widehat f(y)=f(x_0+Vy)\).
For orthonormal \(V\), the lifted residual is orthogonal to the fixed space: \(V^T(\nabla^2f(x_k)Vs_k+\nabla f(x_k))=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(V=I\), the method is full-space Newton.
If \(V=Z\) spans the null space of a fixed equality-constraint matrix, all steps are feasible tangent displacements.
immediate_consequences_latex: The method can converge only to stationarity relative to \(\mathcal S\), characterized by \(V^T\nabla f(x)=0\).
Changing coordinates within \(\mathcal S\) does not change the lifted step.
boundary_notes: A fixed subspace need not contain a full-space stationary point or the full Newton direction.
A changing active set or changing Krylov space belongs to adaptive-subspace Newton, not this definition.

notation.meaning: Objective restricted to fixed reduced coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Subspace Newton
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive-subspace Newton repeatedly chooses a reduced space from current geometry or solver history, solves the projected Newton equation, and updates the space after accepting a step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(x_0\), at iteration \(k\) select a full-column-rank basis \(V_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times p_k}\) from information available through iteration \(k\), such as gradients, curvature vectors, or retained Krylov vectors. With \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\), solve \[(V_k^{\mathsf T}H_kV_k)y_k=-V_k^{\mathsf T}g_k,\qquad s_k=V_ky_k.\] Accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_ks_k\) through the outer globalization rule, update the information used to choose \(V_{k+1}\), and stop at the prescribed stationarity test. Each computed step satisfies projected Newton stationarity in its current subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable near the iterates.
Each \(V_k\) has full column rank and \(V_k^{\mathsf T}H_kV_k\) is nonsingular when solved.
The choice of \(V_k\) uses no information from future iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every computed step, \(s_k\in\operatorname{range}(V_k)\) and \(V_k^{\mathsf T}(H_ks_k+g_k)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced Newton iteration whose subspace may change with local derivatives or solver history.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adaptive-Subspace Newton Iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable. Let \(\mathcal H_k\) contain the iterates, derivatives, linear-solver vectors, active-set estimates, and acceptance diagnostics available at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional minimization with iteration-dependent reduced spaces selected from available local information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adaptive-subspace Newton method consists of a selection map \(\Sigma_k:\mathcal H_k\to\mathrm{Gr}(r_k,n)\), a basis \(V_k\) of \(\mathcal S_k=\Sigma_k(\mathcal H_k)\), and an update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kV_ks_k\), where \(s_k\) satisfies \(V_k^T\nabla^2f(x_k)V_ks_k=-V_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\). Adaptivity means that \(\Sigma_k\) is permitted to change the range or dimension of \(V_k\) in response to \(\mathcal H_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive-subspace Newton recomputes or modifies the step space at each outer iteration using information already observed. It then solves the Newton equation projected onto that selected space and lifts the reduced solution. Unlike fixed-subspace Newton, neither \(\operatorname{range}(V_k)\) nor its dimension must remain constant.
assumptions_latex: Every selected \(V_k\) has full column rank.
The reduced system is solved exactly or by a separately specified inexactness rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal S_k=\Sigma_k(\mathcal H_k),\qquad p_k=V_ks_k,\qquad V_k^T(\nabla^2f(x_k)p_k+\nabla f(x_k))=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The method is a variable-coordinate Newton method for the iteration-dependent local model \(s\mapsto f(x_k)+g_k^TV_ks+\tfrac12s^TV_k^TH_kV_ks\).
special_cases_latex: Newton-CG selects successive Krylov spaces generated by \(H_k\) and \(g_k\).
An active-set realization selects the null space of the current working-set Jacobian.
A spectral realization selects approximate curvature modes obtained from Lanczos information.
immediate_consequences_latex: The physical iterates need not lie in one fixed affine subspace.
Selection quality and reduced-solve accuracy are logically separate components.
boundary_notes: Merely changing the basis while preserving its range is not a substantive subspace adaptation.
No convergence follows without adequacy, decrease, and globalization conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Management Rule for a Sequence of Newton Subspaces
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal S_{k,j}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) denote the subspace used after \(j\) inner enrichments during outer Newton iteration \(k\). Let \(E_{k,j}\) be proposed enrichment directions and let \(C_{k,j}\) be directions retained across an update or restart.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional adaptive Newton methods that enrich, compress, retain, or restart trial spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subspace sequence management rule is a map \(\mathcal M_{k,j}\) that assigns the next space and an action label from the current space and available diagnostics: \((a_{k,j},\mathcal S_{k,j+1})=\mathcal M_{k,j}(\mathcal S_{k,j},E_{k,j},C_{k,j},\mathcal H_{k,j})\). Enrichment requires \(\mathcal S_{k,j+1}=\mathcal S_{k,j}+\operatorname{span}(E_{k,j})\); compression requires \(\mathcal S_{k,j+1}\subseteq\mathcal S_{k,j}+\operatorname{span}(E_{k,j})\); restart requires \(\mathcal S_{k,j+1}=\operatorname{span}(C_{k,j})\); and retention across outer iterations requires \(C_{k+1,0}\subseteq\mathcal S_{k,j_{m final}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subspace sequence management is a formally specified rule for deciding how one trial space becomes the next. It labels each transition as enrichment, compression, restart, or retention and imposes the corresponding inclusion or equality between the old space, new directions, retained directions, and the next space.
assumptions_latex: All proposed and retained vectors belong to the ambient step space.
The rule specifies a finite-dimensional next space for every admissible diagnostic state.
Any maximum-dimension restriction is included in the compression or restart map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(a_{k,j},\mathcal S_{k,j+1})=\mathcal M_{k,j}(\mathcal S_{k,j},E_{k,j},C_{k,j},\mathcal H_{k,j})\] with the transition relation determined by \(a_{k,j}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using basis matrices, enrichment can be written \(V_{k,j+1}=\operatorname{basis}[V_{k,j}\ E_{k,j}]\), with linearly dependent columns removed.
special_cases_latex: Unrestarted Krylov generation uses enrichment only.
Restarted Krylov Newton retains a prescribed subset of Ritz or residual directions.
Changing active constraints deletes or adds null-space directions and therefore induces compression or enrichment.
immediate_consequences_latex: The rule distinguishes the evolution of the trial space from solution of the reduced Newton equation.
A dimension cap forces compression or restart after sufficiently many independent enrichments.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe which diagnostics should trigger a transition.
The inspected sources describe Krylov generation and null-space updates but not this complete four-action taxonomy.

notation.meaning: Directions selected for retention or restart.

knowledge_statements.title: Management Rule for a Sequence of Newton Subspaces
Nested Subspace Sequences
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite quadratic Newton model, enlarging nested subspaces monotonically improves the best model value and cannot increase energy-norm error to the full Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal V_0\subseteq\mathcal V_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nested subspaces, and let \(q(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs\) with symmetric positive-definite \(H\). For each \(j\), let \(s_j\) be the unique minimizer of \(q\) over \(\mathcal V_j\). Then \[q(s_{j+1})\leq q(s_j),\qquad \|s_{j+1}-s_*\|_H\leq\|s_j-s_*\|_H,\] where \(s_*=-H^{-1}g\) and \(\|v\|_H=(v^{\mathsf T}Hv)^{1/2}\). Thus nested enrichment cannot worsen the optimal quadratic-model value or the energy-norm error of the reduced Newton step.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite.
The finite-dimensional subspaces satisfy \(\mathcal V_j\subseteq\mathcal V_{j+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(s_{j+1})\leq q(s_j)\) and \(\|s_{j+1}-s_*\|_H\leq\|s_j-s_*\|_H\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone enrichment of reduced Newton spaces and its effect on quadratic-model minimization.

notation.meaning: quadratic-model minimizer over the j-th space

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits nested subspace sequences, and the positive-definite quadratic formulation is precise. The cited locator appears to identify a general discussion of sequences rather than the claimed monotonic model-value and energy-norm approximation property; a direct theorem, proposition, or relevant subsection is needed.
