knowledge_statements.title: Restarted Subspace Sequences
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restarted sequence enriches a reduced Newton space only to a fixed dimension, then discards and rebuilds the basis while retaining the outer method's acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a maximum dimension \(p_{\max}\geq1\), a seed rule \(\mathcal S\), and an enrichment rule \(\mathcal E\). At cycle \(c\), initialize \(V_{c,0}=\mathcal S(x_c)\). For \(j=0,\ldots,p_{\max}-1\), solve the Newton model projected onto \(\operatorname{range}(V_{c,j})\), test the prescribed inner stopping condition, and otherwise set \[V_{c,j+1}=\operatorname{orth}\!\left([V_{c,j},\mathcal E(x_c,V_{c,j})]\right).\] If the test has not passed when the dimension limit is reached, accept or reject the available step according to the outer rule, discard the current basis, set the next cycle seed from \(\mathcal S\), and continue. The stored basis dimension never exceeds \(p_{\max}\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) returns a nonempty full-rank seed basis.
\(\mathcal E\) supplies candidate directions, and \(\operatorname{orth}\) removes linear dependence.
The projected Newton model is solvable on every accepted basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At all inner iterations, \(\dim\operatorname{range}(V_{c,j})\leq p_{\max}\), and failure to stop at the limit initiates a new basis cycle.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-dimension subspace Newton iteration with periodic discard and reconstruction of the basis.

notation.meaning: basis at inner index j of restart cycle c

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is appropriate for this leaf, but no source supports the proposed seed, enrichment, restart, and outer acceptance procedure. The update also needs an explicit truncation or rejection rule when orthogonalized enrichment would make the basis exceed p_max; the loop bound alone does not guarantee the stated dimension limit for block enrichment.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Restart Enrichment
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-restart enrichment carries selected old-space directions into the new seed basis, combines them with fresh directions, and orthogonalizes under the same storage limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At the end of restart cycle \(c\), let \(V_c\) be the discarded basis and choose a retention matrix \(Y_c\in\mathbb R^{p_c\times\ell}\) with \(\ell<p_{\max}\). Form retained directions \(U_c=V_cY_c\). Given a fresh seed block \(W_{c+1}\), initialize the next cycle by \[V_{c+1,0}=\operatorname{orth}\!\left([U_c,W_{c+1}]\right),\qquad \dim\operatorname{range}(V_{c+1,0})\leq p_{\max}.\] The columns selected through \(Y_c\) may represent approximate invariant, curvature, multiplier-coupling, or previously successful step directions. Subsequent enrichment follows the restarted sequence until the dimension limit or stopping test is reached. Thus selected information crosses the restart while bounded storage is preserved.
assumptions_latex: \(V_c\) has full column rank and \(Y_c\) selects at most \(\ell<p_{\max}\) retained combinations.
The concatenated block is orthogonalized with dependent directions removed.
The retained and fresh blocks fit within the prescribed dimension limit after truncation if necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(V_cY_c)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(V_{c+1,0})\) and \(\dim\operatorname{range}(V_{c+1,0})\leq p_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restarted subspace construction that retains selected directions from the preceding cycle.

notation.meaning: matrix selecting combinations retained from cycle c
fresh seed block for the next cycle

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits cross-restart enrichment, but no direct source is provided. The asserted inclusion range(V_cY_c) subseteq range(V_{c+1,0}) is not guaranteed if the permitted truncation removes retained directions; a sourced method must specify that retained directions are protected or weaken the conclusion accordingly.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Information-Loss Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite Newton model, restart loss equals half the squared energy norm of the discarded correction; a prescribed loss budget gives an exact restart boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite, let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and define \(q(p)=g^Tp+\tfrac12p^THp\). For nested subspaces \(W\subseteq S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(p_U=\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in U}q(p)\) for \(U\in\{W,S\}\). Then
\[
q(p_W)-q(p_S)=\tfrac12\lVert p_S-p_W\rVert_H^2,
\qquad \lVert z\rVert_H^2=z^THz.
\]
Thus a restart from \(S\) to \(W\) respects a model-loss budget \(\varepsilon\ge0\) exactly when \(\lVert p_S-p_W\rVert_H\le\sqrt{2\varepsilon}\). Crossing this boundary means that the discarded subspace component causes model-value loss exceeding \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(p_W)-q(p_S)=\tfrac12\lVert p_S-p_W\rVert_H^2\), with admissible restart iff \(\lVert p_S-p_W\rVert_H\le\sqrt{2\varepsilon}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies the model-value information discarded when an SPD Newton subspace is restarted.

notation.meaning: model minimizer restricted to subspace U

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Newton Model Restricted to a Subspace
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable at \(x\), with \(g=\nabla f(x)\) and symmetric \(H=\nabla^2f(x)\). Let \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{range}(V)\), where \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional minimization; the model is local and may be convex, indefinite, or singular on the selected space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The subspace Newton model is the quadratic function \(\widehat m(s)=f(x)+(V^Tg)^Ts+\tfrac12s^T(V^THV)s\) on \(\mathbb R^r\), equivalently the restriction \(m(p)=f(x)+g^Tp+\tfrac12p^THp\) to \(p\in\mathcal S\) through \(p=Vs\). Its reduced gradient is \(V^Tg\), its reduced Hessian is \(V^THV\), and its stationary coordinates satisfy \(V^THV s=-V^Tg\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace Newton model is the ordinary quadratic Newton model evaluated only on steps in \(\mathcal S\). In basis coordinates it has linear coefficient \(V^Tg\) and curvature matrix \(V^THV\); solving its stationarity equation produces the reduced Newton coordinates.
assumptions_latex: No definiteness assumption is required to define the model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widehat m(s)=f(x)+g^TVs+\frac12s^TV^THVs,\qquad \nabla\widehat m(s)=V^Tg+V^THVs.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\widehat m=m\circ V\), where \(m(p)=f(x)+g^Tp+\tfrac12p^THp\).
With orthonormal \(V\), the model acts on the orthogonal projection coordinates of steps in \(\mathcal S\).
special_cases_latex: For \(V=I\), \(\widehat m\) is the full Newton model.
For \(V=Z\) spanning a constraint null space, \(V^THV\) is the reduced Hessian.
For a Krylov basis \(Q_j\), \(Q_j^THQ_j\) is the small projected matrix used by Newton-Lanczos.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(V^THV\succ0\), the model has a unique minimizer.
The model is invariant under a change of subspace coordinates when the coordinate vector is transformed consistently.
boundary_notes: An indefinite reduced Hessian makes stationarity different from minimization.
A trust-region or regularized subspace model adds constraints or terms not included in this canonical definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Newton Equation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representing the step in a basis and imposing Galerkin orthogonality converts the Newton equation into a smaller coordinate system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\) have full column rank. Restrict the Newton step to \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{range}(V)\) by writing \(p=Vy\). Requiring the residual \(r=HVy+g\) to be orthogonal to \(\mathcal S\) yields the reduced Newton equation
\[
(V^THV)y=-V^Tg.
\]
If \(V^THV\) is nonsingular, the unique reduced step is \(p=-V(V^THV)^{-1}V^Tg\). When \(V\) is square and nonsingular, this step is the full Newton solution of \(Hp=-g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((V^THV)y=-V^Tg\) and \(p=Vy\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Galerkin coordinate form of an unconstrained Newton equation on a prescribed subspace.

notation.meaning: reduced coordinates of the Newton step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced Newton Equation Induced by a Basis
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let the full Newton equation be \(Hp=-g\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), with symmetric \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(g\in\mathbb R^n\). Let \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) have full column rank and set \(p=Vs\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Galerkin reduction with identical trial and test spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The reduced Newton equation associated with \(V\) is \((V^THV)s=-V^Tg\). A solution \(s\in\mathbb R^r\) defines the lifted step \(p=Vs\), whose full residual \(r=Hp+g\) satisfies \(V^Tr=0\). When \(V^THV\) is nonsingular, the coordinate and lifted solutions are unique for the selected subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substituting a subspace step \(p=Vs\) into the Newton equation and imposing Galerkin orthogonality yields the coordinate system \(V^THV s=-V^Tg\). Its solution is lifted to the original variables, and the resulting Newton residual is orthogonal to every column of \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(V^THV)s=-V^Tg,\qquad p=Vs,\qquad V^T(Hp+g)=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The equation is the first-order stationarity condition for \(g^TVs+\tfrac12s^TV^THVs\).
If \(V^TV=I\) and \(P=VV^T\), it is equivalent to \(P(Hp+g)=0\) together with \(p\in\operatorname{range}(V)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(V=I\), it is the full Newton equation.
For a null-space basis \(Z\), it becomes the reduced-Hessian equation used in equality-constrained quadratic programming.
For a Krylov basis, it is the small projected linear system underlying a Krylov Newton step.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(V^THV\succ0\), the lifted step uniquely minimizes the quadratic model over \(\operatorname{range}(V)\).
The lifted solution is unchanged by replacing \(V\) by \(VR\) with nonsingular \(R\).
boundary_notes: For distinct trial and test bases, the reduced equation is Petrov-Galerkin rather than the equation defined here.
A singular reduced matrix may admit no solution or multiple solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected KKT Newton System
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible particular step plus null-space coordinates reduces the equality-constrained KKT Newton system to a tangent-space equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the linearized equality-constrained Newton system with symmetric \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), full-row-rank \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), gradient residual \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and constraint residual \(c\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Choose \(Z\) with \(AZ=0\) and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\), and choose \(p_0\) satisfying \(Ap_0=-c\). Then \(p=p_0+Zy\), where
\[
(Z^THZ)y=-Z^T(g+Hp_0).
\]
After computing \(p\), any \(\delta\lambda\) satisfying \(A^T\delta\lambda=-(g+Hp)\) completes the KKT solution. If \(Z^THZ\) is nonsingular, the primal step is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=p_0+Zy\) with \((Z^THZ)y=-Z^T(g+Hp_0)\), followed by multiplier recovery.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space projection of an equality-constrained primal-dual Newton system.

notation.meaning: basis for the constraint null space

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Galerkin Projection of a Primal-Dual Newton System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\) be a KKT Newton matrix and let \(r=(r_d,r_p)\) be its primal-dual residual. Choose full-column-rank primal and multiplier bases \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\) and \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times t}\), and set \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(U,W)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric Galerkin projection of equality-constrained or primal-dual Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The projected KKT Newton system associated with \((U,W)\) is \((Q^TKQ)y=-Q^Tr\), with lifted correction \((p,\delta\lambda)=Qy\). In block form, for \(y=(s,	au)\), it is \(\begin{bmatrix}U^THU&U^TA^TW\\W^TAU&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}s\\\tau\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}U^Tr_d\\W^Tr_p\end{bmatrix}\). The lifted KKT residual is orthogonal to \(\operatorname{range}(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected KKT Newton system restricts primal and multiplier corrections to selected spaces, projects both block equations onto corresponding test spaces, solves the smaller saddle-point system, and lifts its coordinates to a full primal-dual correction.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and the residual blocks have compatible dimensions.
Uniqueness requires the projected saddle-point matrix \(Q^TKQ\) to be nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q^T\bigl(KQy+r\bigr)=0,\qquad (p,\delta\lambda)=Qy.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The correction is a Galerkin approximation to \(Kz=-r\) in the block trial space \(\operatorname{range}(U)\times\operatorname{range}(W)\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(U=I\) and \(W=I\) gives the full KKT Newton system.
If \(U=Z\) with \(AZ=0\) and feasibility is handled separately, the primal equation reduces to a reduced-Hessian system.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only the projected blocks \(U^THU\) and \(W^TAU\) are needed for the reduced solve.
The lifted residual is generally nonzero outside the test space.
boundary_notes: This definition uses identical block trial and test bases; oblique projections require separate test matrices.
The inspected equality-constrained Newton sources state full KKT and null-space systems but not this exact two-space projected definition.

children.title: Reduced-Hessian Subspace Model
children.top_down_role: Curvature represented on a tangent, null, or active space.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian Subspace Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a quadratic Newton model to subspace coordinates replaces the gradient and Hessian by their projected counterparts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(p)=f_0+g^Tp+\tfrac12p^THp\), where \(H=H^T\), and let \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\) have full column rank. Under the coordinate restriction \(p=Vy\), the subspace model is
\[
\widehat q(y)=q(Vy)=f_0+(V^Tg)^Ty+\tfrac12y^T(V^THV)y.
\]
Its gradient and Hessian are \(\nabla\widehat q(y)=V^Tg+V^THVy\) and \(\nabla^2\widehat q(y)=V^THV\). If \(V\) spans the tangent or null space of active constraints, \(V^THV\) is the reduced Hessian governing feasible second-order curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat q(y)=f_0+(V^Tg)^Ty+\tfrac12y^T(V^THV)y\), with reduced Hessian \(V^THV\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic Newton model restricted to tangent or selected subspace coordinates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced-Hessian Model on a Tangent or Null Space
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) be the Hessian of an objective or Lagrangian at a current point. Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(AZ=0\). Let \(p_Y\) be a particular normal correction when one is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained or active-set Newton models in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The reduced Hessian is \(H_R=Z^THZ\). The reduced-Hessian subspace model for tangent coordinates \(s\) is \(\widehat m(s)=m(p_Y)+[Z^T(g+Hp_Y)]^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_Rs\), with lifted step \(p=p_Y+Zs\). Its stationary equation is \(H_Rs=-Z^T(g+Hp_Y)\). For a feasible tangent step, \(p_Y=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model represents curvature only along directions satisfying the linearized constraints. A null-space basis \(Z\) maps reduced coordinates to tangent displacements, the curvature matrix becomes \(Z^THZ\), and any required normal correction contributes to the reduced linear term.
assumptions_latex: No definiteness is required for definition; uniqueness of the stationary coordinate requires nonsingularity of \(H_R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[H_R=Z^THZ,
\qquad H_Rs=-Z^T(g+Hp_Y),
\qquad p=p_Y+Zs.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(H_R\) is the coordinate representation of the quadratic form \(d\mapsto d^THd\) restricted to \(\ker A\).
Positive definiteness of \(H_R\) is positive definiteness of \(H\) on nonzero tangent directions.
special_cases_latex: For a feasible equality-constrained Newton step, \(p_Y=0\) and \(H_Rs=-Z^Tg\).
For an active set, \(A\) is the working-set Jacobian.
With orthonormal \(Z\), the spectrum is independent of scaling artifacts in the basis.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(H_R\succ0\), the restricted quadratic model has a unique minimizer.
Different null-space bases give congruent reduced Hessians and the same tangent quadratic form.
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness of the full Hessian is sufficient but not necessary for \(H_R\succ0\).
A rank-deficient constraint Jacobian requires a rank-revealing basis construction or removal of redundant constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Families of Newton Subspace Selection Maps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal D_k\) denote the derivative, constraint, residual, and solver data available at iteration \(k\). Let \(\mathrm{Sub}(\mathbb R^n)\) be the set of linear subspaces of \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth Newton methods. The definition classifies selection mechanisms by the mathematical information used to generate the space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Newton subspace selection family is a collection of maps \(\Sigma_k:\mathcal D_k\to\mathrm{Sub}(\mathbb R^n)\). It is active or tangent based when \(\Sigma_k(\mathcal D_k)=\ker A_k\) for a selected constraint Jacobian; Krylov based when it equals \(\mathcal K_j(H_k,g_k)=\operatorname{span}\{g_k,H_kg_k,\ldots,H_k^{j-1}g_k\}\); and curvature based when it is generated by exact or approximate invariant vectors of \(H_k\). A hybrid family returns a sum or intersection of such spaces when dimensionally well-defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selection family is a formally specified map from current Newton data to a trial subspace. Canonical families use an active constraint null space, a Krylov sequence generated by the Newton operator and residual, or curvature modes approximating invariant directions. Hybrid selectors combine these constructions.
assumptions_latex: The selector uses only available data \(\mathcal D_k\).
The returned set is a linear subspace with a computable full-rank basis.
For a null-space selector, the rank used to define \(\ker A_k\) is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal S_k=\Sigma_k(\mathcal D_k)\in\mathrm{Sub}(\mathbb R^n).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A selector may equivalently return a basis matrix \(V_k\), with two outputs identified when their column ranges coincide.
special_cases_latex: Newton-CG uses the Krylov family.
Equality-constrained null-space Newton uses the tangent family.
Newton-Lanczos uses a Krylov basis whose projected Hessian is tridiagonal.
immediate_consequences_latex: The same physical space may have many basis representations.
Selection and reduced-model solution are distinct maps and can be analyzed separately.
boundary_notes: Coordinate subsets are included only when their spans are explicitly defined.
A nonlinear manifold is represented here by its linear tangent space at the current point, not by the manifold itself.

notation.meaning: Data available to the subspace selector.

children.title: Krylov Subspace Newton Steps
children.top_down_role: Subspaces generated by repeated Newton-operator actions.

knowledge_statements.title: Krylov Subspace Newton Steps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build an orthonormal Krylov basis from repeated Hessian actions, solve the projected Newton equation on each current subspace, and stop at the residual tolerance, the dimension cap, or exact invariant-subspace breakdown.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a symmetric matrix \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), a nonzero vector \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a tolerance \(\eta\in[0,1)\), and a maximum dimension \(m_{\max}\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Set \(v_1=g/\lVert g\rVert_2\) and \(V_1=[v_1]\). For \(m=1,\ldots,m_{\max}\), solve
\[
(V_m^THV_m)y_m=-V_m^Tg,
\qquad p_m=V_my_m,
\qquad r_m=Hp_m+g.
\]
Return \(p_m\) if \(\lVert r_m\rVert_2\le\eta\lVert g\rVert_2\) or if \(m=m_{\max}\). Otherwise, orthogonalize \(Hv_m\) against the columns of \(V_m\), including reorthogonalization when required, to obtain a vector \(w_m\). If \(w_m=0\), return \(p_m\); in exact arithmetic the Krylov space is then invariant under \(H\), and Galerkin orthogonality gives \(r_m=0\). If \(w_m\ne0\), set \(v_{m+1}=w_m/\lVert w_m\rVert_2\) and \(V_{m+1}=[V_m,v_{m+1}]\). At iteration \(m\), the columns of \(V_m\) span
\[
\mathcal K_m(H,g)=\operatorname{span}\{g,Hg,\ldots,H^{m-1}g\}.
\]
assumptions_latex: Each reduced system solved before termination is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each output satisfies \(p_m\in\mathcal K_m(H,g)\); it satisfies \(\lVert Hp_m+g\rVert_2\le\eta\lVert g\rVert_2\) when the residual test or exact-breakdown test triggers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Galerkin Newton steps generated by successive applications of the Newton operator.

notation.meaning: full Newton residual at iteration m

review_flags: exact Krylov breakdown behavior made explicit

children.title: Active-Subspace Newton Steps

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Subspace Newton Steps
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose free or tangent directions from the active-set estimate, solve the Newton equation there, and lift the reduced correction to the full space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input \(H=H^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and an identified free or tangent subspace with full-column-rank basis \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\). Form \(H_V=V^THV\) and \(g_V=V^Tg\). If \(H_V\) is nonsingular, solve
\[
H_Vy=-g_V
\]
and output \(p=Vy\). For an active-variable selection, the omitted coordinates of \(p\) are zero. For an active-constraint selection with Jacobian \(A_{\mathcal A}\), require \(A_{\mathcal A}V=0\), so the output obeys \(A_{\mathcal A}p=0\) and is tangent to the currently identified active manifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=-V(V^THV)^{-1}V^Tg\), with \(A_{\mathcal A}p=0\) in the active-constraint case.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton correction restricted to variables or tangent directions selected by an active-set estimate.

notation.meaning: basis of selected free or tangent directions

review_flags: active-subspace formulation covers fixed identified active sets

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton Step on an Identified Active Tangent Space
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider smooth constraints \(c_i(x)=0\) and \(h_j(x)\ge0\). At \(x_k\), let \(\mathcal A_k\) be a selected active index set and let \(A_k\) have rows \(\nabla c_i(x_k)^T\) and \(\nabla h_j(x_k)^T\) for \(j\in\mathcal A_k\). Let \(Z_k\) span \(\ker A_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality- and inequality-constrained Newton or SQP models after an active set has been selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An active-subspace Newton step has the decomposition \(p_k=p_k^N+Z_ks_k\), where \(A_kp_k^N=-r_{p,k}\) supplies any required linearized-feasibility correction and \(s_k\) solves \((Z_k^TH_kZ_k)s_k=-Z_k^T(g_k+H_kp_k^N)\). If the current point is feasible for the selected constraints, one may take \(p_k^N=0\), so the step lies entirely in the active tangent space \(\ker A_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After choosing the constraints treated as active, form their Jacobian and its null space. The Newton correction is a normal component restoring linearized feasibility plus a tangent component found from the reduced-Hessian equation on that null space.
assumptions_latex: The selected active-constraint Jacobian \(A_k\) has the rank used to construct \(Z_k\).
\(H_k\) is the chosen Hessian or Lagrangian-Hessian model.
The normal equation and reduced equation are solvable; uniqueness of the tangent coordinates requires nonsingularity of \(Z_k^TH_kZ_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A_k(p_k^N+Z_ks_k)=-r_{p,k},\qquad Z_k^T(H_k(p_k^N+Z_ks_k)+g_k)=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The step satisfies the KKT equations for the quadratic model with the selected constraints imposed as equalities.
When feasible, it is the stationary point of the quadratic model restricted to \(\ker A_k\).
special_cases_latex: With only equality constraints, \(\mathcal A_k\) is fixed to all constraints.
For bound constraints, \(Z_k\) selects the currently free variables.
On an identified smooth manifold, \(Z_k\) is a basis of its tangent space.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing the active set changes the dimension or orientation of the Newton subspace.
If \(Z_k^TH_kZ_k\succ0\), the tangent component uniquely minimizes the restricted quadratic model.
boundary_notes: An incorrect active set can exclude useful directions or impose spurious tangency.
Rank changes require a rank-revealing basis update.

children.title: Null-Space Newton Bases
children.top_down_role: Constraint-tangent bases for equality-constrained and SQP systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Newton Bases
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null-space basis parametrizes every tangent step and converts the constrained Newton equation into a reduced system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and let \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with
\[
AZ=0,
\qquad \operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A.
\]
Then every homogeneous linearized-feasible step \(p\) satisfying \(Ap=0\) has the unique representation \(p=Zy\). For a quadratic Newton model with symmetric Hessian \(H\) and gradient \(g\), stationarity over these tangent steps is equivalent to
\[
(Z^THZ)y=-Z^Tg.
\]
If \(Z^THZ\) is nonsingular, this equation defines the unique tangent-space Newton step.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is a basis matrix for \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ap=0\) iff \(p=Zy\), and tangent Newton stationarity is \((Z^THZ)y=-Z^Tg\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis representation of equality-constraint tangent directions and their reduced Newton equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basis of the Constraint-Tangent Null Space
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(m<n\). The linearized feasible or tangent directions are the vectors \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ad=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained Newton and SQP systems under full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A null-space Newton basis is a matrix \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) such that \(AZ=0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}Z=n-m\). Hence \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\), and every tangent step has a unique coordinate representation \(d=Zs\). An orthonormal null-space basis additionally satisfies \(Z^TZ=I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null-space Newton basis contains exactly enough independent columns to span all directions annihilated by the constraint Jacobian. It converts unconstrained reduced coordinates into linearized feasible displacements; orthonormal bases also preserve Euclidean coordinate norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[AZ=0,\qquad \operatorname{rank}Z=n-m,\qquad \operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(A^T=QR\) is a full QR factorization with \(Q=[Q_1\ Q_2]\), then \(Z=Q_2\) is an orthonormal null-space basis.
The orthogonal projector onto the tangent space is \(P=ZZ^T\) when \(Z^TZ=I\).
special_cases_latex: For bound constraints, columns of \(Z\) may be coordinate vectors corresponding to free variables.
If \(m=0\), the identity matrix is a null-space basis.
In SQP, \(A\) may be the Jacobian of the current equality constraints and selected active inequalities.
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduced Hessian is \(Z^THZ\).
Any step \(d=Zs\) satisfies the homogeneous linearized constraints exactly.
Different bases of the same null space are related by a nonsingular coordinate transformation.
boundary_notes: If \(A\) is rank deficient, the stated column count must use \(n-\operatorname{rank}A\).
A sparse nonorthogonal basis may yield a more ill-conditioned reduced system than an orthonormal basis.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal tangent-space projector for orthonormal Z.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subspaces Selected by Hessian Curvature Modes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H_k\in\mathbb S^n\) be a Hessian or symmetric Hessian approximation. Let \(Q_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_k}\) have orthonormal columns and define \(T_k=Q_k^TH_kQ_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric Newton models; both exact invariant eigenspaces and approximate Lanczos or Ritz spaces are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A curvature-informed subspace is \(\mathcal S_k=\operatorname{range}(Q_k)\) selected according to spectral information from \(H_k\). It is exact invariant when \(H_kQ_k=Q_kT_k\). It is an \(\varepsilon_k\)-approximate invariant subspace when \(\|(I-Q_kQ_k^T)H_kQ_k\|_2\le\varepsilon_k\). A curvature-informed family specifies which modes are retained, for example those with smallest, largest, negative, or extreme-magnitude Ritz values of \(T_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family chooses Newton trial spaces from directions that represent important curvature of the Hessian. Exact members are invariant eigenspaces. Approximate members have a small off-subspace invariance residual and are commonly obtained from a Lanczos basis and its projected tridiagonal matrix.
assumptions_latex: The mode-selection rule and tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\mathcal S_k=\operatorname{range}(Q_k),\qquad T_k=Q_k^TH_kQ_k,
\qquad \|(I-Q_kQ_k^T)H_kQ_k\|_2\le\varepsilon_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The approximate-invariance condition is \(\|H_kQ_k-Q_kT_k\|_2\le\varepsilon_k\).
For \(\varepsilon_k=0\), \(\mathcal S_k\) is a direct sum of eigenspaces of \(H_k\).
special_cases_latex: Lanczos generates \(Q_j\) spanning a Krylov space with tridiagonal \(T_j=Q_j^TH_kQ_j\).
A negative-curvature subspace retains modes whose Ritz values are negative.
A dominant-curvature subspace retains modes of largest absolute Ritz value.
immediate_consequences_latex: The restricted Newton model has curvature matrix \(T_k\).
Exact invariant selection decouples retained and discarded modes in an eigenbasis.
boundary_notes: A Krylov space is curvature informed only when its selection rule uses the projected spectral information specified here.
Small invariance residual does not by itself guarantee that the gradient is adequately represented.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Subspace Selection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select eigenvectors or Ritz vectors whose curvature values lie in a chosen spectral region, subject to a dimension limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a symmetric matrix \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), a target spectral set \(I\subseteq\mathbb{R}\), and a dimension cap \(k\). Compute or approximate orthonormal eigenvectors \(u_i\) with Ritz or eigenvalues \(\lambda_i\in I\), rank candidates by a declared priority such as decreasing \(|\lambda_i|\), and retain at most \(k\) vectors. With \(V=[u_{i_1},\ldots,u_{i_s}]\), output
\[
\mathcal S_I=\operatorname{range}(V),
\qquad V^THV=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{i_1},\ldots,\lambda_{i_s}).
\]
For approximate eigenvectors, replace exact diagonalization by the projected matrix \(V^THV\); the selection rule remains determined by the associated Ritz values.
assumptions_latex: The target set \(I\) and ranking rule are fixed before selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output subspace is spanned by at most \(k\) spectral or Ritz modes selected from \(I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection of Newton subspaces from prescribed portions of a symmetric Hessian spectrum.
review_flags: locator may support Ritz construction more directly than the general selection rule

source_witnesses.locator: 5 Krylov Subspace Methods p. 75

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Mode Subspaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A curvature-mode subspace is the invariant span of selected Hessian eigenvectors, where each coordinate carries its corresponding eigenvalue curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) admit the orthonormal eigendecomposition \(H=U\Lambda U^T\), with eigenpairs \((\lambda_i,u_i)\). For an index set \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), the curvature-mode subspace associated with \(J\) is
\[
\mathcal S_J=\operatorname{span}\{u_i:i\in J\}.
\]
Writing \(U_J\) for the matrix of selected eigenvectors, \(H\mathcal S_J\subseteq\mathcal S_J\) and \(U_J^THU_J=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i:i\in J)\). Every \(p=U_Jy\) therefore has quadratic curvature \(p^THp=\sum_{i\in J}\lambda_i y_i^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal S_J=\operatorname{span}\{u_i:i\in J\}\) is invariant under \(H\) and has diagonal reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant subspaces assembled from selected eigenmodes of a symmetric Newton matrix.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically standard, precise, and well matched to the terminal container, but the record contains no source reference or inspectable locator. An authoritative spectral-theory or numerical-linear-algebra source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Eigenspace Targeting
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Target a prescribed number of lowest- and highest-curvature eigenmodes and use their orthonormal span, or a converged Ritz approximation to it, as the Newton subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input \(H=H^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and integers \(k_-\ge0\) and \(k_+\ge0\) satisfying \(k_-+k_+\le n\). Order the eigenvalues as \(\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n\). Compute orthonormal eigenvectors for the \(k_-\) smallest and \(k_+\) largest eigenvalues, or compute converged Ritz-vector approximations to those modes, and output
\[
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ext}}=\operatorname{span}\{u_1,\ldots,u_{k_-},u_{n-k_++1},\ldots,u_n\}.
\]
When exact eigenvectors are used, the reduced matrix contains precisely the targeted extreme eigenvalues. When Ritz vectors are used, the output is an approximate extreme spectral subspace determined by the declared Ritz convergence test.
assumptions_latex: Approximate modes satisfy the chosen Ritz convergence test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact eigenvectors produce the requested lower and upper extreme eigenspaces; converged Ritz vectors produce their declared approximation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-limited selection of the smallest- or largest-curvature Hessian eigenspaces.
review_flags: exact extreme-eigenspace selection locator should be confirmed

knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite-Curvature Capture
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative Rayleigh quotient of the reduced Hessian supplies a verifiable full-space negative-curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and let \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\) have orthonormal columns. If a nonzero \(z\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfies
\[
z^T(V^THV)z<0,
\]
then \(d=Vz\ne0\) satisfies \(d^THd<0\). Hence \((z,d)\) is a directly checkable certificate that the selected subspace captures an indefinite-curvature direction of the full quadratic model. In particular, if \(z\) is a normalized eigenvector of \(V^THV\) with Ritz value \(\theta<0\), then \(d^THd=\theta\), and the unrestricted quadratic term decreases without bound along scalar multiples of \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^TV^THVz<0\) certifies \(d=Vz\) with \(d^THd<0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A reduced negative Ritz value certifies negative curvature in the full Newton model.

children.title: Newton Subspace Adequacy Condition
children.top_down_role: The certificate family determining whether a selected subspace retains sufficient Newton information.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adequacy Certificate for a Newton Trial Subspace
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Hp=-g\) be a Newton equation with symmetric \(H\), and let \(P_{\mathcal S}\) be the orthogonal projector onto a selected subspace \(\mathcal S\). Fix tolerances \(\eta_g\in[0,1)\), \(\eta_r\in[0,1)\), and, when curvature is required, \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth Newton models. This definition combines gradient representation, attainable residual, and optional curvature checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The subspace \(\mathcal S\) is \((\eta_g,\eta_r,\mu)\)-Newton adequate when: \(\|(I-P_{\mathcal S})g\|\le\eta_g\|g\|\); there exists \(p\in\mathcal S\) with \(\|Hp+g\|\le\eta_r\|g\|\); and, in the positive-curvature regime, \(d^THd\ge\mu\|d\|^2\) for every \(d\in\mathcal S\). A reduced solve certifies adequacy when its lifted step satisfies these inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton trial space is adequate at prescribed tolerances if it captures the relevant gradient, contains a step attaining the required relative Newton residual, and—when a convex reduced model is required—has uniformly positive restricted curvature.
assumptions_latex: The norm and projector are fixed consistently.
\(g\ne0\); at \(g=0\), the residual ratios require a separate zero-residual convention.
The curvature clause is imposed only in regimes requiring a positive-definite restricted model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\|(I-P_{\mathcal S})g\|\le\eta_g\|g\|,
\quad \inf_{p\in\mathcal S}\|Hp+g\|\le\eta_r\|g\|,
\quad H|_{\mathcal S}\succeq\mu I_{\mathcal S}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an orthonormal basis \(V\), the curvature clause is \(V^THV\succeq\mu I\).
The residual clause is the distance condition \(\operatorname{dist}(-g,H\mathcal S)\le\eta_r\|g\|\).
special_cases_latex: If the exact Newton step lies in \(\mathcal S\), the residual condition holds with \(\eta_r=0\).
An inexact Newton forcing condition is the residual clause without the gradient or curvature clauses.
immediate_consequences_latex: Adequacy is tolerance dependent rather than an intrinsic binary property of the space.
Enlarging \(\mathcal S\) cannot increase the best attainable residual, although it can introduce negative-curvature directions.
boundary_notes: There is no single universally standardized adequacy definition combining all three clauses.
The inspected sources separately support inexact Newton residuals and reduced curvature, not this named combined certificate.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the selected subspace.
Restriction of the Hessian quadratic form to the subspace.

review_flags: The planned node appears to require a project-specific adequacy convention.
No inspected authoritative source states this exact combined condition; a source or narrower contract is required.

children.title: Subspace Residual Certificate
children.top_down_role: Adequacy measured through representation of the Newton residual or stationarity defect.

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace Residual Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace step is certified when its residual is orthogonal to the chosen subspace and small relative to the original Newton residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\) have orthonormal columns. Given reduced coordinates \(y\), define \(p=Vy\) and the full Newton residual \(r=Hp+g\). The pair \((p,r)\) is a subspace residual certificate at tolerance \(\eta\ge0\) when
\[
V^Tr=0,
\qquad \lVert r\rVert_2\le\eta\lVert g\rVert_2.
\]
The first equality verifies exact Galerkin stationarity inside \(\operatorname{range}(V)\); the second verifies that the lifted step satisfies the relative inexact-Newton residual requirement. Both conditions are checkable using matrix-vector products and inner products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V^T(Hp+g)=0\) and \(\lVert Hp+g\rVert_2\le\eta\lVert g\rVert_2\) certify subspace adequacy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable residual test for adequacy of a computed subspace Newton step.

source_witnesses.locator: 5 Krylov Subspace Methods p. 75

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Newton Residual Certificate on a Subspace
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Hp=-g\) be a Newton equation on \(\mathbb R^n\), let \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{range}(V)\), and let \(p=Vs\) be a computed subspace step. Define its full Newton residual by \(r=Hp+g\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact or inexact subspace solves for smooth Newton equations, using a specified vector norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a tolerance \(\eta\in[0,1)\), the pair \((\mathcal S,p)\) has an \(\eta\)-subspace residual certificate when \(p\in\mathcal S\) and \(\|Hp+g\|\le\eta\|g\|\). If \(p\) solves the Galerkin reduced equation, it additionally satisfies \(V^T(Hp+g)=0\). The best certificate attainable by \(\mathcal S\) is \(\eta_*(\mathcal S)=\inf_{p\in\mathcal S}\|Hp+g\|/\|g\|\) for \(g\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate evaluates the full, not merely projected, Newton residual of a step constrained to the selected space. It is valid at tolerance \(\eta\) exactly when that residual is no larger than \(\eta\) times the original stationarity residual. Galerkin orthogonality is an additional relation, not a substitute for the norm bound.
assumptions_latex: \(g\ne0\) for the relative ratio; if \(g=0\), validity is defined by \(Hp=0\).
The same norm is used on both sides of the inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[p\in\mathcal S,
\qquad r=Hp+g,
\qquad \|r\|\le\eta\|g\|.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The subspace admits an \(\eta\)-certificate exactly when \(\operatorname{dist}(-g,H\mathcal S)\le\eta\|g\|\).
For \(p=Vs\), validity is \(\|HVs+g\|\le\eta\|g\|\).
special_cases_latex: \(\eta=0\) certifies that the subspace contains an exact Newton solution.
The standard inexact Newton forcing condition is this certificate applied at each outer iteration with \(\eta=\eta_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\mathcal S_1\subseteq\mathcal S_2\), then \(\eta_*(\mathcal S_2)\le\eta_*(\mathcal S_1)\).
A small projected residual alone does not certify a small full residual.
boundary_notes: For singular or inconsistent Newton systems, the best attainable residual can remain positive even in the full space.
Preconditioned residual norms define a distinct certificate and must identify the weighting operator.

notation.meaning: Full Newton-equation residual of the lifted step.
Smallest relative residual attainable within the subspace.

children.title: Subspace Curvature Certificate
children.top_down_role: Adequacy measured through capture of relevant positive and negative curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace Curvature Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace is curvature-adequate when its reduced Hessian captures both extreme Hessian eigenvalues within tolerance, thereby detecting any negative curvature stronger than that tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and let \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) satisfy \(V^{\mathsf T}V=I_r\). For tolerance \(\varepsilon_H\ge 0\), the subspace \(\mathcal V=\operatorname{range}(V)\) has an \(\varepsilon_H\)-curvature certificate when
\[
0\le \lambda_{\min}(V^{\mathsf T}HV)-\lambda_{\min}(H)\le\varepsilon_H,
\qquad
0\le \lambda_{\max}(H)-\lambda_{\max}(V^{\mathsf T}HV)\le\varepsilon_H.
\]
Thus the reduced model represents the most negative and most positive curvature of \(H\) to additive accuracy \(\varepsilon_H\); in particular, if \(\lambda_{\min}(H)<-\varepsilon_H\), then \(V^{\mathsf T}HV\) has a negative eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal V\) captures both spectral extremes of \(H\) within \(\varepsilon_H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral adequacy of an orthonormal Newton search subspace for a symmetric local Hessian model.

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis of the search subspace

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The certificate content kind and terminal placement are appropriate, and the spectral inequalities and negative-curvature implication are mathematically correct. No source is supplied for this particular two-sided extremal-curvature adequacy certificate.

Write \(B_{\mathcal S}=Z^TBZ\), \(\nu_-(M)=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(M)\}\), and \(\nu_+(M)=\max\{0,\lambda_{\max}(M)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This finite-dimensional definition measures capture of the extreme positive and negative spectral curvature of a symmetric Newton-model matrix. It does not assert that spectral-extreme capture is necessary for every subspace Newton method.

For prescribed \(\kappa_-,\kappa_+\in[0,1]\), the subspace \(\mathcal S\) has a \((\kappa_-,\kappa_+)\)-curvature certificate for \(B\) if \(
u_-(B_{\mathcal S})\ge \kappa_-

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace has the stated curvature certificate when its compressed symmetric model retains prescribed fractions of both the largest negative-curvature magnitude and the largest positive-curvature magnitude of the full model. Unit subspace directions attaining the associated Rayleigh-quotient bounds witness the certificate.

\(\operatorname{CurvCert}(B,\mathcal S;\kappa_-,\kappa_+)\iff [
u_-(Z^TBZ)\ge\kappa_-
u_-(B)]\land[
u_+(Z^TBZ)\ge\kappa_+

special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal S=\mathbb R^n\), then the certificate holds with \(\kappa_- =\kappa_+=1\).
If \(B\succeq0\), the negative-curvature condition is vacuous because \(\nu_-(B)=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\nu_-(B)>0\) and \(\kappa_->0\), then \(Z^TBZ\) is indefinite or negative definite in at least one represented direction.

children.title: Subspace Constraint-Compatibility Certificate
children.top_down_role: Adequacy measured through tangent-space or projected-KKT compatibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace Constraint-Compatibility Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate verifies that represented directions are nearly tangent to the constraints and that the trial step has a small tangent-space KKT residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(P=I-A^{\mathsf T}(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}A\), and let \(V^{\mathsf T}V=I_r\). Given a trial step \(p=Vy\), gradient \(g\), symmetric model matrix \(H\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_K\ge0\), the pair \((V,p)\) has a constraint-compatibility certificate when
\[
\|AV\|_2\le\varepsilon_f,
\qquad
\|P(g+Hp)\|_2\le\varepsilon_K.
\]
The first inequality makes all represented directions approximately tangent; the second verifies approximate stationarity of the quadratic model on the exact tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|AV\|_2\le\varepsilon_f\) and \(\|P(g+Hp)\|_2\le\varepsilon_K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and projected-KKT adequacy for an equality-constrained Newton subspace.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the null space of the constraint Jacobian

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The certificate correctly combines approximate tangency of the represented subspace with an exact-tangent-space model-stationarity residual. Its mathematical formulation is coherent, but the specific combined certificate has no cited source.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent-space and projected-KKT compatibility certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider equality constraints \(c(x)=0\) with Jacobian \(A=\nabla c(x)^T\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) of full row rank. Let \(g_L\in\mathbb R^n\) be a Lagrangian gradient, \(\mathcal T=\ker A\), and \(P_{\mathcal T}\) the orthogonal projector onto \(\mathcal T\). Let \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{Range}(Z)\) with \(Z^TZ=I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition applies to equality-constrained tangent steps at a regular point. It isolates compatibility with linearized feasibility and capture of the projected first-order KKT residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\kappa_T\in(0,1]\), \(\mathcal S\) has a \(\kappa_T\)-constraint-compatibility certificate at \((x,g_L,A)\) if \(A Z=0\) and \(\|P_{\mathcal S}P_{\mathcal T}g_L\|\ge\kappa_T\|P_{\mathcal T}g_L\|\). A certificate is the pair consisting of the exact tangency residual \(AZ\) and the capture ratio \(\chi_T=\|Z^Tg_L\|/\|P_{\mathcal T}g_L\|\), with \(\chi_T=1\) by convention when \(P_{\mathcal T}g_L=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace is constraint-compatible when every represented direction satisfies the linearized equality constraints and the subspace captures at least a prescribed fraction of the tangent component of the Lagrangian gradient. The tangency residual and projected-gradient capture ratio form the certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CompatCert}(\mathcal S;A,g_L,\kappa_T)\iff AZ=0\ \land\ \|Z^Tg_L\|\ge\kappa_T\|P_{\ker A}g_L\|.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under \(AZ=0\) and \(Z^TZ=I\), \(P_{\mathcal S}P_{\mathcal T}=ZZ^T\) and hence \(\|P_{\mathcal S}P_{\mathcal T}g_L\|=\|Z^Tg_L\|\).
special_cases_latex: If \(P_{\mathcal T}g_L=0\), the point satisfies the first-order equality-constrained stationarity equation and the capture inequality is vacuous.
If the columns of \(Z\) span \(\ker A\), then \(\kappa_T=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every step \(p=Zs\) preserves linearized feasibility because \(Ap=0\).
If \(P_{\mathcal T}g_L\ne0\) and \(\kappa_T>0\), then \(-P_{\mathcal S}g_L\) is a nonzero tangent descent direction for the linear model.
boundary_notes: Inequality constraints require an identified critical cone or active-set tangent model and are not covered.
Approximate tangency would require explicit tolerances scaled to the Jacobian and basis norms.

notation.meaning: Fraction of the tangent KKT residual captured by the subspace.

review_flags: No inspected source establishes this exact conjunction of tangency and projected-gradient capture as the named certificate.
A precise source locator and intended treatment of inequalities or approximate feasibility are required.

children.title: Subspace Enrichment Certificate
children.top_down_role: Evidence indicating when the current subspace must be expanded or refreshed.

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace Enrichment Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add an orthogonalized direction when it reveals a substantial omitted residual component or curvature meaningfully lower than the current reduced-Hessian minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) satisfy \(V^{\mathsf T}V=I_r\), let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, let \(g,p\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and set \(r=g+Hp\). Let \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be a candidate direction such that \(z=(I-VV^{\mathsf T})w\ne0\), and set \(u=z/\|z\|_2\). For thresholds \(\eta_r>0\) and \(\delta_H\ge0\), enrichment by \(u\) is certified whenever
\[
|u^{\mathsf T}r|\ge\eta_r\|r\|_2
\quad\text{or}\quad
u^{\mathsf T}Hu<\lambda_{\min}(V^{\mathsf T}HV)-\delta_H.
\]
The enlarged basis \([V,u]\) then exposes either a residual component omitted by \(\operatorname{range}(V)\) or curvature strictly below the reduced model's represented minimum by more than \(\delta_H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([V,u]\) captures certified residual information or previously unrepresented lower curvature.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A computable trigger for adding a residual- or curvature-revealing direction to the current subspace.

notation.meaning: normalized component of the candidate direction orthogonal to the current subspace

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Triggered subspace-enrichment certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the current subspace with orthogonal projector \(P_{\mathcal S}\). Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\) be normalized adequacy scores, where score \(C_i\ge\tau_i\) means that requirement \(i\) is satisfied. Let \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) be a candidate residual, curvature, constraint, or history direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition describes a deterministic enrichment trigger and a quantitative requirement that the proposed direction genuinely enlarge the represented geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For thresholds \(\tau_i\in(0,1]\) and \(\gamma\in(0,1]\), an enrichment certificate is a pair \((i,v)\) such that \(C_i<\tau_i\) and \(\|(I-P_{\mathcal S})v\|\ge\gamma\|v\|>0\). Its certified update is \(\mathcal S^+=\mathcal S+\operatorname{span}\{v\}\), equivalently \(\mathcal S^+=\mathcal S\oplus\operatorname{span}\{(I-P_{\mathcal S})v\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enrichment is certified when at least one quantified adequacy test fails and a proposed direction has a nontrivial component outside the current subspace. The updated subspace is obtained by adjoining that independent component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{EnrichCert}(\mathcal S;i,v)\iff C_i<\tau_i\ \land\ \|(I-P_{\mathcal S})v\|\ge\gamma\|v\|>0.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The angle condition is \(\sin\angle(v,\mathcal S)\ge\gamma\).
The update satisfies \(\dim\mathcal S^+=\dim\mathcal S+1\).
special_cases_latex: For a Newton residual \(r=Bp+g\), one may take \(v=r\) when residual capture fails.
For detected negative curvature, one may take \(v=u\) where \(u^TBu<0\) and the represented curvature score is inadequate.
immediate_consequences_latex: The certified update strictly enlarges the subspace and represents the proposed direction exactly: \(v\in\mathcal S^+\).
At most \(n-\dim\mathcal S\) successive one-vector certified enrichments are possible without deletion or restart.
boundary_notes: A failed score without an independent direction diagnoses inadequacy but does not certify an effective enrichment.
Restarting, deleting, or compressing basis vectors is a separate operation and may reduce dimension.
The definition does not select which failed requirement has priority when several scores fail.

notation.meaning: Normalized score for the ith subspace-adequacy requirement.
Minimum relative component outside the current subspace.

review_flags: No inspected source supports this exact trigger-plus-angle formulation under the supplied node title.
The intended adequacy scores and enrichment policy require authoritative specification.

children.title: Subspace Model Decrease Condition
children.top_down_role: Progress certificates comparing a subspace step with canonical model-decrease benchmarks.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fraction-of-reference subspace model decrease
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(m(p)=m(0)+g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp\) with symmetric \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\). Let \(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed trial-step domain containing \(0\), let \(\mathcal S\) be a subspace, and let \(\mathcal B(g,B,\mathcal S,\mathcal F)\ge0\) be a specified canonical decrease benchmark.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The condition is abstract enough to host projected-gradient, Cauchy-comparison, or represented negative-curvature benchmarks, but the benchmark must be fixed independently of the computed trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\kappa_m\in(0,1]\), a trial step \(p\in\mathcal S\cap\mathcal F\) satisfies the subspace model decrease condition relative to \(\mathcal B\) if \(m(0)-m(p)\ge\kappa_m\mathcal B(g,B,\mathcal S,\mathcal F)\). If several mandatory benchmarks \(\mathcal B_j\) are imposed, the combined condition uses \(\mathcal B=\max_j\mathcal B_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible subspace step has sufficient model decrease when its predicted reduction is at least a fixed fraction of a prescribed nonnegative reference benchmark. When multiple required benchmarks are present, the step is compared with their maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in\mathcal S\cap\mathcal F\quad\text{and}\quad -g^Tp-\tfrac12p^TBp\ge\kappa_m\mathcal B(g,B,\mathcal S,\mathcal F).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: For mandatory benchmarks \(\{\mathcal B_j\}_{j=1}^q\), the condition is equivalent to \(m(0)-m(p)\ge\kappa_m\mathcal B_j\) for every \(j\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal B=0\), the condition requires only nonincrease of the model.
If \(p\) globally minimizes \(m\) over \(\mathcal S\cap\mathcal F\) and \(\mathcal B\) is the decrease of any feasible comparison step, the condition holds with \(\kappa_m=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Whenever \(\mathcal B>0\), the condition gives strictly positive predicted reduction.
The ratio \((m(0)-m(p))/\mathcal B\) is a dimensionless model-quality certificate when \(\mathcal B>0\).
boundary_notes: The condition is not an acceptance test for the objective; actual reduction requires a separate globalization rule.
Allowing the computed step itself to define \(\mathcal B\) would make the condition circular.

notation.meaning: Required fraction of the benchmark decrease.

review_flags: The fraction-of-reference pattern is standard, but no inspected source was available for this named subspace condition and its precise benchmark family.

children.title: Projected-Gradient Decrease
children.top_down_role: Model progress relative to projected first-order information.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Gradient Decrease
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The represented step must reduce the quadratic model by a fixed fraction of a scale determined by the projected gradient, reduced curvature, and step radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q(p)=g^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Hp\), an orthonormal basis \(V\), radius \(\Delta>0\), and \(g_V=V^{\mathsf T}g\), a step \(p=Vy\) satisfies projected-gradient decrease with constant \(\kappa_{pg}\in(0,1]\) if \(\|p\|_2\le\Delta\) and
\[
q(0)-q(p)\ge \kappa_{pg}\|g_V\|_2
\min\!\left\{\Delta,\frac{\|g_V\|_2}{\max\{\|V^{\mathsf T}HV\|_2,\,\|g_V\|_2/\Delta\}}\right\}.
\]
When \(g_V=0\), the right-hand side is defined as zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(0)-q(p)\) obeys the displayed projected-gradient lower bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient quadratic-model reduction measured by the gradient component represented in the subspace.

notation.meaning: quadratic model without its constant term
gradient coordinates in the search subspace

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition is internally consistent and equivalent to a standard projected-gradient Cauchy-scale bound. Its exact max/min normalization is nontrivial and has no cited source, so source verification is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected-gradient path decrease condition
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(m(p)=m(0)+g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp\), where \(B\) is symmetric. Let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(P_{\mathcal S}\) be its orthogonal projector, put \(g_{\mathcal S}=P_{\mathcal S}g\), and impose a radius \(\Delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This condition benchmarks model progress using only first-order information represented by the current subspace, while retaining the quadratic model along the projected-gradient ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the projected-gradient benchmark by \(D_{PG}=\max_{0\le\alpha\le\Delta/\|g_{\mathcal S}\|}\{m(0)-m(-\alpha g_{\mathcal S})\}\) when \(g_{\mathcal S}\ne0\), and \(D_{PG}=0\) otherwise. For \(\kappa_{PG}\in(0,1]\), a step \(p\in\mathcal S\) with \(\|p\|\le\Delta\) satisfies projected-gradient decrease if \(m(0)-m(p)\ge\kappa_{PG}D_{PG}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The benchmark is the best predicted reduction obtained on the radius-truncated ray opposite the gradient projected into the subspace. A trial step passes when it obtains a prescribed fraction of that reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m(0)-m(p)\ge\kappa_{PG}\max_{0\le\alpha\le\Delta/\|P_{\mathcal S}g\|}\left(\alpha\|P_{\mathcal S}g\|^2-\tfrac12\alpha^2(P_{\mathcal S}g)^TB(P_{\mathcal S}g)\right).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \((g_{\mathcal S})^TBg_{\mathcal S}>0\), a maximizing ray parameter is \(\alpha_* =\min\{\|g_{\mathcal S}\|^2/(g_{\mathcal S}^TBg_{\mathcal S}),\Delta/\|g_{\mathcal S}\|\}\).
If \((g_{\mathcal S})^TBg_{\mathcal S}\le0\), a maximizing parameter is \(\alpha_*=\Delta/\|g_{\mathcal S}\|\).
special_cases_latex: If \(P_{\mathcal S}g=0\), then \(D_{PG}=0\).
If \(g\in\mathcal S\), the benchmark is the ordinary truncated steepest-descent-ray benchmark.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(P_{\mathcal S}g\ne0\), then \(D_{PG}>0\), so every passing step has positive predicted reduction.
boundary_notes: A small projected gradient may reflect inadequate subspace capture rather than full-space stationarity.
This condition does not require the accepted step to be collinear with the projected gradient.

notation.meaning: Optimal model decrease along the truncated projected-gradient ray.

knowledge_statements.title: Cauchy-Comparison Decrease
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace step is acceptable when it achieves a fixed fraction of the best model decrease along the feasible projected negative-gradient ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(p)=g^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Hp\), \(V^{\mathsf T}V=I_r\), \(g_V=V^{\mathsf T}g\ne0\), and \(\Delta>0\). Define
\[
t_C\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\le t\le\Delta/\|g_V\|_2}q(-tVV^{\mathsf T}g),
\qquad p_C=-t_CVV^{\mathsf T}g.
\]
A feasible subspace step \(p\in\operatorname{range}(V)\), \(\|p\|_2\le\Delta\), satisfies Cauchy-comparison decrease with \(\kappa_C\in(0,1]\) when
\[
q(0)-q(p)\ge\kappa_C\bigl(q(0)-q(p_C)\bigr).
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(0)-q(p)\ge\kappa_C\bigl(q(0)-q(p_C)\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-model progress compared with the canonical projected steepest-descent step inside a trust-region radius.

notation.meaning: optimal feasible length along the projected negative-gradient ray

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cauchy lower-bound comparison for a subspace step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(m(p)=m(0)+g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp\) with symmetric \(B\), let \(\mathcal S\) be a subspace, put \(g_{\mathcal S}=P_{\mathcal S}g\), and let \(p\in\mathcal S\) satisfy \(\|p\|\le\Delta\) for \(\Delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unlike exact projected-gradient-ray comparison, this condition uses the explicit norm-based Cauchy lower bound and is therefore insensitive to the exact directional curvature denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(D_C=\tfrac12\|g_{\mathcal S}\|\min\{\Delta,\|g_{\mathcal S}\|/\|B\|\}\), with \(\|g_{\mathcal S}\|/\|B\|=+\infty\) when \(B=0\). For \(\kappa_C\in(0,1]\), the step \(p\) satisfies Cauchy-comparison decrease if \(m(0)-m(p)\ge\kappa_C D_C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A radius-feasible subspace step passes the Cauchy comparison when its predicted reduction is at least a fixed fraction of the standard explicit lower bound formed from the projected-gradient norm, radius, and model-matrix norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-g^Tp-\tfrac12p^TBp\ge\frac{\kappa_C}{2}\|P_{\mathcal S}g\|\min\left\{\Delta,\frac{\|P_{\mathcal S}g\|}{\|B\|}\right\}.\)
special_cases_latex: If \(B=0\), then \(D_C=\tfrac12\Delta\|g_{\mathcal S}\|\).
If \(\Delta\ge\|g_{\mathcal S}\|/\|B\|\), then \(D_C=\|g_{\mathcal S}\|^2/(2\|B\|)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(P_{\mathcal S}g\ne0\), every passing step has strictly positive predicted reduction.
Uniform projected-gradient capture converts this bound into one expressed in terms of \(\|g\|\).
boundary_notes: The bound can be conservative because it replaces directional curvature by \(\|B\|\).
When \(P_{\mathcal S}g=0\), the benchmark vanishes and does not detect missing gradient directions or negative curvature.
review_flags: The formula is a standard trust-region-style benchmark, but its precise use as the named subspace condition lacks an inspected supporting locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Captured Negative-Curvature Decrease
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represented negative curvature yields quadratic-in-radius model decrease; an acceptable step captures a fixed fraction of this boundary-direction reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(p)=g^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Hp\), let \(V^{\mathsf T}V=I_r\), and suppose a unit vector \(v\in\operatorname{range}(V)\) satisfies \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv=-\gamma\) with \(\gamma>0\). Choose the sign of \(v\) so that \(g^{\mathsf T}v\le0\). For \(\Delta>0\), the boundary step \(p_{nc}=\Delta v\) satisfies
\[
q(0)-q(p_{nc})=-\Delta g^{\mathsf T}v+\tfrac12\gamma\Delta^2
\ge\tfrac12\gamma\Delta^2.
\]
A computed step captures this decrease if its model reduction is at least a fixed fraction \(\kappa_{nc}\in(0,1]\) of that of \(p_{nc}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(0)-q(p)\ge\kappa_{nc}\bigl(q(0)-q(p_{nc})\bigr)\ge\tfrac12\kappa_{nc}\gamma\Delta^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model reduction obtained from a negative-curvature direction represented by the subspace.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the captured negative-curvature benchmark by \(D_{NC}=\tfrac12\nu\Delta^2\). knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Globalized Newton method restricted to adaptive subspaces
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable. At iterate \(x_k\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), let \(B_k\) be a symmetric Hessian or Hessian approximation, let \(\mathcal S_k=\operatorname{Range}(Z_k)\), and let \(m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition covers deterministic unconstrained schemes whose trial Newton-model step is restricted to a subspace and whose acceptance or stabilization is governed by an explicit globalization state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A globalized Newton subspace method is an iteration \((x_k,\sigma_k)\mapsto(x_{k+1},\sigma_{k+1})\) that selects \(p_k\in\mathcal S_k\) from the reduced model, forms an admissible trial displacement \(s_k=G_k(p_k,\sigma_k)\), accepts it only when a prescribed actual-versus-predicted decrease or sufficient-decrease test \(A_k(s_k,\sigma_k)\) holds, sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) on acceptance and \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) otherwise, and updates the globalization state by a stated rule \(\sigma_{k+1}=U_k(\sigma_k,A_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method computes a Newton-model step in a selected subspace, modifies it through a line-search, trust-region, or regularization state, accepts or rejects the resulting trial displacement using an explicit decrease test, and updates both the iterate and globalization state by fixed rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\in\mathcal S_k,\quad s_k=G_k(p_k,\sigma_k),\quad x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_k+s_k,&A_k\text{ holds},\\x_k,&A_k\text{ fails},\end{cases}\quad \sigma_{k+1}=U_k(\sigma_k,A_k).\)
special_cases_latex: Line search uses \(s_k=\alpha_kp_k\) and treats \(\alpha_k\) as the globalization state or output.
Trust region uses \(\sigma_k=\Delta_k\) and restricts \(\|p_k\|\le\Delta_k\).
Regularization uses \(\sigma_k=\lambda_k\) or a higher-order regularization coefficient.
immediate_consequences_latex: Full-space globalized Newton is recovered when \(\mathcal S_k=\mathbb R^n\) for every \(k\).
boundary_notes: A reduced Newton equation without an acceptance or stabilization mechanism is not globalized under this definition.
The definition alone makes no convergence claim; adequacy, decrease, smoothness, and parameter safeguards must be stated separately.

notation.meaning: Globalization state, such as a radius or regularization parameter.
Trial transformation, acceptance test, and state-update rule.

review_flags: The broad framework is consistent with standard globalization families, but no inspected source provides this exact unifying definition.

children.title: Line-Search Subspace Newton

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Subspace Newton
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the reduced Newton equation, replace a non-descent step by projected steepest descent, and globalize the update with Armijo backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\), constants \(c\in(0,1)\), \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and orthonormal bases \(V_k\), set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\), and solve
\[
(V_k^{\mathsf T}H_kV_k)y_k=-V_k^{\mathsf T}g_k,
\qquad p_k=V_ky_k.
\]
If the solve fails or \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k\ge0\), replace \(p_k\) by \(-V_kV_k^{\mathsf T}g_k\). Choose the smallest integer \(j_k\ge0\) such that, with \(\alpha_k=\beta^{j_k}\),
\[
f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le f(x_k)+c\alpha_kg_k^{\mathsf T}p_k.
\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and stop when the prescribed stationarity tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) satisfies the Armijo decrease test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained reduced Newton iteration globalized by Armijo backtracking and a descent fallback.

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis selected at iteration k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Armijo-globalized subspace Newton iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable and let \(B_k\) be symmetric. Let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_k}\) have orthonormal columns, \(\mathcal S_k=\operatorname{Range}(Z_k)\), and \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\). Fix \(c_1\in(0,1)\) and \(\beta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition is an unconstrained deterministic line-search scheme. It permits an inexact reduced Newton solve but explicitly requires a descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A line-search subspace Newton iteration chooses \(y_k\) so that \(p_k=Z_ky_k\) satisfies \(Z_k^T(B_kp_k+g_k)=r_k\) and \(g_k^Tp_k<0\). It selects the first \(\alpha_k=\beta^j\), \(j\in\{0,1,\ldots\}\), satisfying \(f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_kg_k^Tp_k\), and sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method approximately solves the Newton equation after projection into the selected subspace, requires the lifted direction to be a descent direction, and backtracks geometrically until the Armijo sufficient-decrease inequality holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z_k^T(B_kZ_ky_k+g_k)=r_k,\quad g_k^TZ_ky_k<0,\quad \alpha_k=\beta^{\min\{j\ge0:f(x_k+\beta^jp_k)\le f(x_k)+c_1\beta^jg_k^Tp_k\}},\quad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an exact reduced solve, \(r_k=0\) and \((Z_k^TB_kZ_k)y_k=-Z_k^Tg_k\).
special_cases_latex: If \(Z_k=I\) and \(r_k=0\), this is the standard line-search Newton iteration.
If \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\succ0\) and \(Z_k^Tg_k\ne0\), the exact reduced Newton direction is a descent direction.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every accepted nonzero step strictly decreases \(f\) because \(c_1\alpha_kg_k^Tp_k<0\).
boundary_notes: If the reduced Newton direction is not a descent direction, a modification or fallback direction is required before the stated line search applies.
Wolfe, strong-Wolfe, or nonmonotone searches are nearby variants, not part of this definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Subspace Newton
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimize the reduced quadratic model within a radius, accept by actual-to-predicted reduction, and adapt the radius according to model agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and \(V_k^{\mathsf T}V_k=I\), form
\[
m_k(y)=f(x_k)+(V_k^{\mathsf T}g_k)^{\mathsf T}y+\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}(V_k^{\mathsf T}H_kV_k)y
\]
and compute \(y_k\) with \(\|y_k\|_2\le\Delta_k\) and prescribed Cauchy-comparison decrease. Put \(p_k=V_ky_k\) and
\[
\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+p_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(y_k)}.
\]
Accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\) when \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\), otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Shrink \(\Delta_k\) for poor agreement, enlarge it for \(\rho_k\ge\eta_2\) with an active boundary, and otherwise retain it, where \(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial step is accepted or rejected using \(\rho_k\), and \(\Delta_k\) is updated by the stated agreement rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced Newton model globalized through actual-to-predicted reduction and adaptive radius control.

Fix \(0\le\eta_1<\eta_2<1\), \(0<\gamma_d<1<\gamma_i\), and radius bounds \(0<\Delta_{\min}\le\Delta_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This finite-dimensional definition uses Euclidean trust regions, ratio-based acceptance, and safeguarded radius control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region subspace Newton iteration computes \(p_k\in\mathcal S_k\), \(\|p_k\|\le\Delta_k\), with positive predicted reduction \(D_k=m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)>0\), and defines \(\rho_k=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+p_k)]/D_k\). It sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\) if \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) otherwise. The radius is decreased when \(\rho_k<\eta_1\), retained or moderately changed when \(\eta_1\le\rho_k<\eta_2\), and may be increased when \(\rho_k\ge\eta_2\) and \(\|p_k\|=\Delta_k\), subject to the radius bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method approximately minimizes the quadratic Newton model over the intersection of the current subspace and a trust ball, accepts the trial point according to actual versus predicted reduction, and adjusts the radius according to model agreement and boundary activity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\in\mathcal S_k\cap\{p:\|p\|\le\Delta_k\},\quad \rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+p_k)}{-g_k^Tp_k-\tfrac12p_k^TB_kp_k},\quad x_{k+1}=x_k+\mathbf1_{\{\rho_k\ge\eta_1\}}p_k.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(p_k=Z_ky_k\) and \(Z_k^TZ_k=I\), the reduced constraint is \(\|y_k\|\le\Delta_k\) and the reduced model matrix is \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\).

A truncated conjugate-gradient or Lanczos iterate may define \(p_k\) when it satisfies the required model-decrease condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Subspace Newton
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift the reduced Hessian until it is uniformly positive definite, solve the stabilized reduced Newton equation, and globalize the resulting descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), \(V_k^{\mathsf T}V_k=I\), and \(\delta>0\), form \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\), and choose
\[
\lambda_k\ge\max\{0,\delta-\lambda_{\min}(V_k^{\mathsf T}H_kV_k)\}.
\]
Solve
\[
(V_k^{\mathsf T}H_kV_k+\lambda_kI)y_k=-V_k^{\mathsf T}g_k,
\qquad p_k=V_ky_k.
\]
If \(p_k=0\), stop according to the projected-stationarity test; otherwise select an Armijo step length \(\alpha_k>0\) and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). The shifted reduced matrix has smallest eigenvalue at least \(\delta\), so every nonzero computed direction is descending.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_k^{\mathsf T}H_kV_k+\lambda_kI\succeq\delta I\) and \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k<0\) whenever \(p_k\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced Newton iteration stabilized by a spectral shift that enforces uniformly positive reduced curvature.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The spectral shift guarantees the stated positive-definiteness bound, and the resulting nonzero reduced direction is descending. The algorithm fits the terminal, but no authoritative source is supplied for this regularized subspace-Newton formulation.
