knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectrally regularized reduced Newton step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(B_k\) be symmetric. Let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_k}\) have orthonormal columns and put \(H_k=Z_k^TB_kZ_k\), \(h_k=Z_k^Tg_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers quadratic spectral regularization of an unconstrained reduced Newton system. Cubic regularization is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a prescribed coercivity floor \(\mu_k>0\), choose \(\lambda_k\ge0\) such that \(H_k+\lambda_kI\succeq\mu_kI\), solve \((H_k+\lambda_kI)y_k=-h_k+r_k\), and set \(p_k=Z_ky_k\). The step is a regularized subspace Newton step when its residual satisfies a declared tolerance, for example \(\|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|h_k\|\) with \(\eta_k<1\). A regularized subspace Newton method combines these steps with an acceptance test and updates \(\lambda_k\) according to trial-step success.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method shifts the reduced symmetric Newton matrix until it has a stated positive coercivity margin, solves the shifted reduced system to a prescribed residual tolerance, lifts the solution to the full space, and adapts the shift using an acceptance mechanism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_k+\lambda_kI\succeq\mu_kI,\quad (H_k+\lambda_kI)y_k=-h_k+r_k,\quad \|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|h_k\|,\quad p_k=Z_ky_k.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The minimum admissible exact spectral shift is \(\lambda_k=\max\{0,\mu_k-\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(H_k\succeq\mu_kI\), one may take \(\lambda_k=0\), recovering the unregularized reduced Newton equation.
If \(Z_k=I\), this is a full-space spectrally shifted Newton step.
immediate_consequences_latex: For \(h_k\ne0\), an exact solve gives \(g_k^Tp_k=-h_k^T(H_k+\lambda_kI)^{-1}h_k<0\).
The reduced linear system is nonsingular and has condition number at most \((\lambda_{\max}(H_k)+\lambda_k)/\mu_k\) when the numerator is positive.
boundary_notes: A fixed positive shift can prevent recovery of the unregularized Newton rate unless it vanishes appropriately.
Cubic or higher-order regularization uses a step-dependent nonlinear stationarity equation and is not identical to this definition.
review_flags: No inspected source was available for this exact spectral-shift definition or its parameter-update mechanism.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adequacy–decrease–globalization–recovery convergence interface
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable and let an iteration generate \((x_k,\mathcal S_k,p_k,\sigma_k)\), where \(p_k\in\mathcal S_k\), \(m_k\) is a quadratic Newton model, and \(\sigma_k\) is a globalization state. Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is an interface predicate organizing sufficient inputs to separate global and local convergence analyses; it is not itself a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence satisfies the Newton subspace convergence interface if it is equipped with four declared predicates: adequacy \(A_k\), ensuring quantified capture of required first-order, curvature, and constraint geometry; decrease \(D_k\), ensuring \(m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\ge\kappa\mathcal B_k\) for a nonnegative canonical benchmark; globalization \(G_k\), ensuring accepted steps satisfy a stated actual-decrease or model-agreement rule with safeguarded state updates; and local recovery \(L_k\), ensuring that near a regular solution the lifted reduced step has full Newton residual \(\|\nabla^2f(x_k)p_k+g_k\|\le\eta_k\|g_k\|\) with a declared forcing sequence \(\eta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface consists of four explicit contracts: the subspace captures the geometry needed by the analysis, the trial step achieves benchmark model decrease, globalization controls actual progress, and the local step approaches the full Newton equation at a quantified residual rate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{NSCI}_k\iff A_k\land D_k\land G_k\land L_k,\quad D_k:\ m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\ge\kappa\mathcal B_k,\quad L_k:\ \|\nabla^2f(x_k)p_k+g_k\|\le\eta_k\|g_k\|.\)
special_cases_latex: For a purely global stationarity result, \(L_k\) may be required only after entry into a specified solution neighborhood.
For full-space Newton, adequacy is automatic when \(\mathcal S_k=\mathbb R^n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The interface makes explicit which conditions belong to subspace selection and which belong to globalization or local linear-solve accuracy.
Different line-search, trust-region, and regularization mechanisms can share the same adequacy and local-recovery predicates.
boundary_notes: Satisfaction of the interface does not imply convergence without a theorem adding smoothness, boundedness, and parameter hypotheses.
The benchmark \(\mathcal B_k\), forcing sequence, and geometry captured by \(A_k\) must be specified for each concrete method.

notation.meaning: Adequacy, model-decrease, globalization, and local-recovery predicates.

children.title: Subspace Global Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Global convergence regimes based on adequate projected progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace Global Stationarity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform gradient capture plus bounded sufficient-descent subspace directions and Armijo backtracking forces the full gradient norm to converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, bounded below on the level set of \(x_0\), with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient there. Suppose \(p_k\in\operatorname{range}(V_k)\), \(V_k^{\mathsf T}V_k=I\), and constants \(c_1,c_2,\kappa>0\) satisfy
\[
-g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k\ge c_1\|g_k\|_2^2,
\qquad \|p_k\|_2\le c_2\|g_k\|_2,
\qquad \|V_k^{\mathsf T}g_k\|_2\ge\kappa\|g_k\|_2.
\]
If Armijo backtracking uses fixed parameters in \((0,1)\), then accepted step lengths are uniformly bounded away from zero, \(\sum_k\|g_k\|_2^2<\infty\), and consequently \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2\to0\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below on the initial level set and has Lipschitz gradient there.
The displayed capture, descent, and norm bounds hold uniformly.
Armijo backtracking parameters are fixed in \((0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2^2<\infty\) and \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order global convergence under uniform projected-gradient capture and sufficient-descent line-search steps.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global first-order stationarity certified through subspace projections
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\mathcal S_k\) have orthogonal projector \(P_k\). Define the full and projected stationarity measures \(\chi_k=\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\) and \(\chi_k^{\mathcal S}=\|P_k\nabla f(x_k)\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns unconstrained first-order stationarity. It distinguishes mere projected stationarity from globally meaningful stationarity obtained under a uniform gradient-capture condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence is subspace-globally stationary if there exists \(\kappa_g>0\) such that \(\chi_k^{\mathcal S}\ge\kappa_g\chi_k\) for every nonstationary iterate and \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\chi_k^{\mathcal S}=0\). A weaker subsequential version replaces the limit by \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\chi_k^{\mathcal S}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence has subspace global stationarity when the chosen subspaces uniformly capture a positive fraction of the full gradient and the projected-gradient norm tends to zero. The capture condition prevents convergence of the projected measure from hiding a full-space nonstationary gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\exists\kappa_g>0:\ \|P_k
abla f(x_k)\|\ge\kappa_g\|
abla f(x_k)\|\  orall k,\qquad \|P_k
abla f(x_k)\|	o0.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under uniform capture, subspace global stationarity is equivalent to \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\).
For the weaker version, uniform capture implies \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\nabla f(x_k)\in\mathcal S_k\) for every \(k\), one may take \(\kappa_g=1\).
If \(\mathcal S_k=\mathbb R^n\), projected and full stationarity measures coincide.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every accumulation point \(x_*\) of a subspace-globally stationary sequence is first-order stationary when \(\nabla f\) is continuous.
boundary_notes: Projected-gradient convergence without uniform capture is not a full-space stationarity certificate.
For constrained problems, the gradient must be replaced by a projected-gradient, criticality, or KKT residual appropriate to the feasible geometry.

notation.meaning: Norm of the gradient projected onto the selected subspace.

review_flags: No inspected source supports this exact terminology and uniform-capture definition.
A source is needed to determine whether the intended conclusion is a full limit, a liminf result, or stationarity of accumulation points.

children.title: Newton Subspace Local Rate Condition
children.top_down_role: Local rate regimes governed by the quality and evolution of selected subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton Subspace Local Rate Condition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relative full Newton-equation residual produced by the subspace determines whether local convergence is linear, superlinear, or quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(x_*\), with \(
abla f(x_*)=0\), nonsingular \(H_* =
abla^2f(x_*)\), and locally Lipschitz Hessian. Let \(p_k\in\operatorname{range}(V_k)\) satisfy
\[
\|
abla^2f(x_k)p_k+
abla f(x_k)\|_2\le\eta_k\|
abla f(x_k)\|_2,
\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k.
\]
For sufficiently close \(x_0\), a sufficiently small uniform bound \(\sup_k\eta_k<1\) gives local linear convergence; \(\eta_k	o0\) gives superlinear convergence; and \(\eta_k=O(\|
abla f(x_k)\|_2)\) gives quadratic convergence.
assumptions_latex: The displayed inexact Newton residual condition holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The forcing sequence \(\eta_k\) determines the stated linear, superlinear, or quadratic local rate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact-Newton residual conditions determining linear, superlinear, or quadratic local convergence.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem has the correct mathematical role and describes standard inexact-Newton rate regimes, but it lacks an authoritative locator. The phrase 'sufficiently small uniform bound' also requires source-backed quantitative interpretation; merely stating a bound below one is not universally sufficient without neighborhood and conditioning constants.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact-Newton residual condition induced by evolving subspaces
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable near a point \(x_*\) with \(
abla f(x_*)=0\) and nonsingular Hessian. Let \(g_k=
abla f(x_k)\), \(H_k=
abla^2f(x_k)\), and let \(p_k\in\mathcal S_k\) be the accepted unit-length local step, so \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition is local, unconstrained, and deterministic. It encodes subspace quality through the residual of the full Newton equation rather than through subspace dimension alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The steps satisfy a Newton subspace local rate condition with forcing sequence \(\eta_k\ge0\) if \(\|H_kp_k+g_k\|\le\eta_k\|g_k\|\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). The condition is linear-rate compatible when \(\sup_k\eta_k<1\), superlinear-rate compatible when \(\eta_k\to0\), and quadratic-rate compatible when \(\eta_k=O(\|g_k\|)\), the latter designation presuming a locally Lipschitz Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The local quality of a subspace step is measured by how accurately the lifted step solves the full Newton equation. A uniformly subunit forcing factor is the linear regime, a vanishing factor is the superlinear regime, and a factor proportional to the gradient norm is the quadratic regime when the Hessian is locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\|
abla^2f(x_k)p_k+
abla f(x_k)\|\le\eta_k\|
abla f(x_k)\|\quad	ext{eventually}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(p_k^N=-H_k^{-1}g_k\), the residual condition is \(\|H_k(p_k-p_k^N)\|\le\eta_k\|g_k\|\).
If \(H_k\) and \(H_k^{-1}\) are uniformly bounded locally, then \(\|p_k-p_k^N\|=O(\eta_k\|p_k^N\|)\).
special_cases_latex: Exact eventual Newton recovery corresponds to \(\eta_k=0\).
A fixed forcing factor \(\eta_k\equiv\bar\eta<1\) is the standard inexact local regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: The condition quantifies approximation of the full Newton step even when \(\dim\mathcal S_k<n\).
boundary_notes: The rate labels require separate local convergence hypotheses and are not themselves convergence conclusions.
If globalization continues damping the step near \(x_*\), the full-step residual condition alone does not determine the iterate rate.
Singular-Hessian solutions require different error-bound or semismooth frameworks.

notation.meaning: Relative residual forcing sequence for the full Newton equation.

review_flags: The forcing-sequence regimes are standard in inexact Newton analysis, but the supplied source hint was not inspected and cannot be cited.
The intended relation between subspace approximation and residual forcing needs source confirmation.

children.title: Eventual Full-Newton Recovery
children.top_down_role: Local regimes in which enrichment recovers the effective full Newton step.

knowledge_statements.title: Eventual Full-Newton Recovery
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once each full Newton step lies in the selected subspace, the reduced solve reproduces it exactly; with eventual unit steps and the usual hypotheses for the relevant full-Newton rate theorem, the subspace iteration has the same local rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each iteration \(k\), let \(H_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, let \(g_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(V_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r_k}\) satisfy \(V_k^{\mathsf T}V_k=I_{r_k}\). Assume \(V_k^{\mathsf T}H_kV_k\) is nonsingular, and define
\[
p_k^N=-H_k^{-1}g_k,
\qquad
p_k^S=-V_k(V_k^{\mathsf T}H_kV_k)^{-1}V_k^{\mathsf T}g_k.
\]
If there exists \(K\in\mathbb{N}\) such that \(p_k^N\in\operatorname{range}(V_k)\) for every \(k\ge K\), then \(p_k^S=p_k^N\) for every \(k\ge K\). Consequently, an eventually unit-step subspace iteration has the same updates as full Newton from iteration \(K\) onward and inherits any full-Newton local rate whose hypotheses hold for those iterates.
assumptions_latex: There exists \(K\in\mathbb{N}\) such that \(p_k^N\in\operatorname{range}(V_k)\) for every \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k^S=p_k^N\) for every \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery of the full Newton step once the selected subspace contains it.

notation.meaning: step obtained from the reduced Newton equation
iteration after which the Newton step is always represented

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact eventual recovery of the full Newton displacement
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable and suppose \(H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\) is nonsingular for all sufficiently large \(k\). Define the full Newton step \(p_k^N=-H_k^{-1}g_k\), where \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\). Let \(\mathcal S_k=\operatorname{Range}(Z_k)\) with \(Z_k^TZ_k=I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition is exact and local: it requires recovery of the effective Newton direction, not necessarily recovery of the entire ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The subspace sequence has eventual full-Newton recovery if there exists an index \(K\) such that \(p_k^N\in\mathcal S_k\) for every \(k\ge K\), and the reduced step is solved exactly: \((Z_k^TH_kZ_k)y_k=-Z_k^Tg_k\), \(p_k=Z_ky_k\). Recovery by the iteration additionally requires the globalization mechanism to accept the unit step, so \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\), for every \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eventually, each selected subspace contains the full Newton displacement. An exact reduced solve then produces that same displacement, and full algorithmic recovery also requires the globalization mechanism to accept it without damping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\ p_k^N\in\mathcal S_k,\quad (Z_k^TH_kZ_k)y_k=-Z_k^Tg_k,\quad Z_ky_k=p_k^N,\quad \alpha_k=1.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The containment condition is \((I-P_{\mathcal S_k})H_k^{-1}g_k=0\) for every \(k\ge K\).
Exact step recovery is equivalently \(H_kp_k+g_k=0\) eventually.
special_cases_latex: Eventual full-dimensional enrichment, \(\mathcal S_k=\mathbb R^n\), implies the containment part automatically.
A proper subspace can recover the Newton step when it contains \(H_k^{-1}g_k\), even if it does not contain all Hessian eigendirections.
immediate_consequences_latex: After the recovery index, the iterates coincide with those of the corresponding unit-step full Newton method started from \(x_K\).
The local forcing parameter is eventually \(\eta_k=0\).
boundary_notes: Asymptotic approximation \(\|(I-P_{\mathcal S_k})p_k^N\|/\|p_k^N\|\to0\) is weaker than exact eventual recovery.
Containment alone is insufficient if the reduced system is solved inaccurately or a line search continues to damp the step.

notation.meaning: First index after which exact recovery persists.

review_flags: No inspected source establishes this exact containment-plus-unit-acceptance definition.
The intended node may admit asymptotic rather than exact recovery; source resolution is required.

children.top_down_role: Failures caused by incomplete geometry, unstable bases, or incompatible projections.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quantified failure boundary for a Newton subspace state
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a Newton subspace state be \(\Xi=(g,B,A,Z)\), where \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(B=B^T\), \(A\) is an optional equality-constraint Jacobian, and \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) is the computational basis. Let \(P_Z=Z(Z^TZ)^{-1}Z^T\) when \(Z\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition identifies diagnostic boundaries caused by missing first-order or curvature geometry, loss of basis stability, or incompatibility with linearized constraints. It does not claim that every boundary necessarily causes failure for every globalization method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given thresholds \(\kappa_g,\kappa_-\in(0,1]\), \(\Gamma\ge1\), and \(\varepsilon_A\ge0\), the failure-boundary set \(\mathfrak F\) consists of states satisfying at least one of: \(\|P_Zg\|<\kappa_g\|g\|\); \(\nu_-(Z^TBZ)<\kappa_-\nu_-(B)\); \(Z\) is rank deficient or \(\operatorname{cond}(Z^TZ)>\Gamma\); or \(\|AZ\|>\varepsilon_A\) when tangent steps are required. A boundary certificate records the failed inequality and its normalized violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton subspace state lies on the stated failure side when it inadequately captures the gradient, misses a required fraction of negative curvature, has a rank-deficient or ill-conditioned basis, or violates the required tangent-space compatibility. The failed quantitative test is the diagnostic certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak F=\{\Xi:\ \|P_Zg\|<\kappa_g\|g\|\ \lor\ \nu_-(Z^TBZ)<\kappa_-\nu_-(B)\ \lor\ \operatorname{rank}(Z)<r\ \lor\ \operatorname{cond}(Z^TZ)>\Gamma\ \lor\ \|AZ\|>\varepsilon_A\}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The adequacy region is the complement \(\mathfrak F^c\), where every applicable threshold is satisfied.
special_cases_latex: In unconstrained optimization the \(AZ\) condition is omitted.
For an orthonormal basis, \(Z^TZ=I\), so the basis-conditioning test is automatically satisfied with \(\Gamma\ge1\).
If \(B\succeq0\), the negative-curvature capture test is vacuous.
immediate_consequences_latex: A state in \(\mathfrak F\) identifies at least one concrete target for enrichment, reorthogonalization, or projection repair.
A state outside \(\mathfrak F\) passes only these diagnostics; it need not produce convergence without model-decrease and globalization conditions.
boundary_notes: The numerical thresholds are method-dependent and must be scaled consistently with the chosen norms.
Missing positive curvature, stale Hessian information, and inaccurate reduced solves may require additional failure tests.
The union is diagnostic rather than a theorem asserting divergence.

notation.meaning: Set of Newton subspace states failing at least one declared diagnostic threshold.

review_flags: This union-of-diagnostics definition is synthesized from the blueprint role and lacks an inspected authoritative source.
The intended failure boundaries and normalization conventions may differ and require exact-source review.

children.title: Missed Residual Components
children.top_down_role: Stagnation caused by omission of important first-order components.

knowledge_statements.title: Missed Residual Components
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced Newton solve can report zero projected residual and even return a zero step while an omitted gradient component remains nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, let \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}\) satisfy \(V^TV=I\), and let \(P=VV^T\). A subspace Newton step \(p=Vs\) satisfying \(V^T(HVs+g)=0\) makes only the projected residual vanish: \(P(Hp+g)=0\). The full residual is \(r=Hp+g=(I-P)r\), which need not be small. In particular, if \(V^Tg=0\) and \(V^THV\) is nonsingular, then \(s=0\) and \(p=0\), although \(g\ne0\). Thus omission of a nonzero component \((I-P)g\) can cause immediate stagnation at a nonstationary point.
assumptions_latex: \(V^THV\) is nonsingular for the stagnation example.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V^Tr=0\) does not imply \(r=0\); specifically, \(V^Tg=0\) and \(g\ne0\) imply \(p=0\) but leave a nonzero first-order residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a Galerkin Newton step when the gradient lies outside the trial subspace.

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis of the Newton trial subspace
orthogonal projector onto the trial subspace

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this subspace-stagnation formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Missed residual component in a projected Newton equation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be differentiable, let \(J=F'(x)\), and let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a trial/test subspace with orthogonal projector \(P_S\). For a subspace step \(p\in S\), define the full linearized residual \(r(p)=F(x)+Jp\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic Newton or Gauss-Newton linearizations with an orthogonal Galerkin projection and norm-based stopping tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The residual component missed by \(S\) at \((x,p)\) is \(r_{\mathrm{miss}}(p)=(I-P_S)r(p)\). Given tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{proj}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{full}}\geq0\), a missed-residual event occurs when \(\|P_Sr(p)\|\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{proj}}\) but \(\|r_{\mathrm{miss}}(p)\|>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{full}}\). Thus the projected Newton equation declares adequate solution while a non-negligible component of the full first-order equation remains unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A missed residual component is the part of the full Newton linearization residual orthogonal to the selected subspace. It is operationally missed when the projected residual satisfies its stopping test but the omitted component exceeds the full-system tolerance. This distinguishes genuine full residual reduction from apparent convergence visible only through the projection.
assumptions_latex: \(p\in S\), and all residual norms use the same Euclidean geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MissedRes}(x,p;S)\iff \|P_S(F(x)+F'(x)p)\|\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{proj}}\ \land\ \|(I-P_S)(F(x)+F'(x)p)\|>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{full}}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because \(P_S\) is orthogonal, \(\|r(p)\|^2=\|P_Sr(p)\|^2+\|r_{\mathrm{miss}}(p)\|^2\).
If \(V\) has orthonormal columns spanning \(S\), then \(r_{\mathrm{miss}}(p)=(I-VV^\top)(F(x)+Jp)\).
special_cases_latex: For an exact projected solve, \(P_Sr(p)=0\); it is a full Newton solve exactly when also \((I-P_S)r(p)=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The missed-component magnitude \(\eta_{\mathrm{miss}}=\|(I-P_S)r(p)\|\) is a certificate that projected convergence alone does not imply \(r(p)=0\).
boundary_notes: This definition does not assert that every omitted component causes nonlinear-iteration stagnation; it identifies the first-order information loss that can cause it.
For oblique Petrov-Galerkin projections, the orthogonal decomposition and Pythagorean identity must be replaced by the chosen test projector.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the selected subspace.
Component of the linearized residual invisible to the projected equation.

review_flags: No inspected source supplied an established named definition with these exact two-tolerance quantifiers; the record is a precise formalization of the blueprint role.

children.title: Missed Negative Curvature
children.top_down_role: False adequacy caused by omission of destabilizing curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Missed Negative Curvature
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace Hessian may be positive semidefinite even though an orthogonal, omitted direction has negative curvature and destabilizes the full quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and let \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}\) have orthonormal columns. It is possible that \(V^THV\succeq0\) while some \(z\ne0\), with \(V^Tz=0\), satisfies \(z^THz<0\). The reduced quadratic model therefore detects no negative curvature, whereas the full model \(m(p)=g^Tp+\tfrac12p^THp\) has negative curvature along \(z\). If additionally \(g^Tz=0\), then \(m(tz)=\tfrac12t^2z^THz<0\) for every \(t\ne0\), and it tends to \(-\infty\) as \(|t|\to\infty\). Hence reduced positive semidefiniteness is not a certificate of full-space curvature adequacy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V^THV\succeq0\) does not imply \(H\succeq0\), so a reduced Newton model can miss a full-space direction of strict negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced curvature can appear nonnegative while the full Newton model has an omitted descent direction.

notation.meaning: basis of the reduced trial subspace
full-space Hessian or symmetric Newton matrix

review_flags: No supplied locator directly addresses negative-curvature loss under subspace restriction.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The negative-curvature example is mathematically correct and the failure_boundary kind fits, but the record supplies no source or locator for the stated subspace failure phenomenon.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative curvature missed by a Newton subspace
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H=H^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a Hessian or symmetric model matrix, and let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonzero subspace. Write \(\lambda_{\min}(H)=\min_{\|d\|=1}d^\top Hd\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(H|_S)=\min_{d\in S,\|d\|=1}d^\top Hd\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric Newton, trust-region, or quadratic-model curvature tests using a restricted trial subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given tolerances \(\varepsilon,\varepsilon_S\geq0\), negative curvature is missed by \(S\) when \(\lambda_{\min}(H)<-\varepsilon\) while \(\lambda_{\min}(H|_S)\geq-\varepsilon_S\). Equivalently, the full space contains a unit direction \(d\) with \(d^\top Hd<-\varepsilon\), but every unit direction represented in \(S\) has Rayleigh quotient at least \(-\varepsilon_S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Missed negative curvature occurs when the full quadratic model has a materially negative-curvature direction but the reduced subspace model appears positive semidefinite, up to its curvature tolerance. The reduced model can therefore pass a curvature adequacy test even though the full model remains locally destabilizing.
assumptions_latex: The full and reduced curvature tolerances are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MissedNC}(H,S)\iff \lambda_{\min}(H)<-\varepsilon\ \land\ \lambda_{\min}(H|_S)\geq-\varepsilon_S.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(V\) has orthonormal columns spanning \(S\), then \(\lambda_{\min}(H|_S)=\lambda_{\min}(V^\top HV)\).
For zero tolerances, missed negative curvature means \(H\not\succeq0\) but \(V^\top HV\succeq0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(S=\mathbb R^n\), missed negative curvature is impossible.
If a negative-eigenvalue eigenvector of \(H\) belongs to \(S\), the corresponding negative curvature is not missed.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive semidefiniteness of the reduced Hessian does not imply positive semidefiniteness of the full Hessian unless the subspace is curvature-detecting for \(H\).
boundary_notes: The definition concerns omission of every curvature direction below the selected threshold, not failure to capture the most negative eigenvalue accurately.
Nonsymmetric Jacobians require a different stability notion; their quadratic form depends only on the symmetric part.

notation.meaning: Restriction of the quadratic form induced by H to the subspace S.

review_flags: The formalization is standard linear-algebraically, but no inspected source stated this failure mode as a named canonical definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative curvature missed by a Newton subspace

children.title: Subspace-Basis Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Numerical instability caused by poorly conditioned reduced coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace-Basis Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A poorly conditioned basis squares its condition number in the reduced identity-Hessian system, although an orthonormal basis of the same subspace is perfectly conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}\) have full column rank but nonorthogonal columns, and consider the benign full Newton matrix \(H=I\). The reduced matrix is then \(A=V^THV=V^TV\), and its spectral condition number satisfies \(\kappa_2(A)=\kappa_2(V)^2\). Consequently, solving \(As=-V^Tg\) may amplify relative roundoff and data perturbations on the scale of \(\kappa_2(V)^2\). If \(V=QR\) is a thin QR factorization, the same trial subspace expressed in the orthonormal basis \(Q\) has reduced matrix \(Q^THQ=I\). Thus severe reduced-system ill-conditioning may be caused solely by the chosen coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(H=I\) and conditioning is measured in the spectral norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(V^THV)=\kappa_2(V)^2\), while an orthonormal basis \(Q\) of \(\operatorname{range}(V)\) gives \(\kappa_2(Q^THQ)=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate ill-conditioning can destabilize a reduced solve without reflecting intrinsic subspace geometry.

notation.meaning: thin QR factorization of the reduced basis

review_flags: The identity-Hessian construction is elementary, but no supplied locator directly supports its numerical-stability interpretation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Under the stated specialization H=I, the condition-number identities are correct and fit the container. The numerical perturbation interpretation is nontrivial and lacks an inspectable source locator.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ill-conditioning of subspace coordinates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) have dimension \(k\), and let \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(V)=S\). Coordinates \(y\in\mathbb R^k\) represent full-space vectors by \(p=Vy\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Euclidean subspace methods with a possibly nonorthonormal basis; this definition isolates coordinate conditioning from the intrinsic choice of subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The basis \(V\) is \(\tau\)-ill-conditioned, for a prescribed \(\tau>1\), when \(\kappa_2(V)=\sigma_{\max}(V)/\sigma_{\min}(V)>\tau\). Its coordinate Gram matrix \(G=V^\top V\) then satisfies \(\kappa_2(G)=\kappa_2(V)^2\). The associated subspace-coordinate representation is ill-conditioned because relative perturbations in coefficients or projected data can be amplified by factors governed by \(\kappa_2(V)\), although the geometric subspace \(S\) itself is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subspace-basis ill-conditioning is poor numerical conditioning of the map from reduced coordinates to the represented full-space vector. It occurs when the ratio of the largest to smallest singular value of the basis exceeds a specified threshold. This is a property of the selected coordinates, not necessarily of the underlying subspace.
assumptions_latex: The domain and range use Euclidean norms.
\(\tau>1\) is fixed before declaring the basis ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{BasisIllCond}_\tau(V)\iff \kappa_2(V)>\tau,\qquad \kappa_2(V^\top V)=\kappa_2(V)^2.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\kappa_2(V)=\|V\|_2\|V^\dagger\|_2\), where \(V^\dagger\) is the Moore-Penrose left inverse.
The basis approaches rank deficiency precisely when \(\sigma_{\min}(V)\) approaches zero while \(\sigma_{\max}(V)\) remains bounded away from zero.
special_cases_latex: An orthonormal basis satisfies \(V^\top V=I\) and \(\kappa_2(V)=1\).
Rescaling one basis column can make \(V\) ill-conditioned without changing \(S\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Reorthogonalizing \(V\) can remove basis-induced conditioning while preserving \(\operatorname{range}(V)\).
Conditioning of a reduced Newton matrix \(V^\top HV\) may combine basis ill-conditioning with intrinsic conditioning of \(H\) on \(S\).
boundary_notes: A large condition number of \(V^\top HV\) alone does not establish basis ill-conditioning; the restricted operator may itself be ill-conditioned.
Rank-deficient matrices are excluded as bases; they have infinite condition number and do not provide unique coordinates.

notation.meaning: Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of the full-column-rank basis matrix.
Spectral condition number of the coordinate map.

review_flags: The matrix definition is standard, but the supplied sources were not located at an exact discussion of subspace-basis failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Ill-conditioning of subspace coordinates

children.title: Projection Incompatibility
children.top_down_role: Loss of feasibility or stationarity information under incompatible projections.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Incompatibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection not aligned with the constraint tangent space can satisfy the reduced Newton equations while producing an infeasible step or hiding a KKT residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the linearized equality constraints be \(Ap=0\), and let a reduced step have the form \(p=Vs\). If \(AV
e0\), the trial subspace is not contained in \(\ker A\), so projected stationarity \(V^T(HVs+g)=0\) does not enforce linearized feasibility. Indeed, choose \(s\) with \(AVs
e0\) and set \(g=-HVs+w\), where \(V^Tw=0\). Then the reduced stationarity residual is zero, but \(Ap=AVs
e0\). Conversely, projecting residuals with a map whose nullspace contains a nonzero KKT residual can conceal nonstationarity. Compatibility requires the step projection to preserve the linearized feasible tangent space and the residual projection to be injective on relevant KKT residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reduced stationarity alone does not imply \(Ap=0\); feasibility preservation requires \(\operatorname{range}(V)\subseteq\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An unconstrained trial projection may erase stationarity information or generate infeasible Newton steps.

notation.meaning: basis defining the projected Newton step

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the stated projection-compatibility boundary.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The constructed infeasible reduced step is valid, but the broader requirement that a residual projection be injective on 'relevant KKT residuals' is not formally specified and no source supports the proposed compatibility boundary.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incompatible projection of a stationarity-feasibility residual
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(R:Z\subseteq\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R^m\) be a residual map whose equation \(R(z)=0\) represents full feasibility and stationarity, and let \(\Pi:\mathbb R^m\to Y\) be a linear projection or restriction used to form the reduced equation \(\Pi R(z)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional projected root formulations, including projected KKT and constrained Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The projection \(\Pi\) is solution-incompatible with \(R\) on a set \(U\subseteq Z\) when there exists \(z\in U\) such that \(\Pi R(z)=0\) but \(R(z)\neq0\). It is first-order incompatible at a root \(z_*\) when \(R(z_*)=0\) and \(\ker(\Pi)\cap\operatorname{range}(R'(z_*))\neq\{0\}\). The first condition permits a false projected solution; the second permits a nonzero attainable linearized residual variation to be annihilated by the projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection incompatibility means that solving the projected equation does not preserve the full stationarity and feasibility equation. Globally on a neighborhood it appears as a projected zero that is not a true zero. At a true root it appears infinitesimally when the projection discards a nonzero residual variation produced by the Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is defined on \(U\), and it is differentiable at \(z_*\) for the first-order condition.
The zero of \(R\) encodes every residual block that the full constrained Newton system is intended to enforce.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Incompat}_U(\Pi,R)\iff \exists z\in U:\ \Pi R(z)=0\ \land\ R(z)\neq0.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Solution compatibility on \(U\) is the implication \(\Pi R(z)=0\Rightarrow R(z)=0\) for every \(z\in U\).
If \(R(U)\cap\ker(\Pi)=\{0\}\), then \(\Pi\) is solution-compatible on \(U\).
special_cases_latex: If \(R=(r_{\mathrm{stat}},r_{\mathrm{feas}})\) and \(\Pi R=r_{\mathrm{stat}}\), any point with \(r_{\mathrm{stat}}=0\) and \(r_{\mathrm{feas}}\neq0\) witnesses incompatibility.
An injective restriction of \(\Pi\) to \(R(U)\) cannot create a false projected zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: A projected stopping test based only on \(\|\Pi R(z)\|\) cannot certify full feasibility or stationarity under solution incompatibility.
boundary_notes: The first-order intersection condition is a local information-loss diagnostic; by itself it does not guarantee a nearby nonlinear false root.
This definition does not require the projection to be orthogonal.
review_flags: No inspected source established this exact global-and-linearized definition under the source node's name.
knowledge_statements.title: Incompatible projection of a stationarity-feasibility residual

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton-SQP interface for a fixed active set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), with twice differentiable data. Let \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^\top h(x)+\mu^\top g(x)\), and fix an active inequality index set \(\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming with a fixed active set; active-set changes, nonsmooth complementarity functions, and globalization are outside the defining identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constrained Newton-SQP interface at \((x,\lambda,\mu)\) is the identification of the Newton correction for the active KKT equations with the primal-dual KKT solution of the equality-constrained quadratic model. With \(A_{\mathcal A}(x)\) stacking \(h'(x)\) and \(g'_{\mathcal A}(x)\), \(c_{\mathcal A}(x)=(h(x),g_{\mathcal A}(x))\), and \(B=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,\lambda,\mu)\), both are represented by \(\begin{bmatrix}B&A_{\mathcal A}^\top\\A_{\mathcal A}&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}d\\\delta y\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}\nabla_xL\\c_{\mathcal A}\end{bmatrix}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface is the exact algebraic correspondence between Newton's method applied to the active KKT equations and the optimality equations of the local SQP quadratic subproblem. The primal variable is the SQP step, while the dual correction updates the multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is held fixed while the system is formed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{NewtonKKT}_{\mathcal A}(x,\lambda,\mu)=\operatorname{KKT}\!\left(\min_d\ \nabla f(x)^\top d+\tfrac12d^\top Bd\ \text{ subject to }c_{\mathcal A}(x)+A_{\mathcal A}(x)d=0\right).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The block system is the saddle-point equation for the quadratic model with linearized active constraints.
Replacing \(B\) by an approximation produces a quasi-Newton SQP interface rather than the exact Newton identity.
special_cases_latex: With equality constraints only, \(A_{\mathcal A}=h'(x)\).
With no constraints, the interface reduces to \(Bd=-\nabla f(x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Nonsingularity of the displayed KKT matrix makes the local primal-dual correction unique.
boundary_notes: Inactive inequalities and multiplier-sign tests still determine whether the chosen active set is valid.
A line search, filter, merit function, or trust region globalizes the step but is not part of this local algebraic interface.

notation.meaning: Correction to the multipliers associated with equality and active inequality constraints.
Jacobian of the equality constraints and selected active inequalities.

review_flags: The identity is standard, but the inspected source passages did not provide a precise SQP locator supporting this exact fixed-active-set formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Newton-SQP interface for a fixed active set

children.top_down_role: First-order stationarity and complementarity families underlying constrained Newton equations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-dual stationarity interface for smooth constrained optimization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0\}\), where \(f,h,g\) are continuously differentiable. Let \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^\top h(x)+\mu^\top g(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programs using the convention \(g(x)\leq0\); the interface is a root/complementarity representation, not an optimality theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constrained stationarity interface is the primal-dual system \(0=\nabla_xL(x,\lambda,\mu)\), \(h(x)=0\), \(g(x)\leq0\), \(\mu\geq0\), and \(\mu_jg_j(x)=0\) for every inequality index \(j\). Equivalently, it is the generalized equation \(0\in\nabla f(x)+h'(x)^\top\lambda+N_{\{g\leq0\}}^{\mathrm{mult}}(x)\), with the multiplier normal term represented explicitly by \(g'(x)^\top\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface converts geometric first-order stationarity into a system in primal variables and Lagrange multipliers. Its blocks encode stationarity of the Lagrangian, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity. These are the equations and inequalities subsequently linearized by constrained Newton and SQP methods.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal S=\{(x,\lambda,\mu):\nabla_xL=0,\ h=0,\ g\leq0,\ \mu\geq0,\ \mu\odot g=0\}\) is the constrained primal-dual stationarity set.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Complementarity is equivalently \(0\leq\mu\perp-g(x)\geq0\).
At a feasible point, stationarity can be written \(-\nabla f(x)\in h'(x)^\top\mathbb R^m+g'(x)^\top N_{\mathbb R_-^r}(g(x))\).
special_cases_latex: Without inequalities, the interface contains only Lagrangian stationarity and equality feasibility.
Without equalities, it becomes a stationarity-complementarity system.
immediate_consequences_latex: Any smooth residual or semismooth complementarity reformulation used by a Newton method must preserve the zero set \(\mathcal S\).
boundary_notes: Existence of multipliers at a local minimizer requires an appropriate constraint qualification.
Satisfaction of this first-order interface does not by itself imply local minimality in a nonconvex problem.

notation.meaning: Componentwise product of inequality multipliers and constraint values.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT point for a smooth nonlinear program
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(h_i(x)=0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), and \(g_j(x)\leq0\), \(j=1,\ldots,r\), with continuously differentiable data. Define \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^\top h(x)+\mu^\top g(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming; this record defines KKT satisfaction and does not claim that every local solution satisfies it without a constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A triple \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^r\) is a KKT triple when \(\nabla_xL(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)=0\), \(h(x^*)=0\), \(g(x^*)\leq0\), \(\mu^*\geq0\), and \(\mu_j^*g_j(x^*)=0\) for every \(j\). A feasible point \(x^*\) is a KKT point if at least one multiplier pair \((\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) makes it a KKT triple.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT conditions comprise Lagrangian stationarity, equality and inequality feasibility, nonnegative inequality multipliers, and componentwise complementarity. A KKT point is a primal point for which suitable multipliers exist; the multipliers need not be unique unless additional regularity holds.
assumptions_latex: Equality multipliers \(\lambda^*\) are unrestricted in sign.
Inequality multipliers \(\mu^*\) correspond to constraints written as \(g_j\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\in\operatorname{KKT}\iff\exists(\lambda^*,\mu^*):\ \nabla_xL=0,\ h=0,\ g\leq0,\ \mu^*\geq0,\ \mu^*\odot g=0.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\mathcal A(x^*)=\{j:g_j(x^*)=0\}\), complementarity is equivalent to \(\mu_j^*=0\) for every \(j\notin\mathcal A(x^*)\).
Stationarity is \(-\nabla f(x^*)=h'(x^*)^\top\lambda^*+g'(x^*)^\top\mu^*\).
special_cases_latex: When \(r=0\), the system reduces to equality-constrained Lagrange stationarity.
When \(m=0\), it reduces to inequality feasibility, dual feasibility, complementarity, and stationarity.
immediate_consequences_latex: Strict complementarity means \(\mu_j^*>0\) for every active inequality \(j\).
boundary_notes: KKT conditions are generally necessary only under a constraint qualification and are sufficient only under additional structure such as convexity.
The sign of inequality multipliers reverses if constraints are instead written as \(g_j\geq0\).

notation.meaning: Index set of active inequality constraints.
Lagrangian for the stated sign convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian for a General Nonlinear Program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the convention that equality constraints satisfy c_i(x)=0, inequality constraints satisfy c_i(x)\ge 0, and their multipliers enter with a minus sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonlinear program with objective \(f\), equality-index set \(\mathcal E\), inequality-index set \(\mathcal I\), and constraint functions \(c_i\), its Lagrangian is
\[
\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\sum_{i\in\mathcal E\cup\mathcal I}\lambda_i c_i(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonlinear program with equality and inequality constraints, the Lagrangian is the objective minus the sum of each constraint function multiplied by its Lagrange multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\sum_{i\in\mathcal E\cup\mathcal I}\lambda_i c_i(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness of KKT Multipliers under LICQ
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Captures the precise multiplier-uniqueness assertion; the extract's qualitative claim that strict complementarity usually aids identification and rapid convergence is not promoted to a theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^*\) be a local solution of a continuously differentiable nonlinear program. If LICQ holds at \(x^*\), then the KKT multiplier vector at \(x^*\), when it exists, is unique. Equivalently, if \(\lambda^*\) and \(\mu^*\) both satisfy the KKT conditions at \(x^*\), then
\[
\lambda^*=\mu^*.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local solution where LICQ holds, there is at most one Lagrange multiplier vector satisfying the KKT conditions.
assumptions_latex: \lambda^*\text{ and }\mu^*\text{ satisfy the KKT conditions at }x^*
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda^*=\mu^*

children.title: Equality-Constrained KKT Conditions
children.top_down_role: The stationarity family underlying equality-constrained Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained KKT Conditions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular equality-constrained local minimizer, feasibility holds and the objective gradient is a linear combination of the constraint gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) are continuously differentiable. A feasible point \(x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies the equality-constrained KKT conditions if there exists \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that \[h(x^*)=0,\qquad \nabla f(x^*)+J_h(x^*)^T\lambda^*=0.\] Equivalently, for the Lagrangian \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)\), one has \(h(x^*)=0\) and \(\nabla_xL(x^*,\lambda^*)=0\). If \(x^*\) is a local minimizer and \(J_h(x^*)\) has full row rank, then such a multiplier exists.
assumptions_latex: \(J_h(x^*)\) has full row rank for the necessity assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that \(h(x^*)=0\) and \(\nabla_xL(x^*,\lambda^*)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order KKT system for smooth equality-constrained nonlinear programming.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT conditions for equality constraints
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), where \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are continuously differentiable. Let \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^\top h(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional equality-constrained nonlinear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((x^*,\lambda^*)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) satisfies the equality-constrained KKT conditions when \(h(x^*)=0\) and \(\nabla_xL(x^*,\lambda^*)=\nabla f(x^*)+h'(x^*)^\top\lambda^*=0\). The primal point \(x^*\) is an equality-constrained KKT point when such a multiplier \(\lambda^*\) exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For equality constraints, KKT satisfaction consists exactly of primal feasibility and Lagrangian stationarity. There are no multiplier-sign or complementarity conditions. The stationarity equation states that the objective gradient lies in the span of the equality-constraint gradients.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every component of \(h\) are continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
The equality multipliers are unrestricted real numbers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\in\operatorname{KKT}_{=}(f,h)\iff h(x^*)=0\ \land\ \exists\lambda^*:\nabla f(x^*)+h'(x^*)^\top\lambda^*=0.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\nabla f(x^*)\in\operatorname{range}(h'(x^*)^\top)\) with the corresponding sign absorbed into \(\lambda^*\).
For every linearized feasible direction \(d\in\ker h'(x^*)\), stationarity implies \(\nabla f(x^*)^\top d=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m=0\), the definition reduces to unconstrained stationarity \(\nabla f(x^*)=0\).
If \(h'(x^*)\) has full row rank, the multiplier satisfying stationarity is unique.
immediate_consequences_latex: Newton linearization of these two equations produces the classical equality-constrained saddle-point system.
boundary_notes: At a local minimizer, existence of a multiplier is not automatic when the equality gradients are rank deficient.
Feasibility plus stationarity is not sufficient for local minimality without a suitable second-order or convexity condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Constrained KKT Conditions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT combines stationarity, primal feasibility, nonnegative inequality multipliers, and complementary slackness; a constraint qualification makes it necessary at a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(c(x)\le0\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) are continuously differentiable. A feasible point \(x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies the KKT conditions if there exist \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(\mu^*\in\mathbb{R}^q\) such that \[\nabla f(x^*)+J_h(x^*)^T\lambda^*+J_c(x^*)^T\mu^*=0,\quad h(x^*)=0,\quad c(x^*)\le0,\] \[\mu^*\ge0,\qquad \mu_i^*c_i(x^*)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,q).\] At a local minimizer these conditions are necessary under a constraint qualification such as LICQ or MFCQ.
assumptions_latex: A first-order constraint qualification holds for the necessity assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(\mu^*\in\mathbb{R}^q\) satisfying stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth KKT system with equalities and inequalities written using the nonpositive constraint convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT conditions for inequality constraints
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(g_j(x)\leq0\), \(j=1,\ldots,r\), with continuously differentiable data. Define \(L(x,\mu)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^r\mu_jg_j(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional inequality-constrained nonlinear programming using the \(g\leq0\) convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((x^*,\mu^*)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^r\) satisfies the inequality-constrained KKT conditions when \(\nabla f(x^*)+g'(x^*)^\top\mu^*=0\), \(g(x^*)\leq0\), \(\mu^*\geq0\), and \(\mu_j^*g_j(x^*)=0\) for all \(j\). An inequality-constrained KKT point is a primal point belonging to at least one such pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inequality KKT conditions combine stationarity with primal feasibility, nonnegative multipliers, and complementarity. Complementarity restricts nonzero multipliers to active constraints, thereby producing the active-set and complementarity equations used in constrained Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\in\operatorname{KKT}_{\leq}(f,g)\iff\exists\mu^*\geq0:\ \nabla f(x^*)+g'(x^*)^\top\mu^*=0,\ g(x^*)\leq0,\ \mu^*\odot g(x^*)=0.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(s=-g(x^*)\), feasibility and complementarity are \(s\geq0\), \(\mu^*\geq0\), and \(\mu^*\odot s=0\).
If \(\mathcal A(x^*)=\{j:g_j(x^*)=0\}\), then stationarity uses only active gradients because \(\mu_j^*=0\) for \(j\notin\mathcal A(x^*)\).
special_cases_latex: For a strictly inactive constraint \(g_j(x^*)<0\), complementarity forces \(\mu_j^*=0\).
Under strict complementarity, every active constraint has \(\mu_j^*>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Fixing an active set converts the stationarity and active-feasibility blocks into a smooth equality system suitable for Newton linearization.
boundary_notes: KKT multiplier existence at local minimizers depends on constraint regularity.
Complementarity is nonsmooth if encoded by a minimum or Fischer-Burmeister residual; that encoding is not part of this definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order KKT Necessary Conditions under LICQ
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For the sign convention c_i(x)\ge 0 and \(\mathcal L=f-\sum_i\lambda_i c_i\); includes equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_x f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_i(x)=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\qquad c_i(x)\ge 0\ (i\in\mathcal I),
\]
where \(f\) and all \(c_i\) are continuously differentiable. If \(x^*\) is a local solution and LICQ holds at \(x^*\), then there exists \(\lambda^*\) such that
\[
\nabla_x\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)=0,
\]
\[
c_i(x^*)=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\qquad c_i(x^*)\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal I),
\]
\[
\lambda_i^*\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal I),\qquad \lambda_i^*c_i(x^*)=0\ (i\in\mathcal E\cup\mathcal I).
\]
Consequently, \(\lambda_i^*=0\) for every inactive inequality constraint, and stationarity can be written
\[
0=\nabla f(x^*)-\sum_{i\in\mathcal A(x^*)}\lambda_i^*\nabla c_i(x^*).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At any local solution of a continuously differentiable nonlinear program where LICQ holds, a Lagrange multiplier vector exists that satisfies stationarity, primal feasibility, nonnegative inequality multipliers, and complementarity. Inactive inequality constraints have zero multipliers, so only active constraints appear in stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\lambda^*:\ \nabla_x\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)=0,\ c_i(x^*)=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\ c_i(x^*)\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal I),\ \lambda_i^*\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal I),\ \lambda_i^*c_i(x^*)=0\ (i\in\mathcal E\cup\mathcal I)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact tangent-linearization constraint-qualification interface
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0\}\), let \(x\in\Omega\), and let \(\mathcal A(x)=\{j:g_j(x)=0\}\). Denote the Bouligand tangent cone by \(T_\Omega(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order geometry of smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear constraints; this interface formalizes when linearized constraints faithfully represent feasible tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linearized cone is \(L_\Omega(x)=\{d:h'(x)d=0,\ \nabla g_j(x)^\top d\leq0\ \forall j\in\mathcal A(x)\}\). The exact tangent-linearization constraint qualification holds at \(x\) when \(T_\Omega(x)=L_\Omega(x)\). This equality is the interface connecting actual feasible tangent geometry to multiplier-based stationarity and linearized Newton or SQP constraint equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint qualification is represented here by exact agreement between the true tangent cone and the cone predicted from first derivatives of the active constraints. Without this agreement, the linearized system may admit spurious directions or omit geometric restrictions, and multiplier conclusions based solely on that system can fail.
assumptions_latex: \(T_\Omega(x)\) is the cone of limits of scaled feasible displacements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CQ}_{\mathrm{tan}}(x)\iff T_\Omega(x)=\{d:h'(x)d=0,\ \nabla g_j(x)^\top d\leq0\ \forall j\in\mathcal A(x)\}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under the opposite convention \(c_j(x)\geq0\), the active linearized inequalities become \(\nabla c_j(x)^\top d\geq0\).
The equality says every linearized feasible direction is realizable as a sequential feasible direction; the reverse inclusion always holds under differentiability.
special_cases_latex: For full-row-rank equality constraints alone, the implicit-function geometry gives \(T_\Omega(x)=\ker h'(x)\).
LICQ and MFCQ are checkable sufficient conditions for standard first-order multiplier conclusions, although they are not identical definitions of tangent-cone exactness.
immediate_consequences_latex: When the equality holds, absence of a true feasible descent direction is equivalent to absence of a linearized feasible descent direction.
boundary_notes: Different texts use weaker or stronger conditions under the generic name constraint qualification.
Tangent-cone exactness does not by itself impose second-order curvature regularity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LICQ and MFCQ at a feasible nonlinear-programming point
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{x:h_i(x)=0,\ i=1,\ldots,m;\ g_j(x)\leq0,\ j=1,\ldots,r\}\), let \(x\in\Omega\), and set \(\mathcal A(x)=\{j:g_j(x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programs; the record defines two principal first-order constraint qualifications rather than asserting their consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ requires linear independence of all equality and active-inequality gradients. MFCQ requires independent equality gradients together with one direction tangent to all equalities and strictly entering every active inequality. These are distinct first-order regularity conditions used to support KKT representations and multiplier stability.
assumptions_latex: All constraint functions are continuously differentiable near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{LICQ}(x)\iff\operatorname{rank}[h'(x)^\top\ \ g'_{\mathcal A(x)}(x)^\top]=m+|\mathcal A(x)|\), while \(\operatorname{MFCQ}(x)\iff\operatorname{rank}h'(x)=m\) and \(\exists d:h'(x)d=0,\ g'_{\mathcal A(x)}(x)d<0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: MFCQ is equivalent to the absence of a nonzero abnormal multiplier pair \((\lambda,\mu)\) with \(h'(x)^\top\lambda+g'_{\mathcal A(x)}(x)^\top\mu=0\) and \(\mu\geq0\).
LICQ implies MFCQ whenever the stated active-gradient family is linearly independent.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, both conditions reduce to full row rank of \(h'(x)\).
If no constraint is active and there are no equalities, both conditions hold vacuously.
immediate_consequences_latex: LICQ makes KKT multipliers unique when they exist.
MFCQ excludes abnormal first-order stationarity and supports existence and boundedness of multiplier sets under standard hypotheses.
boundary_notes: MFCQ does not require active inequality gradients to be mutually independent.
Slater's condition is a different, usually convex, qualification and is not included in this definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Constraint Qualification Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order Abadie regularity says that every vector satisfying the quadraticized active constraints is realizable by a second-order feasible arc along the chosen direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{x:h(x)=0,\ c(x)\le0\}\), let \(x\in F\), and let \(d\in T_F(x)\). Define \(T_F^2(x;d)\) as the set of limits \(w\) obtained from feasible arcs \(x+t_kd+	frac12t_k^2w_k\in F\), where \(t_k\downarrow0\) and \(w_k	o w\). The second-order linearized set consists of all \(w\) satisfying \[
abla h_j(x)^Tw+d^T
abla^2h_j(x)d=0\] for every equality and \[
abla c_i(x)^Tw+d^T
abla^2c_i(x)d\le0\] for each active \(i\) with \(
abla c_i(x)^Td=0\). The second-order Abadie constraint qualification along \(d\) is the equality of these two sets.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The qualification holds exactly when \(T_F^2(x;d)=L_F^2(x;d)\), where \(L_F^2(x;d)\) is the displayed second-order linearized set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact sequential-linearized critical-direction qualification
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x^*\) be a KKT point of \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), \(g(x)\leq0\), with multipliers \((\lambda^*,\mu^*)\). Set \(\mathcal A_+=\{j:g_j(x^*)=0,\ \mu_j^*>0\}\) and \(\mathcal A_0=\{j:g_j(x^*)=0,\ \mu_j^*=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programs at a specified KKT pair; the qualification is multiplier-dependent when multipliers are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the linearized critical cone \(G(x^*,\mu^*)=\{d:h'(x^*)d=0,\ \nabla g_j(x^*)^\top d=0\ \forall j\in\mathcal A_+,\ \nabla g_j(x^*)^\top d\leq0\ \forall j\in\mathcal A_0\}\). Define \(S(x^*,\mu^*)\) as the set of limits \(d=\lim d_k\) for which \(t_k\downarrow0\), \(x^*+t_kd_k\) is feasible, and \(g_j(x^*+t_kd_k)=0\) for every \(j\in\mathcal A_+\). The second-order constraint-qualification interface is exact when \(S(x^*,\mu^*)=G(x^*,\mu^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This qualification requires every direction predicted by the multiplier-sensitive linearized critical cone to be realizable by a sequence of feasible displacements that keeps strongly active inequalities active. It connects actual critical geometry to the directions on which the Lagrangian Hessian is tested.
assumptions_latex: The active set is partitioned using the specified multiplier \(\mu^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SOCQ}(x^*,\mu^*)\iff S(x^*,\mu^*)=G(x^*,\mu^*).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inclusion \(S(x^*,\mu^*)\subseteq G(x^*,\mu^*)\) follows from differentiability; exactness requires the reverse inclusion.
Using constraints written as \(c_j\geq0\) reverses the weak-active inequalities in \(G\).
special_cases_latex: Under strict complementarity, \(\mathcal A_0=\varnothing\), so \(G\) is the nullspace of the equality and active-inequality Jacobian.
For equality constraints only, the condition compares feasible sequential tangent directions with \(\ker h'(x^*)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Under exactness, a curvature inequality established on sequential critical directions extends to the entire linearized critical cone.
boundary_notes: This record uses a critical-direction exactness condition, not the unrelated phrase second-order constraint qualification sometimes used for second-order tangent sets.
If multipliers are nonunique, the condition must be checked for the multiplier relevant to the curvature statement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained Lagrangian-curvature conditions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) be a KKT triple for a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program, let \(H_L=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\), and let \(C(x^*,\mu^*)\) be its multiplier-sensitive critical cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonconvex nonlinear programming at a fixed KKT triple.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constrained second-order condition family consists of sign conditions on the Lagrangian quadratic form \(q(d)=d^\top H_Ld\) over critical directions. Its necessary-form predicate is \(q(d)\geq0\) for every sequentially realizable critical direction \(d\). Its sufficient-form predicate is \(q(d)>0\) for every nonzero direction in the linearized critical cone \(C(x^*,\mu^*)\). The two predicates differ both in strictness and in the direction set quantified over.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constrained second-order conditions test the Hessian of the Lagrangian, not merely the objective Hessian, and restrict the test to directions compatible with first-order feasibility and complementarity. Nonnegative curvature is the necessary-form condition; strictly positive curvature on all nonzero linearized critical directions is the sufficient-form condition.
assumptions_latex: Critical directions satisfy the equality tangency, active-inequality sign, and positive-multiplier orthogonality conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SONC}(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\!:\ q\geq0\text{ on }S,\qquad \operatorname{SOSC}(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\!:\ q>0\text{ on }C\setminus\{0\}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: In finite dimensions, strict positivity on \(C\setminus\{0\}\) is equivalent to the existence of \(\gamma>0\) such that \(d^\top H_Ld\geq\gamma\|d\|^2\) for all \(d\in C\).
If the sequential and linearized critical cones coincide, both predicates are evaluated on the same geometric cone, with only nonnegative versus positive curvature distinguishing them.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints, the critical cone is \(\ker h'(x^*)\).
For an unconstrained stationary point, the tests reduce to positive semidefiniteness or positive definiteness of \(\nabla^2f(x^*)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: These predicates determine whether a constrained Newton matrix has adequate curvature on primal feasible directions, separately from its behavior normal to the constraints.
boundary_notes: A predicate called necessary or sufficient becomes an optimality implication only with the hypotheses of the corresponding theorem.
Multiplier nonuniqueness can make the Lagrangian Hessian and critical cone multiplier-dependent.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \mathcal E and \mathcal I be finite index sets and let f and c_i be smooth real-valued functions on a common subset of \mathbb R^n. The constrained problem is \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\ge 0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). Its feasible set is \(\Omega=\{x:c_i(x)=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\ c_i(x)\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal I)\}\), so the problem is equivalently \(\min_{x\in\Omega}f(x)\). Necessary conditions must hold at every solution under their hypotheses, whereas sufficient conditions guarantee that a point is a solution. In the unconstrained twice-differentiable case, a local minimizer x^* satisfies \(
abla f(x^*)=0\) and \(
abla^2f(x^*)\succeq0\); if \(
abla f(x^*)=0\) and \(
abla^2f(x^*)\succ0\), then x^* is a strong local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth constrained nonlinear program minimizes a smooth objective over points satisfying finitely many smooth equality and inequality constraints. The feasible set collects exactly those points, allowing the problem to be written as minimization over that set. Necessary conditions are required of solutions under their hypotheses, while sufficient conditions certify solutions. As the unconstrained baseline, every twice-differentiable local minimizer has zero gradient and positive-semidefinite Hessian, and zero gradient with positive-definite Hessian guarantees a strong local minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the unconstrained second-order statements, }f\text{ is twice differentiable near }x^*
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\Omega=\{x:c_i(x)=0\  orall i\in\mathcal E,\ c_i(x)\ge0\  orall i\in\mathcal I\},\qquad \min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\{f(x):x\in\Omega\}=\min_{x\in\Omega}f(x);\quad x^*	ext{ locally minimizes }f\Rightarrow 
abla f(x^*)=0,\ 
abla^2f(x^*)\succeq0;\quad 
abla f(x^*)=0,\ 
abla^2f(x^*)\succ0\Rightarrow x^*	ext{ is a strong local minimizer}.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Necessary Condition for Constrained NLP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an LICQ local minimizer, the Lagrangian Hessian is nonnegative along every critical direction compatible with the active constraints and KKT multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(c(x)\le0\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}^q\) are twice continuously differentiable. Let \(x^*\) be a local minimizer satisfying LICQ, and let \((\lambda^*,\mu^*)\in\mathbb{R}^m	imes\mathbb{R}^q\) be its KKT multipliers. Define \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\mu^Tc(x)\), \(I(x^*)=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0\}\), and \[C(x^*,\mu^*)=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:J_h(x^*)d=0,\ 
abla c_i(x^*)^Td=0	ext{ if }i\in I(x^*)	ext{ and }\mu_i^*>0,\ 
abla c_i(x^*)^Td\le0	ext{ if }i\in I(x^*)	ext{ and }\mu_i^*=0\}.\] Then every \(d\in C(x^*,\mu^*)\) satisfies \[d^T
abla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)d\ge0.\] Thus the Lagrangian Hessian is positive semidefinite on the constrained critical cone, though not necessarily on the entire space.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
\(x^*\) is a local minimizer satisfying LICQ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)d\ge0\) for every \(d\in C(x^*,\mu^*)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LICQ-based second-order necessity on the KKT critical cone for smooth nonlinear programming.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained second-order necessary-condition predicate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program, let \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) be a KKT triple, let \(H_L=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\), and let \(S(x^*,\mu^*)\) denote the sequential critical-direction set preserving constraints with positive multipliers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming at a specified KKT triple; this record defines the curvature predicate rather than asserting necessity at every local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constrained second-order necessary condition holds at \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) when \(d^\top H_Ld\geq0\) for every \(d\in S(x^*,\mu^*)\). If the critical-direction constraint qualification \(S(x^*,\mu^*)=G(x^*,\mu^*)\) holds, the same condition can be written over the linearized critical cone \(G\): \(d^\top H_Ld\geq0\) for all \(d\in G(x^*,\mu^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second-order necessary-condition predicate requires nonnegative Lagrangian curvature along every critical direction that can be realized by feasible sequences while preserving strongly active constraints. Under exact correspondence between sequential and linearized critical directions, the test extends to the complete linearized critical cone.
assumptions_latex: The sequential critical-direction set is formed relative to \(\mu^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SONC}(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\iff d^\top\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)d\geq0\quad\forall d\in S(x^*,\mu^*).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under \(S=G\), SONC is positive semidefiniteness of the Lagrangian Hessian restricted to \(G\).
For equality constraints with full-rank Jacobian, SONC is \(d^\top H_Ld\geq0\) for every \(d\in\ker h'(x^*)\).
special_cases_latex: In the unconstrained case, SONC is \(\nabla^2f(x^*)\succeq0\).
Under strict complementarity, critical directions are tangent to every active inequality.
immediate_consequences_latex: A direction \(d\in S\) with \(d^\top H_Ld<0\) is a certificate that this SONC predicate fails.
boundary_notes: Nonnegative curvature is not sufficient for strict local minimality.
The theorem making this condition necessary additionally requires local minimality and the source's stated constraint qualification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained second-order sufficient-condition predicate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
For a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program, let \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) be a KKT triple. Let \(H_L=
abla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\), and define \(C(x^*,\mu^*)=\{d:h'(x^*)d=0,\ 
abla g_j(x^*)^	op d=0\ (\mu_j^*>0),\ 
abla g_j(x^*)^	op d\leq0\ (g_j(x^*)=0,\mu_j^*=0)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming at a specified KKT triple.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constrained second-order sufficient condition holds when \(d^\top H_Ld>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in C(x^*,\mu^*)\). Equivalently in finite dimensions, there exists \(\gamma>0\) such that \(d^\top H_Ld\geq\gamma\|d\|^2\) for every \(d\in C(x^*,\mu^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sufficient-condition predicate requires uniformly positive Lagrangian curvature along every nonzero linearized critical direction. Equality-tangent directions and directions tangent to positive-multiplier inequalities are tested, while weakly active inequalities permit only their linearized feasible side.
assumptions_latex: The critical cone is constructed using the stated \(g\leq0\) convention and multiplier \(\mu^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SOSC}(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\iff d^\top\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)d>0\quad\forall d\in C(x^*,\mu^*)\setminus\{0\}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(Z\) spans a linear critical subspace, the condition is \(Z^\top H_LZ\succ0\).
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints, \(C=\ker h'(x^*)\).
For an unconstrained stationary point, SOSC is \(\nabla^2f(x^*)\succ0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Together with the KKT hypotheses, this predicate yields the strict-local-minimum conclusion stated by the cited result.
Uniform positivity supplies a positive reduced-curvature margin for local constrained Newton models.
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness only on the span of positive-multiplier active gradients can be stronger than the critical-cone condition when weakly active constraints exist.
The condition is local and does not imply global optimality for a nonconvex program.
