knowledge_statements.title: Classical Second-Order Sufficient Condition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT, LICQ, and strict positivity of the Lagrangian Hessian on every nonzero critical direction guarantee a strict local minimizer with quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(c(x)\le0\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}^q\) are twice continuously differentiable. Suppose \(x^*\) is feasible, LICQ holds, and \((\lambda^*,\mu^*)\in\mathbb{R}^m	imes\mathbb{R}^q\) satisfies the KKT conditions. Define \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^Th(x)+\mu^Tc(x)\), \(I(x^*)=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0\}\), and \[C(x^*,\mu^*)=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:J_h(x^*)d=0,\ 
abla c_i(x^*)^Td=0	ext{ if }i\in I(x^*)	ext{ and }\mu_i^*>0,\ 
abla c_i(x^*)^Td\le0	ext{ if }i\in I(x^*)	ext{ and }\mu_i^*=0\}.\] If \[d^T
abla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)d>0\qquad	ext{for every }d\in C(x^*,\mu^*)\setminus\{0\},\] then \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer. More precisely, there exist \(\alpha>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) of \(x^*\) such that \[f(x)\ge f(x^*)+\alpha\lVert x-x^*Vert^2\] for every feasible \(x\in U\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
LICQ and the KKT conditions hold at \(x^*\).
The Lagrangian Hessian is positive on every nonzero \(d\in C(x^*,\mu^*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible point \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer satisfying local quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict Lagrangian curvature on the KKT critical cone implies quadratic growth.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Classical active-tangent second-order sufficient condition
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) satisfy KKT for \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), \(g(x)\leq0\). Let \(\mathcal A(x^*)=\{j:g_j(x^*)=0\}\), \(H_L=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\), and \(T_{\mathcal A}=\{d:h'(x^*)d=0,\ \nabla g_j(x^*)^\top d=0\ \forall j\in\mathcal A(x^*)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The classical smooth active-set regime with strict complementarity; this is stronger and more specialized than the general critical-cone SOSC.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The classical second-order sufficient condition holds when strict complementarity \(\mu_j^*>0\) holds for every \(j\in\mathcal A(x^*)\) and \(d^\top H_Ld>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in T_{\mathcal A}\). Thus the Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on the tangent space obtained by treating all active inequalities as equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical condition combines strict complementarity with positive Lagrangian curvature on the nullspace of the equality and active-inequality Jacobian. In this regime the critical cone is a linear tangent space, so the curvature check becomes a reduced-Hessian positive-definiteness test.
assumptions_latex: Every active inequality is strictly complementary: \(\mu_j^*>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{ClassicalSOSC}(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\iff \bigl[\mu_j^*>0\ \forall j\in\mathcal A(x^*)\bigr]\ \land\ \bigl[d^\top H_Ld>0\ \forall d\in T_{\mathcal A}\setminus\{0\}\bigr].\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(Z\) has columns forming a basis of \(T_{\mathcal A}\), then the curvature condition is \(Z^\top H_LZ\succ0\).
Under strict complementarity, \(T_{\mathcal A}\) equals the multiplier-sensitive critical cone.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, strict complementarity is vacuous and the condition is positive definiteness on \(\ker h'(x^*)\).
If \(T_{\mathcal A}=\{0\}\), the curvature condition is vacuous, while KKT and strict complementarity remain required.
immediate_consequences_latex: Under the cited smooth hypotheses, the condition supports a strict local minimum.
With full row rank of the active Jacobian, the associated reduced Hessian and saddle-point Newton system have the standard nonsingularity relationship.
boundary_notes: General SOSC does not require strict complementarity and tests a cone rather than necessarily a subspace.
This condition does not cover degenerate active constraints or weakly active inequalities.

notation.meaning: Tangent space to all equality and active inequality constraints.
Any full-column-rank basis of the active tangent space.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Second-Order Sufficient Condition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong SOSC requires uniform positive Lagrangian curvature on the subspace fixed by equalities and positive-multiplier active constraints, a larger set than the critical cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a KKT point \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\), define the strong critical subspace \[S(x^*,\mu^*)=\{d:J_h(x^*)d=0,\ \nabla c_i(x^*)^Td=0\text{ for every }i\in I_+(x^*,\mu^*)\},\] where \(I_+(x^*,\mu^*)=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0,\ \mu_i^*>0\}\). The strong second-order sufficient condition holds if there exists \(\gamma>0\) such that \[d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)d\ge\gamma\lVert d\rVert^2\qquad\text{for every }d\in S(x^*,\mu^*).\] Since the ordinary critical cone is contained in this subspace, this condition implies the classical second-order sufficient condition and supplies the strengthened curvature hypothesis used in local primal-dual stability results.
assumptions_latex: The problem data are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform positivity holds on \(S(x^*,\mu^*)\), and therefore also on the ordinary KKT critical cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform Lagrangian curvature on the strong critical subspace used in primal-dual stability analysis.

notation.meaning: active inequalities having strictly positive multipliers

review_flags: Definitions of strong SOSC vary; the stated positive-multiplier-subspace convention requires locator-level confirmation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong second-order sufficient condition on the active-constraint tangent space
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(f,c_i\in C^2\) define \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\ge 0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). Let \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\sum_i\lambda_i c_i(x)\), and let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfy the KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming. This slot uses the strong form based on all active constraint gradients; it is particularly natural under LICQ and strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The pair \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies the strong second-order sufficient condition if the active-gradient matrix \(A_*\), whose rows are \(
abla c_i(x^*)^T\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\cup\mathcal A_I(x^*)\), has full row rank, strict complementarity holds, and there exists \(\gamma>0\) such that \[d^T
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)d\ge \gamma\|d\|_2^2\qquad	ext{for every }d\in\ker A_*.\] Equivalently, for any full-column-rank matrix \(Z_*\) with \(\operatorname{Range}(Z_*)=\ker A_*\), the reduced Hessian \(Z_*^T
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)Z_*\) is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KKT pair satisfies the strong second-order sufficient condition when active gradients are independent, active inequality multipliers are strictly positive, and the Lagrangian Hessian is uniformly positive in every nonzero direction tangent to all active constraints. Equivalently, any reduced Hessian formed with a basis of that tangent space is positive definite.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every active constraint are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
\((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies primal feasibility, stationarity, multiplier sign, and complementarity.
\(A_*\) has full row rank and \(\lambda_i^*>0\) for every active inequality \(i\in\mathcal A_I(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\gamma>0\;\forall d\in\ker A_*:\ d^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)d\ge\gamma\|d\|_2^2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(Z_*^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)Z_*\succ0\) for every null-space basis \(Z_*\).

With the stated rank convention, the saddle matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)&A_*^T\\A_*&0\end{bmatrix}\) has the inertia associated with a positive-definite reduced Hessian.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, \(A_*\) is the equality-constraint Jacobian and strict complementarity is vacuous.
If there are no active constraints, the condition reduces to \(\nabla^2 f(x^*)\succ0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The KKT saddle matrix is nonsingular.
\(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer.
boundary_notes: Without strict complementarity, positivity only on the null space of all active gradients is not the general critical-cone second-order sufficient condition.
Positive semidefiniteness is a necessary-type condition and is not this strong sufficient condition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Family of quadratic models used by sequential quadratic programming
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iterate \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) of a smooth nonlinear program, write \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(c_{i,k}=c_i(x_k)\), \(a_{i,k}=\nabla c_i(x_k)\), and let \(B_k=B_k^T\) represent Lagrangian curvature.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality- or inequality-constrained nonlinear programming; the definition concerns the quadratic subproblem, independently of globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP model is a quadratic program in a step \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) of the form \[\min_p\ q_k(p):=f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\] subject to selected linearized constraints \[c_{i,k}+a_{i,k}^Tp=0\quad(i\in\mathcal E_k),\qquad c_{i,k}+a_{i,k}^Tp\ge0\quad(i\in\mathcal I_k),\] possibly together with a trust-region bound or explicit elastic variables. An SQP model family is a collection of these programs indexed by the choices of curvature matrix \(B_k\), retained constraint sets \((\mathcal E_k,\mathcal I_k)\), coordinate representation, regularization, and step domain. The family is quadratic in \(p\) and first-order in its constraint model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP model is a quadratic approximation of the objective or Lagrangian combined with linearizations of the nonlinear constraints. Model families differ through their curvature matrix, equality versus inequality treatment, full-space versus reduced-space coordinates, regularization, elastic variables, and optional trust-region restriction.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and the modeled constraints are differentiable at \(x_k\).
\(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\); it may be exact, approximate, reduced-space induced, or regularized.
Every modeled nonlinear constraint is replaced by its affine first-order expression at \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_k(B_k,\mathcal E_k,\mathcal I_k)=\operatorname*{argmin}_p\{q_k(p):c_{i,k}+a_{i,k}^Tp=0\ (i\in\mathcal E_k),\ c_{i,k}+a_{i,k}^Tp\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal I_k)\}\) is the defining SQP subproblem object.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints, the QP KKT equations are \(\begin{bmatrix}B_k&-A_k^T\\A_k&0\end{bmatrix}\binom{p}{\ell}=\binom{-g_k}{-c_k}\).
Using \(\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)^Tp\) instead of \(g_k^Tp\) gives the same equality-constrained minimizer because \(A_kp=-c_k\) fixes their difference.
special_cases_latex: \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) gives the exact Lagrangian-Hessian model.
Keeping all linearized inequalities gives an IQP model; fixing a working set as equalities gives an EQP model.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(A_k\) has full row rank and \(B_k\) is positive definite on \(\ker A_k\), the equality-QP model has a unique primal step.
boundary_notes: An SQP model does not by itself specify acceptance, multiplier updates, or convergence safeguards.
A quadratically constrained model is outside this canonical SQP family because SQP linearizes the constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Hessian SQP Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact-Hessian SQP minimizes a quadratic model using the Lagrangian Hessian while enforcing linearized constraints; its QP multipliers update the nonlinear-program multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(c(x)\le0\), let \((x_k,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\) be the current primal-dual iterate and set \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\). The exact Lagrangian-Hessian SQP model computes a step \(p_k\) from \[\min_{p\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ \nabla f(x_k)^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\] subject to \[h(x_k)+J_h(x_k)p=0,\qquad c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)p\le0.\] The QP multipliers provide new multiplier estimates, and the primal trial point is \(x_k+p_k\), possibly modified by globalization. Thus the SQP KKT equations are the Newton linearization of the nonlinear KKT system when the active set is fixed.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraints are twice continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed quadratic program is the exact Lagrangian-Hessian SQP model, with primal step \(p_k\) and QP dual variables serving as multiplier estimates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-curvature SQP subproblem obtained by quadraticizing the Lagrangian and linearizing the constraints.

notation.meaning: Lagrangian Hessian at the current primal-dual iterate

review_flags: The supplied locators support Lagrangian second-order models but may not display this exact mixed-constraint SQP formulation.

The map dimensions are also omitted.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Lagrangian-Hessian SQP quadratic model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\lambda^Tc(x)\) for a smooth equality-constrained problem \(c(x)=0\), and let \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) be the current primal-dual iterate with \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-order, finite-dimensional SQP model for smooth constraints; the inequality version replaces the equality system by the corresponding affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Lagrangian Hessian SQP model at \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) is \[\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\ f(x_k)+
abla f(x_k)^Tp+	frac12p^T
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)p\quad	ext{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+A_kp=0.\] Its primal step and new QP multiplier \((p_k,\lambda_{k+1})\) satisfy \[ egin{bmatrix}
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)&-A_k^T\A_k&0\end{bmatrix} inom{p_k}{\lambda_{k+1}}= inom{-
abla f(x_k)}{-c(x_k)}.\] Thus its curvature is the exact Hessian of the nonlinear-program Lagrangian at the current multiplier estimate, rather than the objective Hessian alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model minimizes a quadratic with linear term equal to the objective gradient, curvature equal to the exact Lagrangian Hessian at the current primal-dual iterate, and constraints equal to the first-order linearization of the nonlinear constraints. Its KKT equations coincide with the Newton equations for the nonlinear KKT system.
assumptions_latex: For uniqueness, \(A_k\) has full row rank and the Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on \(\ker A_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k:=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) in the SQP quadratic model, with \(c(x_k)+A_kp=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The model is the Newton linearization of \(F(x,\lambda)=(\nabla_x\mathcal L(x,\lambda),c(x))=0\).
On the affine constraint set, the linear term may be written \(\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)^Tp\) without changing the minimizer.
special_cases_latex: If \(c\) is affine, then \(\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L=\nabla^2f\).
For an unconstrained problem, the model is the ordinary exact-Hessian Newton quadratic.
immediate_consequences_latex: Under the stated rank and reduced-curvature conditions, the KKT coefficient matrix is nonsingular and the model step is unique.
boundary_notes: Using \(\nabla^2f(x_k)\) while omitting nonlinear-constraint curvature is not the exact Lagrangian-Hessian model.
Regularization or quasi-Newton replacement produces a neighboring SQP model family, not this exact model.

notation.meaning: constraint Jacobian at the current iterate

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-QP SQP Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SQP step minimizes a quadratic objective model subject to equality constraints obtained by linearizing the nonlinear equalities and any fixed working-set constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), let \(x_k\) be the current iterate, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)\), and let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) model Lagrangian curvature. The equality-QP SQP step is any solution \(p_k\) of
\[\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\; g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}B_kp\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+A_kp=0.\]
When a working set of inequalities is fixed, its corresponding linearized constraints are included as equalities in the same model.
assumptions_latex: The displayed quadratic program is feasible and attains a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}B_kp:c(x_k)+A_kp=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained SQP subproblem at one nonlinear-programming iterate.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the equality constraints at the current iterate

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-QP SQP Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic SQP subproblem retains the linearizations of all equalities and inequalities, allowing its solution to determine which inequalities are active.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c_E(x)=0\) and \(c_I(x)\geq0\). At \(x_k\), set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(A_{E,k}=\nabla c_E(x_k)\), and \(A_{I,k}=\nabla c_I(x_k)\). Given symmetric \(B_k\), the inequality-QP SQP model computes
\[p_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\;g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}B_kp\]
subject to
\[c_E(x_k)+A_{E,k}p=0,\qquad c_I(x_k)+A_{I,k}p\geq0.\]
Thus activity is determined within the QP rather than prescribed before solving it.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic subproblem is feasible and attains a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\) minimizes the quadratic model over the complete linearized feasible set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP subproblem retaining every current linearized inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian SQP Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal step enforces the linearized equality constraints, and a null-space coordinate parametrizes every remaining feasible displacement. Substitution produces an equivalent quadratic problem whose curvature matrix is the reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable at \(x_k\), and set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Given \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), consider the equality-QP
\[\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\;g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}B_kp\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+A_kp=0.\]
Assume \(A_k\) has full row rank. Let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(A_kZ_k=0\), and choose \(n_k\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(A_kn_k=-c(x_k)\). Every feasible step has the unique form \(p=n_k+Z_kq\). After discarding terms independent of \(q\), the QP becomes
\[\min_{q\in\mathbb R^{n-m}}\;\bigl(Z_k^{\mathsf T}(g_k+B_kn_k)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}q+\tfrac12q^{\mathsf T}R_kq,\qquad R_k=Z_k^{\mathsf T}B_kZ_k.\]
If \(q_k\) solves the reduced problem, the corresponding full step is \(p_k=n_k+Z_kq_k\), and every minimizer of the full QP arises this way.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are differentiable at \(x_k\).
\(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
The equality-QP is feasible and attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_k\) minimizes the reduced problem if and only if \(p_k=n_k+Z_kq_k\) minimizes the full equality-QP.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space representation of an equality-constrained SQP quadratic model.

notation.meaning: full-column-rank basis matrix for the null space of the constraint Jacobian
normal step satisfying the linearized equality constraints
null-space coordinate of a feasible step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Null-space reduced-Hessian SQP model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(c(x)=0\), let \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)\) have full row rank. Choose matrices \(Y_k\) and \(Z_k\) with \(\operatorname{Range}(Y_k)=\operatorname{Range}(A_k^T)\), \(\operatorname{Range}(Z_k)=\ker A_k\), and write \(p=Y_kp_Y+Z_kp_Z\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained or fixed-working-set SQP in finite dimensions; only tangent-space curvature is represented explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reduced-Hessian SQP model first chooses a normal coordinate \(p_Y\) satisfying \[(A_kY_k)p_Y=-c(x_k),\] and then determines the tangential coordinate from a quadratic model \[\min_{p_Z}\ h_k^Tp_Z+\tfrac12p_Z^TM_kp_Z,\qquad h_k:=Z_k^T\bigl(\nabla f(x_k)+B_kY_kp_Y\bigr),\] where \(M_k\in\mathbb S^{n-m}\) represents \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\), usually with \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\). The full step is \(p_k=Y_kp_Y+Z_kp_Z\). In the exact reduced model, \(M_k=Z_k^TB_kZ_k\); reduced quasi-Newton models update only \(M_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced-Hessian model decomposes the SQP step into a normal component that satisfies the linearized constraints and a tangential component in the Jacobian null space. Only the quadratic curvature acting on the tangential coordinates is stored or approximated explicitly.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z_k\) span \(\ker A_k\), while \(A_kY_k\) is nonsingular.
\(M_k\) is symmetric; positive definiteness of \(M_k\) gives a unique tangential minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k=Y_kp_Y+Z_kp_Z\), where \((A_kY_k)p_Y=-c_k\) and \(M_kp_Z=-Z_k^T(\nabla f_k+B_kY_kp_Y)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(M_k=Z_k^TB_kZ_k\), the reduced equations are the null-space elimination of the full equality-QP KKT system.
The reduced Hessian is the bilinear form induced by \(B_k\) on \(\ker A_k\), represented in the basis \(Z_k\).
special_cases_latex: Dropping the cross term gives \(M_kp_Z=-Z_k^T\nabla f_k\), a common reduced quasi-Newton simplification.
At a feasible iterate, \(c_k=0\) permits \(p_Y=0\), so the step is purely tangential.
immediate_consequences_latex: Storage for curvature can fall from an \(n\times n\) matrix to an \((n-m)\times(n-m)\) matrix.
Positive definiteness is required only on the constraint tangent space.
boundary_notes: The coordinate matrices may vary with \(k\); secant pairs must therefore be formed consistently with the chosen reduced coordinates.
This definition presumes an equality system or a fixed working set.

notation.meaning: range-space basis used for the normal step
null-space basis used for the tangential step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularized family of SQP quadratic subproblems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q_k(p)=f_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\) be an SQP model with linearized constraints, where \(B_k\) may be indefinite or poorly conditioned.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional SQP; regularization modifies curvature, step size, or constraint consistency while retaining a quadratic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A regularized SQP model replaces the unmodified model by \[\min_{p,e}\ f_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^T(B_k+R_k)p+\rho_k\Psi(e)\] subject to linearized constraints relaxed by \(e\), and possibly \(\|D_kp\|\le\Delta_k\). Here \(R_k=R_k^T\) is chosen so that \[d^T(B_k+R_k)d\ge\delta_k\|d\|^2\quad\text{for all }d\in\ker A_k\] for some \(\delta_k>0\), or the trust-region bound makes the subproblem well posed without imposing positive definiteness. The elastic penalty \(\Psi(e)\) is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when the original linearization is satisfied. The collection over admissible \((R_k,\rho_k,\Delta_k,D_k)\) is the regularized SQP model family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularized SQP model modifies an SQP quadratic program to control indefinite or nearly singular curvature, excessive steps, or inconsistent constraint linearizations. Typical controls are a symmetric curvature shift, a trust-region restriction, and penalized elastic variables.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) and the linearized constraints are defined at \(x_k\).
\(R_k\) is symmetric, \(\rho_k\ge0\), and \(\Delta_k>0\) when the corresponding controls are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized model is the SQP QP with curvature \(B_k+R_k\), optional domain \(\|D_kp\|\le\Delta_k\), and optional penalized relaxation variables \(e\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A proximal realization uses \(R_k=\sigma_kI\) with \(\sigma_k\ge0\).
A factorization-based realization modifies \(B_k\) only enough to obtain positive reduced curvature.
A trust-region realization sets \(R_k=0\) but bounds \(p\) explicitly.
special_cases_latex: Elastic-mode SQP uses nonnegative violation variables and an \(\ell_1\)-type penalty.
Reduced-space regularization modifies only \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A sufficiently large positive shift makes the reduced quadratic strictly convex.
Elastic variables can make an otherwise inconsistent linearized subproblem feasible.
boundary_notes: Regularization parameters are model controls; their update rules belong to the algorithm rather than this definition.
A curvature shift changes the Newton model and therefore is not exact-Hessian SQP unless the shift is zero.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 18, §18.2–§18.3, “Enforcing Convergence” and “Handling Inconsistent Linearizations,” especially equation (18.12), pp. 534–537

knowledge_statements.title: Convexified SQP Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexified SQP replaces indefinite curvature by a uniformly positive-definite matrix, commonly by flooring eigenvalues, so the quadratic objective is strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an SQP curvature matrix \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) and a prescribed floor \(\delta_k>0\), a convexified SQP model replaces \(B_k\) by a symmetric matrix \(\widehat B_k\) satisfying \(\widehat B_k\succeq\delta_k I\). One canonical choice is obtained from \(B_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{k,i})Q_k^{\mathsf T}\) by
\[\widehat B_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\max\{\lambda_{k,i},\delta_k\})Q_k^{\mathsf T}.\]
The resulting subproblem minimizes \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}\widehat B_kp\) over the chosen linearized constraint set, and its objective is strongly convex on every nonempty affine feasible subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat B_k\succeq\delta_k I\), so the convexified quadratic objective is strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral or diagonal convexification of an SQP quadratic objective.

notation.meaning: orthogonal eigenvector matrix of the original curvature model

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The spectral flooring construction is mathematically coherent and fits convexified SQP models, but the record has no citation. An authoritative SQP source with a specific section, theorem, definition, or page locator is required to establish that this particular construction is used as an SQP convexification model.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilized SQP Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stabilized SQP model penalizes an elastic linearized-constraint residual, ensuring subproblem feasibility while retaining pressure toward constraint satisfaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an equality-constrained problem, an elastic stabilized SQP model introduces a residual variable \(r\in\mathbb R^m\) and, for \(\rho_k>0\), solves
\[\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n,\,r\in\mathbb R^m}\;g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}B_kp+\tfrac{\rho_k}{2}\lVert r\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+A_kp=r.\]
Eliminating \(r\) gives the unconstrained stabilized model
\[g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}B_kp+\tfrac{\rho_k}{2}\lVert c(x_k)+A_kp\rVert_2^2.\]
The elastic formulation remains feasible for every \(p\), including when the unrelaxed linearized constraints are inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elastic subproblem is feasible, and eliminating \(r\) yields the displayed quadratic-penalty model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elastic quadratic stabilization of linearized equality feasibility.

notation.meaning: elastic residual in the linearized constraints
constraint Jacobian at the current iterate

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The elastic residual model is algebraically valid, but “stabilized SQP” covers several distinct primal-dual, elastic, and proximal formulations. Without an authoritative locator, it is uncertain that this penalty-residual formulation represents the intended terminal container rather than merely a generic elastic or quadratic-penalty model.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Control Modifications
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip the curvature eigenvalues between positive lower and finite upper bounds, solve the modified SQP subproblem, and apply the method’s globalization acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a symmetric curvature estimate \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), bounds \(0<\delta_k\leq M_k\), and the current SQP linearized constraints. Compute an eigendecomposition \(B_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{k,i})Q_k^{\mathsf T}\), set
\[\widetilde\lambda_{k,i}=\min\{M_k,\max\{\delta_k,\lambda_{k,i}\}\},\qquad \widetilde B_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\widetilde\lambda_{k,i})Q_k^{\mathsf T},\]
and solve the SQP subproblem using \(\widetilde B_k\). Accept its step when the governing globalization test succeeds; otherwise update the globalization parameter and resolve. The modification guarantees \(\delta_k I\preceq\widetilde B_k\preceq M_kI\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_k I\preceq\widetilde B_k\preceq M_kI\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvalue clipping for uniformly positive SQP curvature.

notation.meaning: eigenvalues of the original curvature matrix

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The eigenvalue-clipping operation and its spectral bound are correct, but no source supports this exact curvature-control algorithm in an SQP setting. The acceptance and parameter-update steps are also unspecified, so their intended algorithmic realization cannot be verified without a direct authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Stability Modifications
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal quadratic term centered at a reference multiplier damps multiplier changes and regularizes the dual block of the primal-dual SQP system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(A_k\) be the equality-constraint Jacobian, and let \(\lambda_k^{\mathrm{ref}}\) be a reference multiplier. A dual-proximal multiplier-stability modification uses the saddle model
\[\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\max_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}\;g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}B_kp+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(c(x_k)+A_kp)-\tfrac{\mu_k}{2}\lVert\lambda-\lambda_k^{\mathrm{ref}}\rVert_2^2,\]
where \(\mu_k>0\). Its stationarity equations include
\[c(x_k)+A_kp-\mu_k(\lambda-\lambda_k^{\mathrm{ref}})=0,\]
which damps changes in the multiplier and contributes the negative definite block \(-\mu_kI\) to the primal-dual Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual stationarity equation is regularized by \(-\mu_kI\) and ties \(\lambda\) to \(\lambda_k^{\mathrm{ref}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual proximal regularization of the primal-dual SQP model.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The displayed dual-proximal saddle model yields the stated regularized dual stationarity equation, but no citation establishes it as the intended multiplier-stability modification in this SQP taxonomy. A specific authoritative source is needed to distinguish this formulation from other stabilized or proximal SQP variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Regularized Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive primal and dual shifts regularize an SQP KKT system against deficient constraint rank and missing curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a possibly rank-deficient constraint Jacobian \(A_k\) and possibly singular curvature matrix \(B_k\), a two-sided degeneracy-regularized SQP system chooses \(\delta_k>0\) and \(\mu_k>0\) and computes \((p_k,\Delta\lambda_k)\) from
\[\begin{pmatrix}B_k+\delta_kI&A_k^{\mathsf T}\\A_k&-\mu_kI\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}p_k\\\Delta\lambda_k\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}r_{d,k}\\r_{p,k}\end{pmatrix}.\]
Here \(r_{d,k}\) and \(r_{p,k}\) are the current dual and primal KKT residuals. The primal shift controls null curvature, while the dual shift controls constraint-Jacobian degeneracy; parameters may subsequently be reduced as regularity is recovered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized coefficient matrix contains positive primal and negative dual diagonal shifts that control the two principal sources of KKT degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided regularization of a possibly singular SQP KKT system.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The two-sided shifted KKT system is a plausible degeneracy-regularized model and does not incorrectly assert nonsingularity. Nevertheless, the interpretation of the two shifts and their use as an SQP degeneracy treatment require an authoritative, inspectable locator; none is supplied.

children.top_down_role: SQP variants grouped separately by curvature realization, feasibility policy, working-set policy, and solve accuracy.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential quadratic programming method and its independent family coordinates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider a smooth nonlinear program and a primal-dual state \((x_k,\lambda_k)\). Let \(Q_k\) denote a quadratic model formed from derivative data and affine constraint models at \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic SQP. Curvature, feasibility/activity policy, solve accuracy, and globalization are treated as independent method coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP method is an iteration that, for each \(k\), forms an SQP quadratic model \(Q_k\), computes an exact or approximate QP solution \((p_k,\ell_k)\), selects an accepted step \(s_k\) from that model output, and updates \[(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})=(x_k+s_k,\mathcal U_k(\lambda_k,\ell_k)).\] An SQP method family is specified by a tuple \[\mathfrak S=(\mathcal B,\mathcal P_{FA},\mathcal T,\mathcal G),\] where \(\mathcal B\) realizes exact or approximate Lagrangian curvature, \(\mathcal P_{FA}\) governs nonlinear feasibility and active-set treatment, \(\mathcal T\) specifies QP/KKT solve accuracy, and \(\mathcal G\) globalizes or accepts the step. Two methods belong to different coordinates when any one of these four mechanisms differs, even if their local QP has the same algebraic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP method repeatedly constructs a quadratic program from local derivatives and linearized constraints, solves it exactly or approximately, accepts or modifies the resulting step, and updates the primal and multiplier estimates. Method families are distinguished independently by curvature, feasibility and activity policy, solve accuracy, and globalization.
assumptions_latex: The objective and modeled constraints are differentiable at every generated iterate.
Each \(Q_k\) has a symmetric quadratic term and affine constraint models.
The update rule maps an accepted primal step and QP multiplier estimate to the next primal-dual state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})=(x_k+s_k,\mathcal U_k(\lambda_k,\ell_k))\) with \((p_k,\ell_k)\) obtained from an SQP QP and \(s_k\) selected by the stated family tuple.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The local exact-Hessian equality-SQP method is Newton's method applied to the KKT mapping.
IQP methods solve the affine inequalities directly; EQP methods first choose a working set and solve an equality QP.
special_cases_latex: \(s_k=p_k\) gives an unglobalized local SQP iteration.
\(s_k=\alpha_kp_k\) with merit-function backtracking gives line-search SQP.

Interior-point methods that never use active affine QP models are not included merely because they solve Newton systems.

children.title: SQP Curvature Realizations
children.top_down_role: SQP families distinguished by exact or approximate Lagrangian curvature.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact and approximate curvature realizations in SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: In an SQP model \(q_k(p)=f_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\), the symmetric matrix \(B_k\) represents second-order Lagrangian information.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional SQP; this classification concerns only the construction of the quadratic term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP curvature realization is a rule \(\mathcal B_k\) assigning a symmetric matrix \[B_k=\mathcal B_k(x_k,\lambda_k,\mathcal H_k)\in\mathbb S^n\] or a reduced matrix \(M_k\in\mathbb S^{n-m}\), where \(\mathcal H_k\) denotes available derivative and iteration history. It is exact when \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\); full-space quasi-Newton when \(B_k\) satisfies a Lagrangian secant update; reduced-space when only \(M_k\approx Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)Z_k\) is maintained; and regularized when a symmetric modification is applied to control definiteness or conditioning. These alternatives define curvature families independently of constraint and globalization policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A curvature realization is the rule that supplies the symmetric quadratic matrix in an SQP subproblem. The standard realizations are the exact Lagrangian Hessian, a full-space quasi-Newton approximation, a reduced-Hessian approximation, and a regularized version of one of these.
assumptions_latex: A Lagrangian \(\mathcal L\) and current multiplier estimate \(\lambda_k\) are defined.
Every realized full-space or reduced-space curvature matrix is symmetric.
A quasi-Newton realization uses iteration history through secant pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k\in\{\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_k,\ B_k^{\mathrm{QN}},\ Z_kM_kZ_k^T\text{ in reduced representation},\ B_k^{\mathrm{base}}+R_k\}\), with the selected member defining the curvature coordinate of the SQP method.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exact curvature may be characterized by Hessian-vector products rather than by explicitly storing the matrix.
Reduced curvature represents the restriction of the Lagrangian Hessian bilinear form to \(\ker A_k\).
special_cases_latex: Damped BFGS is a positive-definite full-space realization.
SR1 permits an indefinite quasi-Newton realization and is naturally paired with trust regions.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing only \(B_k\) changes the curvature realization while leaving the affine constraint model unchanged.
boundary_notes: The objective Hessian alone is generally not exact Lagrangian curvature when constraints are nonlinear.
Positive definiteness is a property of a realization, not a requirement of all trust-region SQP models.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact and approximate curvature realizations in SQP

children.title: Exact-Hessian SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP using exact Lagrangian curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Hessian SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact-Hessian SQP solves successive equality-constrained quadratic models using the current exact Lagrangian Hessian, globalizes the primal-dual step, and terminates when the specified KKT residual tolerances are met.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with Lagrangian \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\). Initialize \((x_0,\lambda_0)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\). At iteration \(k\), form \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)\), and
\[B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k).\]
Solve
\[\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\;g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}B_kp\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+A_kp=0\]
to obtain a step \(p_k\) and a QP multiplier \(\lambda_{k+1}^{\mathrm{QP}}\). Use the prescribed globalization rule to select \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), and set
\[x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k,\qquad \lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+\alpha_k\bigl(\lambda_{k+1}^{\mathrm{QP}}-\lambda_k\bigr).\]
Repeat until the prescribed primal and dual KKT residual tolerances hold, then return the current primal-dual iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are twice continuously differentiable near the iterates.
Each required SQP quadratic subproblem has a primal solution and associated multiplier.
A specified globalization rule returns an accepted \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the stopping test is met, the returned \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) satisfies the algorithm's prescribed primal and dual KKT residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual equality-constrained SQP using the exact Hessian of the Lagrangian.

notation.meaning: exact Hessian of the Lagrangian at the current primal-dual iterate
multiplier associated with the current equality-QP solution

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact-Hessian sequential quadratic programming method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) be a primal-dual iterate for a smooth nonlinear program with Lagrangian \(\mathcal L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact derivative SQP. The subproblem may contain equality constraints, all inequalities, or a fixed working set; exactness refers only to curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact-Hessian SQP method is an SQP iteration whose quadratic subproblem uses \[B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\] at every iteration where the Hessian is defined. For equality constraints it computes \((p_k,\ell_k)\) from \[\min_p\ f_k+\nabla f_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_k+A_kp=0,\] and then sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), where \(s_k=p_k\) locally or is an accepted modification of \(p_k\), and updates the multiplier from the QP multiplier \(\ell_k\). No secant approximation substitutes for \(B_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact-Hessian SQP evaluates the Hessian of the nonlinear-program Lagrangian at the current primal-dual iterate and uses it as the quadratic curvature in every SQP subproblem. Constraint and globalization choices remain independent.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and the modeled constraints are twice differentiable at \(x_k\).
A multiplier estimate \(\lambda_k\) is available to evaluate the Lagrangian Hessian.
The QP is solved or regularized according to the method's separate solve and globalization policies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) for every SQP quadratic model generated by the method.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints and a full local step, the iteration is Newton's method applied to the KKT equations.
Exact Hessian-vector products constitute exact curvature even if \(B_k\) is never assembled explicitly.
special_cases_latex: With affine constraints, exact-Hessian SQP uses \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\).
With no constraints, it reduces to an exact-Hessian Newton method.
immediate_consequences_latex: The quadratic term includes \(-\sum_i\lambda_{i,k}\nabla^2c_i(x_k)\), so nonlinear-constraint curvature is retained.
boundary_notes: A nonzero curvature shift produces regularized exact-Hessian SQP, not the unmodified variant.
Finite-difference or quasi-Newton curvature is not exact unless it equals the Lagrangian Hessian.

notation.meaning: quadratic curvature used in the SQP subproblem

children.title: Quasi-Newton SQP Method
children.top_down_role: SQP using full-space or reduced-space secant curvature models.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Newton SQP Method
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quasi-Newton SQP solves successive quadratic subproblems and updates a full-space approximation to the Lagrangian Hessian with a damped BFGS formula. The damping enforces positive secant curvature and thereby preserves positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), let \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\). Initialize \((x_0,\lambda_0)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) and \(B_0\in\mathbb S^n\) with \(B_0\succ0\). At iteration \(k\), solve the prescribed SQP subproblem using \(B_k\), globalize its primal-dual step, and obtain \((x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})\). Define
\[s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k,\qquad y_k=\nabla_xL(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_{k+1}).\]
Choose a damped secant vector \(\bar y_k\) satisfying \(s_k^{\mathsf T}\bar y_k>0\), and update
\[B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^{\mathsf T}B_k}{s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k}+\frac{\bar y_k\bar y_k^{\mathsf T}}{s_k^{\mathsf T}\bar y_k}.\]
Repeat until the prescribed KKT residual tolerances hold, then return the current primal-dual iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuously differentiable near the iterates.
Whenever the update is applied, \(s_k^{\mathsf T}\bar y_k>0\).
The SQP subproblem and prescribed globalization rule produce an accepted primal-dual iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update is symmetric, satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=\bar y_k\), and preserves \(B_{k+1}\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-space equality-constrained SQP using a damped BFGS approximation to Lagrangian curvature.

notation.meaning: Lagrangian-gradient difference evaluated with the new multiplier at both primal points
damped secant vector with positive secant curvature

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-space or reduced-space quasi-Newton SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) be SQP iterates and define \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\). The target curvature is the Hessian of \(x\mapsto\mathcal L(x,\lambda_{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional SQP with full-space or null-space secant curvature; globalization is not fixed by this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quasi-Newton SQP method replaces \(
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) in the SQP model by a symmetric approximation \(B_k\) updated from Lagrangian secant data. In full space, define \[y_k=
abla_x\mathcal L(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-
abla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_{k+1}),\] and choose an update \(B_{k+1}=\mathcal Q(B_k,s_k,y_k)\) satisfying, exactly or after damping, \[B_{k+1}s_k=y_k.\] In reduced space, maintain \(M_k\approx Z_k^T
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kZ_k\) and impose the corresponding reduced secant equation. The resulting \(B_k\) or \(M_k\) supplies the QP curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quasi-Newton SQP uses a symmetric secant approximation to Lagrangian curvature instead of evaluating the exact Lagrangian Hessian. The approximation can be updated in full space or only on the constraint tangent space.
assumptions_latex: The Lagrangian gradient is evaluable at consecutive iterates using a common multiplier estimate.
The selected update includes any curvature test or safeguard required for its denominator and definiteness properties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{k+1}=\mathcal Q(B_k,s_k,y_k)\) with the Lagrangian secant pair \((s_k,y_k)\), or \(M_{k+1}s_k^Z=y_k^Z\) in reduced coordinates.
equivalent_formulations_latex: BFGS, damped BFGS, SR1, and limited-memory versions are distinct realizations of the full-space definition.
Reduced quasi-Newton SQP updates only the curvature that affects the null-space component of the step.
special_cases_latex: Damped BFGS uses a modified vector \(r_k\) and satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=r_k\) while preserving positive definiteness.
SR1 may retain indefinite curvature and is compatible with trust-region SQP.
immediate_consequences_latex: Second derivatives of individual constraints need not be evaluated explicitly.
A reduced update may require substantially less storage when the tangent-space dimension is small.
boundary_notes: The gradient difference must use the Lagrangian, not merely the objective, unless constraints are affine.
A generic symmetric approximation without a secant-update rule is an approximate-Hessian model but not necessarily quasi-Newton SQP.

notation.meaning: Lagrangian-gradient displacement used in the secant equation

children.title: SQP Feasibility-Activity Policy Pair
children.top_down_role: SQP families distinguished by nonlinear feasibility and active-set treatment.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility and active-set policy coordinates of SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For constraints \(c_i(x)=0\) on \(\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\ge0\) on \(\mathcal I\), define nonlinear infeasibility \(h(x)=\|c_{\mathcal E}(x)\|+\|[c_{\mathcal I}(x)]_-\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth inequality-constrained SQP; the pair separates treatment of nonlinear feasibility from selection of constraints imposed as equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP feasibility-activity policy pair is \((\mathcal F,\mathcal A)\). The feasibility policy \(\mathcal F\) maps the current state and trial step to a decision that either preserves \(h(x)=0\), accepts controlled infeasibility, introduces elastic variables, or invokes restoration to reduce \(h\). The activity policy \(\mathcal A\) maps the current state and QP information to a working set \(W_k\subseteq\mathcal I\), with constraints in \(W_k\) imposed as equalities \[c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp=0\quad(i\in W_k),\] while other inequalities are retained or omitted according to the IQP or EQP realization. The ordered pair, not either coordinate alone, specifies how feasibility and active-set identification interact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasibility coordinate decides whether iterates must remain feasible, may be temporarily infeasible, or enter an elastic or restoration phase. The activity coordinate decides which inequalities are represented as active equalities or are left to an inequality QP.
assumptions_latex: \(h(x)\ge0\) and \(h(x)=0\) exactly at nonlinear feasible points.
\(W_k\subseteq\mathcal I\) is determined from current constraint values, multiplier estimates, or an auxiliary model.
Any constraint imposed in the working set is represented by its affine linearization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\((\mathcal F,
\mathcal A):(x_k,\lambda_k,Q_k)\mapsto(\text{feasibility action},W_k)\) is the policy pair defining these two SQP method coordinates.
equivalent_formulations_latex: IQP uses the solution's active inequalities as its activity estimate.
EQP selects \(W_k\) first and then solves an equality-constrained QP.
special_cases_latex: A feasible-working-set policy maintains \(h(x_k)=0\) and chooses \(W_k\) from near-active inequalities.
An elastic IQP policy adds nonnegative violation variables when affine constraints are inconsistent.
immediate_consequences_latex: Methods with identical curvature can behave differently because their feasibility-activity pairs differ.
boundary_notes: Activity in the QP is an estimate and need not equal the nonlinear active set away from a solution.
A restoration phase is not itself the optimality QP; it is an action of the feasibility policy.

children.title: Feasible SQP Method
children.top_down_role: SQP designed to preserve or rapidly restore nonlinear feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible SQP Method
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible SQP combines a tangent predictor with a nonlinear correction or restoration step so accepted iterates remain feasible within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), initialize a feasible point \(x_0\). At iteration \(k\), compute an SQP predictor \(p_k\) satisfying \(c(x_k)+A_kp_k=0\). Compute a correction \(d_k\), for example by a local constraint-restoration solve, such that
\[c(x_k+p_k+d_k)=0\]
within the prescribed feasibility tolerance. Apply a merit, filter, or feasible-arc acceptance rule to choose an accepted trial point \(x_{k+1}\) on or sufficiently near the constraint manifold. If restoration fails, reject the predictor and invoke the specified restoration phase. Stop when feasibility and stationarity tolerances hold; output the current iterate and multiplier estimate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable near the iterates.
The relevant constraint Jacobians have full row rank.
A feasible initial point and a locally successful restoration procedure are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted \(x_{k+1}\) satisfies the prescribed nonlinear feasibility tolerance, and termination additionally requires stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained feasible SQP with a nonlinear restoration correction.

notation.meaning: constraint Jacobian at the current iterate

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The predictor-correction description is plausible for a feasible equality-constrained SQP family, but the cited general Newton-like-method section does not directly identify the restoration or feasible-arc variant. The alternative acceptance mechanisms and unspecified restoration solve materially determine the method, so a direct source locator is needed before choosing a reliable mathematical version.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility-preserving or feasibility-restoring SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{x:c_{\mathcal E}(x)=0,\ c_{\mathcal I}(x)\ge0\}\) and let \(h(x)=\|c_{\mathcal E}(x)\|+\|[c_{\mathcal I}(x)]_-\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional SQP. The strict variant preserves nonlinear feasibility; the restoration variant permits controlled infeasibility but prioritizes its reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasibility-preserving SQP method is an SQP iteration with \(x_0\in\Omega\) and an acceptance or correction map \(R_k\) such that every accepted iterate satisfies \[x_{k+1}=R_k(x_k,p_k)\in\Omega.\] Its QP step ordinarily satisfies tangent conditions for equalities and currently active inequalities. More generally, a feasibility-restoring SQP method is one whose feasibility policy invokes a restoration step whenever the optimality QP is inconsistent or fails an acceptance test, and accepts restoration iterates only under a prescribed reduction \[h(x_{k+1})\le \theta_k h(x_k),\qquad 0\le\theta_k<1,\] until the optimality phase can resume. These are the preserving and rapidly restoring members of the feasible-SQP family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly feasible SQP method starts feasible and maps every accepted SQP trial back to the nonlinear feasible set. A restoring variant may leave feasibility temporarily, but invokes a phase whose acceptance condition requires a quantified decrease in nonlinear infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(\Omega\) and infeasibility measure \(h\) are defined.
The correction or restoration subproblem is distinct from the optimality QP and has a stated acceptance threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either \(x_k\in\Omega\) for all accepted iterates, or each restoration acceptance satisfies \(h(x_{k+1})\le\theta_kh(x_k)\) with \(\theta_k<1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints, strict feasibility is \(c(x_k)=0\) for every \(k\).
A retraction implementation uses a map \(R_k\) with \(c(R_k(x_k,p_k))=0\).
special_cases_latex: A second-order correction can restore nonlinear feasibility lost by a tangent SQP step.
Elastic-mode SQP provides a feasible QP when the unrelaxed affine constraints are inconsistent, but nonlinear feasibility still requires acceptance or restoration control.
immediate_consequences_latex: In the preserving variant, every accepted objective value is evaluated at a feasible nonlinear-program point.
boundary_notes: Solving only the linearized constraints does not by itself preserve nonlinear feasibility.
A filter method is not automatically a feasible SQP method because it may accept infeasible points.

children.title: Working-Set Method
children.top_down_role: SQP organized around active-set identification and equality-QP subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Working-Set Method
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The working-set SQP method repeatedly solves equality-constrained quadratic subproblems for a proposed active set, adds inactive inequalities that block the step, and removes active inequalities whose multipliers have the wrong sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c_E:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_E}\), and \(c_I:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_I}\), consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_E(x)=0\) and \(c_I(x)\geq0\). Use the Lagrangian sign convention
\[L(x,\lambda,\nu)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c_E(x)-\nu^{\mathsf T}c_I(x),\qquad \nu\geq0.\]
Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) and a working set \(W_0\subseteq I=\{1,\ldots,m_I\}\). At iteration \(k\), solve the SQP quadratic model subject to the linearized equalities and
\[c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^{\mathsf T}p=0\qquad(i\in W_k).\]
If motion along the computed direction reaches a linearized inactive inequality, restrict the step to the first blocking constraint and add a blocking index to the working set. If the equality-QP solution is stationary and some working-set inequality has a negative multiplier under the stated sign convention, remove an index with an inadmissible multiplier and resolve. Apply the prescribed globalization rule to update the nonlinear iterate and repeat. Stop when the prescribed primal-feasibility, stationarity, complementarity, and multiplier-sign tolerances hold.
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(c_E\), and \(c_I\) are continuously differentiable near the iterates.
The inequalities use \(c_I(x)\geq0\) and the Lagrangian term \(-\nu^{\mathsf T}c_I(x)\), so admissible inequality multipliers satisfy \(\nu\geq0\).
Each equality-QP for the current working set is solvable or invokes a specified restoration procedure.
A specified globalization rule governs acceptance of nonlinear trial points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the returned primal-dual iterate and working set satisfy the prescribed feasibility, stationarity, complementarity, and multiplier-sign tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set SQP using equality-QP solves, blocking constraints, and multiplier-sign tests.

notation.meaning: inequalities treated as active in the current equality-QP
nonnegative multipliers for inequalities written as \(c_I(x)\geq0\) under the stated Lagrangian convention

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Working-set SQP method based on equality-QP subproblems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\), let \(W_k\subseteq\mathcal I\) estimate the nonlinear active set at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set SQP for smooth inequality-constrained nonlinear programs, especially the EQP family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A working-set SQP method chooses \(W_k\subseteq\mathcal I\) and computes its principal step from the equality-constrained QP \[\min_p\ f_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\] \[\text{subject to }c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp=0\quad(i\in\mathcal E\cup W_k),\] while inequalities outside \(W_k\) are omitted from that EQP or monitored separately. After solving, the method updates \(W_k\) using constraint violations, blocking constraints, QP multipliers, or an auxiliary LP/QP: an omitted constraint may enter when it blocks the step, and a working-set inequality may leave when its multiplier has the wrong sign. Thus active-set identification and equality-QP solution alternate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A working-set SQP method predicts which inequalities are active, treats those constraints as equalities in a cheaper equality-constrained quadratic program, and updates the prediction from blocking constraints and multiplier signs.
assumptions_latex: The equality and working-set gradients define the affine EQP constraints.
The update policy can add an omitted inequality or delete a working-set inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_p\{f_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp:c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp=0,\ i\in\mathcal E\cup W_k\}\), followed by \(W_{k+1}=\mathcal A_k(W_k,p_k,\ell_k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: This is the EQP form of active-set SQP.
An auxiliary linear program may determine \(W_k\), after which the quadratic term is restored in the EQP.
special_cases_latex: If \(W_k\) equals the solution active set and remains fixed, the local iteration behaves like equality-constrained SQP.
Bound-constrained working sets identify variables fixed at lower or upper bounds.
immediate_consequences_latex: The subproblem dimension is unchanged, but its constraint structure is an equality system amenable to null-space or range-space solution.
boundary_notes: A working set is an estimate; it is not necessarily the set of constraints active at \(x_k\).
Solving the full inequality QP without a separately selected working set is the IQP variant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-based accuracy of an SQP subproblem solve
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For an equality-QP SQP model, let \(K_k=\begin{bmatrix}B_k&-A_k^T\\A_k&0\end{bmatrix}\), \(b_k=(-g_k,-c_k)\), and let \(z_k=(p_k,\ell_k)\) be a computed primal-dual QP pair.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional SQP. Equality-QP residuals are stated explicitly; inequality-QP accuracy additionally includes primal, dual, and complementarity residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The solve accuracy of an equality-SQP subproblem is measured by the KKT residual \[r_k:=K_kz_k-b_k=\binom{B_kp_k+g_k-A_k^T\ell_k}{A_kp_k+c_k}.\] The solve is exact when \(r_k=0\). It is inexact with forcing parameter \(\eta_k\ge0\) and absolute tolerance \(\tau_k\ge0\) when \[\|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|b_k\|+\tau_k.\] For an inequality QP, the residual vector is augmented by violations of affine primal feasibility, multiplier nonnegativity, and complementarity. An SQP solve-accuracy policy is the sequence \(\{(\eta_k,\tau_k)\}\), together with the norm, scaling, and residual components used for termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP solve accuracy is defined through the residual of the quadratic subproblem's KKT conditions. Exact SQP makes this residual zero; inexact SQP bounds it by relative and possibly absolute tolerances. Inequality subproblems also measure complementarity and sign violations.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic subproblem and a primal-dual candidate \((p_k,\ell_k)\) are defined.
A norm and scaling convention are fixed.
For inequality QPs, all primal, dual, and complementarity residual components are included.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|K_kz_k-b_k\|=0\) for an exact solve, and \(\|K_kz_k-b_k\|\le\eta_k\|b_k\|+\tau_k\) for the stated inexact solve.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The two equality-QP residual blocks are stationarity error and linearized-feasibility error.
With \(\tau_k=0\), \(\eta_k\) is a relative forcing term.
special_cases_latex: \(\eta_k=\tau_k=0\) gives exact-subproblem SQP.
A fixed \(0\le\eta_k<1\) gives uniformly reduced relative residuals; \(\eta_k\to0\) requests asymptotically more accurate solves.
immediate_consequences_latex: Solve accuracy is independent of whether \(B_k\) is exact or quasi-Newton.
boundary_notes: A small linear-system residual need not certify a global minimizer of a nonconvex QP.
Residual scaling must be stated because primal and dual blocks can have different units.

children.title: Exact-Subproblem SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP based on accurately solved quadratic subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Subproblem SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each SQP iteration solves its quadratic model and linearized constraints to zero KKT residual before accepting and updating the nonlinear-program iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), initialize \(x_0\), multipliers \(\lambda_0\), and symmetric matrices \(B_k\). At iteration \(k\), compute an exact primal-dual solution \((p_k,\delta\lambda_k)\) of
\[
B_kp_k+\nabla f(x_k)+J_k^{\mathsf T}(\lambda_k+\delta\lambda_k)=0,\qquad c(x_k)+J_kp_k=0.
\]
Choose an accepted step length \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), update the multiplier and Hessian approximation, and stop when the nonlinear KKT residual meets the prescribed tolerance. Exactness means that the quadratic-program KKT residual is zero up to arithmetic precision before the major iterate is updated.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are twice continuously differentiable.
\(J_k=\nabla c(x_k)\), and the displayed quadratic subproblem has a primal-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((p_k,\delta\lambda_k)\) satisfies the quadratic-subproblem KKT equations exactly before \(x_{k+1}\) is formed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained SQP with an exactly solved quadratic model at every major iteration.

notation.meaning: constraint Jacobian at the current iterate

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and equality-constrained SQP scope fit the leaf, and the displayed primal-dual equations are coherent. No citation supports the particular multiplier-increment convention or the definition of an exact subproblem solve, so authoritative SQP sourcing is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SQP with exactly solved quadratic subproblems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(Q_k\) be the chosen SQP quadratic program and let \(\mathcal K_k(p,\ell)\) denote its complete primal-dual KKT residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The word exact refers to the QP solution, not to the Hessian; exact-subproblem SQP can use exact or approximate curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact-subproblem SQP method computes, at every successful iteration, a primal-dual pair \((p_k,\ell_k)\) that is a KKT solution of \(Q_k\): \[\mathcal K_k(p_k,\ell_k)=0.\] For the equality model this means \[B_kp_k+g_k-A_k^T\ell_k=0,\qquad A_kp_k+c_k=0.\] For a convex inequality-QP model it additionally means exact affine primal feasibility, \(\ell_{i,k}\ge0\), and \(\ell_{i,k}(c_{i,k}+a_{i,k}^Tp_k)=0\). When the QP is nonconvex, “exact” must identify the selected local or global QP solution; zero KKT residual alone defines exact stationarity but not global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact-subproblem SQP solves each quadratic model to zero primal-dual KKT residual. For inequality QPs this includes affine feasibility, multiplier signs, and complementarity. This classification is separate from whether the quadratic curvature is exact.
assumptions_latex: A well-defined SQP quadratic program \(Q_k\) is available.
The subproblem has a KKT solution of the type selected by the method.
For the convex inequality case, KKT conditions characterize the QP minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal K_k(p_k,\ell_k)=0\) at every computed SQP subproblem solution.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality QPs, \(\begin{bmatrix}B_k&-A_k^T\\A_k&0\end{bmatrix}\binom{p_k}{\ell_k}=\binom{-g_k}{-c_k}\).
For convex inequality QPs, exact solution is equivalent to exact primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity.
special_cases_latex: Algorithm 18.1 with an exact solve of equation (18.7) is exact-subproblem SQP.
An exact-subproblem quasi-Newton SQP method has zero QP residual although \(B_k\ne\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: There is no inner-solve residual error in the step equations.
boundary_notes: Floating-point computations generally realize this definition only up to a declared numerical tolerance.
Exact stationarity is not synonymous with a global solution for an indefinite QP.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact-Subproblem Local SQP Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration body for local SQP with exact Lagrangian curvature and an exactly solved equality-constrained quadratic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), evaluate
\[
f_k,\quad \nabla f_k,\quad \nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L_k,\quad c_k,\quad A_k.
\]
Solve the equality-constrained quadratic model
\[
\min_p\ f_k+\nabla f_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^T\nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L_kp
\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_kp+c_k=0
\]
for its primal step \(p_k\) and multiplier \(l_k\), and update
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k,\qquad \lambda_{k+1}=l_k.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each local exact-subproblem SQP iteration evaluates the objective, constraints, their first derivatives, and the exact Lagrangian Hessian; solves the equality-constrained quadratic model for its step and multiplier; then takes the full primal step and replaces the multiplier estimate by the QP multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L_k\text{ is used as the quadratic-model Hessian}
(p_k,l_k)\text{ is obtained by solving the stated quadratic subproblem}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k,\qquad \lambda_{k+1}=l_k.

children.top_down_role: SQP allowing controlled inexactness in subproblems, KKT systems, or derivative data.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact SQP Method
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SQP KKT system may be solved approximately when its residual is bounded by a forcing fraction of the current nonlinear KKT residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\), let \(F(z)=(\nabla_xL(x,\lambda),c(x))\), and let \(M_k\) be the SQP KKT matrix. Compute \(d_k\) only approximately so that
\[
M_kd_k=-F(z_k)+r_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|,
\]
where \(0\leq\eta_k<1\). After globalization, set \(z_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Stop when \(\|F(z_k)\|\) and any required feasibility or complementarity residuals meet their tolerances. A forcing sequence with \(\eta_k\to0\) makes the linear-solve error asymptotically negligible; fixed \(\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\) supplies only uniformly controlled inexactness.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near the iterates.
\(M_k\) is a nonsingular or consistently regularized KKT approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|M_kd_k+F(z_k)\|\leq\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|\), with asymptotically exact solves when \(\eta_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-controlled inexact solution of the primal-dual Newton-SQP equations.

notation.meaning: SQP KKT matrix or regularized approximation

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the relative residual condition is one particular inexact Newton-SQP convention. A source is required to support the residual map, KKT approximation, forcing rule, and the stated interpretation of fixed versus vanishing forcing parameters.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-controlled inexact SQP method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For an equality-SQP model define \(K_k=\begin{bmatrix}B_k&-A_k^T\\A_k&0\end{bmatrix}\), \(b_k=(-g_k,-c_k)\), and \(z_k=(p_k,\ell_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional SQP permitting controlled error in the QP/KKT solve; derivative inexactness may be added as a separately bounded error source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact SQP method computes \(z_k\) without requiring \(K_kz_k=b_k\) exactly, but enforces a forcing condition \[\|K_kz_k-b_k\|\le\eta_k\|b_k\|+\tau_k,\qquad 0\le\eta_k<1,\quad\tau_k\ge0.\] For inequality QPs the residual includes stationarity, affine feasibility, multiplier-sign, and complementarity errors. If derivative data are also inexact, write \(\widetilde g_k=g_k+e_k^g\), \(\widetilde A_k=A_k+E_k^A\), and \(\widetilde B_k=B_k+E_k^B\), and require explicit bounds on these perturbations in addition to the inner-solve residual. The sequences of forcing terms and derivative-error bounds are part of the method definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact SQP terminates the quadratic-subproblem or KKT solve when a prescribed relative-plus-absolute residual bound is met instead of requiring a zero residual. If derivatives are approximate, their errors are controlled separately rather than being hidden inside the solve tolerance.
assumptions_latex: A norm and scaling for the primal-dual residual are fixed.
All derivative approximations used by the method have declared error variables or accuracy conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|K_kz_k-b_k\|\le\eta_k\|b_k\|+\tau_k\), with analogous complete KKT residual control for inequality QPs.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(\tau_k=0\), the solve reduces the relative KKT residual by the forcing factor \(\eta_k\).
Setting \(\eta_k=\tau_k=0\) recovers exact-subproblem SQP.
special_cases_latex: A Krylov method may terminate when the displayed residual test first holds.
A fixed forcing bound permits uniformly inexact solves; \(\eta_k\to0\) defines asymptotically exact inner solves.
immediate_consequences_latex: Subproblem work can be reduced when high accuracy is unnecessary far from a solution.
boundary_notes: A residual rule alone supplies no globalization or convergence claim.
Derivative errors and linear-solve residuals are distinct quantities and should not share an unspecified tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Globalization mechanisms for SQP steps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p_k\) be an SQP trial step, \(m_k\) its local model, and \(h(x)\) a nonlinear infeasibility measure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional SQP away from the purely local regime; the definition classifies acceptance and correction mechanisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP globalization is a rule \(\mathcal G_k\) that maps \((x_k,p_k,m_k)\) to an accepted step or a new model-control state while enforcing measurable progress. Principal families are: merit line search, which accepts \(s_k=\alpha_kp_k\) after sufficient decrease of a scalar merit function; trust region, which restricts \(\|p\|\le\Delta_k\) and compares actual with predicted reduction; filter, which accepts a trial point when its objective-infeasibility pair is not dominated and gives sufficient improvement; feasibility restoration, which temporarily prioritizes reduction of \(h\); and second-order correction, which modifies a rejected SQP trial to compensate for nonlinear constraint curvature. A practical globalization may compose several of these rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP globalization decides whether and how a quadratic-model step is accepted from a remote starting point. Standard families use merit-function line searches, trust regions, filters, feasibility restoration, and second-order corrections, either separately or in combination.
assumptions_latex: A trial step and predicted model change are available.
The selected mechanism defines an acceptance statistic: merit decrease, reduction ratio, filter dominance, or infeasibility decrease.
Control parameters such as \(\alpha_k\), \(\Delta_k\), penalty weights, or filter entries have explicit update rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((s_k,\text{state}_{k+1})=\mathcal G_k(x_k,p_k,m_k,h)\), with acceptance satisfying the progress test of the selected globalization family.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the \(\ell_1\) merit function, \(\phi_1(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu\|c(x)\|_1\), line-search acceptance can use an Armijo-type directional-decrease condition.
Trust-region acceptance uses a ratio of actual merit reduction to predicted model reduction.
special_cases_latex: A filter method may invoke restoration when neither objective nor infeasibility progress is acceptable.
A second-order correction may be attempted after a full SQP step is rejected because of constraint curvature.
immediate_consequences_latex: Globalization is logically independent of exact versus quasi-Newton curvature.
The accepted step need not equal the raw QP step.
boundary_notes: Globalization does not mean global optimization; it concerns convergence from nonlocal starting points.
Merit and filter acceptance criteria are distinct even when both monitor feasibility.

children.title: Line-Search SQP Method
children.top_down_role: SQP globalized through merit-function step acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search SQP Method
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP direction is accepted after backtracking finds sufficient directional decrease in an exact penalty merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), compute an SQP direction \(p_k\) and define \(\phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\|c(x)\|_1\). Choose \(\rho_k>0\) so that \(\phi_{\rho_k}'(x_k;p_k)<0\). Starting with \(\alpha=1\), reduce \(\alpha\) geometrically until
\[
\phi_{\rho_k}(x_k+\alpha p_k)\leq\phi_{\rho_k}(x_k)+\sigma\alpha\phi_{\rho_k}'(x_k;p_k),
\]
where \(0<\sigma<1\). Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha p_k\), update multipliers and the Hessian model, and terminate when the nonlinear KKT residual satisfies its tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted step satisfies the displayed Armijo inequality for \(\phi_{\rho_k}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained SQP globalized by Armijo decrease of an exact merit function.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and Armijo construction fit line-search SQP, but the cited locators concern generic line-search methods and do not specifically support the exact-L1 SQP merit function, penalty selection, or multiplier/model updates. An SQP-specific merit-function source is required.
