knowledge_statements.statement_title: Line-search sequential quadratic programming method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, with equalities indexed by \(\mathcal E\) and inequalities written \(c_i(x)\ge 0\), \(i\in\mathcal I\). At iteration \(k\), let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) model the Hessian of the Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, deterministic SQP with a merit-function backtracking line search and a convex or suitably modified quadratic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
\[p_k\in\arg\min_p\;
abla f(x_k)^Tp+	frac12p^TB_kp\quad	ext{s.t.}\quad c_i(x_k)+
abla c_i(x_k)^Tp=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\quad c_i(x_k)+
abla c_i(x_k)^Tp\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal I).\] Define \[\phi_1(x;\mu_k)=f(x)+\mu_k\!\left(\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x)|+\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}[c_i(x)]^-ight),\qquad [t]^-:=\max\{0,-t\}.\] A line-search SQP iteration chooses \(\mu_k>0\) so that \(p_k\) is a descent direction for \(\phi_1\), selects \(\alpha_k\in\{1,	au,	au^2,\ldots\}\), \(0<	au<1\), satisfying \[\phi_1(x_k+\alpha_kp_k;\mu_k)\le \phi_1(x_k;\mu_k)+\eta\alpha_kD\phi_1(x_k;\mu_k)[p_k],\qquad 0<\eta<	frac12,\] and sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), with the multiplier estimate updated toward the QP multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A line-search SQP method forms a quadratic model of the Lagrangian subject to linearized equalities and inequalities, solves that QP for a direction \(p_k\), and globalizes the step by backtracking on an exact-penalty merit function \(\phi_1\). The accepted point is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), where \(\alpha_k\) satisfies a directional sufficient-decrease condition.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k\) is symmetric and the QP has a bounded solution; in the standard line-search realization it is positive definite on the null space of the active linearized constraints.
The penalty parameter \(\mu_k\) is chosen large enough to make \(D\phi_1(x_k;\mu_k)[p_k]<0\) whenever \(p_k\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) is the merit-function-accepted SQP iterate generated from the QP direction.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints, the QP optimality equations are a Newton-type KKT system with \(B_k\) replacing \(\nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(B_k=\nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) gives exact-Hessian line-search SQP; a positive-definite BFGS approximation gives quasi-Newton SQP.
immediate_consequences_latex: Trying \(\alpha_k=1\) first permits eventual full-step behavior when the local SQP step satisfies the acceptance test.
boundary_notes: This definition excludes trust-region acceptance, which constrains \(p\) by a radius rather than scaling a fixed QP direction.
An inconsistent linearization requires an elastic, relaxation, or restoration mechanism not included in the core definition.

children.title: Trust-Region SQP Method
children.top_down_role: SQP globalized through constrained model regions and composite steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region SQP Method
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal step improves feasibility, a tangential step improves the model, and their sum is accepted according to a trust-region reduction ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x_k\), choose a normal step \(n_k\) that reduces \(\|c(x_k)+J_kn\|\) within its radius, then choose a tangential step \(t_k\) satisfying \(J_kt_k=0\) and approximately minimizing the quadratic Lagrangian model, with \(\|n_k+t_k\|\leq\Delta_k\). Put \(p_k=n_k+t_k\) and form
\[
r_k=\frac{\Phi_k(x_k)-\Phi_k(x_k+p_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)}.
\]
Reject the step and shrink \(\Delta_k\) when \(r_k\) is too small; otherwise accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\), and retain or enlarge \(\Delta_k\) according to agreement between actual and predicted reduction.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable, and the quadratic model is defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance is governed by \(r_k\), while \(\|p_k\|\leq\Delta_k\) controls model locality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite-step equality-constrained SQP with trust-region acceptance and radius updates.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits trust-region SQP, but the precise normal/tangential decomposition and reduction ratio depend on the chosen composite-step framework. The record also leaves Phi_k and m_k undefined. An authoritative source is needed before selecting and completing this variant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-region sequential quadratic programming method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), Jacobian \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\), Lagrangian Hessian model \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), and radius \(\Delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained trust-region SQP in composite-step form; inequality-constrained variants use analogous linearized constraints or interior-point variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A composite-step trust-region SQP iteration first computes a normal step \[v_k\in\arg\min_{\|v\|\le\xi\Delta_k}\|c(x_k)+A_kv\|^2,\qquad 0<\xi<1,\] sets \(r_k=c(x_k)+A_kv_k\), and computes \[p_k\in\arg\min_p\;f(x_k)+\nabla f(x_k)^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\quad\text{s.t.}\quad A_kp+c(x_k)=r_k,\quad \|p\|\le\Delta_k.\] For a merit model \(q_{\mu_k}\) and merit function \(\phi_{\mu_k}\), define \[\rho_k=\frac{\phi_{\mu_k}(x_k)-\phi_{\mu_k}(x_k+p_k)}{q_{\mu_k}(0)-q_{\mu_k}(p_k)}.\] The trial point is accepted when \(\rho_k\) exceeds a prescribed threshold; successful iterations set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\) and do not decrease \(\Delta_k\), while unsuccessful iterations keep \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and reduce the radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region SQP method minimizes a quadratic Lagrangian model inside a region \(\|p\|\le\Delta_k\). In composite-step form, a normal step first reduces the linearized constraint residual, after which a constrained quadratic step improves optimality without losing the selected feasibility reduction. Acceptance is governed by the ratio \(\rho_k\) of actual to predicted merit reduction, and the radius is updated according to that ratio.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) have the derivatives required by the models.
The normal subproblem has a computed minimizer or acceptable approximate minimizer, making the relaxed tangential subproblem feasible.
The denominator \(q_{\mu_k}(0)-q_{\mu_k}(p_k)\) is positive whenever the acceptance ratio is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method produces either an accepted full trust-region SQP step \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\) or a rejected trial with a reduced radius.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The constraint \(A_kp+c_k=r_k\), with \(r_k=A_kv_k+c_k\), is equivalent to requiring \(A_k(p-v_k)=0\); hence \(p_k=v_k+t_k\) with tangential component \(A_kt_k=0\).
special_cases_latex: If the exact linearized constraints are compatible within the radius, one may take \(r_k=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Indefinite \(B_k\) can be retained because boundedness is supplied by \(\|p\|\le\Delta_k\).
boundary_notes: Simply adding an exact linearized constraint and a small trust region may make the subproblem infeasible; the normal-step relaxation is part of the composite-step interface.
This definition does not prescribe a particular iterative solver for either subproblem.

notation.meaning: Normal step primarily reducing linearized infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Globalization alternatives and failure boundaries for SQP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded synthesis of sufficient curvature for a unique local SQP step and the principal tradeoffs of line-search and trust-region globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_k\) be the tangent space of the active constraints. If \(\nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L_k\) is positive definite on \(T_k\), the equality-constrained SQP quadratic subproblem has a unique solution. Otherwise, line-search SQP may replace or modify this Hessian to obtain positive-definite curvature and a well-defined descent step, at the risk of distorting the model. Trust-region SQP instead restricts \(p\) to a region in which the model is considered reliable and can accommodate indefinite Lagrangian Hessians, but the trust-region restriction can make the constrained subproblem infeasible and require costlier remedial procedures. Step acceptance for constrained SQP additionally requires a merit function or filter whose parameters or entries are updated compatibly with the computed step; neither globalization family is uniformly superior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive definiteness of the Lagrangian Hessian on the active-constraint tangent space gives a unique equality-constrained SQP step. Away from that regime, line-search SQP can enforce positive-definite curvature, yielding a well-defined descent step but possibly distorting the model. Trust-region SQP can retain indefinite curvature by bounding the step, but the added bound can make the constrained subproblem infeasible and increase computational cost. Merit functions or filters must also be updated consistently with the SQP step, and neither globalization approach is uniformly superior.
assumptions_latex: T_k\text{ is the tangent space of the active constraints at iteration }k.
\text{The SQP step is obtained from a local quadratic model using }\nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L_k\text{ or an approximation }B_k.
\nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L_k\succ 0\text{ on }T_k\text{ is assumed only for the uniqueness conclusion.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L_k\succ_{T_k}0\ \Longrightarrow\ \exists!\,p_k;\quad \text{otherwise globalization may use positive-definite curvature modification or a trust-region restriction, with respective model-distortion and possible-subproblem-infeasibility tradeoffs.}

children.title: Filter-SQP Method
children.top_down_role: SQP using separate objective and feasibility acceptance criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter-SQP Method
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trial point is accepted when it sufficiently improves either constraint violation or objective value relative to every stored filter entry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(\theta(x)=\|c(x)\|\) and maintain a finite filter \(\mathcal F_k\) of pairs \((\theta_i,f_i)\). A trial point \(x^+\) is filter-acceptable when, for every \((\theta_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F_k\),
\[
\theta(x^+)\leq\beta\theta_i\quad\text{or}\quad f(x^+)\leq f_i-\gamma\theta(x^+),
\]
with \(0<\beta<1\) and \(\gamma>0\). Compute an SQP trial step, accept it only if this test and any model safeguard hold, insert its pair into the filter, and remove pairs dominated by it. If acceptance repeatedly fails, invoke a feasibility restoration mechanism.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuous.
\(\mathcal F_k\) contains mutually nondominated objective-violation pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted pair is acceptable relative to all entries of \(\mathcal F_k\) and does not require a scalar penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP globalization by nondominance in objective value and constraint violation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits filter-SQP, but filter acceptability margins and safeguards vary materially across formulations. The displayed objective margin involving theta(x+) and the restoration interface require a specific authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Filter-globalized SQP method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the nonlinear program \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\), \(i\in\mathcal E\), and \(c_i(x)\ge0\), \(i\in\mathcal I\), define \(h(x)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x)|+\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}[c_i(x)]^-\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional SQP whose step acceptance keeps objective reduction and feasibility reduction as separate criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter is a finite set \(\mathcal F\subset\mathbb R^2\) of mutually nondominating pairs \((f_j,h_j)\), where \((f_a,h_a)\) dominates \((f_b,h_b)\) when \(f_a\le f_b\) and \(h_a\le h_b\). A filter-SQP method computes an SQP trial step \(p_k\) from a quadratic model with linearized constraints and accepts \(x^+=x_k+\alpha p_k\) only if, for every \((f_j,h_j)\in\mathcal F_k\), \[f(x^+)\le f_j-\beta h_j\quad\text{or}\quad h(x^+)\le(1-\beta)h_j,\qquad 0<\beta<1,\] together with any model-decrease safeguard required for near-feasible iterations. On acceptance it sets \(x_{k+1}=x^+\), inserts \((f(x^+),h(x^+))\), and deletes every pair dominated by the inserted pair. Rejection causes line-search backtracking or trust-region contraction; failure to obtain an acceptable step invokes restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter-SQP method solves the usual SQP model but does not combine the objective and constraint violation into a penalty function. Instead, it stores mutually nondominating objective–violation pairs. A trial point is acceptable when it gives a prescribed improvement in objective or infeasibility relative to every stored pair. Accepted pairs enter the filter and remove pairs they dominate; rejected trials are shortened or recomputed.
assumptions_latex: The violation measure \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\) vanishes exactly at feasible points.
The SQP step-generation subproblem supplies a trial direction unless control is transferred to restoration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance is determined by separate sufficient improvement of \(f\) or \(h\), without selecting a penalty weight joining the two quantities.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(\beta=0\), basic acceptability is precisely the requirement that \((f(x^+),h(x^+))\) not be dominated by any member of \(\mathcal F_k\).
special_cases_latex: The same filter rule can globalize either a line-search SQP direction or successive trust-region SQP trials.
immediate_consequences_latex: A trial may be accepted while increasing \(f\) if it sufficiently decreases \(h\), or while increasing \(h\) if it sufficiently decreases \(f\).
boundary_notes: A bare nondominance test lacks the margin needed for standard convergence mechanisms; the definition includes a sufficient-improvement margin.
Restoration is a separate feasibility-oriented phase rather than an SQP optimality step.

notation.meaning: Current set of mutually nondominating objective–violation pairs.

children.title: Elastic Feasibility Problem
children.top_down_role: Relaxed subproblems for inconsistent or unreliable linearized constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Elastic Feasibility Problem
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative elastic variables make an inconsistent linearized constraint feasible and impose an L1 cost equal to its residual norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a quadratic model with gradient \(g_k\), symmetric matrix \(B_k\), and linearized equality \(c_k+J_kp=0\), its elastic relaxation is
\[
\min_{p,u,v}\; g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}B_kp+\sigma_k\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}(u+v)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_k+J_kp=u-v,\qquad u\geq0,\ v\geq0.
\]
For every \(p\), minimizing over \(u,v\) yields \(u-v=c_k+J_kp\) and \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}(u+v)=\|c_k+J_kp\|_1\). Thus the relaxation remains feasible even when the original linearized equality is inconsistent, while \(\sigma_k>0\) prices its violation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{u,v\geq0,\ u-v=c_k+J_kp}\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}(u+v)=\|c_k+J_kp\|_1\), and the elastic constraints are always feasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: L1-elastic relaxation of an equality-constrained SQP quadratic subproblem.

notation.meaning: nonnegative positive and negative elastic variables
constraint residual at the current iterate

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the elastic-feasibility leaf, and the stated L1 elastic reformulation is mathematically coherent. Because the record has no inspectable citation for its use as an SQP elastic subproblem, authoritative sourcing is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Elastic relaxation of an SQP feasibility model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(a_{ik}=\nabla c_i(x_k)\), and \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\). Equalities use \(c_i=0\), while inequalities use \(c_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional elastic-mode SQP subproblem for inconsistent or unreliable linearized constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu>0\), the elastic SQP problem is \[\min_{p,v,w,t}\;g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}(v_i+w_i)+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}t_i\] subject to \[c_i(x_k)+a_{ik}^Tp=v_i-w_i\quad(i\in\mathcal E),\qquad c_i(x_k)+a_{ik}^Tp\ge-t_i\quad(i\in\mathcal I),\] \[v_i\ge0,\quad w_i\ge0,\quad t_i\ge0.\] The associated elastic feasibility problem drops the optimality model or gives it secondary priority and minimizes \[\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}(v_i+w_i)+\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}t_i\] over the same linearized constraints, optionally with a step bound. The slacks quantify the smallest admitted violation of the linearized constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The elastic feasibility problem augments every linearized equality with nonnegative positive and negative slacks and every linearized inequality with a nonnegative violation slack. It minimizes their total size, alone or together with a weighted SQP quadratic model. The resulting subproblem is feasible because sufficiently large elastic variables absorb incompatible linearizations.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu>0\), and elastic variables are unrestricted above.
Any additional step-domain restriction admits at least one step paired with sufficiently large elastic variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elastic variables \((v,w,t)\) provide a feasible relaxation and their sum is an \(\ell_1\) measure of linearized infeasibility.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Eliminating \((v,w,t)\) yields the nonsmooth objective \(g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp+\mu\bigl(\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x_k)+a_{ik}^Tp|+\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}[c_i(x_k)+a_{ik}^Tp]^-\bigr)\).
special_cases_latex: If the unrelaxed linearization is feasible and the penalty is sufficiently influential, a solution may have \(v=w=t=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive optimal elastic variables identify constraints responsible for residual model infeasibility.
boundary_notes: Elastic feasibility of the model does not imply feasibility of the original nonlinear constraints.
Exact disappearance of the slacks depends on penalty size and regularity; it is not part of the definition.

notation.meaning: Positive and negative elastic components for equality \(i\).

children.title: Restoration-Phase Interface
children.top_down_role: Feasibility-oriented phases coupled to SQP acceptance mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Restoration-Phase Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When ordinary SQP steps fail, a restoration phase seeks sufficient feasibility improvement before rebuilding the model and resuming optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\theta(x)=\|c(x)\|\). Invoke restoration when the SQP subproblem is incompatible, no acceptable trial step is found, or feasibility progress is inadequate. Starting from \(x_k\), compute a restoration point \(x_k^R\) by approximately minimizing \(\theta\), possibly within bounds or a trust region, until
\[
\theta(x_k^R)\leq\kappa_R\theta(x_k),\qquad 0<\kappa_R<1,
\]
and \(x_k^R\) is acceptable to the active globalization mechanism. Replace \(x_k\) by \(x_k^R\), rebuild the SQP model, and resume optimization. Declare restoration failure if its feasibility target cannot be attained within its prescribed resource limit.
assumptions_latex: The globalization mechanism supplies an acceptance test for the restoration point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful restoration returns \(x_k^R\) with \(\theta(x_k^R)\leq\kappa_R\theta(x_k)\) and then resumes SQP.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility restoration coupled to filter or merit-based SQP acceptance.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the restoration-phase interface. The listed triggers, fixed feasibility-reduction condition, compatibility with the active globalization mechanism, and failure rule describe a particular framework and require an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility-restoration interface for globalized SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\) measure nonlinear constraint violation, with \(h(x)=0\) exactly at feasible points, and let \(\mathcal F_k\) be the current acceptance filter.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-oriented recovery phase coupled to a filter or related SQP acceptance mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restoration-phase interface consists of a trigger, a restoration problem, and a return test. It is triggered when the SQP step-generation problem is infeasible, when filter rejection drives a line-search step below \(\alpha_{\min}>0\), or when trust-region contraction makes the step problem unusable. Starting from \(x_k\), restoration seeks an approximate solution \[x_k^{\mathrm R}\approx\arg\min_{x\in\mathcal X_k^{\mathrm R}} h(x).\] It may return control to the SQP phase only when \[h(x_k^{\mathrm R})\le h_k^{\mathrm{target}}<h(x_k)\] and \((f(x_k^{\mathrm R}),h(x_k^{\mathrm R}))\) is compatible with the filter, meaning it satisfies the applicable filter acceptability margin. The returned point becomes the next SQP base point; if restoration instead approaches a stationary point of \(h\) with positive violation, that outcome is reported as an infeasibility-stationarity termination rather than an optimality step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The restoration interface transfers control from SQP to a subproblem devoted exclusively to reducing constraint violation. Transfer occurs after an infeasible model or persistent rejection. Restoration returns a point only after achieving a prescribed violation reduction and compatibility with the current filter; the point then becomes the base for renewed SQP iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(h(x)\ge0\) for all \(x\) and \(h(x)=0\) exactly on the nonlinear feasible set.
The restoration domain \(\mathcal X_k^{\mathrm R}\) contains the current point or another valid restoration start.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful restoration phase returns \(x_k^{\mathrm R}\) with strictly reduced infeasibility and valid re-entry into the SQP acceptance mechanism.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For standard equality and inequality constraints one may take \(h(x)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x)|+\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}[c_i(x)]^-\).
special_cases_latex: An elastic feasibility subproblem is one possible smooth constrained realization of the restoration objective.
immediate_consequences_latex: Restoration can distinguish failure of the current SQP model from convergence toward an infeasible stationary point.
boundary_notes: Restoration does not primarily minimize \(f\), so a restored point is not accepted merely for improving the objective.
The precise target sequence and restoration solver belong to the encompassing algorithm, not to this interface definition.

notation.meaning: Point returned by the restoration phase.

children.title: Second-Order Correction Interface
children.top_down_role: Corrections addressing nonlinear constraint curvature after an SQP step.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Correction Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small linear correction cancels nonlinear constraint residual left by the SQP step and is accepted only through the existing globalization test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After computing a primary SQP step \(p_k\), evaluate the nonlinear residual \(c(x_k+p_k)\). Compute a small correction \(q_k\), for example the minimum-norm solution of
\[
J_kq_k=-c(x_k+p_k),
\]
subject to a safeguard such as \(\|q_k\|\leq\kappa\|p_k\|^2\). Test the corrected point \(x_k^+=x_k+p_k+q_k\) using the same merit, filter, or trust-region acceptance mechanism as the primary trial. Accept the correction only when it improves acceptability without violating the safeguard; otherwise retain or reject the uncorrected trial according to the globalization rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The correction satisfies \(J_kq_k=-c(x_k+p_k)\) and, when safeguarded, is of second order relative to \(p_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-curvature correction applied after a primary SQP trial step.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the second-order-correction leaf, but q_k=O(||p_k||^2) does not follow from the listed assumptions alone; it also needs the primary SQP step's linearized-feasibility property and local residual estimates. The Jacobian evaluation point and safeguard are variant-dependent and need sourcing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order correction for an SQP trial step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x_k\), let \(p_k\) solve an SQP subproblem for constraints \(c_i(x)=0\), \(i\in\mathcal E\), and \(c_i(x)\ge0\), \(i\in\mathcal I\). Let \(A_k\) contain the constraint gradients and \(B_k\) model the Lagrangian Hessian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth SQP correction addressing nonlinear constraint curvature and the Maratos effect after a primary SQP step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After computing \(p_k\), define for every constraint \[d_{ik}=c_i(x_k+p_k)-
abla c_i(x_k)^Tp_k.\] A second-order-corrected model replaces the original constant term \(c_i(x_k)\) by \(d_{ik}\) and computes \(\widetilde p_k\) from \[\min_p\;
abla f(x_k)^Tp+	frac12p^TB_kp\] subject to \[
abla c_i(x_k)^Tp+d_{ik}=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\qquad 
abla c_i(x_k)^Tp+d_{ik}\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal I).\] Equivalently, when the implementation solves directly for a small correction \(s_k\), it imposes \[A_ks_k\approx-c(x_k+p_k)\] on the relevant active constraints and forms the corrected trial \(x_k+p_k+s_k\). The correction is offered to the merit or filter acceptance test before backtracking the original direction, ordinarily subject to a safeguard such as \(\|s_k\|=O(\|p_k\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order correction reevaluates the nonlinear constraints at the full SQP trial point and uses the observed curvature residual to compute a corrected trial. It either resolves a modified SQP model with corrected constraint constants or adds a small vector \(s_k\) satisfying the linearized equation \(A_ks_k\approx-c(x_k+p_k)\). The corrected point is tested before shortening the primary step.
assumptions_latex: The constraint values at \(x_k+p_k\) and the Jacobian at \(x_k\) are available.
The correction problem is feasible or an acceptable approximate correction can be computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The candidate supplied to the acceptance mechanism is \(x_k+\widetilde p_k\), equivalently \(x_k+p_k+s_k\), with nonlinear constraint curvature compensated to second order.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Taylor expansion identifies \(d_{ik}\) as an approximation to \(c_i(x_k)+\tfrac12p_k^T\nabla^2c_i(x_k)p_k\) when \(p_k\) satisfies the original linearized constraint.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints and a correction-only solve, \(s_k\) may be chosen as a minimum-norm solution of \(A_ks_k=-c(x_k+p_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A safeguarded correction can allow acceptance of an unshortened SQP displacement even when the uncorrected full step fails because of constraint curvature.
boundary_notes: The correction is not a replacement for restoration when the primary model is fundamentally infeasible.
Without a smallness safeguard, the correction need not retain the local SQP step properties.

notation.meaning: Constraint constant corrected using evaluation at the primary trial point.
Additive second-order correction to the primary SQP step.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Penalty–barrier interface to Newton and SQP systems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), equality residual \(c_E(x)\), and inequality residual \(c_I(x)\ge0\) define a smooth nonlinear program. Barrier slacks satisfy \(s>0\) and \(c_I(x)-s=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty and logarithmic-barrier structures only insofar as they define Newton systems, regularizations, or step-acceptance functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A penalty–barrier Newton interface is a parameterized scalar or primal-dual residual model whose stationarity equations are solved by Newton or SQP steps. Representative members are \[Q(x;\rho)=f(x)+\tfrac\rho2\|c_E(x)\|^2,\qquad \Phi_1(x;\rho)=f(x)+\rho\|c_E(x)\|_1,\] and the slack barrier model \[\Phi_{\mu}(x,s)=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^{m_I}\log s_i\quad\text{s.t.}\quad c_E(x)=0,\quad c_I(x)-s=0,\quad s>0.\] Its Newton interface is the linearization \[K_{\theta}(z_k)\Delta z_k=-R_{\theta}(z_k),\] where \(R_{\theta}\) is the gradient/KKT residual of the selected penalty or barrier model and \(K_{\theta}\) is its Hessian or primal-dual Jacobian. Its globalization interface accepts \(z_k+\alpha_k\Delta z_k\) using sufficient reduction of the same penalty/barrier merit quantity or a filter pairing that quantity with constraint violation, while preserving \(s_k+\alpha_ks_k^{\Delta}>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The penalty–barrier Newton interface maps a constrained problem to a parameterized penalty objective or a slack-variable logarithmic-barrier problem, forms the corresponding Newton or primal-dual KKT linear system, and uses the same structure in step acceptance. Quadratic penalties regularize feasibility equations, exact penalties supply merit functions, and barriers enforce strict interiority.
assumptions_latex: The selected residual mapping \(R_\theta\) is differentiable at the Newton iterate; nonsmooth penalties use directional models for acceptance rather than a classical Hessian.
For the logarithmic barrier, every current and trial slack is strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Newton/SQP direction is defined by \(K_\theta(z_k)\Delta z_k=-R_\theta(z_k)\), and acceptance is evaluated in the associated penalty or barrier model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A barrier filter may pair \(f(x)-\mu\sum_i\log s_i\) with \(\|(c_E(x),c_I(x)-s)\|\) instead of combining them with a penalty weight.
special_cases_latex: The quadratic-penalty Newton system can be written as an augmented saddle-point system with a \(-\rho^{-1}I\) multiplier block.

children.top_down_role: Quadratic-penalty regularization and feasibility effects on Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Penalty Method Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic penalization converts equality constraints into a smooth objective whose Newton matrix gains a large normal-space Gram term as the penalty tightens.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), define
\[
\Phi_\mu(x)=f(x)+\frac{1}{2\mu}\|c(x)\|_2^2,
\]
where \(\mu>0\). Its derivatives are
\[
\nabla\Phi_\mu(x)=\nabla f(x)+\mu^{-1}J(x)^{\mathsf T}c(x),
\]
\[
\nabla^2\Phi_\mu(x)=\nabla^2f(x)+\mu^{-1}J(x)^{\mathsf T}J(x)+\mu^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m c_i(x)\nabla^2c_i(x).
\]
A Newton step solves \(\nabla^2\Phi_\mu(x)p=-\nabla\Phi_\mu(x)\). Decreasing \(\mu\) strengthens feasibility enforcement but amplifies the normal-space term \(\mu^{-1}J^{\mathsf T}J\), potentially worsening conditioning.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are twice continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The penalty Newton system has the displayed gradient and Hessian, including the scaled term \(\mu^{-1}J^{\mathsf T}J\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton derivatives and conditioning structure of the equality-constrained quadratic penalty.

Its Newton equation contains the increasingly large term \(\rho A^TA\). Introducing an auxiliary multiplier-like variable yields an equivalent saddle-point system with lower-right block \(-\rho^{-1}I\), exposing the method as a regularized SQP system.

The displayed Newton or augmented system is solved exactly or to the tolerance prescribed by the outer penalty iteration.

children.title: Exact L1 Penalty Method Interface
children.top_down_role: Nonsmooth exact penalties used as SQP merit and globalization devices.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact L1 Penalty Method Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The L1 penalty supplies an exact nonsmooth SQP merit function with an explicitly computable one-sided directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For equality constraints \(c(x)=0\), define the exact penalty merit function
\[
\phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\|c(x)\|_1,
\]
where \(\rho>0\). Its directional derivative is
\[
\phi_\rho'(x;p)=\nabla f(x)^{\mathsf T}p+\rho\sum_{i:c_i(x)\ne0}\operatorname{sign}(c_i(x))\nabla c_i(x)^{\mathsf T}p+\rho\sum_{i:c_i(x)=0}|\nabla c_i(x)^{\mathsf T}p|.
\]
An SQP method may choose \(\rho\) so its step is a descent direction for \(\phi_\rho\), then apply a merit-function line search. Nondifferentiability occurs only through absolute constraint residuals and does not prevent evaluation of this directional derivative.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and each component \(c_i\) are continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi_\rho'(x;p)\) equals the displayed expression and can define SQP descent and line-search tests.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsmooth L1 merit representation and its SQP directional model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact ℓ1-penalty SQP merit interface
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\), \(i\in\mathcal E\), and \(c_i(x)\ge0\), \(i\in\mathcal I\), with \(f,c_i\) continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsmooth exact penalty used to globalize an SQP direction by directional sufficient decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu>0\), define \[\phi_1(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu h_1(x),\qquad h_1(x)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x)|+\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}[c_i(x)]^-.\] An exact-\(\ell_1\)-penalty SQP interface computes a QP direction \(p_k\), chooses \(\mu_k\) so that \[D\phi_1(x_k;\mu_k)[p_k]<0\quad\text{when }p_k\ne0,\] and selects \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfying \[\phi_1(x_k+\alpha_kp_k;\mu_k)\le\phi_1(x_k;\mu_k)+\eta\alpha_kD\phi_1(x_k;\mu_k)[p_k],\qquad 0<\eta<1.\] The resulting update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). Exactness means that, near a regular constrained local solution \(x^*\) with multiplier \(\lambda^*\), every \(\mu>\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\) makes \(x^*\) a local minimizer of \(\phi_1(\cdot;\mu)\), with strictness under the corresponding second-order condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact \(\ell_1\) interface adds a penalty parameter times the sum of equality and inequality violations to the objective. An SQP direction is accepted by a directional Armijo condition for this nonsmooth merit function. Once the penalty exceeds the multiplier threshold, the constrained local solution is also a local minimizer of the penalty function, so feasibility and optimality can be represented with a finite penalty value.
assumptions_latex: The directional derivative of \(\phi_1\) exists along the SQP direction.
For the stated local exactness property, \(x^*\) is a strict constrained local solution satisfying first-order conditions with multiplier \(\lambda^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted SQP iterate decreases the exact \(\ell_1\) merit model, and finite-parameter local exactness holds for \(\mu>\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\) under the stated regularity.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Introducing nonnegative elastic variables converts the piecewise-linear violation term in the SQP model into a smooth quadratic program with linear constraints.
special_cases_latex: With equality constraints only, \(h_1(x)=\|c(x)\|_1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Unlike the quadratic penalty, local exactness does not require \(\mu\to\infty\).
boundary_notes: \(\phi_1\) is generally nondifferentiable at feasible points and at inequality-activity boundaries.
The multiplier threshold is a local exactness threshold, not a global-minimization guarantee.

notation.meaning: Largest absolute optimal multiplier, including equality and active-inequality multipliers.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local exact-penalty correspondence family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{x:c_i(x)=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\ c_i(x)\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal I)\}\), let \(V(x)\ge0\) vanish exactly on \(\Omega\), and define \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exactness statements relating constrained local minimizers to unconstrained local minimizers of a finite-parameter penalty function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact-penalty theorem family for \((f,\Omega,V)\) is a collection of statements establishing a finite threshold \(\bar\rho<\infty\) such that \[x^*\in\operatorname{locmin}_{x\in\Omega}f\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x^*\in\operatorname{locmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}P_\rho\quad\text{for every }\rho>\bar\rho,\] optionally with the converse local correspondence \[x\in U\cap\operatorname{locmin}P_\rho\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x\in\Omega\cap\operatorname{locmin}_{\Omega}f\] for a specified neighborhood \(U\) and all sufficiently large finite \(\rho\). For the standard \(\ell_1\) violation and a constrained solution satisfying first-order conditions with multiplier \(\lambda^*\), the canonical threshold is \(\bar\rho=\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\); a second-order sufficient condition strengthens local minimality to strict local minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact-penalty theorem family consists of finite-threshold correspondence results. Above a threshold \(\bar\rho\), a constrained local solution is also an unconstrained local minimizer of the penalized objective. Some family members additionally exclude nearby infeasible penalized minimizers. For the standard \(\ell_1\) penalty, the natural local threshold is the infinity norm of the solution multiplier.
assumptions_latex: Each family member explicitly states the constraint qualification, multiplier existence, and local first- or second-order conditions needed for its threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness is the existence of a finite \(\bar\rho\) producing a local solution correspondence between the constrained and penalized problems.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Local exactness at \(x^*\) is equivalently the existence of a neighborhood \(U\) and finite \(\bar\rho\) such that \(P_\rho(x)\ge P_\rho(x^*)=f(x^*)\) for every \(x\in U\) and \(\rho>\bar\rho\).
special_cases_latex: For \(V=h_1\), Theorem 17.3 gives \(\bar\rho=\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\) under its stated hypotheses.
immediate_consequences_latex: A finite exact threshold distinguishes this family from quadratic-penalty convergence based on \(\rho\to\infty\).
boundary_notes: One-way exactness does not by itself assert that every penalized local minimizer is feasible.
Local exactness does not imply global equivalence unless additional global hypotheses are stated.

notation.meaning: Set of local minimizers on the indicated domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Nondifferentiable Exact Penalty Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard KKT regularity and second-order sufficiency, any L1 penalty weight exceeding the largest multiplier magnitude preserves the constrained strict local solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\). Let \(x^*\) be a strict local solution with a KKT multiplier \(\lambda^*\), and suppose the linear independence constraint qualification and the second-order sufficient condition hold at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\). Then, for every
\[
\rho>\|\lambda^*\|_\infty,
\]
the point \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer of
\[
\phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\|c(x)\|_1.
\]
Thus a finite penalty parameter suffices locally; no limiting process with \(\rho\to\infty\) is required. The penalty remains generally nondifferentiable at feasible points because the absolute-value terms vanish there.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
LICQ holds at \(x^*\), with KKT multiplier \(\lambda^*\).
The equality-constrained second-order sufficient condition holds at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho>\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\) implies that \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer of \(f(x)+\rho\|c(x)\|_1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exactness threshold for the equality-constrained L1 penalty.

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier at the constrained solution

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nondifferentiable exact-penalty family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a nonlinear program with feasible set \(\Omega\), let \(V:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\) be a locally Lipschitz violation function satisfying \(V^{-1}(0)=\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally Lipschitz, generally nonsmooth finite-parameter penalties, centered on norm-like constraint violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The nondifferentiable exact-penalty family is \[P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V(x),\qquad \rho>0,\] where \(V\) has first-order growth away from feasibility and is not required to be differentiable on \(\Omega\). Its canonical nonlinear-programming member is \[V_1(x)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x)|+\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}[c_i(x)]^-.\] The family is locally exact at a constrained local minimizer \(x^*\) when there exist \(\bar\rho<\infty\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\) such that \[P_\rho(x^*)\le P_\rho(x)\quad\text{for all }x\in U\text{ and all }\rho>\bar\rho.\] For the canonical \(V_1\), a regular strict local solution with multiplier \(\lambda^*\) admits \(\bar\rho=\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\), with strict penalized local minimality when the stated second-order sufficient condition also holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nondifferentiable exact penalty adds a finite weight times a norm-like violation function having linear growth away from the feasible set. The standard member sums absolute equality residuals and negative parts of inequality residuals. Exactness means that every sufficiently large but finite penalty weight makes the constrained solution a local minimizer of the unconstrained penalized function.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is nonnegative, locally Lipschitz near \(x^*\), and vanishes exactly on the feasible set.
The multiplier threshold statement uses the regularity and local optimality hypotheses of the standard \(\ell_1\) exactness result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family represents constrained local minimizers by nonsmooth unconstrained penalties at finite parameter values.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The canonical violation \(V_1\) is the optimal value of a linear elastic-slack problem for the constraint residual vector.
special_cases_latex: Equality-only problems give \(V_1(x)=\|c(x)\|_1\); other unsquared norms produce related nonsmooth penalty families when an exactness result is available.
immediate_consequences_latex: Directional derivatives or generalized derivatives, rather than ordinary gradients, govern descent at feasible points.
boundary_notes: Squared residual penalties have second-order rather than first-order growth and generally are not finite-parameter exact.
The family definition does not assert exactness for every locally Lipschitz violation function; exactness is an additional local property.

notation.meaning: Penalized objective with finite penalty parameter \(\rho\).

knowledge_statements.title: Differentiable Exact Penalty Family
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth augmented penalty is locally exact when, beyond a finite parameter threshold, its nearby minimizers correspond precisely to feasible constrained solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), and let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair. A family \(P_r:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is a locally differentiable exact penalty family at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) if each \(P_r\) is continuously differentiable near that pair and there exist \(\bar r<\infty\) and a neighborhood \(U\) such that, for every \(r\geq\bar r\), \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a local minimizer of \(P_r\) on \(U\), while every local minimizer \((x,y)\in U\) satisfies \(c(x)=0\) and has \(x\) locally solving the original constrained problem.
assumptions_latex: \(P_r\) is continuously differentiable near \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) for all sufficiently large \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all \(r\geq\bar r\), nearby local minimizers of \(P_r\) are feasible and recover local solutions of the constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exactness for smooth penalties defined on an augmented primal-multiplier space.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The leaf calls for exactness results, whereas the record supplies a generic definition. Moreover, requiring every nearby local minimizer of an arbitrary differentiable P_r to be feasible and recover a constrained local solution is stronger than merely asserting local exactness at the designated KKT pair. The cited chapter locator is relevant, but the precise augmented penalty construction and its theorem-level hypotheses must be inspected before a reliable replacement can be formulated.

children.title: Filter Line-Search Barrier Interface
children.top_down_role: The shared filter-globalization interface between SQP and barrier Newton methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Line-Search Barrier Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtracking preserves strict interiority and accepts a trial when it sufficiently improves feasibility or barrier objective relative to every filter entry; otherwise restoration is invoked.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a strictly interior iterate \(z_k=(x_k,s_k)\), barrier parameter \(\mu_k>0\), constraint violation \(\theta(z)\ge 0\), barrier objective \(\phi_{\mu_k}(z)\), filter \(\mathcal F_k\), and Newton-SQP direction \(d_k\), choose the largest trial \(\alpha\in\{1,\beta,\beta^2,\ldots\}\) satisfying the fraction-to-boundary condition \(s_k+\alpha d_k^s\ge(1-\tau)s_k\). Accept \(z_k^+=z_k+\alpha d_k\) only if, for every \((\theta_j,\phi_j)\in\mathcal F_k\),
\[\theta(z_k^+)\le(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_j\quad\text{or}\quad \phi_{\mu_k}(z_k^+)\le\phi_j-\gamma_\phi\theta_j.\]
Insert each accepted nondominated pair into the filter; otherwise continue backtracking or invoke restoration. Reduce \(\mu_k\) only after the prescribed feasibility and centrality tests hold.
assumptions_latex: The Newton-SQP direction and filter measures are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted trial is strictly interior and is not dominated, under the stated margins, by any pair in \(\mathcal F_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic filter globalization for a primal-dual barrier Newton or SQP step.
review_flags: filter acceptance and barrier-update variants differ across implementations
authoritative filter-SQP or filter-interior-point source required

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the interface leaf, and the fraction-to-boundary and filter tests are plausible. However, filter margins, restoration behavior, and barrier-update rules are implementation-dependent and have no cited source. The instruction to choose the largest boundary-feasible step before applying the filter test also leaves the subsequent backtracking selection rule ambiguous.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Filter line search for a primal-dual barrier step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(s\in\mathbb R^{m_I}_{++}\) be inequality slacks, \(c_E(x)=0\), \(c_I(x)-s=0\), and \(\mu>0\) the barrier parameter. A primal-dual Newton step is \((p_x,p_s,p_y,p_z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared globalization interface between filter SQP and nonlinear primal-dual barrier Newton methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the barrier objective and infeasibility measure \[\varphi_\mu(x,s)=f(x)-\mu\sum_{i=1}^{m_I}\log s_i,\qquad h_B(x,s)=\bigl\|(c_E(x),c_I(x)-s)\bigr\|.\] A barrier filter is a set of mutually nondominating pairs \((\varphi_j,h_j)\). Given maximum positivity-preserving step lengths, a line search selects \[\alpha_s\in(0,\alpha_s^{\max}],\qquad \alpha_z\in(0,\alpha_z^{\max}]\] and forms \[x^+=x+\alpha_sp_x,\quad s^+=s+\alpha_sp_s>0,\quad y^+=y+\alpha_zp_y,\quad z^+=z+\alpha_zp_z>0.\] The primal trial is accepted only if \((\varphi_\mu(x^+,s^+),h_B(x^+,s^+))\) is acceptable to the filter with the prescribed sufficient-improvement margin and any required barrier-model decrease test. Rejection causes backtracking; persistent rejection or very small step lengths may transfer control to feasibility restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This interface applies the filter idea to a barrier Newton step. The two filter coordinates are the logarithmic-barrier objective and the equality/slack residual norm. A fraction-to-the-boundary line search preserves positive slacks and dual variables, while filter acceptance requires sufficient progress in either barrier objective or feasibility. Persistent rejection can invoke restoration.
assumptions_latex: The current slacks and inequality multipliers are strictly positive.
The maximum step lengths are chosen so every trial remains in the positive orthant.
The barrier objective is evaluated at a fixed \(\mu\) during the line search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted primal-dual trial preserves strict positivity and is acceptable in the separate barrier-objective and infeasibility coordinates.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Replacing the filter by \(\varphi_\mu(x,s)+\nu h_B(x,s)\) yields a penalty-barrier merit line search, but it introduces a penalty parameter \(\nu\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m_I=0\), the logarithmic term disappears and the interface reduces to an equality-constrained filter line search.
immediate_consequences_latex: Objective and feasibility progress remain separately visible even though the barrier already enforces interiority.
boundary_notes: Filter acceptability alone does not replace fraction-to-the-boundary restrictions.
The barrier parameter update occurs outside the fixed-parameter line-search acceptance test.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local convergence regime of an SQP iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), let \(z=(x,\lambda)\), \(F(z)=(\nabla_x\mathcal L(x,\lambda),c(x))\), and let \(z^*=(x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfy \(F(z^*)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality-constrained SQP; after stable active-set identification, the same definition applies locally to inequalities restricted to their final active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP iteration map \(T\) is locally convergent to \(z^*\) if there exists \(\delta>0\) such that every initial pair satisfying \(\|z_0-z^*\|<\delta\) generates a well-defined sequence \(z_{k+1}=T(z_k)\) that remains in the local regularity neighborhood and obeys \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\|z_k-z^*\|=0.\] Its local Q-order is characterized by constants \(C>0\) and \(q\ge1\) for which \[\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|\le C\|z_k-z^*\|^q\] for all sufficiently large \(k\). In the exact-Hessian local SQP method, \(T\) is Newton's map for \(F(z)=0\); under Lipschitz second derivatives, LICQ, and the second-order sufficient condition, the canonical local regime has \(q=2\). A globalized SQP method enters this regime only when its acceptance mechanism eventually admits the local step, normally with \(\alpha_k=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP local convergence means that all sufficiently close primal–multiplier starting pairs generate well-defined iterates converging to the target KKT pair while remaining in the regular neighborhood. The rate is measured on the primal–dual error. Exact-Hessian local SQP is Newton's method on the KKT equations and has the canonical quadratic local regime under smoothness, LICQ, and second-order sufficiency.
assumptions_latex: The target \(z^*\) is a KKT pair.
The local KKT matrix is nonsingular; LICQ and positive definiteness of the Lagrangian Hessian on the tangent space provide the standard sufficient conditions.
For the quadratic rate, \(f\) and \(c\) are twice differentiable near \(x^*\) with Lipschitz continuous second derivatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a neighborhood from which SQP converges to \(z^*\); exact-Hessian local SQP has Q-quadratic primal–dual convergence under the canonical assumptions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For exact-Hessian equality-constrained SQP, the QP KKT equations are exactly the Newton equations for \(F(z)=0\).
special_cases_latex: For inequality constraints, strict complementarity and active-set identification reduce the local iteration to the equality-constrained regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: A globalization device must become locally inactive, or accept full steps, to preserve the unmodified local rate.
boundary_notes: This is a local property and does not assert convergence from remote starting points.
Quasi-Newton and inexact solves require additional approximation or forcing conditions for superlinear or quadratic rates.

children.title: SQP Second-Order Sufficient Condition

knowledge_statements.title: SQP Second-Order Sufficient Condition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a KKT point of a smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear program, the Lagrangian Hessian must be positive on every nonzero critical direction; this gives strict local minimality and positive reduced SQP curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R^m\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R^p\) be twice continuously differentiable, and consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le 0\). Let \((x^*,\lambda^*,
u^*)\) satisfy the KKT conditions with \(
u^*\ge 0\), and define \(L(x,\lambda,
u)=f(x)+\lambda^T h(x)+
u^T g(x)\) and \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\). Define the critical cone by
\[\mathcal C^*=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:
abla h(x^*)^Td=0,\ 
abla g_i(x^*)^Td=0\ 	ext{for }i\in\mathcal A^*	ext{ with }
u_i^*>0,\ 
abla g_i(x^*)^Td\le 0\ 	ext{for }i\in\mathcal A^*	ext{ with }
u_i^*=0\}.\]
The SQP second-order sufficient condition is
\[d^T
abla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,
u^*)d>0\qquad	ext{for every }d\in\mathcal C^*\setminus\{0\}.\]
Under this condition, \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer, and the local SQP model has positive curvature on every nonzero feasible critical direction.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
The point and multipliers satisfy the KKT conditions with \(\nu^*\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrangian Hessian is strictly positive on \(\mathcal C^*\setminus\{0\}\), and \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-cone SOSC for a smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear program at a KKT point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order sufficient condition supporting local SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\), \(i\in\mathcal E\), and \(c_i(x)\ge0\), \(i\in\mathcal I\), with Lagrangian \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\sum_i\lambda_ic_i(x)\). Let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfy the KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Twice-differentiable finite-dimensional nonlinear programming with the sign convention \(c_i\ge0\) and \(\lambda_i\ge0\) for inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A^*=\{i\in\mathcal I:c_i(x^*)=0\}\) and define the critical cone \[\mathcal C(x^*,\lambda^*)=\left\{d:\begin{array}{l}\nabla c_i(x^*)^Td=0\quad(i\in\mathcal E),\\\nabla c_i(x^*)^Td=0\quad(i\in\mathcal A^*,\ \lambda_i^*>0),\\\nabla c_i(x^*)^Td\ge0\quad(i\in\mathcal A^*,\ \lambda_i^*=0)\end{array}\right\}.\] The SQP second-order sufficient condition is \[d^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)d>0\qquad\text{for every }d\in\mathcal C(x^*,\lambda^*)\setminus\{0\}.\] For an equality-constrained problem this reduces to positive definiteness on the tangent space \(\ker A(x^*)\). Under strict complementarity, the critical cone is the null space of the Jacobian of the equalities and active inequalities, which is precisely the reduced space on which the local SQP quadratic model must have positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SQP second-order sufficient condition requires the Lagrangian Hessian to be strictly positive in every nonzero critical direction. Critical directions are tangent to equalities and positively multiplied active inequalities and point into weakly active inequalities. In the equality-constrained or strictly complementary regime, this is positive definiteness of the reduced Hessian on the active-constraint tangent space.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and all active \(c_i\) are twice differentiable at \(x^*\).
\((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfies primal feasibility, dual feasibility, complementarity, and Lagrangian stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on the critical cone, furnishing the local curvature condition used by SQP.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If columns of \(Z\) span the active-constraint tangent space under strict complementarity, the condition is \(Z^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)Z\succ0\).
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, \(\mathcal C=\{d:A(x^*)d=0\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Together with LICQ, the local equality-constrained KKT matrix is nonsingular.
The condition makes the local SQP quadratic model strictly convex on feasible tangent directions even if the full Lagrangian Hessian is indefinite.
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness on all of \(\mathbb R^n\) is stronger than required.
Without strict complementarity, replacing the critical cone by the null space of all active gradients may impose an unnecessarily strong condition.

notation.meaning: Set of active inequality constraints at \(x^*\).
Critical cone determined by activity and multiplier signs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Q-superlinear convergence of SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\to x^*\) be primal SQP iterates, let \(A_k\) be the active-constraint Jacobian, and define the orthogonal tangent projector \(P_k=I-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}A_k\). Let \(B_k\) be the SQP Hessian model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exact-, quasi-Newton-, and inexact-SQP regimes after the active set and globalization mechanism have stabilized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SQP iterates converge Q-superlinearly to \(x^*\) when \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|}{\|x_k-x^*\|}=0.\] For a convergent equality-constrained quasi-Newton SQP sequence under the standard smoothness, LICQ, and second-order sufficient assumptions, the canonical projected Dennis–Moré condition is \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\left\|P_k\bigl(B_k-\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)\bigr)(x_{k+1}-x_k)\right\|}{\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|}=0.\] This condition characterizes Q-superlinear convergence of the local quasi-Newton SQP iteration. Exact-Hessian SQP has the stronger Q-quadratic local rate. An inexact SQP realization belongs to the superlinear regime when its KKT residual forcing terms vanish rapidly enough that the computed step is asymptotically indistinguishable, relative to its norm, from the exact local SQP step. A globalized realization must eventually accept the full step or an asymptotically equivalent corrected step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP is locally Q-superlinear when each new primal error is a vanishing fraction of the preceding error. For quasi-Newton SQP, the relevant Hessian accuracy is only its projected action along the taken step; the projected Dennis–Moré residual divided by the step norm must tend to zero. Exact Hessians yield quadratic convergence, while inexact solves retain superlinear convergence only when their relative residual forcing tends to zero. Full local steps must eventually be accepted.
assumptions_latex: The iterates converge to a regular KKT pair satisfying LICQ and the second-order sufficient condition.
The active set is fixed locally, or has been correctly identified.
For the projected characterization, \(A_k\) has full row rank and \(B_k\) is symmetric.
Globalization eventually permits \(\alpha_k=1\) or an asymptotically equivalent corrected displacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The error ratio tends to zero; for quasi-Newton SQP this is characterized by the projected Dennis–Moré condition under the stated local assumptions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In a combined primal–dual norm, one may define superlinear convergence by \(\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|/\|z_k-z^*\|\to0\) when multiplier estimates share the same local rate.
special_cases_latex: With \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) and Lipschitz second derivatives, local SQP is Q-quadratic.
Reduced-Hessian approximations satisfying only a two-sided projected condition may yield two-step superlinear rather than one-step Q-superlinear convergence.
immediate_consequences_latex: The full matrix sequence \(B_k\) need not converge to the Lagrangian Hessian; accurate projected action along SQP displacements is sufficient.
boundary_notes: A merely bounded forcing term generally yields at most linear local convergence for inexact solves.
Persistent line-search damping can destroy the stated local superlinear rate even when the Hessian condition holds.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the active-constraint tangent space.
Exact, quasi-Newton, or otherwise approximate Lagrangian Hessian used by SQP.

children.title: Exact-Hessian SQP Local Rate
children.top_down_role: Local fast convergence with exact Lagrangian curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Hessian SQP Local Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once the correct active constraints are fixed, exact-Hessian full-step SQP is Newton's method for the KKT equations and converges quadratically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w=(x,y)\) collect the primal variables and multipliers for the equality constraints formed by the original equalities and the identified active inequalities, and let \(F(w)=(\nabla_xL(x,y),c(x))\). Suppose \(F(w^*)=0\), \(F'\) is locally Lipschitz, and \(F'(w^*)\) is nonsingular. If exact-Hessian SQP solves
\[F'(w_k)\Delta w_k=-F(w_k),\qquad w_{k+1}=w_k+\Delta w_k,\]
then, for \(w_0\) sufficiently close to \(w^*\), the iterates are well defined and
\[\|w_{k+1}-w^*\|\le C\|w_k-w^*\|^2\]
for all sufficiently large \(k\). Thus exact-Hessian, full-step SQP is locally quadratically convergent.
assumptions_latex: The active set is correctly identified and remains fixed locally.
The reduced KKT Jacobian \(F'(w^*)\) is nonsingular.
The second derivatives defining \(F'\) are locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(C>0\) and a neighborhood of \(w^*\) in which \(\|w_{k+1}-w^*\|\le C\|w_k-w^*\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic local rate after reduction to the correctly identified active constraints.

notation.meaning: primal-dual variable for the reduced KKT system

review_flags: confirm the cited iteration is stated with a quadratic primal-dual rate

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact-Hessian SQP Local-Rate Regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(f\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are twice continuously differentiable. Let \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Tc(x)\), let \(z=(x,\lambda)\), and let \(z_*=(x_*,\lambda_*)\) be a KKT point. An SQP iteration solves the equality-constrained quadratic model using \(B_k\) and sets \(z_{k+1}=z_k+s_k\) once full steps are used.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained SQP near a regular KKT point; the definition describes the exact-curvature fast-rate regime and does not itself assert that an arbitrary globalization mechanism enters it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \(\{z_k\}\) is in the exact-Hessian SQP local-rate regime at \(z_*\) if there exists \(k_0\) such that \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) and the undamped SQP step is taken for every \(k\ge k_0\), and \(z_k\to z_*\) with \(\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|\le C\|z_k-z_*\|^2\) for some \(C>0\) and all sufficiently large \(k\). If only \(\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|/\|z_k-z_*\|\to0\) is established, the regime is called exact-Hessian superlinear rather than quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact-Hessian SQP has its canonical local quadratic rate when, from some index onward, its quadratic-program Hessian is exactly \(\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\), full primal-dual SQP steps are taken, the iterates converge to \(z_*\), and their errors satisfy \(\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|\le C\|z_k-z_*\|^2\). The weaker ratio limit \(\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|/\|z_k-z_*\|\to0\) defines the corresponding superlinear regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) eventually and \(\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|=O(\|z_k-z_*\|^2)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Quadratic convergence is equivalently \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|/\|z_k-z_*\|^2<\infty\), provided the denominator is nonzero eventually.
special_cases_latex: For unconstrained minimization, \(m=0\), \(z=x\), and the definition reduces to the local quadratic-rate regime of the full-step Newton method.
immediate_consequences_latex: Quadratic convergence implies \(q\)-superlinear convergence whenever \(z_k\ne z_*\) eventually.
boundary_notes: Exact evaluation of the Lagrangian Hessian does not by itself imply the stated rate; regularity, second-order sufficiency, smoothness, and eventual full-step acceptance are normally needed in a convergence theorem.
The definition excludes quasi-Newton matrices and nonvanishing linear-system residuals.
review_flags: No supplied locator was inspected in this round; an exact SQP local-convergence source supporting the primal-dual quadratic-rate formulation is required.

children.title: Quasi-Newton SQP Local Rate
children.top_down_role: Local fast convergence governed by secant-model quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Newton SQP Local Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stable reduced quasi-Newton model satisfying the Dennis-Moré condition yields superlinear primal-dual SQP convergence after active-set identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w_k=(x_k,y_k)\to w^*\) be full-step SQP iterates after active-set identification, and let \(B_k\) approximate \(\nabla_{xx}^2L(w^*)\). Write \(p_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), and let \(Z^*\) span the null space of the active-constraint Jacobian. If the reduced KKT system is strongly regular, the matrices \(Z^{*T}B_kZ^*\) remain uniformly nonsingular, and the reduced Dennis-Moré condition
\[\frac{\|Z^{*T}(B_k-\nabla_{xx}^2L(w^*))p_k\|}{\|p_k\|}\longrightarrow0\]
holds, then
\[\frac{\|w_{k+1}-w^*\|}{\|w_k-w^*\|}\longrightarrow0.\]
Hence the quasi-Newton SQP primal-dual iterates converge locally superlinearly.
assumptions_latex: The correct active set is fixed and full steps are taken.
The solution satisfies strong regularity and the SQP iterates converge to it.
The reduced Hessian approximations are uniformly nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal-dual error satisfies \(\|w_{k+1}-w^*\|=o(\|w_k-w^*\|)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Superlinear local rate under a reduced Dennis-Moré secant-quality condition.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \(\{z_k\}\) is in the quasi-Newton SQP local superlinear-rate regime at \(z_*\) if \(z_k\to z_*\), full SQP steps are taken eventually, and the reduced Dennis–Moré discrepancy satisfies \(\|Z_*^T(B_k-\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_*,\lambda_*))p_k\|/\|p_k\|\to0\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quasi-Newton SQP is in its local superlinear regime when its symmetric Hessian approximations become exact along the accepted steps in the reduced Dennis–Moré sense, full steps are eventually used, the primal-dual iterates approach \(z_*\), and the error ratio \(\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|/\|z_k-z_*\|\) tends to zero.

special_cases_latex: For \(m=0\), take \(Z_*=I\); the condition becomes the ordinary Dennis–Moré condition for unconstrained quasi-Newton iterations.
immediate_consequences_latex: The rate is faster than every fixed linear contraction factor asymptotically, although it need not be quadratic.
boundary_notes: A secant equation alone is not equivalent to the reduced Dennis–Moré limit.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact SQP Local Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly small KKT residuals give linear convergence; vanishing forcing terms give superlinear convergence; residual-proportional forcing gives quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(w)=0\) be the locally reduced KKT system with nonsingular, locally Lipschitz Jacobian near \(w^*\). Suppose the inexact SQP step satisfies
\[F'(w_k)\Delta w_k=-F(w_k)+r_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|F(w_k)\|,\qquad w_{k+1}=w_k+\Delta w_k.\]
For \(w_0\) sufficiently close to \(w^*\), any uniform bound \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1\) gives local linear convergence. If \(\eta_k\to0\), convergence is superlinear. If additionally \(\eta_k=O(\|F(w_k)\|)\), convergence is quadratic. The same conclusions hold when Hessian-model error is absorbed into \(r_k\) and obeys the corresponding forcing bound.
assumptions_latex: The active constraints are fixed locally and \(F'(w^*)\) is nonsingular.
The computed step satisfies the displayed residual forcing condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local rate is linear for \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1\), superlinear for \(\eta_k\to0\), and quadratic for \(\eta_k=O(\|F(w_k)\|)\).

notation.meaning: linear KKT solve and model residual

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-Controlled Inexact SQP Local Rate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F(z)=(\nabla_xL(x,\lambda),c(x))\) be the KKT residual for a smooth equality-constrained problem, with nonsingular Jacobian \(J_F(z_*)\). An inexact SQP/Newton step \(s_k\) satisfies \(J_F(z_k)s_k=-F(z_k)+r_k\), and \(z_{k+1}=z_k+s_k\) once full steps are taken.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local finite-dimensional primal-dual SQP viewed as an inexact Newton method for a regular KKT system. Both model error and linear-solve residual are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The iterates are in an inexact SQP local-rate regime with forcing sequence \(\{\eta_k\}\) if \(z_k\to z_*\), \(\|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|\) with \(0\le\eta_k<1\), and any approximate KKT matrix \(M_k\) used in place of \(J_F(z_k)\) obeys \(\|(M_k-J_F(z_k))s_k\|\le\delta_k\|F(z_k)\|\). The regime is locally linear when \(\limsup(\eta_k+\delta_k)<1\), superlinear when \(\eta_k+\delta_k\to0\), and quadratic when \(\eta_k+\delta_k=O(\|F(z_k)\|)\), subject to eventual full steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact SQP rate is defined through the residual of its approximate KKT solve and the error in its KKT model. Uniformly subunit relative error defines the linear regime, vanishing combined error defines the superlinear regime, and combined error proportional to the current KKT residual defines the quadratic regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup(\eta_k+\delta_k)<1\) defines the linear regime; \(\eta_k+\delta_k\to0\) defines the superlinear regime; and \(\eta_k+\delta_k=O(\|F(z_k)\|)\) defines the quadratic regime.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(M_k=J_F(z_k)\), one may set \(\delta_k=0\), leaving the standard relative residual condition \(\|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|\).
special_cases_latex: Exact KKT solves have \(r_k=0\); exact KKT models additionally have \(\delta_k=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A fixed forcing bound below one permits only a linear-rate designation without stronger decay information.
boundary_notes: Norm-dependent constants are suppressed, but the asymptotic classifications are invariant under equivalent finite-dimensional norms.
Globalization, constraint degeneracy, and persistent step damping are outside this definition.

notation.meaning: Residual of the computed Newton-KKT step.

review_flags: An inspected source extending inexact Newton forcing terms to the stated SQP KKT model-error decomposition is required.

children.title: Active-Set Identification Regime
children.top_down_role: The local regime in which inequality-constrained SQP stabilizes to an equality-constrained Newton system.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Identification Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ, strict complementarity, and local convergence cause exact SQP subproblems to identify the true active set finitely, after which equality-constrained Newton equations apply.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^*\) be a KKT point with active inequality set \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\). Assume LICQ, strict complementarity \(\nu_i^*>0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal A^*\), and the second-order sufficient condition. For an SQP sequence converging primal-dually to \((x^*,\lambda^*,\nu^*)\), whose QP subproblems are solved exactly and whose local steps are accepted, there exists \(K\) such that
\[\mathcal A_k^{\mathrm{QP}}=\mathcal A^*\qquad\text{for all }k\ge K.\]
Thereafter inactive constraints remain strictly slack, active QP constraints bind, and the SQP step is the Newton step for the equality-constrained KKT system formed from \(h\) and \(g_{\mathcal A^*}\).
assumptions_latex: LICQ, strict complementarity, and SOSC hold at the limiting KKT point.
The primal-dual SQP sequence converges to that point.
Local QP subproblems are solved exactly and accepted steps preserve convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For some finite \(K\), \(\mathcal A_k^{\mathrm{QP}}=\mathcal A^*\) for every \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite local identification under strict complementarity and nondegenerate QP steps.

notation.meaning: active inequality set at the solution
binding inequality set in the kth SQP subproblem

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Active-Set Identification Regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to equalities \(c(x)=0\) and inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), \(i=1,\ldots,q\). At a feasible solution \(x_*\), define \(\mathcal A_* =\{i:g_i(x_*)=0\}\). Let \(\mathcal A_k\) denote the inequality working set imposed as equalities in the SQP subproblem or selected by its multiplier rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local inequality-constrained SQP. The definition concerns finite stabilization of the algorithmic working set, not merely convergence of slacks to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP sequence is in the active-set identification regime at \(x_*\) if there exists a finite \(k_0\) such that \(\mathcal A_k=\mathcal A_*\) for every \(k\ge k_0\), the constraints outside \(\mathcal A_*\) remain strictly inactive locally, and the SQP step is thereafter computed from the equality-constrained Newton-KKT system formed by \(c\) and \(g_{\mathcal A_*}\). Under strict complementarity, the identified set may equivalently be written \(\{i:\lambda_{*,i}>0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite identification occurs when, after some iteration, the SQP working set equals the solution's true active inequality set forever. From that point onward, inactive inequalities remain locally slack and the step is the equality-constrained Newton/SQP step for the original equalities together with the identified active inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists k_0\ \forall k\ge k_0:\ \mathcal A_k=\mathcal A_*\), followed by an equality-constrained Newton-KKT system on \(c\) and \(g_{\mathcal A_*}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With strict complementarity, \(\mathcal A_*=\{i:\lambda_{*,i}>0\}\), so stabilization may be expressed by eventual agreement of the positive-multiplier index set.
special_cases_latex: If \(q=0\), identification is vacuous and the method is equality constrained from the outset.
immediate_consequences_latex: After identification, local rate analysis may be conducted on a fixed-dimensional equality-constrained KKT system.
boundary_notes: Without strict complementarity, weakly active constraints can prevent unique or finite working-set identification.
Approximate equality \(g_i(x_k)\approx0\) is not by itself finite identification.

notation.meaning: Active inequality index set at the solution.

review_flags: The active-set source hint was not inspected for a nonlinear SQP finite-identification statement and its regularity qualifications.

children.title: Full SQP-Step Acceptance
children.top_down_role: The transition from globalized steps to the fast local full-step regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Full SQP-Step Acceptance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If actual merit decrease matches the SQP model asymptotically and the penalty stabilizes, Armijo accepts the unit step eventually.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p_k\) be an SQP direction and \(\Phi_\rho\) an exact-penalty merit function. Suppose \(x_k\to x^*\), the penalty parameter is eventually fixed, the model predicts a decrease \(\Delta m_k<0\), and
\[\Phi_\rho(x_k+p_k)-\Phi_\rho(x_k)=\Delta m_k+o(-\Delta m_k).\]
For an Armijo parameter \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), the unit step satisfies
\[\Phi_\rho(x_k+p_k)-\Phi_\rho(x_k)\le\sigma\Delta m_k\]
for all sufficiently large \(k\). Consequently the line search accepts \(\alpha_k=1\) eventually. The expansion condition may be ensured by a second-order correction or another mechanism that removes the nonlinear-constraint discrepancy responsible for the Maratos effect.
assumptions_latex: The SQP iterates and directions enter the local convergence neighborhood.
The exact-penalty parameter is eventually constant and \(\Delta m_k<0\).
The displayed actual-versus-predicted decrease expansion holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(K\) such that the line search accepts \(\alpha_k=1\) for every \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual unit-step acceptance under accurate local modeling and absence of the Maratos obstruction.
review_flags: confirm eventual unit-step acceptance and correction hypotheses in cited section
