knowledge_statements.statement_title: Eventual Full SQP-Step Acceptance
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(d_k\) be an SQP trial direction and let a globalization rule choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), producing \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). For a merit function \(\Phi_{\rho_k}\), a typical sufficient-decrease test has the form \(\Phi_{\rho_k}(x_k+d_k)\le \Phi_{\rho_k}(x_k)+\sigma D\Phi_{ho_k}(x_k;d_k)\), where \(0<\sigma<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local transition from a line-search or trust-region globalization phase to undamped SQP steps. The definition is independent of the particular sufficient-decrease formula used.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP iteration has eventual full-step acceptance at a limit point \(x_*\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x_*\) and an index \(k_0\) such that, whenever \(k\ge k_0\) and \(x_k\in U\), the unscaled SQP trial step satisfies every acceptance test of the globalization mechanism and the accepted step length is \(\alpha_k=1\). Consequently, \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full SQP-step acceptance means that after a finite index, once the iterates are in a neighborhood of the target KKT point, the raw SQP step passes the globalization test without backtracking or truncation. Thus the accepted step length is exactly \(1\) and the local iteration is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists U\ni x_*,\ \exists k_0\ \forall k\ge k_0:\ x_k\in U\Rightarrow \alpha_k=1\text{ and }x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a backtracking line search whose first trial is \(1\), eventual full-step acceptance is equivalent to eventual termination of every line search at its first trial.
special_cases_latex: In an inactive trust-region regime, the analogous condition is \(\|d_k\|<\Delta_k\) together with acceptance of the untruncated SQP step.
immediate_consequences_latex: Once full steps are accepted, damping no longer masks the intrinsic local rate of the SQP/Newton map.
boundary_notes: Convergence to a KKT point alone does not ensure eventual full steps; merit-function curvature can cause the Maratos effect.
Acceptance of \(\alpha_k\to1\) is weaker than finite eventual equality \(\alpha_k=1\).
review_flags: No inspected source supports the precise neighborhood-and-index formulation for full SQP-step acceptance.

children.title: SQP Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Constraint, subproblem, curvature, and globalization failures affecting Newton-SQP systems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: SQP Failure-Boundary Set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a nonlinear program and an SQP state \(z=(x,\lambda,B,\rho,\Delta)\), let \(Q(z)\) denote the quadratic subproblem, \(K(z)\) its Newton-KKT matrix, and \(G(z)\) the globalization acceptance mechanism. Let \(\mathcal R\) be the set of states where the local SQP step is well-defined, sufficiently descending, stably solvable, and eligible for acceptance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A structural definition collecting distinct loss-of-well-posedness mechanisms. It does not claim that every numerical failure belongs to a single smooth hypersurface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SQP failure-boundary set is \(\partial_F\mathcal R:=\overline{\mathcal R}\setminus\operatorname{int}(\mathcal R)\), with operational failure region \(\mathcal F=\mathcal Z\setminus\mathcal R\). A state lies in \(\mathcal F\) when at least one defining reliability condition fails: the linearized constraints are inconsistent; \(K(z)\) is singular or too ill-conditioned for the required accuracy; the quadratic model lacks the required reduced curvature or is unbounded on its feasible recession cone; multiplier estimates are nonisolated or unstable; or \(G(z)\) persistently rejects or excessively damps otherwise valid local steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP failure boundaries separate states where the quadratic subproblem, KKT solve, curvature model, multiplier estimate, and globalization rule jointly define a reliable accepted step from states where at least one of these requirements fails. The boundary is \(\overline{\mathcal R}\setminus\operatorname{int}(\mathcal R)\), while the complement of \(\mathcal R\) is the operational failure region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_F\mathcal R=\overline{\mathcal R}\setminus\operatorname{int}(\mathcal R)\), where \(\mathcal R\) enforces linearized feasibility, stable KKT solvability, adequate reduced curvature, multiplier stability, and globalization acceptance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\mathcal R=\bigcap_{j=1}^s\mathcal R_j\) is decomposed by reliability requirement, then \(\mathcal F=\bigcup_{j=1}^s(\mathcal Z\setminus\mathcal R_j)\).
special_cases_latex: For equality-constrained exact-Hessian SQP without globalization, only linearized feasibility, KKT regularity, and reduced-curvature conditions remain.
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition distinguishes structural failure of the SQP state from ordinary slow convergence inside \(\mathcal R\).
boundary_notes: The word boundary is used in a state-space sense; individual failure sets may have nonsmooth intersections or nonempty interiors.
Thresholds for excessive conditioning or solve error must be fixed by a numerical reliability specification.
review_flags: This is a synthesized taxonomy-level definition; a source explicitly supporting the combined state-space formulation was not supplied or inspected.
knowledge_statements.title: SQP Failure-Boundary Set

children.title: Inconsistent Linearized Constraints
children.top_down_role: Failure of the SQP subproblem caused by incompatible local constraint models.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Linearized Constraints
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible equations x=0 and x²=0 have mutually inconsistent linearizations at every nonzero nearby iterate, making the ordinary SQP subproblem infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the feasible system on \(\mathbb R\)
\[h_1(x)=x=0,\qquad h_2(x)=x^2=0,\]
whose feasible set is \(\{0\}\). At any iterate \(x_k\ne0\), the SQP linearized constraints require
\[x_k+p=0,\qquad x_k^2+2x_kp=0.\]
The first equation gives \(p=-x_k\), whereas the second gives \(p=-x_k/2\); hence no step satisfies both. Thus the standard equality-constrained SQP subproblem is infeasible even arbitrarily near the feasible solution. Elastic variables, constraint relaxation, or a feasibility-restoration phase are required to produce a step.
assumptions_latex: The SQP subproblem imposes both first-order equality models exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linearized constraint system has no solution \(p\), although the original nonlinear system is feasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A feasible nonlinear equality system whose SQP linearization is infeasible away from its solution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: inconsistency follows directly by solving the two displayed scalar equations
external source desirable for taxonomy alignment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inconsistency of SQP Linearized Constraints
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider nonlinear equalities \(c(x)=0\) and inequalities \(g(x)\le0\). At \(x_k\), the standard SQP constraint model seeks \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)d=0\) and \(g(x_k)+J_g(x_k)d\le0\). Define its linearized feasible set \(\mathcal L_k\) by these relations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional SQP subproblem feasibility. The definition concerns incompatibility of the affine constraint model, independently of the quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The constraints are inconsistent at the SQP linearization point \(x_k\) if \(\mathcal L_k=\varnothing\); equivalently, no step \(d\) simultaneously satisfies all linearized equalities and inequalities. For equality constraints alone, inconsistency is equivalent to \(-c(x_k)
otin\operatorname{range}J_c(x_k)\). A quantitative inconsistency measure is \(
u_k:=\inf_d\max\{\|c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)d\|,\|(g(x_k)+J_g(x_k)d)_+\|\}\), with inconsistency characterized by \(
u_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearized constraints are inconsistent when their affine equality-and-inequality system has no feasible step. With equalities only, this means that \(-c(x_k)\) is outside the range of the equality Jacobian. Equivalently, the least achievable combined linearized violation \(\nu_k\) is strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L_k=\varnothing\), equivalently \(\nu_k>0\); for equalities only, \(-c(x_k)\notin\operatorname{range}J_c(x_k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: By a theorem of alternatives, affine inconsistency can also be certified by suitable dual multipliers separating the incompatible equality and inequality system.
special_cases_latex: If \(J_c(x_k)\) has full row rank and there are no inequalities, the equality linearization is always consistent.
immediate_consequences_latex: The ordinary SQP quadratic subproblem has no feasible solution, irrespective of its Hessian matrix.
Elastic variables, restoration phases, or feasibility relaxations are required to construct a substitute step.
boundary_notes: A feasible but badly conditioned linearized system is not inconsistent.
Nonlinear infeasibility and linearized infeasibility are distinct; either can occur without the other away from a solution.

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the SQP affine constraint model.

review_flags: The definition is standard, but no inspected source locator was available for the mixed equality-inequality formulation and violation measure.

children.title: Maratos Effect
children.top_down_role: Rejection of locally fast SQP steps caused by nonlinear constraint curvature and merit acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Maratos Effect
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order constraint curvature can make a merit function reject an accurate unit SQP step, thereby preventing the expected superlinear local rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be twice continuously differentiable. Suppose \(p_k\to 0\) and the SQP step satisfies \(c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)p_k=0\). Taylor expansion gives
\[c(x_k+p_k)=\tfrac12 D^2c(x_k)[p_k,p_k]+o(\|p_k\|^2),\]
so \(\|c(x_k+p_k)\|=O(\|p_k\|^2)\); this residual is of order \(\Theta(\|p_k\|^2)\) along any subsequence on which the leading curvature term has a corresponding nonzero lower bound. Near a solution, the objective decrease and the exact-penalty contribution \(\rho\|c(x_k+p_k)\|\) can therefore have the same second-order scale. If the positive penalty contribution exceeds the margin permitted by the merit-function sufficient-decrease test, the line search rejects \(\alpha_k=1\) despite the Newton-SQP accuracy of \(p_k\). Repeated rejection can prevent superlinear convergence unless a second-order correction or an appropriate alternative acceptance mechanism is used.
assumptions_latex: \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is twice continuously differentiable near the iterates.
A merit line search penalizes the nonlinear residual \(c(x_k+p_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unit step may fail sufficient decrease because the nonlinear constraint residual is \(O(\|p_k\|^2)\) and can have the same second-order scale as the predicted objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Merit-function rejection caused by second-order constraint violation in a tangential SQP step.
review_flags: authoritative SQP source for the Maratos effect required
exact merit-function rejection inequality depends on the globalization variant

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maratos Effect in Globalized SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(d_k\) be a fast local SQP step near a regular constrained solution \(x_*\), and let \(\Phi_\rho\) be a merit function used by a line search. Although \(d_k\) satisfies the first-order linearized constraints, nonlinear constraint curvature can give \(c(x_k+d_k)=O(\|d_k\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local line-search SQP using a merit acceptance test. The effect is defined by rejection or damping caused by second-order constraint violation, not by a defective Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Maratos effect occurs along an SQP sequence if, arbitrarily close to \(x_*\), the undamped step \(d_k\) has the local fast-step accuracy required by the SQP model but fails the merit-function acceptance test because the \(O(\|d_k\|^2)\) nonlinear constraint residual contributes an adverse second-order term. Consequently, \(\alpha_k=1\) is rejected for infinitely many sufficiently large \(k\), or accepted step lengths remain bounded away from one, preventing realization of the undamped local superlinear or quadratic rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Maratos effect is the persistent rejection or damping of otherwise correct fast local SQP steps near a solution. It arises because a step that satisfies the linearized constraints can leave a second-order nonlinear constraint residual, and the merit function penalizes that residual enough to fail its full-step decrease test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining behavior is recurrent failure of full-step acceptance, \(\alpha_k<1\), attributable to \(c(x_k+d_k)=O(\|d_k\|^2)\) in the merit test despite a locally accurate SQP direction.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a line search testing \(\alpha=1\) first, the effect is equivalently the failure of the full step to satisfy sufficient decrease solely because of second-order constraint curvature.
special_cases_latex: A second-order correction may replace \(d_k\) by \(d_k+s_k^{\mathrm{soc}}\) so that the corrected nonlinear constraint residual is of higher order.
immediate_consequences_latex: Persistent damping can reduce or destroy the local superlinear rate of the underlying SQP step.
boundary_notes: Rejection caused by an inaccurate Hessian, an inexact KKT solve, or a non-descent direction is not, by itself, the Maratos effect.
The effect is tied to the chosen globalization test and may be absent for suitable filters or corrections.
review_flags: No inspected source locator was provided for the precise recurrent-rejection definition of the Maratos effect.

children.top_down_role: Rank loss and unstable multipliers in constrained Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint Degeneracy Coupled to Multiplier Instability
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At a feasible point \(x_*\), collect equality gradients and gradients of active inequalities as columns of \(A_*\). KKT stationarity is \(\nabla f(x_*)+A_*\lambda_*=0\), together with the sign restrictions on inequality multipliers. The associated Newton-KKT matrix is \(K_*=[\begin{smallmatrix}H_*&A_*\\A_*^T&0\end{smallmatrix}]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local constrained Newton/SQP systems at a degenerate active set. The definition separates multiplier instability caused by rank loss from unrelated scaling errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Degeneracy–multiplier instability coupling is present at \(x_*\) when \(\operatorname{rank}A_*<\dim(\lambda)\) and the admissible multiplier set \(\Lambda(x_*):=\{\lambda:\nabla f(x_*)+A_*\lambda=0,\ \lambda_I\ge0\}\) is non-singleton, or the local multiplier solution mapping fails to be single-valued and locally Lipschitz under arbitrarily small perturbations of stationarity and feasibility data. Quantitatively, instability is witnessed when perturbed systems admit multiplier changes \(\Delta\lambda_j\) with \(\|\Delta\lambda_j\|/\|e_j\|\to\infty\) for perturbations \(e_j\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coupling occurs when active constraint gradients lose rank and this loss makes KKT multipliers nonunique or arbitrarily sensitive. Small perturbations of the stationarity or constraint data can then produce multiplier changes whose size divided by the perturbation size becomes unbounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}A_*<\dim(\lambda)\) together with nonuniqueness of \(\Lambda(x_*)\) or failure of a locally Lipschitz multiplier solution map.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Ignoring multiplier sign restrictions, rank loss gives a nonzero \(v\in\ker A_*\); whenever \(\lambda_*+tv\) remains admissible, it yields the same stationarity equation and hence multiplier nonuniqueness.
special_cases_latex: Under LICQ, \(A_*\) has full column rank and the KKT multiplier, when it exists, is unique.
immediate_consequences_latex: The KKT matrix can be singular even when the primal solution is locally isolated.
Multiplier-dependent Hessian estimates and penalty updates may become unstable.
boundary_notes: Rank deficiency does not always imply multiple sign-feasible inequality multipliers; admissibility must be checked.
Large multipliers caused solely by poor numerical scaling are not necessarily constraint degeneracy.

notation.meaning: Matrix of equality and active-inequality gradients.

review_flags: An inspected variational-analysis or nonlinear-programming source is required for the exact multiplier-mapping stability characterization.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Degeneracy Coupled to Multiplier Instability
Constraint-Degeneracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear dependence among the equality and active inequality gradients destroys independent normal coordinates, makes the associated unregularized KKT matrix singular, and can cause multiplier nonuniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_h}\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_g}\) be differentiable at a feasible point \(x^*\), and let \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\). Let \(A^*\in\mathbb R^{(m_h+|\mathcal A^*|)\times n}\) have as its rows the equality gradients \(\nabla h_j(x^*)^T\) and active inequality gradients \(\nabla g_i(x^*)^T\). The constraint system is LICQ-degenerate when
\[\operatorname{rank}(A^*)<m_h+|\mathcal A^*|.\]
Equivalently, there exists \(q\in\mathbb R^{m_h+|\mathcal A^*|}\setminus\{0\}\) such that \(A^{*T}q=0\). Hence the active constraints do not define independent local normal directions, and the unregularized KKT matrix using \(A^*\) is singular. If a KKT multiplier exists and perturbation along \(q\) preserves the sign restrictions on active inequality multipliers, then that multiplier is nonunique. Consequently, standard KKT nonsingularity, unique-multiplier, and strong-regularity conclusions cannot be inferred from the usual LICQ-based theory.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_h}\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_g}\) are differentiable at the feasible point \(x^*\).
The matrix \(A^*\) contains every equality gradient and every active inequality gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: LICQ fails; the unregularized KKT matrix using \(A^*\) is singular, and LICQ-based unique-multiplier and strong-regularity conclusions are unavailable without additional structure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-gradient dependence as the boundary of regular KKT and SQP sensitivity theory.

notation.meaning: nonzero coefficient vector witnessing row dependence
numbers of equality and inequality constraints

multiplier nonuniqueness requires admissibility of the dependence perturbation

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Instability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vanishing constraint-Jacobian singular value leaves the primal solution fixed but makes its Lagrange multiplier grow like the reciprocal singular value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\varepsilon>0\), consider
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^2}-x_2\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad A_\varepsilon x=0,\quad A_\varepsilon=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\varepsilon\end{pmatrix}.\]
The unique feasible primal point is \(x_\varepsilon^*=0\). Stationarity for \(L(x,\lambda)=-x_2+\lambda^TA_\varepsilon x\) gives
\[(0,-1)^T+A_\varepsilon^T\lambda_\varepsilon^*=0,\qquad \lambda_\varepsilon^*=(0,\varepsilon^{-1})^T.\]
Thus \(x_\varepsilon^*\) remains fixed while \(\|\lambda_\varepsilon^*\|\to\infty\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). The multiplier sensitivity is therefore unbounded as the smallest singular value of the constraint Jacobian tends to zero.
assumptions_latex: Multipliers use the displayed Lagrangian sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multiplier norm satisfies \(\|\lambda_\varepsilon^*\|=\varepsilon^{-1}\to\infty\) although \(x_\varepsilon^*=0\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A rank-degenerating equality family with bounded primal solutions and unbounded multipliers.

external source desirable for sensitivity interpretation

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Loss Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP KKT matrix loses rank through dependent active gradients or through a degenerate reduced Hessian on feasible tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the SQP KKT matrix
\[K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix},\]
two independent rank-loss mechanisms are immediate. If \(A\) lacks full row rank, there exists \(y\ne0\) with \(A^Ty=0\), so \(K(0,y)^T=0\). If \(A\) has full row rank but there exists \(d\ne0\) with \(Ad=0\) and \(Hd\in\operatorname{range}(A^T)\), choose \(y\) satisfying \(A^Ty=-Hd\); then \(K(d,y)^T=0\). Thus singularity arises either from dependent active gradients or from degeneracy of the Hessian on the constraint tangent space.
assumptions_latex: The matrix \(A\) is the Jacobian of the equality and fixed active constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either displayed mechanism supplies a nonzero null vector of \(K\), so the Newton-SQP linear system is singular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic mechanisms producing singular equality-constrained SQP KKT systems.

notation.meaning: Lagrangian Hessian or SQP Hessian model

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: both singularity claims follow by direct block multiplication

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Sensitivity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As an equality-constraint gradient vanishes, primal solutions may remain bounded while their unique multipliers diverge, destroying locally bounded multiplier sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider 
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\ \tfrac12(x-1)^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad \varepsilon x=0.
\]
For every \(\varepsilon\ne0\), the unique primal solution is \(x_\varepsilon=0\), and stationarity gives the unique multiplier \(\lambda_\varepsilon=1/\varepsilon\). Hence \(|\lambda_\varepsilon|\to\infty\) as \(\varepsilon\to0\), although \(x_\varepsilon\) remains bounded. At \(\varepsilon=0\), the constraint Jacobian loses rank and the limiting problem has solution \(x_0=1\). Thus no locally bounded multiplier selection extends through this rank-loss boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_\varepsilon=1/\varepsilon\) is unbounded as \(\varepsilon\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank loss can make equality-constrained KKT multipliers arbitrarily sensitive even while each perturbed problem is regular.

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Active Constraints
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly active inequality is binding at a KKT point but has zero multiplier; its presence makes multiplier-based working-set identification ambiguous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the nonlinear program with inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfy the KKT conditions with \(\lambda_i^*\ge0\). An index \(i\) is weakly active at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) precisely when
\[
g_i(x^*)=0\quad\text{and}\quad \lambda_i^*=0.
\]
The weakly active set is \(\mathcal A_0(x^*,\lambda^*)=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0,\ \lambda_i^*=0\}\). If this set is nonempty, strict complementarity fails, so activity cannot be identified solely from positivity of the limiting multipliers.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\in\mathcal A_0(x^*,\lambda^*)\iff g_i(x^*)=0\) and \(\lambda_i^*=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard inequality-constrained KKT meaning, emphasizing failure of strict complementarity and working-set ambiguity.

knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite SQP Subproblems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative curvature along a feasible tangent direction makes an unregularized SQP quadratic subproblem unbounded, so its Newton direction is not a global model minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the feasible SQP quadratic model
\[
q(p)=g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp,\qquad Ap=-c,
\]
where \(B=B^T\). If there exists a nonzero tangent direction \(d\) satisfying \(Ad=0\) and \(d^TBd<0\), then for every feasible \(p_0\), the ray \(p_0+td\) remains feasible and \(q(p_0+td)\to-\infty\) as \(|t|\to\infty\) in at least one orientation. Consequently, the unbounded subproblem has no global minimizer; a constrained Newton direction requires curvature modification, negative-curvature handling, or a trust-region restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ad=0\) and \(d^TBd<0\) imply \(\inf_{Ap=-c}q(p)=-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unregularized equality-constrained SQP model without a trust-region bound.

notation.meaning: feasible tangent direction of negative curvature

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Indefinite SQP Quadratic Subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x_k\), an SQP subproblem minimizes \(q_k(d)=g_k^Td+\tfrac12d^TB_kd\) over an affine linearized feasible set \(\mathcal L_k\), where \(B_k=B_k^T\). Let \(\mathcal R_k\) be the recession cone of \(\mathcal L_k\), and for equality constraints let \(Z_k\) span \(\ker J_c(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional quadratic SQP models. Indefiniteness is assessed on feasible directions, not merely over the full ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SQP subproblem is indefinite if there exists a nonzero feasible direction \(v\) in the tangent or critical direction space such that \(v^TB_kv<0\). For equality constraints this is equivalent to the reduced Hessian \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\) having a negative eigenvalue. If such a direction also belongs to the recession cone \(\mathcal R_k\), then \(q_k(d+tv)\to-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\) after accounting for the linear term, and the subproblem is unbounded below along a feasible ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP quadratic model is indefinite when its Hessian has negative curvature along a nonzero direction allowed by the linearized constraints. In an equality-constrained problem, this is exactly a negative eigenvalue of the reduced Hessian. If a negative-curvature direction is also a feasible recession direction, the quadratic subproblem can be unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists v\ne0\) feasible to first order with \(v^TB_kv<0\); for equalities, \(\lambda_{\min}(Z_k^TB_kZ_k)<0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints, reduced positive semidefiniteness fails precisely when \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\not\succeq0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(B_k\succ0\), the objective is strictly convex on every affine feasible set and no feasible negative-curvature direction exists.
A full-space indefinite \(B_k\) may still be positive definite on the constraint null space.
immediate_consequences_latex: A stationary KKT point of the quadratic model need not be a local minimizer.
Trust regions, curvature modifications, or negative-curvature steps may be needed to define a reliable step.
boundary_notes: Indefiniteness does not automatically imply unboundedness when constraints or a trust region bound the feasible set.
Singularity without negative curvature is a distinct semidefinite degeneracy.

notation.meaning: Null-space basis for the equality-constraint Jacobian.
Recession cone of the linearized feasible set.

children.title: Penalty-Parameter Instability
children.top_down_role: Poor globalization caused by unsuitable merit-penalty behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Parameter Instability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The true KKT multiplier gives a sufficient local exact-penalty threshold under regularity and second-order conditions. If an SQP method updates its penalty from unbounded multiplier estimates, the resulting penalty sequence must also become unbounded and can distort globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and define \(\phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\lVert c(x)\rVert_1\). If an SQP step \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(J_c(x)p=-c(x)\), then
\[
D\phi_\rho(x;p)=\nabla f(x)^Tp-\rho\lVert c(x)\rVert_1.
\]
Let \(x^*\) be a KKT point with multiplier \(\lambda^*\). Under LICQ and a second-order sufficient condition, every \(\rho>\lVert\lambda^*\rVert_\infty\) is a standard sufficient local exactness choice for the one-norm penalty. If an algorithm instead enforces \(\rho_k>\lVert\widehat\lambda_k\rVert_\infty+\delta\) for some \(\delta>0\), then an unbounded sequence of multiplier estimates \(\{\widehat\lambda_k\}\) forces \(\{\rho_k\}\) to be unbounded, which can overemphasize feasibility in merit-function globalization.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
\(x^*\) satisfies the KKT conditions with multiplier \(\lambda^*\), LICQ, and a second-order sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\lVert\widehat\lambda_k\rVert_\infty\to\infty\), then every penalty sequence satisfying \(\rho_k>\lVert\widehat\lambda_k\rVert_\infty+\delta\) obeys \(\rho_k\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-norm merit-function globalization for equality-constrained SQP, distinguishing the true exactness threshold from instability of multiplier-based penalty updates.

notation.meaning: one-norm exact penalty or merit function
KKT multiplier at the local solution
algorithmic multiplier estimate at iteration k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Merit Penalty-Parameter Instability
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an SQP globalization use an exact-penalty merit function \(\Phi_{\rho}(x)=f(x)+\rho V(x)\), where \(V(x)\ge0\) measures constraint violation and \(\rho_k>0\) is updated from iteration data. Let \(d_k\) be the SQP trial direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Line-search or merit-function SQP with an adaptively updated penalty weight. The definition addresses instability of the update and its acceptance consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Penalty-parameter instability occurs when the sequence \(\{\rho_k\}\) fails to enter a finite stable exactness-and-acceptance regime: there is no finite \(\bar\rho\) and index \(k_0\) for which \(\rho_k=\bar\rho\) or remains in a bounded admissible interval for all \(k\ge k_0\), while \(d_k\) is a descent direction for \(\Phi_{\rho_k}\) and locally valid full SQP steps pass the acceptance test. Operational manifestations include \(\rho_k\to\infty\), persistent oscillation across incompatible descent thresholds, or repeated changes that cause excessive emphasis on feasibility or objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The penalty parameter is unstable when it never settles into a bounded range that simultaneously makes the merit function exact enough, makes the SQP direction descending, and permits valid local steps to be accepted. Divergence, persistent oscillation, or repeated threshold-crossing updates are canonical manifestations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There do not exist a bounded admissible interval \(I\subset(0,\infty)\) and \(k_0\) such that \(\rho_k\in I\) for all \(k\ge k_0\) and the required descent and local full-step acceptance conditions both hold.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For monotone nondecreasing updates, instability of the bounded-regime type reduces to \(\rho_k\to\infty\).
special_cases_latex: A fixed parameter \(\rho\) above an appropriate multiplier threshold is the stable exact-penalty special case, provided it also yields the required descent test.
immediate_consequences_latex: Excessive growth can make merit decrease dominated by feasibility and can worsen scaling.
Persistent changes can obstruct eventual full-step acceptance.
boundary_notes: A finite number of penalty updates during globalization is not instability.
The appropriate threshold depends on the merit function, multiplier estimates, and normalization of the violation measure.
review_flags: Penalty-parameter instability is formulated operationally here; no inspected source supports this exact bounded-regime definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Newton-Solve Reliability System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a Newton or KKT step be defined by \(A_ks_k=b_k\), with computed step \(\widehat s_k\). The matrix may be symmetric positive definite, symmetric indefinite, or a saddle-point matrix. Let \(r_k=b_k-A_k\widehat s_k\), and let \(D_{1k},D_{2k}\) be optional nonsingular scaling matrices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision direct or iterative solution of Newton systems. Reliability means that accuracy, structural validity, conditioning, and computational work are jointly monitored.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Newton solve reliability system is a tuple \(\mathscr S_k=(A_k,b_k,\widehat s_k,r_k,\mathcal C_k,\mathcal W_k)\) equipped with acceptance tolerances such that: \(\|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|b_k\|\); a backward-error certificate asserts \((A_k+\Delta A_k)\widehat s_k=b_k+\Delta b_k\) with prescribed relative bounds; structural certificates in \(\mathcal C_k\) verify the required rank, definiteness or inertia; conditioning and scaling estimates determine whether the residual implies adequate forward accuracy; and \(\mathcal W_k\) records factorization, refinement, and reuse work. The computed step is reliable exactly when every required certificate passes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton solve reliability system consists of the linear system, computed step, residual, numerical certificates, and work record. A solve is accepted only when its relative residual and backward error are small enough, the matrix has the required structural properties, conditioning makes the attained accuracy meaningful, and the work/accuracy policy is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Reliable}(\mathscr S_k)\iff\|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|b_k\|\) and all required backward-error, inertia or rank, conditioning, scaling, and work-accuracy certificates in \(\mathcal C_k\) pass.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a nonsingular \(A_k\), a residual certificate can be converted into the a posteriori bound \(\|\widehat s_k-s_k\|\le\|A_k^{-1}\|\|r_k\|\).
special_cases_latex: For a well-conditioned SPD Hessian solved by Cholesky, the structural certificate is positive definiteness and the principal numerical certificate is the scaled residual or backward error.
For KKT systems, an inertia certificate may be required in addition to residual accuracy.
immediate_consequences_latex: A small unscaled residual alone is insufficient when \(A_k\) is badly conditioned or poorly scaled.
boundary_notes: This definition is a system-level contract, not a claim that one solver supplies every certificate.
Tolerance selection depends on the outer Newton forcing requirement.
review_flags: This composite reliability-system definition requires a dedicated numerical-linear-algebra source; none was inspected.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomplete Cholesky preconditioning and its tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines the sparse-factor construction with its computational rationale and principal failure boundary; claims of spectral improvement are approximate and problem dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $A=A^T\succ0$. An incomplete Cholesky preconditioner computes a sparse factor $\widetilde L$—typically with density comparable to the lower triangle of $A$—such that $A\approx\widetilde L\widetilde L^T$, and uses
\[
M=\widetilde L\widetilde L^T,\qquad C=\widetilde L^T,
\]
so that
\[
C^{-T}AC^{-1}=\widetilde L^{-1}A\widetilde L^{-T}\approx I.
\]
The operation $My=r$ is performed by two triangular substitutions without explicitly forming $M$; with comparable sparsity, its cost is of the same order as a sparse product $Ap$. Effectiveness, factor storage and construction cost, and application cost are problem-dependent tradeoffs. Sparsity restrictions can cause loss of positive definiteness, instability, or factorization breakdown; diagonal modification can restore positive definiteness, while permitting more fill can improve robustness at increased storage and per-iteration cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incomplete Cholesky replaces the exact Cholesky factor of a positive-definite matrix by a sparser approximate factor and applies the resulting preconditioner through two triangular solves. If the approximation is good, the transformed matrix is close to the identity and has a favorable spectrum. There is no universally best preconditioner: effectiveness must be balanced against construction, storage, and application costs, often using problem structure. Aggressive sparsity can destroy positive definiteness or cause instability and breakdown; diagonal shifts or additional fill can remedy these failures at extra cost.
assumptions_latex: \widetilde L\text{ is stored sparsely and permits triangular solution}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde L^{-1}A\widetilde L^{-T}\approx I,\quad My=r\text{ is applied by two triangular solves, with robustness governed by diagonal modification and allowed fill.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct Factorization Solver for Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\) be a nonsingular Newton, modified-Hessian, or KKT matrix, and let \(b_k\in\mathbb R^N\). A direct method constructs explicit triangular or orthogonal factors of a permuted and possibly scaled representation of \(A_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional dense or sparse linear algebra. The definition distinguishes factorization-based direct methods from Krylov and other iterative approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A direct Newton-system solver is a map that computes permutations \(P_k,Q_k\), optional scalings \(D_{1k},D_{2k}\), and finite factors \(F_{1k},\ldots,F_{pk}\) satisfying \(P_kD_{1k}A_kD_{2k}Q_k=F_{1k}\cdots F_{pk}\) up to floating-point backward error, and obtains \(\widehat s_k\) from a fixed finite sequence of factor solves and permutations. Canonical instances are Cholesky for SPD matrices, pivoted \(LDL^T\) for symmetric-indefinite matrices, and pivoted \(LU\) or \(QR\) for general matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct Newton-system solver factors a permuted and possibly scaled Newton or KKT matrix into a finite product of structured factors, then computes the step by triangular or orthogonal solves. Its defining feature is factorization of the matrix rather than convergence of an iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_kD_{1k}A_kD_{2k}Q_k=F_{1k}\cdots F_{pk}+E_k\), followed by a finite factor-solve sequence producing \(\widehat s_k\), where \(E_k\) is the factorization backward error.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In exact arithmetic and for nonsingular factors, the returned vector satisfies \(A_k\widehat s_k=b_k\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A_k\succ0\), one may use \(P_kA_kP_k^T=L_kL_k^T\).
For a symmetric KKT matrix, a symmetry-preserving form is \(P_kA_kP_k^T=L_kD_kL_k^T\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Multiple right-hand sides can reuse the factors.
Iterative refinement may improve the computed solution without refactorizing.
boundary_notes: Sparse direct methods may use iterative ordering heuristics, but their numerical solve remains factorization based.
A preconditioner factorization used only inside Krylov iteration is not by itself a direct solve of the Newton system.
review_flags: No inspected source locator supports the full family-level definition spanning SPD, indefinite, and general direct factorizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Newton Factorizations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite Newton matrix has a unique Cholesky factorization, reducing the Newton solve to forward and backward triangular substitutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every symmetric positive-definite matrix \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), there exists a unique lower-triangular matrix \(L\) with positive diagonal such that
\[
H=LL^T.
\]
The Newton equation \(Hp=-g\) is therefore solved by the two triangular systems \(Ly=-g\) and \(L^Tp=y\). Conversely, existence of such an \(L\) implies that \(H\) is symmetric positive definite. No numerical pivoting is required in exact arithmetic, although a symmetric permutation may be applied before sparse factorization to reduce fill.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique lower-triangular \(L\) with positive diagonal satisfying \(H=LL^T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense or sparse Cholesky representation for a symmetric positive-definite Newton matrix.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.3.3 Symmetric Positive Definite Matrices p. 63

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-Definite Newton Factorization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be the symmetric matrix defining a Newton model, with \(H\succ0\). The Newton direction solves \(Hp=-g\). A symmetric permutation \(P\) may be used to reduce sparse fill.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct solution of symmetric positive-definite Newton systems. The defining factorization is Cholesky or its algebraically equivalent \(LDL^T\) form without indefinite pivot blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A positive-definite Newton factorization is a factorization \(PHP^T=LL^T\), where \(P\) is a permutation and \(L\) is nonsingular lower triangular with positive diagonal. Equivalently, \(PHP^T=\widetilde L D\widetilde L^T\), where \(\widetilde L\) is unit lower triangular and \(D\) is positive diagonal. The Newton direction is obtained from \(Ly=-Pg\), \(L^Tw=y\), and \(p=P^Tw\). Existence with strictly positive pivots characterizes positive definiteness in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite Newton factorization is the Cholesky representation of a symmetric positive-definite Newton matrix, possibly after symmetric permutation. It has a nonsingular triangular factor with positive diagonal and solves the Newton equation by two triangular substitutions. The equivalent \(LDL^T\) form has a strictly positive diagonal factor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\succ0\) and \(PHP^T=LL^T\) with \(L_{ii}>0\), equivalently \(PHP^T=\widetilde L D\widetilde L^T\) with \(D_{ii}>0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(H\succ0\) is equivalent to existence of a unique Cholesky factor with positive diagonal for a fixed ordering.
In the unpermuted case, the leading principal minors are positive if and only if Cholesky proceeds with positive pivots.
special_cases_latex: For diagonal \(H\succ0\), \(L=H^{1/2}\).
A sparse permutation changes fill and work but not positive definiteness.
immediate_consequences_latex: The Newton equation has a unique solution.
The direction satisfies \(g^Tp=-p^THp<0\) whenever \(g\ne0\).
boundary_notes: Semidefinite or indefinite matrices do not admit a nonsingular real Cholesky factor of this form.
Modified Cholesky first perturbs an indefinite matrix and therefore factors a modified, not the original, Newton matrix.

notation.meaning: Positive diagonal factor in the unit-lower-triangular form.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric-Indefinite Newton Factorizations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric indefinite Newton or KKT matrix can be solved using a pivoted block LDL-transpose factorization with one-by-one and two-by-two diagonal blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a real symmetric nonsingular matrix \(K\), a symmetric-pivoting direct method computes a permutation \(P\), unit lower-triangular \(L\), and block-diagonal \(D\) such that
\[
P^TKP=LDL^T,
\]
where the diagonal blocks of \(D\) have order one or two. The system \(Kz=b\) is solved by applying \(P\), two triangular substitutions, and independent solves with the blocks of \(D\). Two-by-two pivots permit stable treatment of indefinite matrices for which an unpivoted Cholesky factorization does not exist.
assumptions_latex: Symmetric row and column permutations are permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A pivoted representation \(P^TKP=LDL^T\) yields a direct solve for \(Kz=b\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pivoted Symmetric-Indefinite Newton Factorization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K=K^T\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\) be a nonsingular but not necessarily positive-definite Newton or KKT matrix. Symmetric pivoting preserves symmetry while controlling element growth and avoiding zero or unstable pivots.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct factorization of dense or sparse real symmetric-indefinite systems, including saddle-point KKT matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric-indefinite Newton factorization is a pivoted decomposition \(PKP^T=LDL^T\), where \(P\) is a permutation, \(L\) is unit lower triangular, and \(D\) is block diagonal with nonsingular \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) symmetric pivot blocks. A computed step for \(Ks=b\) is obtained by permuting \(b\), solving with \(L\), solving the block-diagonal system in \(D\), solving with \(L^T\), and undoing the permutation. The inertia of \(K\) equals the sum of the inertias of the blocks of \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric-indefinite Newton factorization is a symmetry-preserving, pivoted \(LDL^T\) decomposition whose diagonal factor contains nonsingular scalar or two-by-two symmetric blocks. It solves Newton and KKT equations through triangular and block-diagonal substitutions and exposes the matrix inertia through those pivot blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(PKP^T=LDL^T\), with unit lower-triangular \(L\) and nonsingular symmetric \(1\times1\) or \(2\times2\) blocks in \(D\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: By congruence, \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(D)\).
special_cases_latex: If all pivot blocks are positive scalars, the factorization reduces to the positive-definite \(LDL^T\) case.
KKT saddle-point matrices typically require both positive and negative inertia.
immediate_consequences_latex: The factors provide both a direct solve and a structural inertia certificate.
Symmetric pivoting can be combined with fill-reducing ordering in sparse systems.
boundary_notes: An unpivoted factorization can fail on a nonsingular indefinite matrix because an intermediate pivot may vanish.
The factorization does not make an indefinite quadratic model convex; it only solves the associated linear system.

notation.meaning: Counts of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues of \(K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Multifrontal Newton Solvers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multifrontal solver assembles dense fronts along an elimination tree, eliminates completed variables, propagates Schur updates, and solves using the stored factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a sparse symmetric matrix \(K\), right-hand side \(b\), and an elimination ordering. Construct the associated elimination tree. At each tree node, assemble a dense frontal matrix from original entries of \(K\) and update matrices received from its children; eliminate the fully summed variables by a Cholesky or pivoted \(LDL^T\) kernel, then pass the resulting Schur-complement update to the parent. After processing the root, solve \(Kz=b\) by forward and backward traversals of the stored frontal factors. Output \(z\) and its residual \(b-Kz\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is sparse and symmetric.
The selected numerical factorization succeeds without an unresolved singular pivot.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(z\) satisfies \(Kz=b\) in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination-tree multifrontal factorization for a sparse symmetric Newton matrix.

notation.meaning: symmetric block factorization used for indefinite fronts

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparse Multifrontal Newton-System Solver
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\) be a sparse Newton or KKT matrix with a chosen elimination ordering. The ordering induces an elimination tree. Each tree node owns a set of fully summed variables and an update set shared with its parent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse direct factorization by frontal assembly. The definition covers Cholesky, \(LDL^T\), and \(LU\)-type multifrontal variants, with pivoting qualifications determined by matrix class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse multifrontal Newton solver is a direct method that represents sparse elimination as an elimination tree and, at each node \(j\), assembles a dense frontal matrix \(F_j\) from original entries of \(A\) and Schur-complement contribution blocks received from child nodes. It factors the fully summed pivot variables in \(F_j\), forms the remaining Schur-complement update \(U_j\), and passes \(U_j\) to the parent. After the tree factorization, forward and backward tree traversals apply the assembled factors to solve \(As=b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multifrontal Newton solver organizes sparse direct elimination as a tree of dense frontal matrices. Each front combines original sparse entries with update matrices from its children, eliminates variables that are fully assembled there, and sends a Schur-complement contribution to its parent. Tree traversals then apply the resulting factors to the Newton right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_j=A_j+\sum_{i\in\operatorname{child}(j)}E_{ij}^TU_iE_{ij}\) is assembled and partially factored at every tree node, and its Schur update \(U_j\) is propagated to the parent before factor solves produce \(s\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The method is an elimination-tree organization of sparse Gaussian, Cholesky, or symmetric-indefinite elimination in which algebraically related updates are accumulated into dense fronts.
special_cases_latex: For \(A\succ0\), each front may use Cholesky without numerical pivoting.
For symmetric-indefinite KKT matrices, fronts may require threshold pivoting and delayed pivots.
immediate_consequences_latex: Independent child subtrees can be processed concurrently before their parent front is assembled.
Fill-reducing orderings change front sizes and therefore memory and arithmetic work without changing the exact solution.
boundary_notes: Multifrontal describes the assembly and elimination organization, not a particular ordering or pivot rule.
Delayed pivots can alter the predicted front structure and memory use.
An incomplete multifrontal factorization used only as a preconditioner is not an exact direct multifrontal solve.

notation.meaning: Dense frontal matrix at elimination-tree node \(j\).
Schur-complement contribution passed to the parent front.
Index-assembly operator embedding a child update into its parent front.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton Factorization Lifecycle
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K_k\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\) be the nonsingular Newton or KKT coefficient matrix at outer iteration \(k\), and let \(b_{k,j}\) denote one or more right-hand sides associated with that matrix.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional direct solution of a sequence of related Newton systems; the definition covers symbolic reuse, numerical refactorization, factor updates, and repeated triangular solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Newton factorization lifecycle is a sequence of states \(\mathcal F_k=(P_k,\mathcal S_k,F_k,\sigma_k)\), where \(P_k\) is a permutation, \(\mathcal S_k\) is stored symbolic sparsity information, \(F_k\) is a numerical factor satisfying a declared relation such as \(P_k^TK_kP_k=L_kD_kL_k^T\), and \(\sigma_k\) records validity. For each transition \(k\to k+1\), an action \(a_k\in\{\mathrm{reuse},\mathrm{update},\mathrm{refactor}\}\) is selected. Reuse retains applicable symbolic or numerical data; update constructs factors for \(K_{k+1}=K_k+U_kV_k^T\) without a complete new factorization; refactor recomputes numerical factors, and possibly ordering, from \(K_{k+1}\). A factor state is accepted for a right-hand side \(b_{k,j}\) only if the recovered solution \(z_{k,j}\) satisfies the prescribed residual test \(\|K_kz_{k,j}-b_{k,j}\|\leq\tau_{k,j}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton factorization lifecycle is the mathematical state process that creates, reuses, updates, tests, and eventually replaces factors of related Newton matrices. Its state records a permutation, symbolic sparsity data, numerical factors, and their validity. At each matrix change it chooses reuse, a structured factor update, or fresh factorization. A state is valid for a solve only when the resulting vector satisfies the specified residual tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(K_k\) is square and nonsingular whenever a solve is certified.
Every numerical factor state declares an exact or approximate factorization relation and a residual tolerance \(\tau_{k,j}\geq0\).
A reuse action is permitted only for data whose structural or numerical validity conditions remain true for \(K_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifecycle defines both the algebraic representation used to solve each system and the transition rule governing which factorization work is retained across related systems.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a fixed \(K_k\) and several right-hand sides, the lifecycle may retain one factorization and perform separate forward, block-diagonal, and backward substitutions for every \(b_{k,j}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(K_{k+1}=K_k\), numerical factors may be reused exactly.
If only numerical values change while the sparsity pattern is fixed, \(P_k\) and \(\mathcal S_k\) may be reused while numerical factors are recomputed.
immediate_consequences_latex: The marginal cost of an additional right-hand side is the cost of substitutions and residual checking rather than a second factorization.
Accumulated updates may be discarded and replaced by a fresh factorization when storage, solve time, or stability limits are exceeded.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert that low-rank updates are stable or cheaper for every matrix sequence.
Approximate preconditioners without a direct factorization relation belong to a different lifecycle unless they are explicitly included as factor states.

notation.meaning: Newton or KKT coefficient matrix at outer iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Newton Factorization Updates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When sparsity is unchanged, retain the symbolic elimination structure and update only numerical factors, reverting to full analysis if stability checks fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given successive sparse Newton matrices \(K_k\) with a common structural nonzero pattern, first compute a fill-reducing permutation and symbolic elimination structure for \(K_0\). At iteration \(k+1\), retain that symbolic data, insert the numerical entries of \(K_{k+1}\), and recompute only the numerical Cholesky or pivoted \(LDL^T\) factors. Solve \(K_{k+1}z_{k+1}=b_{k+1}\) with the new numerical factors and accept them only if the pivot and residual tests prescribed by the solver succeed; otherwise perform a fresh symbolic analysis and factorization.
assumptions_latex: Successive matrices have the same structural sparsity pattern.
The retained ordering remains admissible for the chosen numerical factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful numerical refactorization produces factors for \(K_{k+1}\) without repeating symbolic analysis.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numeric refactorization across Newton iterations while retaining valid symbolic elimination data.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The symbolic/numeric separation is standard in sparse direct solvers, but reuse under pivoted indefinite factorization and the proposed fallback tests depend on the solver and pivoting strategy. No authoritative source or specific solver contract is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton Factorization Reuse
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse is exact when the Newton matrix is unchanged; otherwise it is admissible only when the resulting step meets the chosen residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let stored factors represent a nonsingular matrix \(K_j\). Exact reuse at iteration \(k
eq j\) is valid when \(K_k=K_j\); only the triangular solves must be repeated for the new right-hand side \(b_k\). If \(K_k\neq K_j\), using the stored factors defines an inexact step \(z_k\), which is acceptable under a prescribed relative-residual condition
\[
\lVert K_kz_k-b_k\rVert\le\eta_k\lVert b_k\rVert,
\]
with \(0\le\eta_k<1\). Failure of this condition requires factor updating, iterative correction, or refactorization.
assumptions_latex: The stored factors solve systems with nonsingular \(K_j\).
A norm and forcing tolerance \(\eta_k\in[0,1)\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reuse is accepted only if \(K_k=K_j\) or \(\lVert K_kz_k-b_k\rVert\le\eta_k\lVert b_k\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and residual-controlled reuse of a previously computed Newton factorization.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Exact reuse for an unchanged matrix is correct, but the relative linear residual condition is presented as a generally sufficient acceptance condition for an inexact Newton step. Its validity depends on the nonlinear residual, norm, scaling, conditioning, and forcing-term framework, none of which is sourced here.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Factorization Modifications
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-k matrix change can reuse an existing factorization through a small dense correction, provided the correction matrix is nonsingular and required definiteness survives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, and define a rank-at-most-\(r\) modification \(\widehat K=K+UV^T\), where \(U,V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\). If \(I_r+V^TK^{-1}U\) is nonsingular, then
\[
\widehat K^{-1}=K^{-1}-K^{-1}U\bigl(I_r+V^TK^{-1}U\bigr)^{-1}V^TK^{-1}.
\]
Thus solves with \(\widehat K\) can reuse solves with the factors of \(K\) plus an \(r\)-dimensional dense solve. A downdate is invalid when the small matrix becomes singular or when required definiteness is lost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed low-rank inverse formula represents \((K+UV^T)^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-action formula underlying rank-k updates or downdates of Newton factorizations.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The displayed Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury formula is correct, and representation is a defensible kind for the leaf. However, the cited sections concern symmetric rank-one and rank-two optimization updates and do not clearly support the general UV-transpose rank-r inverse formula, factorization reuse claim, or definiteness-sensitive downdate boundary. A directly supporting locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton Refactorization Triggers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refactor when residual, pivot stability, inertia, sparsity, or working-set tests show that retained factors no longer represent a reliable Newton solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_k\) be computed from reused or modified factors for the current Newton system \(K_kz=b_k\). Refactorization is triggered if at least one prescribed test fails:
\[
\lVert K_kz_k-b_k\rVert>\eta_k\lVert b_k\rVert,
\]
the factorization encounters an unacceptable pivot or pivot-growth indicator, the computed inertia differs from the inertia required by the Newton or KKT model, or a sparsity-pattern or working-set change invalidates the symbolic structure. If no trigger occurs, the factors may remain in service for that solve; otherwise fresh analysis or numerical factorization is required.
assumptions_latex: The solver specifies residual, pivot, and inertia acceptance tests.
\(K_k\) and \(b_k\) define the current Newton system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any failed acceptance test triggers fresh numerical or symbolic factorization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational conditions requiring replacement of reused or incrementally modified Newton factors.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the appropriate content kind, but the listed residual, pivot-growth, inertia, sparsity, and working-set triggers form a solver- and model-dependent policy. No source defines the acceptance thresholds or the required inertia for the relevant Newton/KKT model.

children.title: KKT Decomposition Families
children.top_down_role: Algebraic decompositions exposing full-space, Schur-complement, and null-space structures.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT Decomposition Family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(C\in\mathbb S^m_+\), and \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&-C\end{bmatrix}\). Consider \(K\begin{bmatrix}p\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}r_d\\r_p\end{bmatrix}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric KKT systems. Invertibility requirements are stated separately for each decomposition rather than imposed on the whole family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A KKT decomposition family is the collection of algebraically equivalent solution representations obtained from the block system by: (i) full-space factorization of \(K\); (ii) dual or constraint-space reduction, when \(H\) is invertible, using \(S_d=C+AH^{-1}A^T\); (iii) primal reduction, when \(C\) is invertible, using \(S_p=H+A^TC^{-1}A\); and (iv) null-space reduction for \(C=0\), using a basis \(Z\) satisfying \(AZ=0\). A member of the family is defined only when its pivot block and reduced matrix are nonsingular. Each member must recover a pair \((p,y)\) satisfying both original block equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KKT decomposition family consists of the full coupled factorization and the standard block-elimination or null-space representations of the same saddle-point equations. The dual reduction eliminates primal variables through the curvature block, the primal reduction eliminates multiplier variables through a nonsingular lower block, and the null-space reduction restricts curvature to feasible directions. Each representation is valid only under its own invertibility conditions and must recover a solution of the original KKT system.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(C\) are symmetric and the block dimensions are conformable.
For the dual reduction, \(H\) and \(S_d=C+AH^{-1}A^T\) are nonsingular.
For the primal reduction, \(C\) and \(S_p=H+A^TC^{-1}A\) are nonsingular.
For the null-space reduction, \(C=0\), \(A\) has full row rank, and \(Z\) has full column rank with \(\mathcal R(Z)=\mathcal N(A)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admissible family member is an exact coordinate or elimination representation of the same equation \(K(p,y)^T=(r_d,r_p)^T\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The Schur reductions are block Gaussian eliminations, while the null-space reduction is elimination by the direct-sum coordinates \(p=Yp_Y+Zp_Z\).
special_cases_latex: For equality-constrained quadratic programming, \(C=0\), so the full-space, dual Schur, and null-space members are standard; the primal Schur member requires regularization or another nonzero lower block.
immediate_consequences_latex: Different members can have different dimensions, conditioning, sparsity, and factorization requirements despite being algebraically equivalent.
boundary_notes: The definition does not claim numerical equivalence in finite precision.
Generalized Schur complements with singular pivot blocks are excluded.

notation.meaning: basis matrix for the null space of A

children.title: Full-Space KKT Factorization
children.top_down_role: Direct treatment of the coupled saddle-point matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Space KKT Factorization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-space method directly factors the coupled primal-dual KKT matrix. Full row rank of the constraint Jacobian and nonsingularity of the Hessian reduced to a genuine null-space basis guarantee a unique primal step and multiplier correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), with \(m\le n\). The primal step \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) and multiplier correction \(\delta\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) for the quadratic model with constraint \(Ap=-c\) satisfy
\[
\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}p\\\delta\lambda\end{pmatrix}
=-\begin{pmatrix}g\\c\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Assume that \(A\) has full row rank, and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\). If \(Z^THZ\) is nonsingular, then the full-space KKT matrix is nonsingular and uniquely determines \((p,\delta\lambda)\). A symmetric-indefinite \(LDL^T\) factorization can solve this coupled system directly without explicitly forming a Schur complement or constructing a reduced system.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, with \(m\le n\).
\(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) has full column rank and satisfies \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\) is nonsingular and uniquely determines \((p,\delta\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled saddle-point representation and direct factorization for an equality-constrained Newton or SQP step.

notation.meaning: Lagrangian Hessian or symmetric Hessian approximation
full-column-rank basis matrix for the null space of A

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Space Symmetric-Indefinite KKT Factorization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\in\mathbb S^{n+m}\) be nonsingular, with \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct finite-dimensional treatment of the complete coupled equality-constrained KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A full-space KKT factorization is a symmetric-indefinite factorization \(P^TKP=LDL^T\), where \(P\) is a permutation matrix, \(L\) is unit lower triangular, and \(D\) is block diagonal with nonsingular \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) pivot blocks. For a right-hand side \(b=(r_d,r_p)^T\), the full-space solution is defined by \(Lq=P^Tb\), \(Dw=q\), \(L^Tu=w\), and \((p,y)^T=Pu\). The factorization is full-space because neither primal nor multiplier variables are algebraically eliminated before factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-space KKT factorization applies a symmetric-indefinite factorization directly to the entire coupled saddle-point matrix. Symmetric permutations control stability and sparsity; the diagonal factor can contain one-by-one or two-by-two pivot blocks. A KKT solution is recovered by permutation, forward substitution, block-diagonal solution, backward substitution, and inverse permutation.
assumptions_latex: Every pivot block of \(D\) is nonsingular.
The permutation and pivoting rule preserve the declared factorization relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered vector satisfies \(K(p,y)^T=b\) and is unique.
equivalent_formulations_latex: An unsymmetric \(LU\) factorization can solve the same system, but it is not the symmetry-preserving full-space factorization defined here.
special_cases_latex: If \(m>0\) and the reduced Hessian is positive definite, the KKT matrix remains indefinite and therefore ordinary Cholesky factorization of \(K\) is inapplicable.
immediate_consequences_latex: One factorization can serve multiple right-hand sides through repeated substitutions.
The inertia of \(K\) can be read from the pivot-block inertia of \(D\).
boundary_notes: A singular KKT matrix requires rank-revealing or regularized methods outside this definition.
The definition does not prescribe a particular sparse ordering or pivot threshold.

notation.meaning: permutation, unit lower-triangular factor, and block-diagonal pivot factor

children.title: Primal Schur-Complement Reduction
children.top_down_role: Reduction emphasizing primal variables and curvature blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Schur-Complement Reduction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the constraint-space variable produces an equivalent system in the primal step, followed by direct multiplier recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given the symmetric block system
\[H p+A^{\mathsf T}y=r_p,\qquad Ap-Dy=r_d,\]
where \(p,r_p\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y,r_d\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(D\) is nonsingular, elimination of \(y\) gives the primal Schur-complement equation
\[\bigl(H+A^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}A\bigr)p=r_p+A^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}r_d.\]
Every solution \(p\) of this reduced equation determines
\[y=D^{-1}(Ap-r_d),\]
and the resulting pair \((p,y)\) solves the original block system. Conversely, the primal component of every solution of the block system satisfies the reduced equation.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(D\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) are symmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) solves the primal Schur system and \(y=D^{-1}(Ap-r_d)\) exactly when \((p,y)\) solves the block system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block elimination of constraint-space variables when the constraint regularization block is invertible.

notation.meaning: Primal curvature and constraint regularization blocks.

children.title: Dual Schur-Complement Reduction

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Schur-Complement Reduction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the primal step gives an equivalent multiplier-space system, after which the primal step is recovered by solving with the curvature block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the block equations
\[H p+A^{\mathsf T}y=r_p,\qquad Ap-Dy=r_d,\]
where \(p,r_p\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(y,r_d\in\mathbb R^m\), assume that \(H\) is nonsingular. Eliminating \(p=H^{-1}(r_p-A^{\mathsf T}y)\) yields
\[\bigl(D+AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\bigr)y=AH^{-1}r_p-r_d.\]
After solving this dual Schur-complement equation, recover
\[p=H^{-1}(r_p-A^{\mathsf T}y).\]
These operations are algebraically reversible, so the reduced equation and recovery formula are equivalent to the original block system. For equality-constrained KKT equations, \(D=0\).
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\) solves the dual Schur system and \(p=H^{-1}(r_p-A^{\mathsf T}y)\) exactly when \((p,y)\) solves the block system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-space reduction obtained by eliminating the primal variable through an invertible curvature block.

children.title: Null-Space KKT Reduction
children.top_down_role: Reduction to tangent-space curvature with separate feasibility recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space KKT Reduction
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible particular step plus a null-space correction reduces the KKT equations to the Hessian restricted to tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[Hp+A^{\mathsf T}y=r_p,\qquad Ap=r_d,\]
where \(p,r_p\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y,r_d\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(A\) has full row rank. Let the columns of \(Z\) span \(\ker A\), and choose any \(p_F\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ap_F=r_d\). Writing \(p=p_F+Zq\) and projecting the first equation gives
\[Z^{\mathsf T}HZq=Z^{\mathsf T}(r_p-Hp_F).\]
If \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) is nonsingular, this equation uniquely determines \(q\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\). The multiplier is then the unique \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying
\[A^{\mathsf T}y=r_p-Hp.\]
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) has full column rank and \(AZ=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) is nonsingular, the reduced equation and recovery equations determine the unique KKT solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained KKT reduction to tangent-space curvature, with separate feasibility and multiplier recovery.

children.title: Newton-Solve Certificates
children.top_down_role: Computable evidence used to accept, reject, or refine approximate Newton directions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton-Solve Certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Kz=b\) be a Newton or KKT system, let \(\widehat z\) be a computed direction, and let \(\mathcal A\) denote the acceptance requirements of the outer method.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable, finite-dimensional evidence for accepting or refining an approximate deterministic Newton-system solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Newton-solve certificate is a finite tuple \(\mathcal C(\widehat z)=(r,\rho,\iota,\chi)\) together with explicit acceptance predicates, where \(r=K\widehat z-b\) is the linear residual, \(\rho\) is a declared scaled or preconditioned residual measure, \(\iota\) is optional curvature or inertia information, and \(\chi\) is optional constraint-compatibility information. It is valid for \(\mathcal A\) precisely when every required predicate is computable from the supplied data and holds, for example \(\|r\|\leq\eta\|b\|\), \(\rho\leq\eta_P\), a prescribed inertia count, or \(\|A\widehat p-r_p\|\leq\tau_c\). Omitted components cannot certify requirements that depend on them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton-solve certificate is a collection of computable quantities and explicit tests attached to an approximate Newton direction. It can contain the ordinary residual, a solver-adapted residual, curvature or inertia data, and a measure of linearized constraint compatibility. The direction is certified only for the acceptance requirements whose corresponding tests are present and satisfied.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient matrix, right-hand side, computed direction, norms, scalings, and thresholds are explicitly identified.
Each certificate component is evaluated for the same system and computed direction.
All required acceptance predicates in \(\mathcal A\) are stated quantitatively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If all predicates required by \(\mathcal A\) hold, \(\widehat z\) is accepted as an approximate solution at the declared tolerances; otherwise the certificate requires rejection or further refinement.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A forcing-term certificate for an inexact Newton step is the special case \(\|K\widehat z-b\|\leq\eta\|b\|\).
special_cases_latex: For an unconstrained Newton equation, compatibility and multiplier-related components are absent.
For a direct KKT solve, residual and inertia information may both be extracted from the factorization workflow.
immediate_consequences_latex: Certificate validity is relative to declared tolerances and does not imply exact solution.
Different outer methods may accept the same direction under different predicates.
boundary_notes: A small residual alone does not certify favorable curvature, descent, or good forward error for an ill-conditioned matrix.
The definition does not prescribe how a failed certificate must be repaired.

children.title: Linear Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence of approximate satisfaction of a Newton system.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The computed residual certifies approximate equation satisfaction; converting it to a solution-error guarantee additionally requires conditioning information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a linear Newton system \(Ks=b\) and computed step \(\widehat s\), form the residual
\[r=b-K\widehat s.\]
The inequality
\[\lVert r\rVert\leq \tau_{\mathrm{abs}}+\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\bigl(\lVert K\rVert\lVert\widehat s\rVert+\lVert b\rVert\bigr)\]
is a directly verifiable normwise residual certificate. If \(K\) is nonsingular, it additionally implies the forward-error bound
\[\lVert\widehat s-s\rVert\leq \lVert K^{-1}\rVert\,\lVert r\rVert.\]
Thus a small residual certifies a small solution error only when the inverse amplification is controlled.
assumptions_latex: \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) is a compatible vector and induced matrix norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed residual test certifies normwise approximate satisfaction, and nonsingularity yields \(\lVert\widehat s-s\rVert\leq\lVert K^{-1}\rVert\lVert r\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise evidence that a computed step approximately solves a finite-dimensional Newton system.
