knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Residual Certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^N\), and \(\widehat z\in\mathbb R^N\) be an approximate solution of \(Kz=b\). Fix a norm and tolerances \(\tau_{\rm abs},\tau_{\rm rel}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise backward-residual evidence for finite-dimensional approximate Newton or KKT solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linear residual is \(r=K\widehat z-b\). An absolute-relative linear residual certificate is the inequality \(\|r\|\leq\tau_{\rm abs}+\tau_{\rm rel}\|b\|\). For an inexact Newton equation \(H_kp=-g_k\), the standard forcing certificate is \(r_k=H_k\widehat p_k+g_k\) and \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|g_k\|\), where \(0\leq\eta_k<1\). The certificate records the norm, scaling, and evaluated residual value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear residual certificate measures how closely a computed vector satisfies the stated linear system. It consists of the residual and a quantitative absolute-relative inequality. For an inexact Newton step, the usual form bounds the residual of the Newton equation by a forcing parameter times the gradient norm.
assumptions_latex: \(K\), \(b\), and \(\widehat z\) refer to the same assembled or matrix-free linear operator.
The norm and tolerances are fixed before interpreting the certificate.
For the relative-only test, \(b\neq0\) unless exact residual zero is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Satisfaction of the inequality certifies approximate equation satisfaction at the declared normwise tolerance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(\tau_{\rm abs}=0\) and \(b\neq0\), the certificate is \(\|K\widehat z-b\|/\|b\|\leq\tau_{\rm rel}\).
special_cases_latex: For exact arithmetic and zero tolerances, the certificate reduces to \(K\widehat z=b\).
For \(H_kp=-g_k\), choosing \(\tau_{\rm rel}=\eta_k\) gives the standard inexact Newton termination condition.
immediate_consequences_latex: The residual is directly computable using one application of \(K\) if it has not already been maintained by the solver.
boundary_notes: A small residual is not a forward-error bound unless conditioning information is also available.
Recursive iterative-solver residuals may drift from the explicitly recomputed residual in finite precision.

children.title: Preconditioned Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Residual evidence interpreted in a solver-adapted metric.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse-preconditioner norm certifies the residual as a bounded functional in the solver-adapted metric, but does not alone bound Euclidean error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be symmetric positive definite and let \(r=b-K\widehat s\). The computable quantity
\[\lVert r\rVert_{M^{-1}}=\sqrt{r^{\mathsf T}M^{-1}r}\]
defines a preconditioned residual certificate. For any correction \(e\), the residual action satisfies
\[|r^{\mathsf T}e|\leq \lVert r\rVert_{M^{-1}}\lVert e\rVert_M.\]
Hence \(\lVert r\rVert_{M^{-1}}\leq\eta\) certifies that the equation defect, regarded as a linear functional on the \(M\)-normed correction space, has norm at most \(\eta\). This certificate depends on the selected preconditioner and is not by itself a Euclidean forward-error bound.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\) is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert r\rVert_{M^{-1}}\leq\eta\) implies \(|r^{\mathsf T}e|\leq\eta\lVert e\rVert_M\) for every \(e\in\mathbb R^N\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual evidence measured in the dual norm induced by a positive-definite preconditioner.

notation.meaning: Symmetric positive-definite preconditioner defining the solver metric.
Residual of the computed linear solve.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The dual-norm identity and functional interpretation are mathematically precise and the certificate kind fits, but no source with an inspectable locator is supplied for this nontrivial preconditioned-residual formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioned Residual Certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Kz=b\) have residual \(r=K\widehat z-b\), and let \(M\in\mathbb S_{++}^N\) be a declared symmetric positive-definite preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SPD-preconditioned residual metrics for finite-dimensional Newton equations or SPD reduced KKT systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The \(M^{-1}\)-preconditioned residual norm is \(\|r\|_{M^{-1}}=(r^TM^{-1}r)^{1/2}\). A preconditioned residual certificate is \(\|r\|_{M^{-1}}\leq\tau_{\rm abs}+\tau_{\rm rel}\|b\|_{M^{-1}}\), together with identification of \(M\) and the procedure used to apply \(M^{-1}\). Equivalently, if \(M=C^TC\) with nonsingular \(C\), then \(\|r\|_{M^{-1}}=\|C^{-T}r\|_2\), the Euclidean residual norm of the symmetrically transformed system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preconditioned residual certificate assesses the residual in the metric induced by a positive-definite preconditioner. It bounds the square root of \(r^TM^{-1}r\), with absolute and relative scaling. Factoring \(M=C^TC\) shows that this is the ordinary residual norm in transformed coordinates.
assumptions_latex: The same fixed \(M\) is used for the residual and right-hand-side scaling in the reported test.
Applications of \(M^{-1}\) are defined accurately enough for the declared certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality certifies small residual in the solver-adapted \(M^{-1}\) metric.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For preconditioned CG, \(r^TM^{-1}r=r^Ty\) where \(My=r\).
special_cases_latex: With \(M=I\), the certificate becomes the Euclidean residual certificate.
immediate_consequences_latex: The scalar \(r^TM^{-1}r\) is normally available from a preconditioned CG iteration.
boundary_notes: Changing \(M\) changes the metric and therefore the meaning of a fixed numerical tolerance.
For indefinite KKT preconditioners, \(r^TM^{-1}r\) need not define a norm and is outside this definition.

children.title: Curvature-Inertia Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Evidence about positive, null, or negative curvature in Newton and KKT matrices.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Curvature-Inertia Certificate System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(Z\) span \(\mathcal N(A)\), and let \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic inertia information from symmetric factorizations and its interpretation as curvature on the constraint tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric matrix \(B\), define \(\operatorname{inertia}(B)=(n_+(B),n_-(B),n_0(B))\). A curvature-inertia certificate system for the equality-constrained Newton model consists of: (i) the inertia of the reduced Hessian \(H_R=Z^THZ\), classifying positive, negative, and null tangent curvature; and (ii) a symmetry-preserving factorization \(P^TKP=LDL^T\) whose pivot-block inertia supplies \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)\). The certificate is consistent when \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(H_R)+(m,m,0)\). Positive tangent curvature is certified by \(\operatorname{inertia}(H_R)=(n-m,0,0)\), equivalently \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A curvature-inertia certificate records how many positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues occur in the reduced Hessian and in the full KKT matrix. A symmetric-indefinite factorization exposes the full-system inertia through its pivot blocks. For full-row-rank equality constraints, the KKT inertia equals the reduced-Hessian inertia plus one positive and one negative direction per constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has full column rank and spans \(\mathcal N(A)\).
The factorization is symmetry preserving and its pivot blocks are classified using a declared numerical threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate distinguishes positive, null, and negative tangent curvature and checks its consistency with the full KKT inertia.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Positive definiteness of \(Z^THZ\) is equivalent to the KKT inertia \((n,m,0)\) under the stated rank condition.
special_cases_latex: For \(m=0\), the system reduces to the inertia certificate of the unconstrained Hessian.
immediate_consequences_latex: A zero inertia count detects singularity in exact arithmetic.
A negative eigenvalue of \(Z^THZ\) certifies a feasible negative-curvature direction.
boundary_notes: Finite-precision classification requires a tolerance for near-zero pivots.
Inertia does not quantify eigenvalue magnitudes or conditioning.

notation.meaning: numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues
reduced Hessian on the null space of A

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible direction and its Rayleigh quotient certify positive, nearly zero, or negative curvature along that direction only.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be symmetric and let \(A\) be the active-constraint Jacobian. A nonzero vector \(d\) satisfying \(Ad=0\) is a tangent direction. Its Rayleigh quotient
\[\rho_H(d)=\frac{d^{\mathsf T}Hd}{d^{\mathsf T}d}\]
is directly checkable. The inequalities \(\rho_H(d)\geq\gamma>0\), \(|\rho_H(d)|\leq\varepsilon\), and \(\rho_H(d)\leq-\gamma<0\) respectively certify positive, near-null, and negative curvature along \(d\). A single positive-direction certificate does not establish positive definiteness on the entire tangent space; that requires a uniform lower bound over all nonzero tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sign and magnitude of \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd/(d^{\mathsf T}d)\) certify directional curvature within the linearized constraint tangent space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A tangent direction and its quadratic form certify curvature of the reduced Hessian.

notation.meaning: Rayleigh quotient of the curvature matrix along the direction.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 Negative Curvature Direction Method p. 147

knowledge_statements.title: Inertia Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact symmetric indefinite factorization certifies matrix inertia from its diagonal blocks; for a full-row-rank equality-constrained KKT matrix, the target inertia is equivalent to positive definiteness of the reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a real symmetric matrix \(K\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\), suppose an exact symmetric factorization
\[P^{\mathsf T}KP=LDL^{\mathsf T}\]
is available, where \(P\) and \(L\) are nonsingular and \(D\) is symmetric block diagonal. Sylvester's law of inertia gives
\[\operatorname{In}(K)=\operatorname{In}(D).\]
Thus the eigenvalue signs of the one-by-one and two-by-two diagonal blocks of \(D\) certify the counts of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues of \(K\). For the equality-constrained KKT matrix
\[\mathcal K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\]
where \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, let the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) span \(\ker A\). Then
\[\operatorname{In}(\mathcal K)=(n,m,0)\]
if and only if \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) is positive definite.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and \(L\) are nonsingular and \(D\) is symmetric block diagonal.
For the KKT interpretation, \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) has full column rank and its columns span \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{In}(K)=\operatorname{In}(D)\); for \(\mathcal K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), \(\operatorname{In}(\mathcal K)=(n,m,0)\) exactly when \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Congruence-factorization evidence for the numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues.

notation.meaning: Triple of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts.
Permutation or congruence factor, nonsingular triangular factor, and symmetric block-diagonal factor.
Basis matrix for the null space of the constraint Jacobian.
Target KKT inertia with n positive, m negative, and no zero eigenvalues.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-dual inertia test and Hessian regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to a primal-dual interior-point coefficient matrix when rank deficiency does not independently force singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K(\delta) denote the primal-dual matrix obtained by replacing \nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L with \nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L+\delta I. The desired positive-definiteness condition is certified when \operatorname{In}(K(0))=(n+m,l+m,0). If this inertia is not obtained and \Sigma\succ0, successively increase \delta>0 until \operatorname{In}(K(\delta))=(n+m,l+m,0). The inertia may be read from a symmetric-indefinite factorization. A rank deficiency that itself makes the primal-dual matrix singular requires an additional regularization mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a problem with n variables, l equalities, and m inequalities, the primal-dual matrix has the desired curvature when it has n+m positive, l+m negative, and no zero eigenvalues. Its inertia can be obtained from a symmetric-indefinite factorization. If the signature is wrong, shift the Lagrangian Hessian by an increasingly large positive multiple of the identity until the signature is obtained; a separate regularization is needed if rank deficiency independently causes singularity.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm E})=l\ \text{or, more generally, no rank deficiency precludes nonsingularity}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{In}(K(\delta))=(n+m,l+m,0)\quad\text{for a sufficiently large accepted shift }\delta.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Curvature Detection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small Ritz value together with a small Ritz residual certifies an eigenvalue of the reduced Hessian near zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) be the symmetric reduced Hessian. For a unit vector \(q\), define
\[\theta=q^{\mathsf T}Bq,\qquad w=Bq-\theta q.\]
There exists an eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(B\) satisfying
\[|\lambda-\theta|\leq\lVert w\rVert_2.\]
Consequently, if \(|\theta|+\lVert w\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon\), the pair \((q,\theta)\) certifies the presence of reduced curvature within \([ -\varepsilon,\varepsilon ]\). Exact null curvature is certified when \(w=0\) and \(\theta=0\); otherwise the certificate only establishes proximity to singularity at the stated tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z\) form an orthonormal basis for \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(|\theta|+\lVert w\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon\), then \(B\) has an eigenvalue \(\lambda\) with \(|\lambda|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ritz residual evidence that the reduced curvature operator has an eigenvalue near zero.

notation.meaning: Reduced Hessian on the constraint null space.
Ritz value associated with the unit vector q.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The Ritz residual eigenvalue enclosure is a nontrivial spectral theorem central to the certificate, but no source or inspectable locator is provided. An authoritative numerical linear algebra source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Curvature Classification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangent direction with a negative Rayleigh quotient certifies failure of reduced positive semidefiniteness; a margin quantifies the negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be symmetric and \(A\) the active-constraint Jacobian. A pair \((d,\gamma)\) with \(d\neq0\), \(Ad=0\), and \(\gamma>0\) is a strict negative-curvature certificate when
\[d^{\mathsf T}Hd\leq-\gamma\lVert d\rVert_2^2.\]
It proves that the reduced Hessian is not positive semidefinite and that its smallest eigenvalue is at most \(-\gamma\). If only \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd<0\) is established, negative curvature is still certified but without a quantitative separation margin. A vector violating \(Ad=0\) does not classify tangent-space curvature unless its constraint incompatibility is included in a perturbation bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd\leq-\gamma\lVert d\rVert_2^2\) implies \(\lambda_{\min}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)\leq-\gamma\) for any orthonormal null-space basis \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of negative reduced curvature by tangent feasibility and a separated Rayleigh quotient.

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis for the null space of A.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 Negative Curvature Direction Method p. 147

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Reliability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Computed curvature signs transfer to the intended matrix when perturbation is smaller than its spectral gap; at or beyond the gap scale, signs can change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a computed factorization or curvature calculation is exact for \(K+E\), where \(K\) is the intended symmetric matrix. Let
\[\delta=\min_i|\lambda_i(K)|.\]
If \(\lVert E\rVert_2<\delta\), eigenvalue signs cannot cross zero, so \(K\) and \(K+E\) have the same inertia. If \(\lVert E\rVert_2\geq\delta\), inertia transfer is not guaranteed: for any \(\delta>0\), take
\[K=\operatorname{diag}(\delta,2\delta),\qquad E=\operatorname{diag}(-2\delta,0).\]
Then \(\min_i|\lambda_i(K)|=\delta\), \(\lVert E\rVert_2=2\delta\), and one positive eigenvalue becomes negative. Thus a computed inertia or curvature sign is reliable only when backward error is smaller than a certified spectral separation from zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert E\rVert_2<\delta\) preserves inertia, whereas perturbations of size at least \(\delta\) can change a curvature classification.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-gap boundary for transferring computed curvature or inertia certificates to the intended matrix.

notation.meaning: Backward perturbation associated with the computed certificate.
Minimum absolute eigenvalue of the intended matrix.

children.title: Constraint-Compatibility Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Compatibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linearized-constraint residual certifies compatibility; under full row rank it also bounds distance to the affine feasible-step set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For linearized constraints \(Ap=r_d\), define the compatibility residual
\[r_c=Ap-r_d.\]
The inequality
\[\lVert r_c\rVert_2\leq\tau_c\]
is a directly verifiable absolute compatibility certificate. If \(A\) has full row rank, the distance from \(p\) to the affine feasible set \(\mathcal F=\{z:Az=r_d\}\) is
\[\operatorname{dist}_2(p,\mathcal F)=\lVert A^{\dagger}r_c\rVert_2\leq\lVert A^{\dagger}\rVert_2\tau_c.\]
Thus a small constraint residual implies a nearby compatible direction only when the constraint Jacobian is sufficiently well conditioned.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert Ap-r_d\rVert_2\leq\tau_c\) and \(\operatorname{dist}_2(p,\mathcal F)\leq\lVert A^{\dagger}\rVert_2\tau_c\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual evidence that a computed direction satisfies the linearized constraint equations.

notation.meaning: Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of the constraint Jacobian.
Affine set of exactly compatible directions.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let the linearized constraint equation for a Newton direction \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) be \(Ap=r_p\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Fix a norm and tolerances \(\tau_c^{\rm abs},\tau_c^{\rm rel}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality or active-constraint linearizations; nonlinear feasibility beyond the linearized model is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constraint-compatibility residual is \(c_p=A\widehat p-r_p\). An approximate direction \(\widehat p\) has a constraint-compatibility certificate when \(\|c_p\|\leq\tau_c^{\rm abs}+\tau_c^{\rm rel}\|r_p\|\). If \(r_p=0\), this certifies approximate tangency to \(\mathcal N(A)\). In a null-space representation \(\widehat p=Y\widehat p_Y+Z\widehat p_Z\) with \(AZ=0\), the same certificate is \(\|AY\widehat p_Y-r_p\|\leq\tau_c^{\rm abs}+\tau_c^{\rm rel}\|r_p\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint-compatibility certificate measures whether a computed Newton direction satisfies the required linearized constraint equation. Its residual is \(A\widehat p-r_p\), bounded by declared absolute and relative tolerances. For a homogeneous equation it measures tangency; in null-space coordinates only the feasibility component contributes.
assumptions_latex: \(A\), \(r_p\), and \(\widehat p\) correspond to the same linearization point and sign convention.
The norm and tolerances are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Satisfaction of the inequality certifies compatibility with the linearized constraint structure at the stated tolerance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a KKT system whose second block equation is \(A\widehat p=r_p\), the compatibility residual is exactly the second block of the full linear residual.
special_cases_latex: If the current iterate is feasible and the desired step is tangent, \(r_p=0\) and exact compatibility is \(A\widehat p=0\).
If \(AY\widehat p_Y=r_p\) is solved exactly, every value of \(\widehat p_Z\) preserves exact linearized compatibility.
immediate_consequences_latex: A full residual certificate implies a compatibility bound whenever the chosen product norm controls its constraint block.
boundary_notes: Linearized compatibility does not by itself imply feasibility of a full nonlinear trial step.
Rank deficiency of \(A\) does not invalidate the residual definition, but may affect attainable tolerances.

notation.meaning: required right-hand side of the linearized constraint equation

children.title: Newton Work-Accuracy Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Implementation-level work models for balancing derivative, factorization, preconditioning, and inner-iteration costs.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton Work-Accuracy Interface
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), let \(K_kz=b_k\) be the Newton system, let \(\eta_k\in[0,1)\) be the requested relative residual accuracy, and let \(q_k\) encode a permitted solver configuration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic accounting interface linking requested inner accuracy to derivative, setup, factorization, preconditioning, iteration, and storage work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Newton work-accuracy interface is a pair of maps \((\mathcal W_k,\mathcal E_k)\). The work map assigns \(\mathcal W_k(q_k,\eta_k)=(W_k^{\rm der},W_k^{\rm setup},W_k^{\rm fact},W_k^{\rm prec},W_k^{\rm iter},S_k)\), whose entries count derivative products, assembly or symbolic setup, numerical factorization, preconditioner construction, inner iterations or triangular solves, and peak storage. The accuracy map returns \(\mathcal E_k(q_k,\eta_k)=\|K_k\widehat z_k-b_k\|/\|b_k\|\). The interface is feasible when \(\mathcal E_k(q_k,\eta_k)\leq\eta_k\). Total scalar work is obtained only after declaring nonnegative unit costs and applying them to the work vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton work-accuracy interface is a formal accounting map. Given a solver configuration and requested tolerance, it reports separate derivative, setup, factorization, preconditioner, inner-iteration, solve, and storage costs, together with the achieved relative residual. A configuration is feasible when it meets the requested accuracy; scalar cost comparisons require explicit weights.
assumptions_latex: Work counters and their units are fixed consistently across compared configurations.
The achieved residual is evaluated for the same Newton system and norm.
Any amortized reuse horizon is included in \(q_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface defines the feasible work set \(\{\mathcal W_k(q,\eta):\mathcal E_k(q,\eta)\leq\eta\}\) for comparing Newton-system solution strategies at a common accuracy.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With unit-cost vector \(c\geq0\), scalar work is \(c^T\mathcal W_k(q_k,\eta_k)\).
special_cases_latex: For a matrix-free method, \(W_k^{\rm fact}=0\) while derivative-product and inner-iteration counts dominate.
For a reused direct factorization, factorization work may be amortized over several right-hand sides.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two solvers are not work-comparable until their achieved accuracies and cost units are aligned.
boundary_notes: The definition is an accounting object, not a complexity theorem.
Wall-clock time, communication, and energy require additional declared counters or weights.

children.title: Outer-Inner Work Balance
children.top_down_role: The allocation of work between nonlinear iterations and linear-system refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Inner Work Balance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set each inner linear-solve tolerance through a forcing term: fixed, vanishing, and residual-proportional terms support linear, superlinear, and quadratic outer convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonlinear equations \(F(x)=0\), choose an approximate Newton step \(s_k\) satisfying
\[\lVert F(x_k)+F'(x_k)s_k\rVert\leq\eta_k\lVert F(x_k)\rVert,\qquad 0\leq\eta_k<1.\]
Under local nonsingularity and Lipschitz continuity of \(F'\), a uniform bound \(\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\) permits local linear convergence; \(\eta_k\to0\) permits superlinear convergence; and \(\eta_k=O(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert)\) permits quadratic convergence. Inner refinement beyond the forcing scale does not improve the convergence order guaranteed by that scale, so the largest forcing term compatible with the desired outer rate balances work.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuously differentiable near a root \(x_*\).
\(F'(x_*)\) is nonsingular and \(F'\) is locally Lipschitz.
The iterates remain in the local convergence neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The asymptotic behavior of \(\eta_k\) determines whether the inexact Newton iteration can attain linear, superlinear, or quadratic local convergence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact-Newton forcing terms link linear-solve accuracy to attainable outer convergence rates.

notation.meaning: Approximate Newton step at the kth outer iteration.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The stated inexact-Newton forcing-term rate distinctions are nontrivial convergence results and no authoritative source with a theorem, section, or page locator is supplied. Principle is an appropriate content kind, but the rate claims require sourcing.

children.title: Derivative-Product Work
children.top_down_role: Work measured through Jacobian-vector, Hessian-vector, and finite-difference products.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Product Work
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An m-step matrix-free Newton solve using one derivative product per Krylov iteration has m core derivative products. With cached-base forward differences, those products require m additional residual evaluations, apart from initialization or verification overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be differentiable at \(x_k\), set \(F_k=F(x_k)\) and \(J_k=F'(x_k)\), and consider the Newton equation \(J_kp=-F_k\). Suppose a Krylov method terminates after \(m_k\) iterations and applies \(J_k\) exactly once per iteration. The core derivative-product work is then exactly \(m_k\) Jacobian-vector products, excluding any products used for initialization or independent residual verification. For optimization with \(F=\nabla f\), these products are Hessian-vector products \(v\mapsto \nabla^2f(x_k)v\). If each product is instead approximated by \(J_kv\approx [F(x_k+h_kv)-F(x_k)]/h_k\), where \(h_k>0\) and \(F(x_k)\) is cached, the \(m_k\) products require exactly \(m_k\) additional evaluations of \(F\), again excluding initialization and verification work.
assumptions_latex: The Krylov recurrence applies \(J_k\) exactly once per iteration.
For finite-difference products, \(h_k>0\) and \(F(x_k)\) is cached.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\mathrm{deriv},k}=m_kW_{Jv}\), and the cached forward-difference implementation uses \(m_k\) additional residual evaluations, excluding initialization and verification overhead.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts derivative-operator products in a matrix-free inexact Newton solve.

notation.meaning: residual F(x_k) at the current iterate
Jacobian F'(x_k) of the residual map at the current iterate
cost of one Jacobian-vector or derivative-operator product

children.title: Factorization Storage Complexity
children.top_down_role: Storage, fill, ordering, and reuse costs for assembled Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Factorization Storage Complexity
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\) be sparse and let a direct method compute \(P^TKP=LDL^T\) or \(PK=LU\). Write \(\operatorname{nnz}(B)\) for the number of stored nonzeros of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit sparse direct factorizations, including ordering data and reusable symbolic or numerical state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The factorization storage complexity is the number of scalar and index locations required to retain the factors and auxiliary state. For symmetric-indefinite storage, define \(S_{LDL}=\operatorname{nnz}(L)+\operatorname{nnz}(D)+S_P+S_{\rm sym}+S_{\rm upd}\); for unsymmetric storage define \(S_{LU}=\operatorname{nnz}(L)+\operatorname{nnz}(U)+S_P+S_{\rm sym}+S_{\rm upd}\). The fill count is \(F_{LDL}=\operatorname{nnz}(L)+\operatorname{nnz}(D)-\operatorname{nnz}_{\triangle}(K)\), with an analogous \(LU\) definition. Storage complexity for a matrix family is the asymptotic or instance-wise value of these quantities under a declared ordering, pivoting rule, and update/reuse policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factorization storage complexity counts the nonzeros retained in triangular and pivot factors plus permutations, symbolic analysis, and accumulated update data. Fill is the factor storage beyond the corresponding stored entries of the original matrix. The measure is meaningful only after the ordering, pivoting, and reuse policy are declared.
assumptions_latex: The sparse storage convention and treatment of symmetric duplicates are fixed.
Permutation, symbolic, and update storage are included or explicitly reported as zero.
The ordering and numerical pivoting policy are identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quantities \(S_{LDL}\), \(S_{LU}\), and their fill counts define storage requirements for assembled Newton-system factorizations.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A fill ratio may be reported as \((\operatorname{nnz}(L)+\operatorname{nnz}(D))/\operatorname{nnz}_{\triangle}(K)\) when the denominator is nonzero.
special_cases_latex: For dense Cholesky, triangular factor storage is \(N(N+1)/2\) scalars.
A matrix-free Krylov method has no direct-factor storage but requires separate vector and preconditioner storage accounting.
immediate_consequences_latex: Reordering can change fill and storage without changing the represented linear system.
Accumulated factor updates can increase storage until a fresh factorization discards them.
boundary_notes: Nonzero count does not capture cache behavior or byte differences among scalar and index types.
Numerical pivoting can create fill beyond symbolic predictions.

notation.meaning: number of stored nonzero entries in B

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Fill Growth
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symbolic elimination adds fill edges between remaining neighbors; each fill edge becomes one additional strict-lower factor entry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be structurally symmetric, let \(G(A)=(V,E)\) be its undirected sparsity graph, and let \(P_\pi AP_\pi^T=LDL^T\) be a symbolic factorization without numerical cancellation. During elimination in ordering \(\pi\), connect every pair of currently uneliminated neighbors of the eliminated vertex. If \(F_\pi\) is the set of newly created edges, then the strict lower triangle of \(L\) has \(|E|+|F_\pi|\) structural nonzeros. Consequently, factor storage grows from the original graph by exactly \(|F_\pi|\) lower-triangular entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{nnz}(L)=n+|E|+|F_\pi|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact symbolic fill count for a symmetric sparse factorization under a fixed ordering.

notation.meaning: undirected sparsity graph of the symmetric matrix
fill edges generated by ordering π

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Memory Demand
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor memory is linear in factor nonzeros, with additional linear storage for indices, diagonal data, permutations, pivots, and workspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a stored symmetric factorization \(PAP^T=LDL^T\), let \(s_L=\operatorname{nnz}(L)\), count the unit diagonal of \(L\), and let \(b\) be the scalar byte width. Storing numerical values of \(L\) and diagonal \(D\) requires \(b(s_L+n)\) bytes when \(D\) is diagonal. A compressed sparse representation additionally uses one index per stored entry and \(n+1\) column pointers, so with index width \(b_i\) its principal storage is \(b(s_L+n)+b_i(s_L+n+1)\) bytes, excluding permutation arrays, pivot metadata, workspace, and allocator overhead.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is diagonal and \(L\) is stored sparsely by columns.
Each numerical scalar uses \(b\) bytes and each index uses \(b_i\) bytes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{\mathrm{principal}}=b(s_L+n)+b_i(s_L+n+1)=\Theta(s_L+n)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage bound for sparse symmetric factors and their symbolic metadata.

notation.meaning: number of stored entries in the triangular factor
byte widths of numerical scalars and indices

knowledge_statements.title: Ordering Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an arrowhead pattern, center-first elimination causes quadratic fill, while leaf-first elimination causes none, showing strong ordering sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the symmetric arrowhead sparsity graph on \(n\) vertices: one center is adjacent to each of \(n-1\) leaves, and no leaves are mutually adjacent. Eliminating the center first makes all leaves a clique and creates \(\binom{n-1}{2}\) fill edges. Eliminating every leaf before the center creates no fill. Hence two permutations of the same matrix pattern can yield respectively \(\Theta(n^2)\) and \(\Theta(n)\) factor nonzeros. Sparse-factor storage and arithmetic complexity therefore cannot be determined from \(\operatorname{nnz}(A)\) alone; they depend essentially on the elimination ordering.
assumptions_latex: The matrix has the stated structurally symmetric arrowhead pattern.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{nnz}(L_{\mathrm{center\ first}})=\Theta(n^2)\) while \(\operatorname{nnz}(L_{\mathrm{leaves\ first}})=\Theta(n)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demonstrates asymptotically different fill under two orderings of one sparsity graph.

notation.meaning: symbolic triangular factor under the specified ordering
number of graph vertices and matrix order

knowledge_statements.title: Reuse Storage Costs
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symbolic reuse keeps linear-size structural metadata; caching q numerical factors needs storage proportional to q times the factor nonzeros.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k\) share a fixed sparsity pattern and permutation with earlier Newton matrices. Reusing only symbolic analysis retains the elimination tree, permutation, and factor index structure, requiring \(\Theta(n+s_L)\) persistent index storage, while new numerical factors still require \(\Theta(s_L)\) scalar storage. Reusing a complete numerical factorization retains an additional \(\Theta(s_L)\) scalars and is exact only while the coefficient matrix is unchanged. If \(q\) complete factors are cached simultaneously, persistent factor-value storage is \(\Theta(qs_L)\); sequential refactorization with one buffer remains \(\Theta(s_L)\).
assumptions_latex: All matrices have a common structural pattern and ordering.
Each cached factor has \(s_L\) stored entries up to constant-factor pivot data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{\mathrm{symbolic}}=\Theta(n+s_L)\), \(M_{\mathrm{one\ numeric}}=\Theta(s_L)\), and \(M_{\mathrm{q\ cached}}=\Theta(qs_L)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental storage needed to reuse symbolic or numerical factorization state.

notation.meaning: stored entries in one factor structure
number of simultaneously cached numerical factors

children.title: Preconditioner Investment Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between preconditioner construction, reuse, and iterative acceleration.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preconditioner Investment Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(M_\theta\) be a preconditioner selected from a family indexed by construction parameter \(\theta\), and suppose it is reused for \(R\geq1\) linear solves. Let \(j_i(\theta)\) be the iterations needed for solve \(i\) to meet its declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Amortized deterministic comparison of preconditioner construction, storage, application, reuse, and iterative acceleration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The preconditioner investment tradeoff is the minimization or comparison of the amortized work functional \[W_{\rm avg}(\theta,R)=\frac{W_{\rm build}(\theta)}{R}+W_{\rm maintain}(\theta,R)+\frac1R\sum_{i=1}^R j_i(\theta)\bigl(W_{K,i}+W_{M^{-1}}(\theta)\bigr),\] subject to every solve attaining its prescribed residual tolerance and to \(S_M(\theta)\leq S_{\max}\). Here construction and maintenance are investments, while fewer iterations represent acceleration. A choice \(\theta_1\) dominates \(\theta_2\) for horizon \(R\) if it uses no more average work and storage and is strictly better in at least one of them at equal achieved accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The preconditioner investment tradeoff compares the up-front cost of building a preconditioner, its maintenance and storage, its per-application cost, its reuse horizon, and the Krylov iterations it saves. Construction cost is amortized over the solves that reuse it. Comparisons require equal residual accuracy, and dominance means no greater amortized work or storage with a strict improvement in at least one measure.
assumptions_latex: Each \(M_\theta\) is applicable to the chosen iterative method and linear systems.
All compared solves use the same accuracy criterion.
Build, maintenance, operator-application, and preconditioner-application costs use compatible units.
The reuse horizon \(R\) and storage budget \(S_{\max}\) are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The functional defines when additional preconditioner investment is repaid by reduced iterative work over the declared reuse horizon.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For one solve, set \(R=1\); for a fixed matrix with many right-hand sides, construction cost is divided across all right-hand sides.
special_cases_latex: The identity preconditioner has negligible construction cost but may have a large iteration count.
Allowing more incomplete-factor fill usually raises build, storage, and application costs while potentially reducing iterations.
immediate_consequences_latex: A preconditioner can be unattractive for one solve yet beneficial when reused many times.
Iteration count alone is insufficient to rank preconditioners with different setup and application costs.
boundary_notes: The definition does not guarantee monotonic iteration reduction as investment increases.
Parallel communication and robustness costs require additional terms if material.

notation.meaning: number of solves sharing the investment

source_refs.locator: Section 5.3, “Practical Preconditioners”: tradeoff among effectiveness, construction and storage cost, and cost of solving with the preconditioner; incomplete-Cholesky fill discussion

review_flags: The amortized functional and dominance relation formalize the qualitative tradeoffs stated by the source.
knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Investment Tradeoff

source_witnesses.locator: Section 5.3, “Practical Preconditioners”: tradeoff among effectiveness, construction and storage cost, and cost of solving with the preconditioner; incomplete-Cholesky fill discussion

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Setup Cost
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioning costs one setup plus one application per inner iteration; reuse divides setup work across solves but retains its storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear Newton system \(A_kp=b_k\), let construction of a preconditioner \(M_k\) cost \(S_k\) work units and \(B_k\) bytes of retained storage. If a preconditioned iterative solve performs \(m_k\) iterations, each requiring one application of \(M_k^{-1}\) costing \(C_k\), then preconditioner-specific work for that solve is \(S_k+m_kC_k\). When the same preconditioner is reused across \(r\) solves with iteration counts \(m_1,\ldots,m_r\), its average setup contribution per solve is \(S_k/r\), while retained storage remains \(B_k\) throughout the reuse interval.
assumptions_latex: The constructed preconditioner remains stored during all \(r\) solves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\mathrm{prec}}=S_k+C_k\sum_{j=1}^{r}m_j\), with average setup cost \(S_k/r\) and retained memory \(B_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates one-time construction, per-application, and retained-storage costs.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The accounting model and complexity-bound role fit the setup-cost leaf, but the record supplies no source or inspectable locator for its preconditioner construction, application, reuse, and retained-storage model. An authoritative iterative-methods or preconditioning reference is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Amortization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Setup is amortized when accumulated iteration savings exceed setup work; the reuse count must exceed setup cost divided by per-solve savings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compare an unpreconditioned solve requiring \(m_0\) iterations of cost \(C_0\) each with a preconditioned solve requiring \(m_1\) iterations of base cost \(C_0\) plus preconditioner-application cost \(C_M\). If setup cost \(S\) is shared by \(r\) solves having the same cost profile, then preconditioning reduces total work exactly when \(r m_0C_0>S+r m_1(C_0+C_M)\). Equivalently, amortization occurs when the per-solve saving \(\Delta=m_0C_0-m_1(C_0+C_M)\) is positive and \(r>S/\Delta\).
assumptions_latex: The compared solves have the same stopping criterion and base iteration cost.
Setup is performed once and reused for \(r\) solves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta>0\) and \(r>S/\Delta\) are necessary and sufficient for strict work reduction in this model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Break-even condition for paying setup cost through reduced iteration work.

notation.meaning: incremental cost of one preconditioner application
work saved per solve before setup allocation

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The break-even algebra is correct within the stated homogeneous cost model, and condition is the appropriate content kind. However, no source or inspectable locator supports the selected amortization model, so the record cannot pass source review.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Reuse Horizons
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reuse horizon extends through the last solve for which cumulative iteration savings still recover the original setup cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let one preconditioner, built at solve zero with setup cost \(S\), be reused for successive systems. For reuse step \(j\), let \(m_j\) be the preconditioned iteration count, \(m_j^{(0)}\) the count without it, \(C_0\) the base iteration cost, and \(C_M\) its application cost. The profitable reuse horizon is the largest integer \(r^*\) such that cumulative saved work covers setup: \[r^*=\max\left\{r\geq 1:\sum_{j=1}^{r}\left[m_j^{(0)}C_0-m_j(C_0+C_M)\right]\geq S\right\}.\] If no such integer exists, the horizon is zero.
assumptions_latex: All solves use a common stopping criterion.
Iteration counts include degradation caused by preconditioner staleness.
Setup cost is charged once at the start of the reuse interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reusable preconditioner is cumulatively profitable through exactly the indices satisfying the displayed inequality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the maximal profitable lifetime of a fixed preconditioner under operator drift.

notation.meaning: preconditioned and unpreconditioned iteration counts at reuse step j

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: No authoritative source is supplied, and the proposed maximum need not exist when the reuse sequence is unbounded. Moreover, cumulative profitability need not be monotone in r, so the displayed set does not generally define a horizon through which every prefix remains profitable. A sourced definition must specify a finite candidate interval or a prefix-persistence condition and address an empty or unbounded feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceleration Payoff Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioning pays off only when reduced iteration work exceeds both setup and application overhead; fewer iterations alone do not guarantee savings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Over \(r\) Newton systems, let the baseline require iteration counts \(m_j^{(0)}\) at cost \(C_0\) per iteration. Let a preconditioner require setup work \(S\), iteration counts \(m_j\), and incremental application cost \(C_M\) per iteration. The preconditioner has a positive acceleration payoff precisely when \[S+(C_0+C_M)\sum_{j=1}^{r}m_j<C_0\sum_{j=1}^{r}m_j^{(0)}.\] Thus a lower iteration count alone is insufficient: setup and application overhead must be smaller than the saved baseline iteration work. Equality is the break-even boundary.
assumptions_latex: Both strategies enforce the same accuracy and stopping criterion.

children.title: Numerical Reliability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scaling, conditioning, rank, pivoting, and stale-information effects on Newton solves.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Operational reliability regimes for a finite-dimensional Newton solve
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is the Newton or KKT matrix, \(b\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\) is nonsingular, \(s=A^{-1}b\), and \(\widehat s\) is a computed step with residual \(r=b-A\widehat s\). Positive diagonal matrices \(D_r,D_c\) scale equations and variables. A computed factorization is represented by \(\widehat F\), its reconstruction \(\mathcal A(\widehat F)\), and backward perturbation \(E=\mathcal A(\widehat F)-A\). The unit roundoff is \(u\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is an operational, tolerance-parameterized definition for dense finite-dimensional exact Newton systems solved in floating-point arithmetic. It classifies reliability rather than prescribing a particular factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tolerances \(\tau_b,\tau_f,\tau_s,\tau_q>0\), define \[\eta_b=\frac{\|r\|_2}{\|A\|_2\|\widehat s\|_2+\|b\|_2},\qquad \eta_F=\frac{\|E\|_2}{\|A\|_2},\qquad \kappa_s=\inf_{D_r,D_c\succ0\ {m diagonal}}\kappa_2(D_rAD_c),\qquad q=u\kappa_s.\] The solve is in the reliable regime when \(\eta_b\leq\tau_b\), \(\eta_F\leq\tau_f\), \(q\leq\tau_q\), and every structural decision used by the solver—numerical rank, pivot acceptance, or inertia—has a separation margin exceeding \(\tau_s\|A\|_2\). It is backward-stable but forward-sensitive when the two backward-error inequalities hold but \(q>\tau_q\). It is structurally ambiguous when a singular-value, pivot, or eigenvalue separation test fails. It is factorization-unreliable when \(\eta_F>\tau_f\), and scaling-sensitive when \(\kappa_2(A)\) is large while \(\kappa_s\) is acceptable. These cases constitute the numerical reliability regimes of the Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the Newton system \(As=b\), reliability is classified using normalized residual error \(\eta_b\), factorization backward error \(\eta_F\), the best condition number attainable by positive diagonal row and column scaling \(\kappa_s\), and explicit separation margins for rank, pivots, and inertia. Given tolerances, a solve is reliable when both backward errors are small, \(u\kappa_s\) is small enough for forward information to survive rounding, and all structural classifications are separated from zero. It is backward-stable but forward-sensitive when the computed equation is accurate but conditioning can amplify its perturbation. It is structurally ambiguous when rank, pivot, or inertia decisions lie within their numerical thresholds. It is factorization-unreliable when the reconstructed factors do not represent a small perturbation of the intended matrix. It is scaling-sensitive when unscaled conditioning is poor but compatible diagonal scaling makes the system acceptably conditioned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal R(A,b,\widehat s,\widehat F)\in\{\text{reliable},\text{backward-stable/forward-sensitive},\text{structurally ambiguous},\text{factorization-unreliable},\text{scaling-sensitive}\}\] is determined by the stated error, conditioning, scaling, and separation tests.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For nonsingular \(A\), the forward error satisfies \[\widehat s-s=A^{-1}r,\] so a small residual alone is not a forward-reliability certificate when \(\|A^{-1}\|_2\) is large.
special_cases_latex: If \(A\) is well scaled, well conditioned, and factored by a backward-stable method, then \(\eta_b=O(u)\), \(\eta_F=O(u)\), and \(u\kappa_2(A)\ll1\) place the solve in the reliable regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: A backward-stable solve can belong to a forward-sensitive regime; backward stability and forward accuracy are therefore distinct classifications.
Changing variable or residual units may alter \(\kappa_2(A)\) without altering the exact Newton step after the corresponding inverse transformation.
boundary_notes: The tolerance values are application- and precision-dependent; the definition does not assign universal numerical constants.
Singular systems, least-squares Newton steps, and regularized systems require corresponding pseudoinverse or regularization-aware regimes.
Preconditioner staleness is represented here only through the resulting conditioning or factorization tests; its dedicated definition appears in its own slot.

notation.meaning: Normwise relative residual, used as a backward-error indicator.

Best Euclidean condition number over positive diagonal row and column scalings.

children.top_down_role: Solver degradation caused by incompatible variable, residual, or constraint scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Sensitive Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingular diagonal variable and residual scalings preserve the exact physical Newton step after coordinate conversion, but they can make the transformed system arbitrarily ill-conditioned in the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be differentiable, let \(J(x)=F'(x)\), and consider the Newton system \(J(x)p=-F(x)\). For nonsingular diagonal scalings \(D_x,D_r\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), define \(x=D_xz\) and \(\widehat F(z)=D_rF(D_xz)\). Then \(\widehat J(z)=D_rJ(D_xz)D_x\), and an exact scaled step \(\widehat p\) corresponds to the same physical step through \(p=D_x\widehat p\). This exact-step equivalence does not preserve Euclidean conditioning. In particular, for \(n=2\), \(J=I_2\), \(D_x=I_2\), and \(D_r=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon)\) with \(0<\varepsilon\leq1\), one has \(\kappa_2(D_rJD_x)=1/\varepsilon\). Thus diagonal scaling can make a well-conditioned Newton equation arbitrarily ill-conditioned as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is differentiable at the point under consideration.
Conditioning is measured in the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact-step equivalence does not imply numerical equivalence: \(\kappa_2(D_rJD_x)\) can be arbitrarily larger than \(\kappa_2(J)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning failure induced solely by incompatible variable and residual units.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaling sensitivity of a Newton linear system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) be a Newton or KKT operator and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Positive diagonal matrices \(D_r\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) and \(D_c\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) represent changes of residual and variable units. Under \(y=D_c^{-1}s\), the equivalent scaled system is \((D_rAD_c)y=D_rb\). For the condition-number definition below, \(A\) is square and nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns finite-dimensional normwise sensitivity caused by incompatible equation and variable scales. It distinguishes scaling sensitivity from intrinsic near-rank-deficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the diagonal-equilibration condition number and scaling-sensitivity ratio by \[\kappa_{\rm eq}(A)=\inf_{D_r,D_c\succ0\ {m diagonal}}\kappa_2(D_rAD_c),\qquad \mathfrak S(A)=\frac{\kappa_2(A)}{\kappa_{\rm eq}(A)}.\] Given thresholds \(K>1\) and \(\Gamma>1\), the Newton system is \((K,\Gamma)\)-scaling-sensitive when \[\kappa_2(A)\geq K,\qquad \mathfrak S(A)\geq\Gamma,\qquad \kappa_{\rm eq}(A)<\kappa_2(A).\] Thus the unscaled system is ill conditioned, but a substantial part of that ill conditioning can be removed by compatible positive diagonal changes of residual and variable units. Residual-scale incompatibility may additionally be recorded by \(\rho_b=\max_i |b_i|/\min_{i: b_i\neq0}|b_i|\), and variable-scale incompatibility by the corresponding dynamic range of prescribed typical variable magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A square nonsingular Newton system is scaling-sensitive when its unscaled Euclidean condition number is large but positive diagonal scaling of equations and variables can reduce that condition number by a prescribed substantial factor. The scaled equation \((D_rAD_c)y=D_rb\), with \(s=D_cy\), represents the same exact Newton step in different residual and variable units. The ratio \(\mathfrak S(A)=\kappa_2(A)/\kappa_{\rm eq}(A)\) separates removable scale imbalance from intrinsic ill conditioning: a large ratio signals sensitivity to the chosen units, whereas a value near one indicates that diagonal rescaling cannot materially repair the system. Large dynamic ranges among residual components or typical variable magnitudes are supplementary indicators, not sufficient conditions by themselves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A\text{ is }(K,\Gamma)\text{-scaling-sensitive}\iff \kappa_2(A)\geq K\text{ and }\frac{\kappa_2(A)}{\inf_{D_r,D_c\succ0}\kappa_2(D_rAD_c)}\geq\Gamma.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The variable transformation \(s=D_cy\) and residual transformation by \(D_r\) give \[As=b\iff (D_rAD_c)y=D_rb.\] Hence diagonal scaling changes numerical representation and conditioning but not the recovered exact step.
special_cases_latex: If \(A=\alpha B\) for a nonzero scalar \(\alpha\), then \(\kappa_2(A)=\kappa_2(B)\); uniform scalar scaling alone does not create scaling sensitivity.

If \(A\) is diagonal and nonsingular, choosing \(D_r=\operatorname{diag}(|a_{ii}|^{-1})\) and \(D_c=I\) gives \(\kappa_2(D_rAD_c)=1\), so disparate diagonal magnitudes are entirely removable by row scaling.
immediate_consequences_latex: A small unscaled residual can emphasize large-scale equations and conceal poor satisfaction of small-scale equations; a scaled residual \(\|D_r(b-A\widehat s)\|\) avoids that unit-dependent comparison.
Scaling sensitivity does not imply that the exact Newton direction lacks affine invariance; it concerns finite-precision formation, solution, and stopping tests.
boundary_notes: The infimum is a mathematical benchmark and need not be computed exactly by an implementation.
A large \(\kappa_{\rm eq}(A)\) indicates intrinsic conditioning or near-rank-deficiency rather than merely incompatible scales.
For rectangular systems, replace \(\kappa_2\) by the ratio of largest to smallest nonzero singular values and state the intended rank explicitly.

notation.meaning: Positive diagonal residual or row scaling.
Positive diagonal variable or column scaling.
Best condition number attainable by positive diagonal equivalence scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Rank-Deficient Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near rank deficiency amplifies a linear residual by as much as the reciprocal of the smallest singular value, so a small residual need not imply an accurate Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(p=J^{-1}b\) be the exact solution of the Newton system \(Jp=b\). For an approximate step \(\widetilde p\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define the residual \(r=b-J\widetilde p\). Then \(p-\widetilde p=J^{-1}r\), and hence \(\|p-\widetilde p\|_2\leq \|r\|_2/\sigma_{\min}(J)\). This factor is sharp: equality holds when \(r\) is a unit left singular vector associated with \(\sigma_{\min}(J)\). Therefore, as \(\sigma_{\min}(J)\downarrow0\), a small residual alone does not guarantee a small Newton-step error, and the error component in the corresponding right singular direction can be arbitrarily amplified.
assumptions_latex: \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular but may be ill-conditioned.
Residual and step error are measured in the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|p-\widetilde p\|_2\leq \|r\|_2/\sigma_{\min}(J)\), and the amplification factor \(1/\sigma_{\min}(J)\) is attainable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-error amplification as the smallest singular value approaches zero.

notation.meaning: linear-system residual b-J tilde p of the approximate Newton step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Numerical near-rank-deficiency of a Newton operator
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(p=\min\{m,n\}\), and let \(A=U\Sigma V^T\) be a singular-value decomposition with \(\sigma_1\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_p\geq0\). A numerical rank tolerance \(\tau_{\rm rank}\in(0,1)\) is fixed relative to \(\sigma_1=\|A\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition applies to finite-dimensional Newton, Jacobian, and KKT operators. It covers rectangular matrices and separates exact rank deficiency from tolerance-dependent numerical rank deficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The \(\tau_{\rm rank}\)-numerical rank of \(A\) is \[r_{\tau}(A)=\#\{i: \sigma_i(A)>\tau_{\rm rank}\sigma_1(A)\}.\] The operator is near rank deficient at tolerance \(\tau_{\rm rank}\) when \[r_{\tau}(A)<p\quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{rank}(A)=p,\] equivalently, when \(0<\sigma_p(A)\leq\tau_{\rm rank}\sigma_1(A)\). It is exactly rank deficient when \(\sigma_p(A)=0\). For a square nonsingular Newton system, near rank deficiency is equivalently \(\kappa_2(A)=\sigma_1(A)/\sigma_n(A)\geq\tau_{\rm rank}^{-1}\). The associated unstable right directions are \(\mathcal V_{\tau}=\operatorname{span}\{v_i:\sigma_i\leq\tau_{\rm rank}\sigma_1\}\), and the unstable left or multiplier directions are \(\mathcal U_{\tau}=\operatorname{span}\{u_i:\sigma_i\leq\tau_{\rm rank}\sigma_1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-rank Newton operator is near rank deficient when its smallest singular value is positive but no larger than a prescribed fraction of its largest singular value. The numerical rank counts only singular values exceeding that relative threshold. Thus exact rank deficiency means that the smallest singular value is zero, while near rank deficiency is a finite-precision or application-tolerance classification. The right singular vectors belonging to small singular values identify step directions that the operator maps only weakly; the corresponding left singular vectors identify residual or multiplier directions with poor determination. For a square nonsingular system, the same condition is that the Euclidean condition number exceeds the reciprocal rank tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A\text{ is near rank deficient}\iff 0<\sigma_p(A)\leq\tau_{\rm rank}\sigma_1(A).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For square nonsingular \(A\), \[0<\sigma_n\leq\tau_{\rm rank}\sigma_1\iff \kappa_2(A)\geq\tau_{\rm rank}^{-1}.\]
The Euclidean distance from \(A\) to a rank-deficient matrix equals \(\sigma_p(A)\), so the relative distance is \(\sigma_p(A)/\sigma_1(A)\).
special_cases_latex: For a KKT matrix, small singular values may arise from nearly dependent constraint gradients, weak reduced curvature, or both; the SVD definition does not conflate these mechanisms.
If \(A\) is symmetric, singular values are the absolute values of its eigenvalues, so near rank deficiency is \(0<\min_i|\lambda_i(A)|\leq\tau_{\rm rank}\|A\|_2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For any unit \(v\in\mathcal V_{\tau}\), \(\|Av\|_2\leq\tau_{\rm rank}\|A\|_2\), so small data perturbations can produce large changes along \(\mathcal V_{\tau}\).
Numerical rank depends on the tolerance and scaling; both must accompany any reported numerical rank.
boundary_notes: A small singular value created solely by poor units should be reassessed after compatible scaling.
The definition does not select a regularization, truncation, or minimum-norm solution.
For structurally singular systems, rank should be compared with the intended structural rank rather than automatically with \(p\).

notation.meaning: Numerical rank at relative singular-value tolerance \(\tau_{\rm rank}\).
Right singular subspace associated with threshold-small singular values.
Left singular subspace associated with threshold-small singular values.

children.title: Indefinite-Factorization Reliability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Reliability failures in indefinite factorizations and curvature classification.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reliability boundary for symmetric-indefinite factorization and inertia
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A=A^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\). A symmetric-indefinite factorization has the form \(PAP^T=LBL^T\), where \(P\) is a permutation, \(L\) is unit lower triangular, and \(B\) is block diagonal with \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) symmetric blocks. Computed factors \(\widehat L,\widehat B\) have reconstruction error \(E=P^T\widehat L\widehat B\widehat L^TP-A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns finite-dimensional real symmetric matrices and the reliability of inertia or curvature classification obtained from a pivoted block factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the relative factorization error and zero-eigenvalue separation by \[\eta_F=\frac{\|E\|_2}{\|A\|_2},\qquad \delta_0(A)=\frac{\min_i|\lambda_i(A)|}{\|A\|_2}.\] Given tolerances \(\tau_F,\tau_I>0\), the factorization is inertia-reliable when \[\eta_F\leq\tau_F\quad\text{and}\quad \min_i|\lambda_i(\widehat B)|>\tau_I\|A\|_2.\] The system lies on the indefinite-factorization reliability boundary when \[\delta_0(A)\leq\tau_I\quad\text{or}\quad\eta_F>\tau_F.\] On this boundary, a perturbation at the admitted numerical scale can change the classification of an eigenvalue as positive, zero, or negative, or the computed factors may fail to represent a sufficiently small perturbation of \(A\). Away from it, the inertia read from the \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) blocks of \(\widehat B\) is the numerical curvature classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric-indefinite factorization is reliable for curvature classification when it reconstructs the matrix with small relative backward error and every eigenvalue of its block-diagonal factor is separated from zero by more than the chosen inertia tolerance. The reliability boundary consists of matrices whose spectrum approaches zero at that scale, together with computed factorizations having excessive reconstruction error. Near the boundary, a small admissible perturbation can change an eigenvalue from positive to negative through zero, so the reported inertia is numerically ambiguous. The use of pivoting and \(2\times2\) blocks is part of the factorization model because an unpivoted diagonal \(LDL^T\) factorization of an indefinite matrix can exhibit excessive element growth and amplify rounding errors.
assumptions_latex: \[P^TP=I,\quad L\text{ is unit lower triangular},\quad B\text{ has symmetric }1\times1\text{ and }2\times2\text{ diagonal blocks}.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A\text{ is on the reliability boundary}\iff \frac{\min_i|\lambda_i(A)|}{\|A\|_2}\leq\tau_I\text{ or }\frac{\|E\|_2}{\|A\|_2}>\tau_F.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For symmetric \(A\), \(\min_i|\lambda_i(A)|=\sigma_{\\min}(A)\); the spectral part of the boundary is therefore the symmetric near-rank-deficiency boundary.
In exact arithmetic, congruence gives \(\operatorname{inertia}(A)=\operatorname{inertia}(B)\), with each nonsingular \(2\times2\) block contributing the signs of its two eigenvalues.
special_cases_latex: If \(A\succ0\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(A)>\tau_I\|A\|_2\), a successful Cholesky factorization is separated from the indefinite boundary.
A nonsingular \(2\times2\) pivot block with negative determinant has one positive and one negative eigenvalue and therefore contributes one direction of each curvature sign.
immediate_consequences_latex: A stable factorization can still yield ambiguous inertia when the true matrix has eigenvalues too close to zero.
A large or tiny pivot is not by itself an invariant curvature certificate; the eigenvalues of the pivot block and the global backward error must be assessed.
boundary_notes: The inertia tolerance must dominate the relevant rounding and data uncertainties; no universal value is asserted.
This definition does not require modifying \(A\) to be positive definite.
Nonsymmetric indefinite matrices do not possess an inertia under congruence in this sense.

notation.meaning: Relative backward reconstruction error of the computed factorization.
Relative spectral separation of a symmetric matrix from singularity.
Triple counting positive, zero, and negative eigenvalues of \(A\).

knowledge_statements.title: Pivoting Instability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearly singular accepted pivots can create large multipliers and element growth, defeating uniform backward-stability guarantees for indefinite factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In floating-point symmetric-indefinite elimination, an accepted pivot block \(D_j\) determines multipliers through solves with \(D_j\). If \(D_j\) is nearly singular, then \(\|D_j^{-1}\|\) is large, so bounded incoming entries can generate large multipliers and large Schur-complement updates. Define the element-growth factor \(\rho=\max_j\|A^{(j)}\|_{\max}/\|A\|_{\max}\), where \(A^{(j)}\) is the active matrix after \(j\) eliminations. A pivoting strategy crosses its numerical reliability boundary when accepted pivots permit unbounded \(\|D_j^{-1}\|\) or \(\rho\); no uniform small backward-error guarantee can then follow from machine precision alone.
assumptions_latex: The factorization uses symmetric pivot blocks of order one or two.
No uniform lower bound is imposed on accepted pivot-block singular values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unbounded \(\|D_j^{-1}\|\) or growth factor \(\rho\) is a failure boundary for uniform numerical reliability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reliability boundary for indefinite elimination with small pivots and element growth.

notation.meaning: accepted one-by-one or two-by-two pivot block
active Schur complement after j eliminations

A specific authoritative source on symmetric-indefinite pivoting stability is required before the hypotheses and conclusion can be validated.

knowledge_statements.title: Inertia Instability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inertia preservation is certified when the symmetric backward-error bound is smaller than the matrix's spectral distance from singularity; once that separation is lost, the bound alone cannot exclude an eigenvalue-sign change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and nonsingular, and let a computed symmetric factorization represent \(K+E\), where \(E=E^{\mathsf T}\). If \(\|E\|_2<\min_i|\lambda_i(K)|\), then \(K+E\) and \(K\) have the same inertia. If \(\min_i|\lambda_i(K)|\leq\|E\|_2\), this norm bound alone does not certify preservation of inertia: a symmetric perturbation within the permitted bound may move an eigenvalue through zero and change the positive or negative eigenvalue counts.
assumptions_latex: \(E=E^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is the factorization backward perturbation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|E\|_2<\min_i|\lambda_i(K)|\Longrightarrow \operatorname{inertia}(K+E)=\operatorname{inertia}(K)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation boundary for certifying inertia computation of symmetric Newton or KKT matrices.

notation.meaning: triple of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts
symmetric backward perturbation induced by the computed factorization
eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix K

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Misclassification Risk
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computed curvature sign is certified only when its magnitude exceeds the worst directional effect of the Hessian or factorization error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\), let \(\widehat H=H+E\) with \(E=E^{\mathsf T}\), and let \(d\neq0\). Then \(|d^{\mathsf T}\widehat H d-d^{\mathsf T}Hd|\leq\|E\|_2\|d\|_2^2\). Hence the sign of the computed curvature \(d^{\mathsf T}\widehat H d\) certifies the sign of the true curvature only if \(|d^{\mathsf T}\widehat H d|>\|E\|_2\|d\|_2^2\). When this strict separation fails, positive, negative, or zero curvature may be misclassified within the perturbation model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|d^{\mathsf T}\widehat H d|>\|E\|_2\|d\|_2^2\Longrightarrow \operatorname{sign}(d^{\mathsf T}Hd)=\operatorname{sign}(d^{\mathsf T}\widehat H d)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign reliability of directional curvature under Hessian or factorization perturbations.

notation.meaning: true symmetric Hessian or reduced-Hessian operator

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Singular Pivot Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pivot has a finite normwise perturbation certificate when its inverse amplifies the pivot perturbation to less than one. As that quantity approaches one, the certificate deteriorates; reaching one loses this guarantee but does not by itself prove singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a block elimination step, let \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times p}\) be a nonsingular pivot block and let \(\Delta D\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times p}\) be its computed perturbation. If \(\|D^{-1}\Delta D\|_2<1\), then \(D+\Delta D\) is nonsingular and \(\|(D+\Delta D)^{-1}\|_2\leq\|D^{-1}\|_2/(1-\|D^{-1}\Delta D\|_2)\). Thus the Neumann-series certificate for the pivot solve and its Schur-complement update deteriorates as \(\|D^{-1}\Delta D\|_2\) approaches one; at or above one, this certificate supplies no finite sensitivity bound, although the perturbed pivot need not be singular.
assumptions_latex: \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times p}\) is a nonsingular scalar or block pivot.
\(\Delta D\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times p}\) models the computed pivot perturbation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local normwise certification boundary for scalar or block pivots in indefinite Newton factorizations.

children.top_down_role: Misleading residual progress in ill-conditioned Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Error Mismatch
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual reduction can overstate solution accuracy: an ill-conditioned Newton matrix may turn a tiny residual into a large step error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular Newton matrix \(A\), exact step \(s_*=A^{-1}b\), approximation \(\widehat s\), residual \(r=b-A\widehat s\), and error \(e=s_*-\widehat s\), one has \(e=A^{-1}r\). Therefore \(\|e\|_2\leq\|A^{-1}\|_2\|r\|_2\), while \(\|r\|_2\geq\sigma_{\min}(A)\|e\|_2\). A small residual alone need not imply a small step error when \(\sigma_{\min}(A)\) is small; a scale-aware bound is \(\|e\|_2/\|s_*\|_2\leq\kappa_2(A)\|r\|_2/\|b\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-error interpretation of residuals for nonsingular, ill-conditioned Newton systems.

notation.meaning: linear-system residual b minus A times the approximate step
forward error in the Newton step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual–forward-error mismatch in an ill-conditioned Newton solve
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, \(As=b\) with \(b\neq0\) and \(s\neq0\), and let \(\widehat s\) be an approximate Newton step. Define \(r=b-A\widehat s\) and \(e=\widehat s-s\). Norms are Euclidean.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition concerns normwise residual and forward error for a fixed finite-dimensional linear Newton system. It does not treat nonlinear residual reduction between outer iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the relative residual, relative forward error, and mismatch amplification by \[\rho=\frac{\|r\|_2}{\|b\|_2},\qquad \varepsilon=\frac{\|e\|_2}{\|s\|_2},\qquad \mathfrak M(A,b,\widehat s)=\begin{cases}\varepsilon/\rho,&\rho>0,\\0,&\rho=\varepsilon=0,\\+\infty,&\rho=0<\varepsilon.\end{cases}\] Given tolerances \(0<\tau_r<\tau_e\), residual–error mismatch occurs when \[\rho\leq\tau_r\quad\text{but}\quad\varepsilon>\tau_e.\] Since \(Ae=-r\), the residual measures backward equation satisfaction whereas the forward error is filtered through \(A^{-1}\). The condition number \(\kappa_2(A)\) bounds the possible amplification and provides the computable warning indicator \(\kappa_2(A)\rho\), but the definition of mismatch uses the actual forward error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual–error mismatch occurs when an approximate Newton step has a small relative linear residual but remains unacceptably far from the exact step. The relative residual \(\rho\) measures how accurately the computed vector satisfies the equation, while the relative forward error \(\varepsilon\) measures the error in the step itself. Their ratio \(\mathfrak M\) records the observed amplification. Because \(Ae=-r\), a nearly singular or ill-conditioned matrix can map a large step error into a small residual. Consequently, residual progress alone is not a reliable proxy for step accuracy unless the conditioning of the Newton matrix is also controlled.
assumptions_latex: \[\widehat s\in\mathbb R^n,\quad r=b-A\widehat s,\quad e=\widehat s-s.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{residual–error mismatch}\iff \frac{\|b-A\widehat s\|_2}{\|b\|_2}\leq\tau_r\quad\text{and}\quad\frac{\|\widehat s-s\|_2}{\|s\|_2}>\tau_e.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The standard condition estimate gives \[\frac{\|e\|_2}{\|s\|_2}\leq\kappa_2(A)\frac{\|r\|_2}{\|b\|_2}.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(A\) is orthogonal up to a nonzero scalar, then \(\kappa_2(A)=1\), and relative residual and relative forward error cannot exhibit large normwise amplification.
If \(r=0\) in exact arithmetic and \(A\) is nonsingular, then \(\widehat s=s\), so mismatch is impossible.
immediate_consequences_latex: A stopping test based only on \(\|r\|_2\) may accept an inaccurate Newton step when \(\kappa_2(A)\) is large.
Scaling changes the meaning of an unweighted residual; residual and condition estimates should be evaluated in compatible scaled norms.
boundary_notes: The exact forward error is generally unavailable in computation; condition estimates or independent certificates are used as surrogates.
Componentwise residual–error mismatch is a distinct variant and may differ from this normwise definition.
For singular systems, the reference solution must be specified, such as a minimum-norm solution, before forward error is defined.

notation.meaning: Relative forward error in the Newton step.
Observed ratio of relative forward error to relative residual.

children.top_down_role: Degradation caused by reusing derivative or preconditioning information beyond its reliable regime.
