knowledge_statements.statement_title: Staleness of reused Newton operators and preconditioners
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be the nonsingular Newton operator at iteration \(k\). Information formed at iteration \(j\leq k\) is reused: either an approximate operator \(B_j\) in place of \(A_k\), or a nonsingular left preconditioner \(P_j\) for solving \(A_ks=b_k\). Norms are Euclidean operator norms.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers deterministic finite-dimensional Newton or Krylov solves with reused derivative, factorization, or preconditioning information. It measures staleness algebraically rather than by iteration age alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the relative operator defect and preconditioner defect by \[\eta_{\rm op}(k,j)=\frac{\|A_k-B_j\|_2}{\|A_k\|_2},\qquad \eta_{\rm pc}(k,j)=\|I-P_j^{-1}A_k\|_2.\] For a step \(s\neq0\), define the directional model defect \[\eta_{\rm dir}(k,j;s)=\frac{\|(A_k-B_j)s\|_2}{\|A_k\|_2\|s\|_2}.\] Given tolerances \(\tau_{\rm op},\tau_{\rm pc}>0\), the reused information is stale at iteration \(k\) when \(\eta_{\rm op}(k,j)>\tau_{\rm op}\) for an operator model, or \(\eta_{\rm pc}(k,j)>\tau_{\rm pc}\) for a left preconditioner. Its staleness effect is the resulting loss of model fidelity or deterioration of the preconditioned operator away from the identity. Iteration age \(k-j\) is not itself a staleness criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reused derivative or preconditioning information is stale when it no longer approximates the current Newton operator within a prescribed algebraic tolerance. Operator staleness is measured by the relative difference between the current operator \(A_k\) and a reused model \(B_j\); a directional version measures only the defect along a proposed step. Preconditioner staleness is measured by the distance of the current left-preconditioned operator \(P_j^{-1}A_k\) from the identity. These quantities describe the effect of reuse directly. A preconditioner may remain fresh over many iterations if the operator changes little, while information from the immediately preceding iteration may already be stale after a large or nonsmooth change.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{operator stale}\iff\eta_{\rm op}(k,j)>\tau_{\rm op},\qquad \text{preconditioner stale}\iff\eta_{\rm pc}(k,j)>\tau_{\rm pc}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(A_k=A_j+\Delta A_{k,j}\), reuse of an exact old inverse gives \[I-A_j^{-1}A_k=-A_j^{-1}\Delta A_{k,j}.\] Thus staleness combines operator change with amplification by the old inverse.
For right preconditioning, the analogous defect is \(\|I-A_kP_j^{-1}\|_2\); left and right defects need not coincide for nonnormal matrices.
special_cases_latex: If \(A_k=A_j\) and \(P_j=A_j\), then \(\eta_{\rm pc}(k,j)=0\); reuse is exact regardless of \(k-j\).
For a rank-one update \(A_k=A_j+uv^T\), \(\eta_{\rm op}=\|uv^T\|_2/\|A_k\|_2=\|u\|_2\|v\|_2/\|A_k\|_2\) when \(B_j=A_j\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\eta_{\rm pc}<1\), every singular value of \(P_j^{-1}A_k\) lies between \(1-\eta_{\rm pc}\) and \(1+\eta_{\rm pc}\), providing a direct quality certificate in the Euclidean norm.
A small directional defect can justify a step even when the global operator defect is large; the two tests answer different questions.
boundary_notes: For nonnormal preconditioned operators, distance from the identity is stronger than eigenvalue clustering and may be conservative.
Approximate application of \(P_j^{-1}\) introduces an additional error not represented by \(\eta_{\rm pc}\).
The thresholds depend on the required inner-solve accuracy and outer Newton forcing terms; no universal values are asserted.

notation.meaning: Relative discrepancy between the current Newton operator and reused operator information.
Distance of the left-preconditioned current operator from the identity.
Operator discrepancy restricted to a specified step direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Operator Effects
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solving the old Newton system accurately does not necessarily solve the current one: the current residual also contains the change in the operator applied to the step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(A_k,A_j\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be the current and reused Newton operators, respectively, with \(j<k\), and let \(F_k,s,q\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Suppose the current Newton equation is \(A_k s=-F_k\), while the computed step satisfies the stale equation \(A_j s=-F_k+q\), where \(q\) is the inner-solve residual. The residual in the current equation is \(A_k s+F_k=(A_k-A_j)s+q\). Consequently, \(\|A_k s+F_k\|_2\leq\|A_k-A_j\|_2\|s\|_2+\|q\|_2\); reducing \(q\) alone does not remove the defect caused by operator staleness.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k,A_j\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) are the current and reused Newton operators, and \(j<k\).
\(A_j s=-F_k+q\) defines the computed step and inner residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_k s+F_k=(A_k-A_j)s+q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: True-residual defect caused by solving with a previously assembled Newton operator.

notation.meaning: current nonlinear residual or Newton right-hand-side vector up to sign
residual of the stale linear solve

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Preconditioner Effects
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reused preconditioner remains effective while the current preconditioned operator stays close to identity; increasing staleness weakens conditioning guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_j\) be a nonsingular preconditioner retained from iteration \(j\) and applied to the current nonsingular Newton matrix \(A_k\). Then \(P_j^{-1}A_k=I+P_j^{-1}(A_k-P_j)\), so \(\|I-P_j^{-1}A_k\|_2\leq\|P_j^{-1}\|_2\|A_k-P_j\|_2\). If \(\eta_k=\|I-P_j^{-1}A_k\|_2<1\), every singular value of \(P_j^{-1}A_k\) lies in \([1-\eta_k,1+\eta_k]\), and its two-norm condition number is at most \((1+\eta_k)/(1-\eta_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_k<1\Longrightarrow\kappa_2(P_j^{-1}A_k)\leq\frac{1+\eta_k}{1-\eta_k}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral and norm degradation when a fixed preconditioner is reused for changing Newton operators.

notation.meaning: preconditioner constructed or refreshed at iteration j
normwise departure of the preconditioned operator from identity

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.4 Quasi-Newton Versions p. 256

knowledge_statements.title: Reuse-Horizon Limits
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An old Newton operator has a sufficient reuse certificate while the product of its inverse sensitivity, the operator-variation bound, and the distance from the refresh point is below one. Crossing one loses this guarantee but does not itself prove that the current operator is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathcal{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(\|A(x)-A(y)\|_2\leq L\|x-y\|_2\) for all \(x,y\in\mathcal{R}\), where \(x_j,x_k\in\mathcal{R}\), and suppose \(A_j=A(x_j)\) is nonsingular. Define \(A_k=A(x_k)\) and \(\rho_{j,k}=\|A_j^{-1}\|_2L\|x_k-x_j\|_2\). If \(\rho_{j,k}<1\), then \(A_k\) is nonsingular and \(\|A_k^{-1}\|_2\leq\|A_j^{-1}\|_2/(1-\rho_{j,k})\). Accordingly, this sufficient reuse certificate is valid only up to the first considered iterate for which \(\rho_{j,k}\geq1\); failure of the inequality means loss of this certificate, not necessarily singularity of \(A_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(A:\mathcal{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is Lipschitz continuous in the two-norm with constant \(L\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{j,k}<1\Longrightarrow A_k\text{ is nonsingular and }\|A_k^{-1}\|_2\leq\frac{\|A_j^{-1}\|_2}{1-\rho_{j,k}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient iteration-distance limit for certifying reuse of an earlier Newton operator.

notation.meaning: Newton operator at the last refresh iterate
Newton operator at the current iterate
operator Lipschitz constant in the two-norm

knowledge_statements.title: Staleness Degradation Detection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a rigorous upper bound on the preconditioned operator's departure from identity. A bound below the chosen contraction threshold certifies retention; exceeding the threshold or losing a bound below one triggers refresh.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k,P_j\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), with \(P_j\) nonsingular, and let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Compute a rigorous bound \(\eta_k\geq\|I-P_j^{-1}A_k\|_2\). If \(\eta_k<1\), then \(A_k\) is nonsingular, the equation \(A_kz_*=b\) has a unique solution, and the stationary correction \(z^{(m+1)}=z^{(m)}+P_j^{-1}(b-A_kz^{(m)})\) satisfies \(\|z^{(m+1)}-z_*\|_2\leq\eta_k\|z^{(m)}-z_*\|_2\). Given a prescribed threshold \(\tau\in(0,1)\), retain \(P_j\) while \(\eta_k\leq\tau\), and flag staleness degradation when \(\eta_k>\tau\) or no bound below one can be certified.
assumptions_latex: \(\eta_k\) is a rigorous upper bound satisfying \(\eta_k\geq\|I-P_j^{-1}A_k\|_2\).
\(\tau\in(0,1)\) is fixed before applying the detection rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_k\leq\tau<1\Longrightarrow A_k\text{ is nonsingular and }\|z^{(m+1)}-z_*\|_2\leq\tau\|z^{(m)}-z_*\|_2\), where \(z_*=A_k^{-1}b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise certificate and refresh trigger for a reused Newton preconditioner.

notation.meaning: rigorous upper bound on the normwise staleness indicator
unique solution of the current linear system when the certificate is below one
